That’s fine; I’ll be upset about it and I’m sure I’ll make the same mistake again until I ruin our friendship because that’s what I do. I’m a naturally destructive person and I’ll drag you down with me to make sure I’m not wallowing in my grief alone.”

     

                With a quiet huff of laughter, bristling slightly at Lena’s words, Kara climbed to her feet, crossing her arms over her chest. She’d borrowed one of Lena’s robes too, snagging it from the back of the ensuite door, but now she wished she was dressed so she could have the dignity of leaving when this inevitably soured. She wasn’t sure there would be much dignity in leaving in last night’s dress in broad daylight though.

     

                “That’s fine,” Kara curtly replied. “All I’m asking for is honesty. And you’ll never be alone in your grief because I might’ve had a shit husband but I loved him too, so you can self-destruct as much as you want but regardless of whether you push me away or not, I’m going to be right beside you anyway.”

     

                Lena scoffed, taking a drag of her cigarette and turning her head to blow the smoke away from Kara. They lapsed into silence and Lena toyed with the packet of Marlboro’s on the table. “She was a social smoker. I always hated the habit but I couldn’t bring myself to throw them away afterwards. Now I smoke them when I get stressed and I have to wonder if that was why she used to smoke them, because it was getting to be too much for her.”

     

                Putting the cigarette out in the dregs of her coffee, Lena gave Kara a despairing look. Her voice was gravelly and defeated as she continued.

     

                “You’re miles ahead of me Kara. You’re dating again and I can’t ever even see myself in a place where I could replace her, but I want that for you. I don’t know what you’re looking for but … you and me, it’s not going to be pretty. I’ve already been incredibly selfish to sleep with you twice when I know it’s just to fill that hole inside me and I’m sorry for that-“

God knows it would be a million times better for me to screw you than those random hookups that I know aren’t going to lead anywhere - I know that and you’re right, I don’t know why I put myself through it. Except that I do, because the loneliness is eating me up and maybe that’s why I’d be happy to be used by you because at least it feels like I have someone in some way. We’re going to be there for each other emotionally anyway; it wouldn’t have to mean anything else if it was physical.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena raked a hand through her hair and then abruptly climbed to her feet. The chair legs screeched across the floor and she stood a few feet from Kara, her expression unreadable.

     

                “You don’t … want to date me?”

     

                “Honestly, Lena, I don’t feel like having my heart broken again. So no, I don’t want to date you. I just like talking to you. And … I’d be lying if I said it wasn’t nice to just feel wanted. I know how you felt when you said that, so …”

     

                Shoulders going slack with relief, Lena let out an awkward laugh. “Well … now I just sound like a narcissistic bitch.”

     

                Snorting, Kara’s mouth twitched with a quick smile. “No, you sound like someone who’s scared to get in over her head. That’s okay though, I’m scared too. There are only so many people you can lose before the thought of losing anyone else becomes crippling.”

     

                “How’d you manage it? Losing so many people?” Lena softly asked, an aching sadness softening her face.

     

                Shrugging half-heartedly, Kara sighed. “You kind of just get used to it, or … you just end up numb and detached, I guess. I’d probably manage as well in a relationship as you would, so don’t worry about that. But … if it’s the loneliness, well … I wouldn’t mind the company.”

     

                The corner of Lena’s mouth twitched, a shallow dimple making a brief appearance, and there was a vulnerable doubt in her green eyes. Yesterday’s makeup smudged beneath her eyes, making her bags more prominent, the smell of coffee and whisky and tobacco shrouding her, she was a beautifully dishevelled mess. Hesitating, she bit her lip and then looked down, her hands going to the belt of her robe.

     

                Undoing it, she pushed it over her shoulders and then let it slide the rest of the way off, stepping closer towards Kara. Blinking in surprise at the sudden turn of things, Kara barely dared to breathe as she kept her eyes on Lena’s face.

     

                “It’s the loneliness,” Lena murmured in agreement. “I feel like it’ll swallow me if I don’t do something about it.”

     

                “We can help each other,” Kara whispered, her lips barely moving as her eyes darted down to Lena’s mouth, her hand moving on its own accord, grazing the bare skin of her waist.

     

                Leaning in, Lena kissed her slowly and it was different when they were stone-cold sober, more deliberate and less fervent. Kara felt a warm flush spread through her body, conscious of the fact that it had been a long time since someone had made her feel that way, like she was desirable as she was, as a person and not just a one-night stand, and not just a widow. Wrapping her arms around her tightly, Kara kissed her back hard, neediness almost overwhelming her as she tasted the coffee and cigarettes on Lena’s lips. 

     

                It was quick, Kara’s breaths stilling as she knelt on the hard kitchen floors with her cheek against Lena’s thigh, her friend perched on the counters, leaning back against the marble backsplash as her chest heaved. Hesitating, Kara turned her head, pressing a cheek to the smooth pale skin of Lena’s thigh before she pushed herself to her feet, fixing her robe.

     

                Lena slid down, reaching for her and Kara caught her hand, a quick smile on her face. “You don’t have to. And I should go.”

     

                “Oh. Okay,” Lena murmured, brow crumpling as she ducked past Kara to scoop up her robe. 

     

                Pulling it on as Kara found her dress from last night, Lena belted it and cleared her throat as Kara got past the self-consciousness of undressing in front of Lena and slipped into her clothes. Turning as she fumbled for her zipper, she raised her eyebrows, blue eyes curious and slightly wary.

     

                Lena stepped in and gestured for her to turn, her fingers smoothly drawing up the zipper for Kara. Then her fingers skimmed back down Kara’s back and she paused, long enough for Kara to turn again, reading the doubt on her face.

     

                “Are we going to do this again?”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Kara didn’t know what to say for a moment. “I- well … that depends. If- if you wanted to we could, but … well, we don’t have to either. I know things get a bit confusing after a few drinks.”

     

                “Drunk me just has the courage to act on sober thoughts,” Lena said with a thin smile. “And I don’t think drinking will work as an excuse for just now.”

     

                A crooked smile hitched Kara’s mouth, “you don’t need any excuses. You never have to explain yourself to me.”

     

                “Of course I do. I can’t go around being a dick without cause, can I?”

     

                Snorting, Kara folded the robe in her hands and set it neatly down on the island counter. “You’re not a dick. Although maybe I’m biassed.”

     

                “How so?”

     

                “Well, you’re my best friend,” Kara said as if it was surprising she had to say it.

     

                Surprise blossomed on Lena’s face as well, her eyes widening a fraction as her eyebrows rose. “Am I?”

     

                Kara blinked, cocking her head to the side. “Of course you are.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                She finished gathering her things together; her phone where she’d left it on the coffee table last night, her handbag on the floor, her coat hanging by the door with her discarded heels, wincing at the thought of wearing them home, new blisters forming beneath last night’s. Flipping her hair out from under her collar, buttoned up over the short dress, Kara faced Lena and gave her a tender smile.

     

                “Come here.”

     

                Wrapping her in a gentle hug, they swayed for a moment and Kara felt some of the tension in her chest recede. It didn’t feel so awkward between them now, their cards on the table and their deliberate choices relieving some of that lingering unease that had plagued them. It had felt inevitable that they’d slip back into that drunken desire at some point, even as Kara was determined to not fuck it up, but it didn’t feel like such a mistake as last time.

     

                Giving her cheek a quick kiss, nothing more to it than a quick reassurance to a friend, Kara pulled back and gave Lena a soft smile. “Are we still on for the oyster bar on Tuesday?”

     

                “Sure, I’ll see you then,” Lena agreed.

     

                “Okay. Call if you need anything, okay? Or if you get into your own head about it too much. I don’t mind listening.”

     

                “Have a good day.”

     

                Kara left after that, feeling oddly thoughtful as her worries weighed heavily on her mind. There was a lot to consider when it came to Lena, beyond the simplicity of the arrangement they’d sketched an outline for. She’d burrowed her way into Kara’s life, and not just outside of Group but as a fixture at drinks, her friends slowly but surely becoming their friends, and it would be disastrous if things become so blurred that their friends caught wind of what was going on, not least of all because of their emotional states at present. Alex had cautioned Kara enough times for her to behave ignorantly of the consequences but she didn’t think what they were doing would be enough to break their friendship apart.

     

                Riding the bus home, not feeling nearly hungover enough to look the state that she was in, Kara walked from her stop home in her heels, cold air on her legs, and let herself into the apartment. The smell of bread and coffee from a nearby shop made her stomach rumble and she considered whether she should’ve asked Lena for breakfast or if that would have been making too much out of it. They ate together all the time but it would inherently feel different after sex.

     

                Getting wrapped up in her thoughts of what would and wouldn’t blur this newly drawn line, she checked her bank account to see how much was left in it hastily showered and changed into jeans and a flannel shirt before scraping her hair into a messy bun and pulling her coat back on. Making her way to the coffee shop, she ordered herself a bagel and a latte and spent a couple of hours tucked away in the corner before resigning herself to the monotony of real life by going grocery shopping, pushing a squeaky cart around as she loaded up on cronuts, feta, pop tarts and buying a measly bunch of kale in an attempt to feel like she had it together before returning home and doing some laundry.

     

                The rest of the day was a throwaway after that, watching Netflix as she idly flipped through books without really reading them, and then scrolled through social media, seeing engagements and pregnancy announcements and weddings, until it made her feel too bitter and she gave up. She called Alex, who was at a farmer’s market with Kelly, then Winn, who was at a tech expo, then James, who was at the gym and Nia, who was having happy hour drinks with people from work. Of course, Kara could’ve called Lena, who was never doing anything except working or sitting home alone as if waiting for Kara to see if she was free, but it felt too soon, not enough space.

     

                Instead, Kara called her mother and spent an hour on the phone, realising with a sudden start that Eliza was probably what she’d look like in a few years, in a decade, if she hadn’t moved on. Her mother’s loneliness struck her suddenly as overwhelmingly obvious and she faltered on the phone, the burning urge to ask why she’d never remarried after Jeremiah, how she’d stood being alone for so many years afterwards. Of course, Kara knew why; Eliza had two daughters to focus all of her attention on, to fill the hours that her husband no longer occupied, giving her some purpose that Kara didn’t have, childless as she was. 

     

                She hung up not long after that, feigning some set plans with Lena so that her mom wouldn’t worry too much. At just shy of thirty-five, Kara thought she was too old to have someone worrying about her but there was no use telling Eliza that, wearily agreeing to her warnings and her assurances to look after herself.

     

                The sky was the peach of an early sunset, the city already aglow with neon and headlights and billboards, the drone of traffic a comforting constant as Kara made herself a grilled cheese and poured a La Croix into a glass with vodka. Alone at the kitchen table, she ate her dinner and sipped her drink, the vodka taking the edge off her stress as a stack of bills lay unopened beside her. Wallowing in her loneliness as she tried not to worry about money, Kara thought about how different it had been having someone else to split life with, what it had been like to wake up next to Mike every day and how much she missed that, and then her thoughts slipped to how it had been nice to sleep beside Lena, even if it hadn’t been the same. 

     

                After three drinks, all of them made a little stronger than she probably should have, Kara swallowed two painkillers with water and fell into bed, the night still relatively early but the darkness making her lethargic. That could’ve been the vodka too, but she felt pleasantly numb and loose-limbed as she sprawled across the bed, listening to a TEDTalk as the glow of her phone screen lit up the room.

     

                The video was interrupted by a phone call, Lena’s name lighting up her screen, and Kara chewed on her lip for a moment as her stomach swooped, wondering if she should answer it or not. Too old for childish games, she answered it and hesitated before pressing the phone to her ear.

     

                “Hey.”

     

                Voice soft with caution, Lena warily greeted her and Kara felt an ache in her chest, understanding flooding her as she felt a stab of pity and compassion for her friend. 

     

                “Did you get inside your head?” Kara murmured.

     

                Lena’s laugh was a breathless huff on the other end. “A little.”

     

                Rolling onto her side, her eyes sliding shut as she made herself comfortable, Kara softly sighed. “What’s wrong?”

     

                “I just … I wish I could know how she’d feel about this.”

     

                “You knew her; how do you think she’d feel?”

     

                There was a long pause of quiet static before Lena sighed. “I know that … at the end, she wanted me to move on. I always stubbornly insisted that I never would but … now I’m afraid that this has- this has maybe shown that … maybe my promises were never worth that much. If I could sleep with someone else, maybe our vows weren’t all that important to me. I thought they were ...”

     

                “You haven’t moved on and you kept your vows to the end. Even if you did move on, even if you break your vows now, it doesn’t make you a bad person. You loved her very much.”

     

                “It’s not the end,” Lena raggedly replied and Kara could tell that she’d been drinking - a lot more than the three drinks she’d had herself. “That’s the worst part, it’s not over and it’ll never end and this is just going to be my life now.”

     

                “It won’t always feel this way.”

     

                “What do you know?” Lena sharply retorted. “You don’t know the half of it.”

     

                Kara quietly scoffed, “don’t I?”

     

                “Forget it. I shouldn’t have called; that’s my mistake.”

     

                Sagging with weary resignation, Kara sighed. “No, Lena, it’s-”

     

                The line went dead before she could convince her to stay on the line, talking through whatever was bothering her, whatever feelings Kara may have exacerbated with her own selfish desire to have someone fill the hole in her life. A rough sigh scraped her throat as she tossed her phone beside her on the mattress, rolling over and burying her face in her pillows.

     

                She fell asleep soon after and didn’t hear from Lena until Tuesday, confirming their dinner plans for that evening. Kara had expected her to cancel and was surprised, if a little wary, when she arrived at the oyster bar, a packet of dog treats she’d bought at work for Aristotle in hand as Lena walked from where she’d parked her car. They ate too many oysters, the cold lozenges hard to swallow at times and Kara let Lena drive her home before saying goodnight, neither of them speaking about anything that had happened as they lingered in the pleasant aftermath of dinner and listened to the radio as they crawled through inner-city traffic.

     

                Things were normal at Group that Thursday and Lena was at drinks on Friday, and their lives followed their usual routines, save for the eclipsing difference that occasionally, perhaps only once or twice a month, or in a bad spell maybe once or twice a week, they would get drunk enough to end up in someone’s bed. The next time it had been at Kara’s after karaoke and falafel from a food truck, the time after that when a taco night had turned into shots of tequila, the bite of salt and lime cutting through it, and then once when they’d both been sober again and Kara had accidentally stayed over and they’d gone out for breakfast the next morning, Lena smoking as Kara held Aristotle’s leash and they ate breakfast burritos and sipped ice coffees in the park.

     

    An ease had come between them, smoothing things out so that Lena no longer cried anymore afterwards and Kara didn’t feel like they were fucking things up. It was almost nice, in a             way, like dating without the complexity of feelings, although there were definitely some there, buried and ignored for the sake of companionship. It added a depth to their friendship that hadn’t existed before though, trust and honesty strengthening it as they navigated their way through it without letting it touch their normal life. 

     

                For the first time in a long while, Kara felt comfortable in her life, the routine of her burgeoning social life and full-time work leaving her practically back where she was before Mike had died - just without her husband beside her. There were moments where she was low and drank a little too much and sustained herself on takeout, but she’d been making a real effort to go to pilates and yoga classes, near-daily walks with Aristotle - even if Lena didn’t join them, wrapped up in a new project - and trying out new recipes that she’d always strayed away from because Mike would scoff and make some comment about how awful it would be. 

     

                Even Alex commented approvingly on the progress she was making over breakfast one Saturday morning after Kara had wound up at her sister’s place after drinks. Kelly had just come in from a night shift at the hospital so they were quiet as they murmured over eggs and bacon, drinking coffee with cream and sugar as Kara feigned as much enthusiasm as she could for Group, which she lauded as the reason she was processing her grief so well. Of course, she knew the real reason was that it had been a year of Lena’s company that had lessened the burden of carrying it alone.

     

                Kara told her sister everything but this was one thing she kept to herself. She knew what Alex would say and she knew she’d be somewhat right about it, but Kara didn’t want to admit that to herself, not when she was doing so well. It had seemed impossible that she’d find her spark again but it was there, still burning strongly amidst the oppressive darkness of everything that had happened, and being around Lena made it flare even brighter. Kara liked who she was around Lena, none of her history mattered, only the person she was now and the things she wanted to do that she’d never had the time or been able to.

     

                It was freeing, in a sense, to visit art galleries and museums and attend concerts and comedy shows, things that Mike had never wanted to go to with her. The only place he’d ever wanted to go was to baseball matches, and there was only so much sport Kara could endure. Lena frequently came with her but even when she didn’t, Kara found a sense of peace in walking around a spacious gallery in the hush, or idly browsing the shelves of a bookstore with the low murmur of other shoppers, buying clothes for herself that she hadn’t thought was her style, hadn’t thought Mike would like, and finding that she enjoyed being a little high maintenance, getting a manicure or a facial and cutting in the bangs she’d grown out as a teenager and had flirted with getting again until Mike had said he didn’t like bangs. 

     

                It was startling to her how much he’d inhibited, and she hadn’t even really noticed it, hadn’t thought about the compromises she’d made and the labour she’d put into their marriage to dress him and feed him and entertain him. And for what? He’d been selfish with his time and affection and maybe that was why Kara had given into Lena so easily, who was reserved and unfamiliar with it but never intentionally held back. Her honesty was brutal at times and they never held hands or cuddled or kissed outside of sex, but it was never out of indifference and that made all the difference in the world. 

     

                There was an ease between them though, casual touches that spoke of a deeper intimacy, and they were usually good at keeping it hidden, especially considering Alex worked long and odd hours as a surgeon, and Kelly as a psychiatrist, which meant they were frequently absent from drinks. But her sister had an eagle eye when she was around and Kara wasn’t always so careful.

     

                They were at Al’s again one Friday in early September, playing games of pool on the worn table and chatting over their drinks as they huddled around a small table. It was a quiet night, not as rowdy as usual and with no karaoke, and Kara sat beside Lena, the two of them frequently in their own little bubble as they ducked their heads together, murmuring some comment and sharing their laughter. When Lena drained her glass of wine, Kara gently cupped her elbow as she leaned in.

     

                “Want another one?”

     

                “Go on then,” Lena said after a brief hesitation, a smile quirking her lips.

     

                Nodding, Kara raised her eyebrows as she looked around at the rest of her friends. “Anyone else want another one?”

     

                When her eyes landed on Alex’s face, her expression fell and Kara’s stomach lurched slightly as she quickly averted her gaze, a flush of embarrassment washing over her. Alex was known for her honesty and never cared much for keeping things secret within their friend group, and Kara could see she’d done the math and wouldn’t hold back from blurting out her sudden revelation in front of everyone else.

     

                “Oh, you-” Alex started, her brown eyes almost affronted as she stared at her sister, who quickly cut her off, chair screeching back as Kara shot to her feet.

     

                “Alex, come help me get the next round,” she cut her off.

     

                Turning, she stalked away from the table with hunched shoulders, waiting for the barrage of comments from her sister. Reaching the bar first, Kara breathlessly ordered two beers, a glass of wine and a whisky before Alex stepped up beside her, her accusing stare burning into the side of Kara’s head.

     

                “You’re screwing her?” she quietly hissed.

     

                “Only a couple of times,” Kara confessed, feeling her face redden. 

     

                Alex softly punched her arm. “You idiot.”

     

                “Yeah, probably,” Kara scrunched her nose in a sheepish manner. “She was just so lonely, Alex-”

     

                “For God’s sake, Kara, you’re thirty-four . You’d think you’d have more common sense at that age.”

     

                Spluttering, Kara straightened slightly, shoulders squaring. “Well, you’re thirty-seven, so maybe you’re too old to be so involved in my sex life.”

     

                “Don’t be an ass,” Alex scoffed, mouth turning down at the corners. “I’m just looking out for you. I don’t want you to get hurt.”

     

                Nudging her sister, Kara gave her a crooked, wry smile. “I’m a widow . You couldn’t protect me from that and I don’t think anything else will hurt that much so … I’m good.”

     

                “Yeah, but she-”

     

                “Don’t give her a hard time, okay? It’s bad enough as it is without people getting down on us for trying to find some way to cope. I didn’t say anything about how much you used to drink when Maggie dumped you.”

     

                Alex let out a quiet huff and snagged two bottles of beer from the bar, “yeah, well, sometimes I wish you had.”

     

                Shoulders slumping defeatedly, Kara sighed and forked over the cash to Al before carrying the remaining drinks back. She doled out bottles of beer and set Alex’s whisky down a little too hard before handing Lena her wine only a little more gently. 

     

                “Is everything alright?” Lena murmured.

     

                Making a small sound at the back of her throat, Kara pressed her bottle to her lips and tipped her head back, cheeks still slightly burning with annoyance as she drained half of her drink and set it back down. Looks were exchanged and Alex was a little surly as she swirled her whisky in the glass and Querl launched into a story about his work as the attention was drawn away from the sisters. Whenever Kara’s eyes met Alex’s, a silent argument seemed to ensue through facial expressions, and when James went to get the next round, Kara climbed to her feet and sighed. 

     

                Rounding the table, she clapped a hand down on Alex’s shoulder and gently squeezed. “Come and have a game with me.”

     

                Grunting in acknowledgement, Alex raised her glass to her lips and sipped the dregs while Kara walked over to the unoccupied pool table and picked up a cue. Carefully chalking the tip of it, she blew off the loose powder and watched as Alex pretended to take her time. She let her sister break first and leaned on her cue as she watched Alex line up her shot, the crack cutting through the quiet din of the bar.

     

                “You’re an idiot,” Alex said as she straightened up, pocketing two stripes and lining up her next shot.

     

                “Yeah,” Kara agreed. “It helps though.”

     

                Alex snorted, “right, a good orgasm will fix all your problems. It had better be good or you’re an even bigger idiot.”

     

                Making a scathing sound at the back of her throat, Kara nudged the end of Alex’s cue as she made her shot. Her sister whirled around, giving her a withering look of annoyance and Kara gave her a quick grin. “Don’t be an asshole.”

     

                “I’m scared for you.”

     

                Kara’s smile turned a little strained and she gestured for Alex to take another shot. “Don’t be. I’m old enough to know what I’m doing.”

     

                “Still young enough for heartbreak, and to make stupid mistakes.”

     

                “We’re not dating.”

     

                “You see how that’s worse , right?”

     

                Alex stepped out of the way and Kara hunched over the table, closing one eye as she tried to aim straight. She hit her ball squarely but didn’t pocket it. 

     

                “If she was a nice, normal woman, I’d tell you to go for it in a heartbeat - you think I can’t see how much happier you are now? And it’s not just time healing it, it’s her and I know that and I could kiss her for it - but it’s not that simple and you know it. You’re going to get hurt.”

     

                Her throat closed up tightly and Kara looked down as she gripped her cue tightly, swallowing past the lump as Alex took her next shot, just managing to miss the pocket. Kara took her turn, pocketing two and missing a third before she managed to reply. 

     

                “Don’t you think it’s better for me to lessen the pain for a little while instead of wallowing in it like I was?”

     

                “Yes,” Alex admitted after a moment, “but I’m afraid that you’ll slip even deeper into it again if this all goes badly.”

     

                Letting out a weary, rough sigh, Kara raked a hand through her hair, messing up her newly chopped bangs. She quickly ruffled her fingers through it to try and straighten it out again. “I can’t really bring myself to think past the now. It’s either now or the past and I- it’s too much to constantly be stuck in the memories so I’m just- I’m doing what I can. It’s not ideal, I know that. It’s better than it was though and … it’s just nice to have the company. She makes me feel less alone.”

                Alex’s shoulders rose and fell with a quiet breath and she pressed a hand against Kara’s back, giving it a quick rub. “Alright. You’re not alone though, you know that, right?”

     

                Mouth hitching into an uneven smile, sad blue eyes softening, Kara nodded. “I know. It’s just different.”

     

                Accepting that, Alex took her shot and they played out the rest of the game, Kara’s shoddy skills no match for her sister. It helped smooth things over to let Alex win anyway, so Kara didn’t bristle and demand a rematch like she ordinarily would have, even though she usually lost every time anyway. The odd tension dissipated quickly and they were quietly laughing and joking as they returned to their table, fresh drinks waiting for them and Lena in conversation with Nia about Cat Grant’s latest book.

     

                Her eyes slid sideways to Kara, whose cheek dimpled slightly with a smile as she picked up her beer and took a sip. Giving Lena a shallow nod, she felt the reassuring pat of her hand on her thigh and felt her stomach twinge slightly, feeling almost guilty for enjoying the simple intimacy of the gesture.  They stayed for another hour or so and then collectively left, leaving through the front door to flag down cabs to take them home. Shoulders hunched in her jacket as a cold wind assaulted them, Kara glanced at Alex.

     

                “Ride with me?”

     

                Hesitating, Alex shook her head, her eyes sliding past Kara. “No, you make sure Lena gets home okay. I’ll share with Nia and Querl; it’s less of a trek.”

     

                Brow furrowing slightly, Kara didn’t protest and turned to Lena, raising her eyebrows suggestively. Nodding, Lena got the next cab and ushered Kara into the back as they called goodbyes over their shoulders, another cab already pulling up for the next lot. Shutting them into the warm interior, Lena heavily sighed and buckled herself in before looking at Kara.

     

                “She knows, then?”

     

                Looking startled by Lena’s intuitive guess, she gave her a sheepishly strained smile. “She guessed.”

     

                “You could’ve told her, just for the record,” Lena said with a small laugh. “We’re all adults here. I mean, I know why you didn’t, and a big part of me is relieved, but I would hate to come between you and your sister.”

     

                “You’re not. She’s just worried.”

     

                “Well, I guess she was right to be worried last time, about watching yourself around me.”

     

                “And this time?”

     

                Lena looked out the window, her mouth turning down slightly at the corners. “We’re both on the same page. That’s all that matters.”

     

                Cocking her head to the side, Kara raised her eyebrows. “And what page are we on tonight?”

     

                Turning back to her, Lena’s face softened with a smile, green eyes bright from a few drinks. She considered the question for a second and then lowered her voice, a warm murmur that made Kara’s skin prickle. “Come back to mine.”

    Chapter 11

                Pulling her chair in a fraction more as she settled at the table in Al’s with her next beer before her, Kara took a sip as her eyes roamed around the bar. Her phone weighed heavily in her pocket, silent despite the voicemails she’d left for the serious tone of her best friend asking her to leave a message.

                Lowering her beer bottle, Kara frowned, fishing out her phone again. “I called her but she didn’t answer.”

    [Kara]: hey are you coming to Al’s?

     

                Rejoining the conversation, she set her phone down on the sticky tabletop and sipped her beer, half of her mind distracted. It was five minutes before the screen lit up with the first text, two more bubbles appearing on the lockscreen in rapid succession.

     

    [Lena]: not tonight

     

    [Lena]: not having a good day

     

    [Lena]: sorry

     

                Picking her phone up, Kara quickly typed out a response and stared at the screen, watching the three little dots appear and then disappear as Lena contemplated her reply.

    [Lena]: no

     

                Setting her phone back down, Kara let out a short, frustrated sigh. Running a hand over her face she snagged her bottle and took another sip, face pinched with worry.

She kissed her sister’s cheek and apologetically said her goodbyes, snagging her denim jacket from the table as she swept past. When she passed by Kelly, her sister-in-law caught her arm, making her pause.

     

                Producing a business card with a quick flourish, Kelly leaned in, Kara ducking her head down slightly to hear her over the din of the music. “Take this, just in case.”

Murmuring her thanks, she pocketed it and left the bar.

     

                She’d used up all of her cash for the next round and didn’t have enough change for the bus, so Kara caught a cab, Lena’s address rolling off her tongue as she settled in on the cracked seats. The vents pumped out hot air that made her feel a little flushed, shifting restlessly as she kept checking her phone for any further texts, wondering if she should let Lena know she was coming over.

     

                In the end, she decided against it, knowing her friend well enough to know she’d try and convince Kara to stay for drinks. Caught in the tail-end of rush-hour traffic, Kara’s knee bounced as she watched the neighbourhood change from cheap diners, little convenience stores and graffiti and alleyways of trash, music spilling out of a dozen bars in a cacophony of noise to the quieter, upscale bars and restaurants, the boutiques and finance businesses closed for the day. Lena’s part of town was like a pocket of quiet, the only noise the traffic passing by, muffled behind the thick glazing of her penthouse windows.

     

                As they rounded the corner a block from Lena’s home, Kara’s eyes snagged on the 7-Eleven, neon lights garishly out of place in the otherwise relatively muted neighbourhood. Asking the driver to pull over, Kara paid with her card and clutched it in her hand as she ducked out into the night, yanking open the door and stepping into the brightly lit store.

     

                Nodding to the cashier, she made her way up and down the aisles, grabbing a cheap bottle of wine, knowing Lena had better at her place but knowing you needed the sour sickliness of the cheap stuff to really numb you to your feelings. Grabbing a six-pack of beers as well, and then two pints of ice cream - cookie dough, which was Lena’s favourite, and then fudge, which Kara had grown fond of in her low moments - before adding a dozen little powdered donuts to the pile. Asking for a packet of Marlboros at the counter, eyes snagging on the display of cigarettes and thinking maybe Lena needed them and had run out of her dead wife’s, Kara paid for her pile and took the plastic bag. 

     

                Walking the rest of the way to Lena’s, Kara got someone else to buzz her in when Lena didn’t answer, and rode the elevator up to the top floor. Knocking on Lena’s door, she shifted restlessly as she waited, hearing the muffled buzz of the television inside, Aristotle barking, the scratch of his claws as he ran to the door to greet her.

     

                When Lena didn’t answer, Kara pounded on the door in case she hadn’t heard, and then tried calling her. Her call went straight to voicemail and she listened to the polished sound of Lena’s voice before hanging up. Opening up their messages, Kara worked the plastic bag handles over her wrist to type out a new text.

     

    [Kara]: at your door

     

    [Kara]: brought snacks

                There was the shuffle of movement inside, padding footsteps growing closer, and then the door swung inwards to reveal Lena, looking mildly taken aback at the fact that Kara was on her doorstep. Her eyes were red, her cheeks even paler than usual and splotchy. Her face crumpled to a scowl, embarrassment making her harden as she ducked her head.

     

                “You’re supposed to be at drinks.”

     

                “A bad day shouldn’t be spent alone,” Kara gently reasoned.

                Lena was watching an old episode of The Wire , a bottle of scotch on the coffee table, her glass over-full. Sitting beside her, kicking off her boots, Kara unpacked the bag, setting the sweating tubs of ice cream down and then fetching two spoons.                 “I-”

     

                “You don’t have to explain to me,” Kara quickly hushed her.

     

                Nodding, Lena swallowed thickly, her mouth turning down at the corners as she scraped the tip of the spoon through the softening ice cream.                 “You didn’t have to come,” Lena gravelly replied after a few minutes of suffocating silence.

     

                “I know but I wanted to make sure you were okay; that’s what friends do. It wasn’t really much of a choice between shitty beers or you. Besides, I brought the shitty beer with me.”

     

                Lena let out a hoarse laugh, running a hand through her hair. “Careful or I’ll tell Alex.”

     

                “She told me to come. Also robbed me for the next round as well, so she won’t mind too much.”

     

                Leaning forward, Kara snagged the cans of beer from the confines of the bag and worked it out of the plastic loops before holding the rest up. “Want one?”

                “Are you okay?”

Looking wary, Lena set a pair of pyjamas down on the vanity and grabbed a fresh towel from the rolled pyramid stack her housekeeper maintained for her.

     

                Giving her a quick smile, Kara turned the taps off and then cleared her throat, gesturing to the door. “Take your time. I can occupy myself.”

     

                She slipped back outside and used the time to order Thai food from the pricier restaurant a few blocks west, eyeing the price grimly as she tried to mentally budget her latest paycheck with the mortgage she was already struggling to cover by herself. A few weeks ago she’d briefly considered the idea of getting a roommate, closing off a section of the living room so they could fit a bed, but it would’ve been an awkward fit and probably would have meant the loss of her sofa. Instead, Kara just drank another beer and stamped down the stress of being a widow who couldn’t afford her single income.

     

                The food arrived thirty minutes later, just as Lena was getting out of the bath, and Kara set the table in the kitchen and unpacked the bag, steaming containers of rice and Massaman, red curry and little pork curry puffs. Lena’s hair was wet and tangled down her back as she appeared, pink-cheeked as she towelled the ends of her hair.

     

                “You should eat something,” Kara murmured.

     

                Nodding, Lena quietly thanked her and took a seat. Kara dished up some rice for herself first and spooned curry over it as Lena helped herself, neither of them saying much as they ate. It was filling and hot and Kara felt better for it, the few beers she’d already drained on top of her drinks at Al’s making her feel a little bloated and buzzed. The last thing she needed was a hangover in the morning.

     

                After they finished, Lena went back to the sofa to drink in silence, running her fingers over Aristotle’s short fur as she stared at the TV with a glassy-eyed look on her face. Kara loaded the dishwasher and added in a few of the coffee cups and glasses that hadn’t been broken in the sink and then set it on to run before making her way back to the living room. She lingered behind Lena for a moment and stared at the back of her before breaking the silence.

     

                “Come on, let’s go to bed.”

     

                Draining her last drink and climbing to her feet without protest, Lena directed Aristotle to the bed tucked away in the corner of the kitchen and made her way to her room. Kara followed after her, a little hesitant, and then climbed into bed beside Lena. She was grateful for the wide bed, which made it easier to think she was alone, that she wasn’t lying beside her friend who she had conflicted feelings about, trying not to make more out of it as she went to sleep relatively sober in a bed that wasn’t hers.

     

                Waking slowly the next morning, the stale taste of beer in her dry mouth, the smell of cigarettes and whisky and some floral shampoo filling her nose, Kara blinked herself awake to find her face pressed into the back of Lena’s neck. Blinking quickly, Kara jerked back, her hot hand slipping off the soft skin of Lena’s thigh where it had been resting as her stomach swooped.

     

                The act of waking up curled around someone else filled her with panic, but it also made her flush with a feeling that wasn’t altogether unpleasant. She couldn’t remember waking up like that before, her and Mike having distinct halves of the double bed crammed into their bedroom, never touching, never facing inwards towards each other. But here, in Lena’s gigantic bed, Kara had shuffled all the way across the mattress to hold her as if she had the right to.

     

                Easing herself out of bed as her stomach knotted uneasily, Kara slipped out to the kitchen and helped herself to coffee before slipping on her shoes and jacket and grabbing Aristotle’s leash. She took him for a quick walk around the block to get some fresh air and help give herself some clarity before returning to the apartment. Drinking another coffee, she lingered in the kitchen as she waited for Lena to wake up.

     

                Lena stumbled into the kitchen an hour later, her face almost grey with a hangover as she gave Kara a rueful look, wretched and quiet. Filling a glass of water and fetching two of the pills she’d found in a drawer, Kara gave her a weak smile and offered to make breakfast. 

     

                Washing the pills down with water, Lena made a sound of objection, sitting heavily at the kitchen table and closing her eyes. Head tipped back, fingers pressed to her forehead where a headache pounded, she looked like the picture of regret. Lowering the blinds a fraction to keep the room dim, Kara made her a cup of black coffee and set a couple of saltine crackers in front of her so she could at least get something in her stomach.

     

                After ten minutes, Lena climbed to her feet and made a swift exit, followed by the muffled sounds of vomiting a minute later. Hesitating, Kara climbed to her feet and went to check on her, knocking on the closed bathroom door and then letting herself in. She held Lena’s hair back for her and crouched beside her on the tiled floor until the vomiting stopped, and Lena’s breaths were quick and shallow as she turned her head to the side, voice rasping as she let out a frayed laugh.

     

                “Don’t say I told you so.”

     

                “Wouldn’t dream of it.”

     

                Kara’s voice was warm with amusement, although she didn’t let Lena see the smile she fought back, sitting patiently with her until she clambered ungainly to her feet. Leaving her to freshen up, Kara pulled open cupboards and raided the fridge and pantry, scrambling eggs in a pan as she decided something hot and semi-greasy would at least help soak up the half bottle of whisky and God knew what else Lena had consumed alone last night.

     

                Looking peaky and disgruntled, Lena thanked her and picked at her breakfast, forcing down a few mouthfuls and then sipping the coffee Kara had set in front of her. She looked as undone as Kara had ever seen her, pale and red-eyed with dark circles ringing them. Pity knifed through Kara, and an echo of familiarity, like she was looking at herself from twelve months ago.

     

                Once she’d finished eating, Kara whisked her plate away and ignored Lena’s protests when she started washing the dishes, the encircling grasp of her fingers on Kara’s bicep trying to make her give in. Glancing sideways at her, Kara’s cheek dimpled with a shallow smile.

     

                “Sit. You look like you might throw up again.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena gave her a wry smile and relented, curled up on her chair, damp strands clinging to her hairline as her body temperature struggled to lower itself. She managed not to vomit again and once Kara had finished tidying up, righting the pillows on the sofa and straightening the throw, it was almost lunchtime. 

     

                Clearing her throat, Kara found Lena beneath the sheets in her bed, the curtains still tightly shut, casting the room in gloomy grey. Hovering in the doorway, Kara toyed with her fingers.

     

                “I’m going to head off now.”

     

                Head rising from the pillow, Lena blearily squinted at her, her voice rasping as she replied. “Okay. Thank you.”

     

                “Don’t mention it,” Kara murmured, her mouth curving into a smile. “Feel better.”

     

                “Mm. I should’ve listened to you.”

     

                Cracking a smile, Kara’s nose wrinkled and she ducked her head down. “I took Aristotle for a walk this morning and he’s all set for food and water so don’t worry about him. Leftovers are in the fridge.”

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                Nodding, Kara hesitated before she just nodded again. “I’ll see you soon.”

     

                She caught the bus home after that, her own apartment feeling cluttered, cramped and overwhelmingly lonely as she stood in the middle of the open space and ignored the fresh stack of bills on the table. Feeling a little out of sorts herself, Kara opted for a nap but was restless and brooding, the bed too empty and her hand resting on the soft worn sheets as it keenly remembered the touch of soft, warm skin earlier that morning. 

    Chapter 12

                The weeks leading up to Kara’s birthday were quietly stressful as she worked every day, dealing with vomiting dogs and cats who hadn’t eaten a bite in days, hit-and-runs and troubling deliveries that left her exhausted and even more stressed about money. The bills kept coming and Kara felt like she was in a burning building, trapped as everything fell apart around her and she had no choice but to watch. She didn’t tell anyone about it and it was ironic that she was handling her grief better just in time for debt to swallow her up.

     

                She’d never gotten around to telling Alex about the credit card debts in their name that had been hidden from her, racked up over years of secret spending and left for Kara to pay off by remortgaging the apartment. Her sister thought she was managing the mortgage fine alone, that Kara’s decent job - if a little on the lower end of the average salary for a vet - easily covered it, and it might have if she didn’t have so many other things to pay off. Her savings were down to nothing with all the leave she’d taken after Mike’s passing and she hadn’t told her sister she’d remortgaged the house to cover what she could.

     

                The morning of her birthday, she was up at five, lacing on her running shoes with the sudden urge to try and regain some control of her life. She jogged through the early morning traffic, the sky a deep grey as September gave way to October, autumn in full swing. Lungs burning and legs aching, unused to the long cardio, she returned home in time to shower and dress for work, catching her bus as she listened to her meditation Podcast and nursed a cup of coffee she’d poured into a travel mug to cut down on how much she spent on Starbucks. Not that it would help, not by a mile , but it gave her the illusion of being financially responsible.

     

                Arriving at work ten minutes early, she greeted the receptionist and slipped back through to the staff room. James was already there, making a cup of tea, and he straightened from his slouched position against the cupboards, a smile lighting up his face.

     

                “There you are! Happy birthday.”

     

                She let him wrap her in a bear hug, smiling tiredly as she gave his back a pat and pulled away. “Thank you.”

     

                “Brought you a treat to celebrate,” James said, bypassing her to the small table where a large cookie had been iced with ‘happy birthday kara’.  

     

                “Thanks.”

     

                She made herself another coffee and had some of the cookie with him, both of them chatting in the kitchen with the ease of two people who had been friends for a long time. William arrived shortly after, giving Kara a warm smile that sparked a flicker of guilt despite the months since her drunken mistake and she thanked him when he wished her a happy birthday. They were all having their drinks after work in celebration but were going somewhere fancier than Al’s, despite Kara’s protests as she eyed her dwindling bank account with trepidation.

     

                There wasn’t much time to talk then as Kara was whisked away to her first patient, a Beagle with cataracts, and spent her morning fussing over a variety of household pets as she fed them treats to distract them from the needles or examinations, weighing puppies and checking scars, reading charts and instructing owners on how to administer medications. Her lunch break was occupied by a phone call with Eliza, eating the leftovers she’d brought with her as she assured her mother she was fine, that she was sleeping properly, despite the evident bags beneath her eyes. 

     

                Exhausted by the time she wearily plodded her way from the bus stop to her apartment, Kara came to a stop on the sidewalk at the sight of Lena leaning against her car as she waited for her. Lips parting, Kara’s brow furrowed and she doubled her pace, confused by her appearance.

     

                “Happy birthday,” Lena greeted her, handing off a bouquet of flowers and holding up a little gift bag by the handles.

     

                “Oh. Thank you,” Kara replied with surprise.

     

                Shadowing her to the front door, Lena followed Kara upstairs to the apartment. “How was your day?”

     

                “Oh … you know. Birthdays are never really that special past twenty-one, are they?”

     

                Humming in agreement, Lena waited for her to open the door and stepped inside after her as Kara kicked off her shoes and dumped her backpack. Moving into the kitchen for a vase, she put the bouquet in it and then took the gift bag back out to Lena, who gave her a quick smile.

     

                “New perfume that’s all the rage in Paris at the moment. I thought you’d like it.”

     

                Removing the bottle, Kara sniffed it and hummed appreciatively. “Oh, nice. Thank you, that’s really thoughtful.”

     

                Nodding, Lena hesitated a moment and then gestured to the table, taking in the stack of bills with red stamped across the envelopes. “Is everything okay?”

     

                Flushing, Kara hurriedly gathered the bills into a messy pile and let out a strained laugh, embarrassment evident in her ducked head and tense shoulders. She shuffled the wad and set an old college textbook down on top to weigh them down. Running a hand over her face, stressed and a little frazzled, Kara shook her head.

     

                “Yeah, yeah, it’s fine. I, uh, I just … I have a lot of repayments for things. It’s getting harder to stay on top of it all doing it alone. And … well, Mike had a lot of credit card debt when he passed away. I knew about the student loans - he took private ones, unfortunately - but I didn’t realise- he never told me about the amount he racked up on the cards he took out in our names. Anyway, um …”

     

                “How bad is it?” Lena hesitantly asked, unsure whether she was being too nosy asking a question like that.

     

                Wincing, Kara shrugged nonchalantly. “Well, I had to remortgage this place to settle it all as part of his estate afterwards so it, uh, it’s … you know. It is what it is.”

     

                “I- didn’t he have life insurance? What about his 401k?”

     

                Kara choked on a laugh, digging the heels of her palms into her eyes as she nudged her glasses up. “He didn’t have life insurance because … he thought it was a waste because he was so young. His work never covered it. And his 401k … he didn’t have that much in it so it all went to covering the debt. His loans alone were way more than that. I could’ve sold this place but … I mean, it was my place too. I guess I shouldn’t have missed all those days of work, huh?”

     

                Lena didn’t so much as crack a smile at Kara’s weak attempt to laugh it off, her expression grave and eyes a little wide. “Didn’t you have any equity in the place?”

     

                “Equity?” Kara snorted. “No, we made our minimum repayments and the rest went to student loans and savings. I burnt through all my savings paying the mortgage while I was off work. I mean … we weren’t rich.”

     

                Nodding, Lena’s brow furrowed slightly and she opened her handbag, rummaging around for her chequebook. “How much do you need?”

                

                A small sound of confusion escaped Kara as her expression clouded. Lena met her eyes, clicking a pen as she raised her eyebrows a fraction, nothing arrogant or condescending about her expression, nothing but serious concern. Letting out a strained laugh, Kara raked a hand through her hair and looked away.

     

                “Come on, what, you’re going to write me a check?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “I know you have your own business but I doubt you have enough savings to even cover it.”

     

                It was Lena’s turn to laugh, not unkindly, just at Kara’s ignorance. “Humour me.”

     

                “I’m not going to take money from you.”

     

                “Why not?” Lena asked as her face furrowed.

     

                “It’s my mess. My finances.”

                

                “And you’re my friend.”

     

                “Lena … thank you but no.”

     

                They were both silent for a moment and Lena folded her arms over her chest, chequebook in one hand and pen in the other as she stared at Kara. Head hung as she gripped the back of a chair, Kara swallowed thickly, her eyes smarting with tears as she blinked then away quickly.

     

                “How much?” Lena pressed again.

     

                Exhaling sharply, Kara closed her eyes, rubbing her temple as if a headache was forming. The stress of trying to manage alone was getting to her and she pulled a chair out and heavily sank down onto it.

     

                “Just shy of half a million,” Kara quietly confessed, her eyes red as she wiped her sleeve across her face.

     

                Inhaling, Lena’s mouth thinned and she nodded, leaning down to scrawl the figure on a blank check. Signing with a flourish, she tore it free and set it down, sliding it towards Kara, who looked at it and then up at Lena.

     

                “I’m not taking that.”

     

                “Kara, I- look, you need the money. I have the money.”

     

                “I’m not taking all of your savings-“

     

                A quiet huff of laughter escaped Lena as a pained smile twitched the corners of her mouth. Sinking down onto the seat across from Kara, Lena set her handbag down and closed her eyes.

     

                “I think I might have misled you or you just haven’t realised but I- my company is bigger than you think. I told you, I have multiple offices. Up and down America, and in Canada and London. That's … a few thousand employees. Big projects. Big money. ”

     

                “You- but … you work. You’re always at work. You don’t … you’re not yachting or shopping or- you drive a Lexus. A nice Lexus but … I thought you were just … well off.”

     

                Lena opted against letting Kara know her car could’ve paid off almost half of her debt. Clearing her throat, looking a little uncomfortable to be explaining her financial situation to someone on the verge of drowning in debt, Lena clenched her hands on top of the table. 

     

                “I’m … more than well off. I like to live below my means but the truth is, well, I come from money. So did my wife. If you need the money, I can give it to you.”

     

                “I can’t pay you back that much. I’d be sixty by the time I repaid you.”

     

                “I can give it to you.”

     

                “No.”

     

                “Don’t be stubborn.”

     

                “No.”

     

                Roughly sighing, annoyed by Kara’s determination to fix it herself, Lena clicked her tongue. “Have you missed any payments on the mortgage yet?”

     

                “I’ve been late a couple of times but I’ve paid them. It’s getting harder each month. Interest rates went up again recently and my student loans … it’s just pure interest at this rate. I can’t keep up.”

     

                On the verge of tears again, Kara blinked rapidly and swallowed thickly, a lump caught in her throat. Clenching another fistful of her hair, she blew the air out of her cheeks and avoided Lena’s eyes.

     

                “Can I see the bills?” Lena hesitantly asked.

     

                Wrinkling her nose, wincing slightly at the prospect of letting someone see just how bad it had gotten, slowly piling up over the last year and a half, Kara relented. It didn’t matter now; Lena knew so why not reveal everything to her? It wouldn’t make a difference but perhaps it would lessen Kara’s stress slightly to confess it to someone. 

     

                She hadn’t even told Alex yet, knowing her sister would only worry and wouldn’t be able to help, her own student loans from almost a decade of medical school eclipsing Kara’s even. Reaching for the textbook, Kara lifted it and pulled the stack of bills towards her before she set them before Lena.

     

                Pushing her chair back, Kara climbed to her feet and walked into the kitchen, pink-cheeked as she made coffee for them and let Lena read the letters without the embarrassment of sitting there watching her. Taking a few minutes to stand at the sink, breathing slowly as she tried to keep it together, even as her life fell apart around her, Kara squared her shoulders and picked up the cups.

     

                Returning to the open living area, Kara set the mugs down and sank back down onto her seat. Lena gave her a cursory glance, surrounded by the bills and a furrowed look of concentration on her face.

     

                “What’s your pay like?”

     

                “Salary works out to be sixty-six after tax.”

     

                Giving her a long, unreadable look for a moment, Lena nodded. Taking a sip of her coffee, she cleared her throat.

     

                “What’s that, five-five a month?” Lena mentally calculated, writing the figure down on a legal pad she’d fetched from somewhere. “Mortgage repayments are … two thousand a month. Student loan repayments are nineteen hundred a month.”

     

                She talked aloud as she checked the statements, jotting down the figures as she went. 

     

                “Utilities … let’s call it two-sixty a month. What’s your food bill like?”

     

                “I don’t know … maybe three hundred?”

     

                “Alcohol?”

     

                “I don’t know. Maybe fifty bucks a week? More.”

     

                “Health insurance?”

                

                “Work covers it.”

     

                “Gym membership? Streaming services? Public transport?”

     

                Pressing her fingertips against her eyelids, Kara shrugged helplessly. “SoulCycle occasionally.”

     

                “Forty per class,” Lena supplied for her. “We’ve been going together twice a month so I’ll put you down for that over the year.”

     

                “I use Alex’s HBO. But I pay for Netflix.”

     

                “Okay, well, I don’t need to know which subscription you have, just the cost.”

     

                “Ten dollars a month. My bus pass is fifty a month.”

     

                “What else do you buy?”

     

                “I don’t know. Coffee. Sometimes I need new clothes, new scrubs. Makeup. Takeout. Books. I get my hair done and … a new prescription for my glasses. I visit my mom a couple of times a year. Birthday presents, Christmas presents, all of that.”

     

                “Right, I’ll go with three hundred a month on miscellaneous. It’ll average out over the year. That brings us to … four hundred a month left over.”

     

                “I have my credit card as well,” Kara sheepishly murmured, sinking down in her seat as her cheeks heated.

     

                Fixing her with a stern look, Lena blinked slowly. “How much?”

     

                “Twenty-thousand.”

     

                “On what?”

     

                “I- well … I didn’t work much for a bit there. It sort of just … built up while I tried to keep paying for everything. My savings were pretty much gone instantly and I had to cover funeral costs as well - Mike’s mom covered most of it but there was still a bit. Who knew it was so expensive to die.”

     

                Exhaling sharply, Lena nodded. “Right. Will you at least let me wipe that out for you? Birthday gift?”

     

                “No.”

     

                “You’re a pain in the ass,” Lena grumbled. “Alright. Leave this with me; I’ll speak to my financial advisor. See if I can get her to work up a plan for you.”

     

                With an agonised look of embarrassment, Kara rubbed her forehead. “You don’t have to do that.”

     

                “I know, I want to. And cancel your Netflix; I’ll give you my login.”

     

                Snorting, Kara couldn’t help the small smile on her lips. “Thank you.”

     

                Nodding, Lena took a sip of her coffee and then jotted down the credit card debt as well before hesitating. “What’s your credit score?”

     

                “Six fifteen.”

     

                “Okay. Not the worst.”

     

                “What do you think I should do?” Kara whispered.

     

                Lips pursed, Lena tapped the legal pad. “I’m not sure what my advisor will say-“

     

                “I want your opinion; what would you do?”

     

                “Me? I’d sell the apartment. Wipe out your mortgage, the biggest chunk of your debt, with it - prices in this area should’ve risen with the cost of living so you’ll probably make enough to cut down your credit card too. Student loans … well, I’m assuming you studied for a while so you’re probably still working through a chunk of it for post-grad. What was your term?”

     

                “I refinanced the whole lot for twenty years to do my masters. I’m about halfway through it now.”

     

                “Well, without the mortgage you’ll be able to make bigger repayments instead of interest only. That’ll benefit you long-term-”

     

                “I’ll still need to pay rent somewhere.”

     

                “You’ll have options there. Depending on how much you’re willing to fork out there, you can probably put away a thousand a month into a savings account and we can open up an investment portfolio for you to help pad out your 401k. ”

     

                Kara laughed at the mere idea of it, the thought of having money to invest and so much to put away in savings so out of touch with her reality. Lena’s confidence seemed unshakable but Kara’s prospects had dropped severely with the death of her husband and it had been a slow descent into money troubles that she didn’t see a way out of. She didn’t want to sell their apartment, she didn’t want to move back in with Alex and Kelly or worse, live with a stranger to cheapen her rent. Kara was used to living alone now, she liked her own schedule, her own company.

     

                “Can I also make a suggestion?”

     

                “Sure.”

     

                “The vet I take Aristotle to-”

     

                “Cheating on me with another vet? Ouch.”

     

                “Funny. Anyway, he has to take home probably double what you’re on. Have you considered looking for a new job?”

     

                Face crumpling with a guilty wince, Kara shrugged, chewing her bottom lip. “I mean … I have thought about it but I’ve worked there since I was in college. James is a good friend of mine-”

     

                “If I let friends cloud my judgement, I’d be broke.”

     

                “You literally just offered to pay off my debt.”

     

                “I’m talking about work. I didn’t even let my wife give me business advice and she ran her own company too. I’m just saying, you can’t let sentimentality get in the way of what’s best for you. Maybe consider looking around for somewhere that pays a bit better, if you can. It’s just another option that could benefit you in the future.”

     

                “Right. Thanks.”

     

                Climbing to her feet, Lena picked up her bag and jerked her head towards the door. “Now, come on or we’ll be late to dinner.”

     

                Looking down at herself, Kara spluttered. “I’m not even dressed.”

     

                Eyeing her scrubs, Lena snorted. “Right. Might want to find something a bit nicer than that; I picked somewhere good.”

     

                “How good?”

     

                “Don’t stress it. It’s your birthday, you’re not paying.”

     

                “I-”

     

                “Get ready!” Lena quietly exclaimed, shooing her. “It’s your birthday; you’re having a good fucking night and that’s the end of it.”

     

                Floundering for a moment, Kara turned and stalked off to the bathroom, turning on the shower and shedding her work scrubs. Beneath the hot water, she hastily scrubbed herself clean and climbed out, being quick so she didn’t test Lena’s patience any further.

     

                Emerging from the bathroom in a towel, she paused at the sight of Lena ironing in the living room, her attention snagged by the shout. “Here.”

     

                A navy satin slip dress was thrust towards her and she left damp footprints in her wake as she went to fetch it. “Um … thanks.”

     

                “It’s a nice dress.”

     

                “Oh. Thanks.”

     

                “We have to be there in twenty minutes,” Lena reminded her, glancing at her watch.

     

                Cringing, Kara hurried to dress and hastily twisted her hair up in a claw clip before applying as much makeup as she had time for before she gathered up her keys and phone and stopped to spray herself in her newly gifted perfume. Balancing on one foot, she got one heel on and then the other and was pulling her coat from the rack as Lena led the way.

     

                “Sorry, I didn’t mean to sidetrack you. You were supposed to have more time,” Lena sighed.

     

                A frayed laugh escaped Kara and she ran a hand over her dress, “time is the least of my problems right now.”

     

                Lena hovered in the doorway for a moment, a grave look on her face as she stared at Kara. She bit her bottom lip for a second, hesitating as she wrestled with the decision to say what was on the tip of her tongue.

     

                Relenting after a moment, Lena reached out and squeezed Kara’s arm reassuringly. “Try not to worry. Worst case, you can swallow your pride and take the check.”

     

                A huff of laughter escaped Kara as she hugged her coat to her chest, a thin smile on her lips. Giving Lena a vulnerable look of doubt, Kara nodded and then stepped forward, wrapping her in a gentle hug, which she probably needed for herself rather than out of gratitude.

     

                “Thank you. I really do appreciate it.”

     

                “I know,” Lena whispered, rubbing her back. “Now, we’re really going to be late. Alex will probably kill me; she said she was coming straight from work.”

     

                Lena drove them, which hadn’t been part of Kara’s initial plan as she’d intended on using her bus pass, and they snagged a parking spot nearby, feeding quarters to the machine and then hurrying to the restaurant. Kara hadn't been there before but Lena had raved about it so she’d gone along with the plan with very little input but as they arrived outside, a doorman letting them in, bouncers in black suits and servers in starched white shirts and fitted pants carrying trays of drinks and three-plating dishes. The air even smelled expensive as their coats were taken and Kara looked around, wood and stone and leather filling the place.

     

                “Oh, um, this is fancy.”

     

                “Well, yeah, it’s your birthday. Come on, they’re already here.”

     

                They were escorted to the reserved table, all of her friends already seated with their first round of drinks, and Kara flushed and smiled at the chorus of happy birthdays. Sheepishly ducking her head as she took a seat beside Lena, she thanked everyone and was handed half a dozen gift bags that she stowed beneath the table.

     

                Ordering a round of lemon drops for the table, Lena fell into conversation with Kelly and Winn and Kara reassured Alex that she’d spoken to Eliza earlier and that she was having a good day. She didn’t trouble her sister with her struggles, perhaps a large part of her too proud to admit it, and the conversation quickly turned away from her as she settled in with her cocktail.

     

                They had round after round and Kara ordered the steak with a mushroom sauce, quickly warming up with the alcohol. Some of her stress dissipated and her shoulders slumped as her smiles came more easily. Noticing, Lena gave her knee a squeeze beneath the table and Kara gave her a small smile, warmth kindling in her chest. It was easy to pretend everything was okay when she was surrounded by her friends, laughing and drinking and getting drunker as the night wore on.

     

                Lena picked up the check after dessert, a candle stuck into a slice of chocolate torte for Kara, and they all relocated to a bar. It was a more appropriate place for their increasing rowdiness as the night wore on, lemon drops swapped for a few rounds of black sambuca and all Kara could taste was liquorice by the end of the night. 

     

                Unsteady on her feet, laden with her gifts and her voice too loud in the street as she sang a duet with Winn while they waited for cabs, she felt slightly unbalanced. Looping an arm around Lena’s shoulders, forgetting whether everyone else had clued into their quiet hookups, Kara lowered her voice as they ducked their heads together.

     

                “Are you coming back to mine?”

     

                Lena let out a huff of laughter. Her lips brushed Kara’s cheek and left a smudge of red as she made herself heard over the traffic and pulsing bass of various bars lining the street. 

     

                “Everyone deserves to get laid on their birthday.”

     

                “Can’t argue with your logic.”

     

                Her laugh somewhat halting, Lena pressed a quick kiss beneath Kara’s ear and then paused. “The perfume smells good on you.”

     

                “Thanks. I forgot to tell you … I forgot to tell you you look nice.”

     

                “So do you.”

     

                “You always look nice though.”

     

                “Let’s go.”

     

                The next cab pulled up and they shouted a chorus of goodbyes as they stumbled towards it, Kara’s hand finding Lena. Blowing her sister a kiss, she was dragged into the back a moment later, laughing and a little dizzy as everything seemed to distance itself.

     

                Sinking against the seats, Kara slipped into a daze that she didn’t fully come out of until she woke the next morning. Woke to the warmth of Lena nestled up beside her, bare skin sticking as they both slowly woke at the same time. Lena’s cheek was on her shoulder, her arm across Kara’s waist, and Kara’s eyes were narrowed against her poor vision as her mind woke a little slower.

     

                Then Lena jolted as if Kara had pinched her, scrambled upright as her eyes widened and she blinked. Looking around, Lena looked momentarily horrified and hurriedly pulled the blankets up.

     

                “Oh … um …”

     

                “How much did we drink?” Kara rasped.

     

                Makeup smudged around her eyes and what had been left of her lipstick smudged along Kara’s jaw and collarbones, Lena swallowed dryly. All that Kara could taste was liquorice and the almost medicinal taste of vodka that she couldn’t remember drinking.

     

                “I don’t know but I already regret it,” Lena mumbled, digging the heels of her palms into her eyes.

     

                “You alright?”

     

                “Yep. Mhm. I, uh, I think it’s probably been about a decade since I woke up in someone else’s bed.”

     

                She knew Lena was referring to their close proximity more than the act of waking up beside each other in Kara’s bed, and Kara felt a wince of guilt in her chest. 

     

                “Sorry, it’s a bit small.”

     

                “I- uh … that’s okay. Um … my dress …”

     

                Kara rolled out of bed, running a hand through her hair, which had been undone at some point last night and was a mess of bedhead. Rummaging around in her cramped closet, she pulled out a pair of jeans and a thin sweater and tossed them onto the foot of the bed.

     

                “You’re not putting on a skin-tight dress this early. What time is it anyway? I need to get ready for work.”

     

                Squinting at her phone, Kara choked on a surprised sound as the screen displayed just past eleven and she saw half a dozen texts and calls from James and William. Stomach sinking, Kara pinched the bridge of her nose, exhaling sharply.

     

                “How is it eleven o’clock? What time did we sleep?”

     

                Groaning, Lena rolled back over, burying her face in the pillows and muffling her response. “Fuck, I had a meeting this morning.”

     

                “I had patients!”

     

                “Oh no, think of the kittens you’ve abandoned.”

     

                “Very funny,” Kara sighed, thinking about her lost wages as she anxiously chewed on her bottom lip.

     

                “Did we drink when we came back?” Lena asked.

     

                “I think so; all I can taste is vodka.”

     

                “You’re a terrible influence.”

     

                “Me?” Kara spluttered.

     

                Rolling onto her back, arms splayed wide with her eyes closed, Lena smiled slightly. “You invited me back here.”

     

                “You said everyone deserves to get laid on their birthday.”

     

                “And I stand by it. I also think … it was a terrible decision and you might be stuck with me monopolising your bed for the rest of the day until my hangover disappears.”

     

                A smile softened Kara’s face and they lapsed into silence long enough for her to realise she hadn’t put any clothes on. Quickly turning, she dragged on pilled heather grey sweatpants and a worn t-shirt, a headache at her temples and her vision terribly blurry until she fetched her glasses.

     

                “I’ll get you some Tylenol.”

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                Vanishing to the kitchen to find a near-empty bottle of vodka, and not the expensive kind that went down smoothly, Kara grumbled under her breath as she cursed herself. They’d ransacked the PopTarts too and she swept crumbs into the trash after putting the coffee machine on.

     

                Draining a glass of water with some pills, she carried the same back to Lena, whose face was pinched with irritation, eyes closed. Sitting on the edge of the bed, trying not to jostle the mattress, Kara watched her sit up and handed her the pills.

     

                Swallowing them down with the water, Lena pressed her flushed cheek against the glass as she held it tightly, leaching however much coolness she could get from it. After a moment she let out a weary sigh.

     

                “The pillows smell like you.”

     

                Whatever Kara had been expecting her to say, it hadn’t been that. Blinking, she raised her eyebrows slightly. “Probably.”

     

                “It’s weird. It’s weird to be around someone else so much, remembering all the things I’d taken for granted. I used to steal her pillows at night, move towards her side of the bed and just take them while I slept. I’d wake up every morning to the smell of her and for so long now … I’ve just woken up to myself.”

     

                “I used to like wearing his t-shirts from the night before in the morning. It was like being wrapped up in him.”

     

                “When we first started dating, I used to get a thrill out of using her things when I stayed over. Her shampoo, her perfume, her lipstick. Even when we lived together, I used to like using her things.”
