                “He used to have all of those specially branded hygiene products for men,” Kara snorted, shaking her head. “You know those ridiculous-sounding ones? Carbon Anarchy body wash - for men. So dumb but he loved his routine and insisted on his manly things. I kept buying it afterwards, for a while. I couldn’t shower without crying at the smell of it though so I had to stop.”

     

                “We used to bring each other home flowers on the days we worked really late and missed dinner together. I miss coming home to a bouquet.”

     

                “He bought me my backpack. The ugly one I take to work. Said I could use it to go hiking with him - he was always trying to get me into his hobbies so we could spend time together without him having to give up his time. I didn’t even appreciate it, I just … made some comment about how I hated hiking, didn’t have time for it, and that he’d wasted money. He was dead a few weeks later and that was the last thing he bought me.”

     

                “Funny what we miss, isn’t it? It’s not always the important stuff.”

     

                Humming in agreement, Kara stared at the rumpled sheets for a moment as they were both lost to memories. Sighing as she broke herself out of it, she gave Lena a tight smile and took the glass.

     

                “Come on, I’ve made coffee. And I found the culprit from last night.”

     

                “Was it vodka?”

     

                “Practically a whole bottle.”

     

                “Yeah, it feels like it.”

     

                They drank their coffee in the kitchen, finding scattered clothes in the process, and then Lena suggested breakfast. Hesitant about accepting, Kara relented when Lena firmly insisted on paying and said she was going regardless and didn’t want to eat alone.

     

                Showering quickly, taking turns, they dressed and walked, using the cool air to clear their heads. Quiet for the most part, they walked until they found a cafe that looked promising. Both of them sat at the table, slumped and tired, and Kara picked at the stack of pancakes before her with little appetite as Lena drained cup after cup of coffee and barely touched her food.

     

                “What’s on your mind?” Lena asked.

     

                Shrugging, Kara’s mouth turned down at the corners. “Nothing. Just a lot going on. It’s times like this when I miss him most; special occasions, stressful situations. He had a way of never seeming to care about anything, as if it would just magically figure itself out.”

     

                “Well, I’m certainly not him but I can promise you it will figure itself out. I can be your last resort, at the very least.”

     

                Quietly scoffing with laughter, Kara’s mouth twitched with a small smile. “You’re not a last resort. I just- I’m not going to take advantage of your generosity.”

     

                “It’s not taking advantage when it’s freely given.”

     

                “Maybe. But maybe you’re more important to me than you think and I don’t want to ruin our friendship over money.”

     

                “That wouldn’t be the thing to ruin it,” Lena said with a wry smile.

     

                Returning the smile as she cut a triangle out of her stack, Kara raised her eyebrows. “What would?”

     

                Pressing her mouth into a flat line, Lena hesitated and then shrugged nonchalantly. “Seems like testing fate to say it, doesn’t it?”

     

                “I don’t know what you’re going to say.”

     

                “I’ll keep it to myself for now.”

     

                “How do I know I won’t accidentally ruin it then?”

     

                Cheeks shallowly dimpling, Lena’s eyes softened with sadness. “Because I’m the destructive one. If things go south … it’ll be my fault, I can guarantee it. That’s just the way it works.”

     

                “Well … tough. You’re stuck with me; I don’t know what I’d do without you so you can’t get rid of me. Even if it goes south.”

     

                Her laugh was pitiful and Kara wanted to wince as it came out, quickly taking a bite to stifle any other desperate words that might escape her. She chewed quickly and kept her eyes down until she looked up and found Lena studying her. Flushing, Kara swallowed and took a sip of her coffee, running a hand through her hair as she shifted restlessly.

     

                “Don’t be so sure of that,” Lena said after a long minute, giving Kara a crooked smile. “I have a knack for pushing people away very effectively. There’s a reason why my wife’s the only person who stuck around.”

     

                “Well … I can’t bring her back for you so I guess I’ll be the second.”

    Chapter 13

                A few weeks later, the morning after Lena’s thirty-third birthday where she’d stayed the night to repay the favour of late-night company, Kara broached the topic of her apartment. She’d met with Lena’s financial advisor a couple of times and had spent the last week deliberating over her options. None of them were ideal but she’d finally settled on one and cleared her throat as she stepped into the kitchen a few minutes after Lena had left the bedroom.

     

                “I’ve decided to sell,” Kara announced, scooping up her jeans as she stared at Lena, wrapped up in her robe as she leaned against the window frame, smoking.

     

                She glanced over at Kara, raising her eyebrows a fraction in surprise as she took a drag. “Really?”

     

                “Mhm. I think … you were right and it’s probably the best plan for now. Your advisor seems to think so, seems to think I can drop my debt down to just under six figures.”

     

                Blowing smoke out of the window, Lena cocked her head to the side. “Okay. That’s good. I mean … I’m sorry but …”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara grimly agreed, cheeks dimpling as her mouth thinned.

     

                “Let me know what they appraise it for; I’ll put in a fair offer.”

     

                Surprise flashed across Kara’s face and she shoved a leg into her jeans as her brow furrowed. “You’re not buying my apartment.”

     

                “Why not? It would be a good investment for me; you’ll be a good tenant.”

     

                “I love you for offering-”

     

                “Don’t say that,” Lena softly cut her off, a muscle twitching in her jaw.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Kara got her other leg in and shimmied the jeans up, zipping them up. She moved across the room, giving Lena an exasperated look as she took the cigarette from her mouth.

     

                “You know I didn’t mean it in that way. You’re my best friend, and we’re sleeping together - that doesn’t mean you need to fix my problems for me.”

     

                Taking a drag of the cigarette, Kara exhaled out the window and then set it back between Lena’s lips, giving her cheek a quick pat. “You should stop smoking.”

     

                Grunting in reply as she reached up to remove the cigarette, flicking ash outside, Lena’s eyes cut sideways to her. “You could let me help though.”

     

                “You are helping.”

     

                “Financially.”

     

                “I just turned thirty-five, I’m a big girl.”

     

                “Belated birthday present,” Lena said with a quick grin.

     

                Snorting, Kara looked around, raking a hand through her hair. “Have you seen my shirt?”

     

                “Don’t put it on on my account.” At Kara’s withering look, Lena smiled and jerked her chin towards the living room. “I think I remember removing it out there.”

     

                Finding her shirt, Kara shrugged it on and ran a hand through her hair before quickly tying it up. Returning to the kitchen, she stifled a yawn and accepted the cup of coffee Lena held out to her.

     

                “Thanks.”

     

                “Breakfast?”

     

                “Sure.”

     

                Draining half of her own coffee, Lena set her mug down and moved around the kitchen as she pulled out pans and raided the pantry and the fridge. Kara perched on the edge of the counters as she watched her cook, the smell of bacon filling the kitchen and summoning Aristotle, who wagged his tail and nosed Lena’s leg until she showered him with affection.

     

                “So, what’s the plan?” Lena asked as she nudged an omelette out of the pan.

     

                Scooping out some bacon, she added it to the plate and then held it out to Kara as she rounded on her with an expectant look on her face. Sliding off the counter, Kara took the plate, her mouth turning down slightly at the corners.

     

                “I don’t know,” Kara sighed, making her way to the table as Lena served up her own breakfast.

     

                Going back to fetch the cutlery, Kara shrugged. “I guess once it sells I’ll have to ask Alex if I can stay there for a few weeks until I find a rental.”

     

                “Once it sells … you could always come and stay with me,” Lena slowly suggested.

     

                Kara laughed, setting their places at the table as Lena passed behind her and took a seat. Sinking down onto her own seat, Kara gave her a wary look.

     

                “Oh, you’re being serious.”

     

                “I have the room.”

     

                “Lena, I-” Kara speechlessly stammered for a moment. “I can’t afford the mortgage on my place, let alone half the rent here. A penthouse, are you serious?”

     

                “Kara … I own it. I’m not even paying a mortgage myself.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Kara looked around the kitchen with its marble countertops and splashback, the herringbone floors, and the floor-to-ceiling windows with a spectacular view of the city and the bay. She was trying to do the numbers in her head, calculating how much a place like that would cost, how many zeros should be added on but she couldn’t even begin to guess. It had been apparent from the very beginning that Lena was wealthy, but she’d severely underestimated her, thinking the plain, well-crafted and tailored clothes were nice but probably not quite as high-end as the labels she was familiar with, the penthouse was nice but would probably take a long time for her to pay off even with her modest income. 

     

                She’d paid more attention recently, taking in the unfamiliar logos, the materials, and the quality of everything Lena owned, from her liquor to her furniture. It wasn’t flashy or ostentatious but Kara realised she’d still low-balled it, and now she was caught off-guard again by the casual mention of Lena’s wealth. Even at her age, Kara didn’t know anyone who owned their own place outright - even Alex and Kelly with their respected careers were still renting while they saved enough for a deposit on a family house out in the suburbs.

     

                “You own it outright? Jesus, Lena. I mean … how do you even afford a place like this?”

     

                Lips twitching slightly, Lena cut into her breakfast. “Our lives are drastically different. I’ve told you before. Boarding school, my wife was big in tech-”

     

                “How big?”

     

                “Up there,” Lena hedged. “Like … the Bill Gates of her field.”

     

                Groaning, Kara put her head in her hand. “And you?”

     

                “About the same. Architecture … well, it’s not quite as high profile as tech. The people who are interested in it would know me but my life is relatively low-key.”

     

                “Yeah, I gathered.”

     

                “Seriously though,” Lena continued, eating her mouthful and staring at Kara with a mildly pointed look. “You can live here. I have two spare rooms. It’s closer to your work and it has a gym and a pool. Sauna too, if that sort of thing interests you. You’ll save a lot more and I’ll even split the bills with you if that helps put your mind at ease.”

     

                Setting her knife and fork down as she chewed slowly, face clouded thoughtfully as she considered it, Kara didn’t know how to respond. “It’s just- it’s not like that with us. I mean … I don’t know if it’s a good idea.”

     

                “Financially, for you, it’s arguably the best idea.”

     

                “Personally, for us ,” Kara sighed, gesturing between them, “I don’t think it is.”

     

                Humming, Lena didn’t reply as she finished eating, the scrape of their cutlery filling the silence. Waiting until she’d finished, Kara whisked their plates away and started stacking the dishwasher as Lena made them fresh coffees and fed the scraps of bacon to the dog.

     

                “Why are you so against it?”

     

                “Come on, you don’t see the problem?” Kara asked. “You of all people. First of all, I would have thought you’d hate the idea of a roommate.”

     

                “You’re my best friend. One of them. I’d do the same for Sam - I have. Single mom struggling to cover rent? I moved her into one of my properties and that was that. Granted, I didn’t live there at the time but she wasn’t as proud as this.”

     

                “Which brings me to my second point; we’re sleeping together. That’s a whole other host of problems.”

     

                “Is it? Like what?” Lena blithely replied, setting a cup down for Kara.

     

                She cradled her own and took a sip, arching an eyebrow as Kara quietly scoffed with laughter. Wiping a hand on her jeans, she pursed her lips and narrowed her eyes.

     

                “Sex is fine-”

     

                “Just fine? You wound me.”

     

                “It’s fine when it’s just every couple of weeks, or when we’ve had a few drinks but if we’re living together-”

     

                “Oh, I see, I’m just so irresistible you won’t be able to help yourself?” Lena laughed.

     

                Looking peevish, Kara finished the last of the dishes and washed her hands before towelling them dry. Pushing the buttons on the machine, she started a cycle and then rounded on Lena.

     

                “That’s not far from the truth. I just think it would be a bad idea for us to be cooped up in here with each other. Things might get … complicated.”

     

                “I’m not offering you a room in exchange for easy access to sex if that’s what you’re worried about.”

     

                “I’m not,” Kara defensively replied. “I know you don’t have any ulterior motives-”

                

                “Not entirely true. Maybe it gets lonely here and I’d like the company - but that doesn’t mean I’m going to jump you every time we pass in the kitchen.”

     

                Weakly laughing, Kara’s mouth hitched into a crooked smile. “You’re not? That’s a pity.”

     

                “Look, I know what you’re trying to say. But you and I … we know where we stand, so it’s fine. It’s not going to be complicated by feelings or all the baggage of a relationship, so … think about it,” Lena insisted, giving her arm a quick pat. 

     

                “Sure. And thank you. I don’t want you to think I’m ungrateful-“

     

                “I don’t think that. It’s … a tough situation to be in. It’s different but I understand; growing up, I hated feeling beholden to my mom, having her be the one who had all the power of where I lived and what I ate. We never got along so I always felt like I was living in her house at her whim, you know? It’s nice to have a claim to something that belongs to you. I’m sorry you’re losing that.”

     

                Shrugging as she smiled slightly, Kara buried her hands in her pockets. “It is what it is.”

     

                She stayed to take Aristotle for a walk after that, questioning Lena about his last round of vaccines and reminding her to schedule him in. She offered to do it herself and Lena accepted it, looking at Kara’s schedule with her and choosing a slot to bring him in. They walked around the park for a while after that, Kara reluctant to leave just yet as she kept Lena company. Some of that was out of a sense to lessen her friend’s loneliness.

     

                Lena’s birthday had been relatively quiet in comparison to Kara’s one. She’d bought her flowers and an expensive candle and insisted on paying for dinner, Lena relenting with a bewildered tenderness in her green eyes. They shared a slice of cake for dessert and afterwards, Kara had gone back to the penthouse, sharing a bottle of wine and then lingering when things slipped into their usual murky territory of a mistake waiting to happen, falling asleep in Lena’s bed and then waking early Sunday morning to a rather domestic routine. 

     

                After they finished walking Aristotle, Lena mentioned she had some errands to run so Kara took her leave. Kissing her cheek, she told her to have a good day and decided to walk home, taking her an hour but giving her enough time to drink in the autumn sunshine as she nursed an iced coffee from the closest Starbucks and listened to a new Podcast. 

     

                When she returned home, Kara looked around her apartment with fresh eyes, drinking in the sights she’d taken for granted. They’d moved in a few years after marrying with the intention of moving on to a bigger place in time for kids, but a good chunk of their relationship had existed within those walls. They’d played music on the stereo; left the laundry and bills on the table as they ate around their mess; Mike had once put a hole in the plaster after her threw his Playstation controller at it, now patched over; Kara had once come home so drunk she’d vomited on the doorstep and Mike had put her in the shower while she cleaned up; there was the deep furrows of furniture that hadn’t been moved in years on her carpeted bedroom floor. 

     

                The thought of moving away from the last place that held pieces of him made her heart ache in her chest but it hadn’t all been good. She’d been in the living when she’d gotten the phone call about the accident, they used to fight all the time in the kitchen, food burning on the stove as their voices filled the space, her loneliness used to eat her up as she lay in bed alone at nights when he didn’t come home until the early hours of the morning, reeking of beer. Now it was her staying out all night drinking, sleeping at another woman’s place no less. 

     

                Once the decision had been made, it lessened the burden Kara had been saddled with and the knot of worry that had settled in her chest loosened as she made arrangements. Her apartment had been appraised by a realtor Lena had recommended, valuing it at a little bit more than what she owed the bank for the mortgage, and they were confident it would sell quickly. Kara wasn’t sure if that was a good thing or a bad thing, knowing she’d miss the place but knowing a blank slate would probably be for the best.

     

                In a way, it felt like the logical next step to moving on. Things with Mike had been so complicated, the dynamic of their relationship going from infuriating to sweet and leaving her still so confused about how she should feel and how long she should grieve. Kara knew that to lose someone meant to never really get over them and she missed her husband but couldn't move past her anger at the shit situation he’d left her in either. Relinquishing the apartment to rid herself of a large chunk of their debt felt a little bit like letting go of some of her anger, even if it left her with nothing.

     

                Kara hadn’t broken the news to anyone yet, trying to track down a free spot in Alex’s busy schedule to let her know. Her sister always seemed to be at the hospital though, or they were drinking with friends and it seemed like a bad time to get into it. It wasn’t something Kara wanted to bring up over beers at Al’s with everyone listening in on how bad her financial situation was; it would be bad enough having to confess just to Alex.

     

                After work a couple of weeks after her decision, she called Alex as she walked from the bus stop, the day already bleeding to night as she stepped around buskers and panhandlers, neon lights turning nebulous as the sunlight waned. Alex picked up after three rings and Kara fell into easy conversation with her as a sheepish feeling welled up. A part of her had been dodging her sister’s calls for the most part as a way to delay asking if she could move back in but she knew she had to bite the bullet eventually. 

     

                She didn’t really want to be thirty-five moving in with her sister though and she knew that Alex would be gracious about it but didn’t want to be thirty-seven and on the verge of marriage with her sister living with her either. It would be a shit position for everyone and Kara had considered Lena’s offer but wasn’t sure how to feel about it.

     

                “Hey,” she eventually managed to get in as Alex paused to let herself into her apartment. “When are you off next? I was hoping we could get coffee or something.”

     

                “I don’t know, this week is a bit hectic. A lot of surgeries scheduled. I should be home by six on Thursday; why don’t you come over after Group? Dinner.”

     

                “Oh, yeah, okay. Dinner.”

     

                “Alright. I promised Kelly I’d sort dinner out tonight so I have to go.”

     

                “Okay, I’ll see you Thursday.”

     

                “See you then. Love you.”

     

                “You too.”

     

                Hanging up, Kara shoved her phone into her pocket and wondered whether she should have told her then and asked about the spare room. Anxiously worrying at her bottom lip, she walked the rest of the block and let herself into her apartment and resolved to wait a few more days for dinner.

     

                It was a busy week, work monopolising her time and a brief moment of delight when Lena brought Aristotle in. Kara gave her a steep discount, as promised, and then picked up the remaining amount as she told Lena the vaccines were free as a perk of Kara’s employment. She didn’t think James would care if she had given them to her for free but Kara considered it a secret thank you for her friend’s help.

     

                They’d gotten dinner afterwards and spoke about going to Group tomorrow, questioning the necessity of it even though they both knew they’d go. It was routine now, something they’d done week in and week out for a year and a half, without any real benefit aside from the gratifying feeling that they were doing something. Every Thursday, that donut and cup of tea as they sat side by side seemed like a mandatory part of life, regardless of how they felt about it.

     

                After Group the next day, Lena still insisted on driving Kara, even though she was heading to Alex’s instead of home. It felt like old times again, back at the beginning, when Kara hadn’t plucked up the courage to move back home. It wouldn’t be home for much longer anyway.

     

                “Thanks,” Kara murmured as Lena pulled up outside, the car idling in front of the lobby.

     

                “I’ll see you tomorrow at drinks?”

     

                Nodding, Kara gave her a quick smile and unbuckled herself. Grabbing her bag, she paused with her hand on the door handle.

     

                “Do you want to come in for dinner? They’ll have ordered plenty.”

     

                Hesitating, Lena gave her a small smile. “Thank you but I should get home. It’s been a long day.”

     

                “Let me know when you get home.”

     

                “Alright. Enjoy dinner.”

     

                “Have a good night.”

     

                She climbed out and gently shut the door and Lena waited until Alex buzzed her into the lobby through the intercom before pulling away. Making her way up to her sister’s apartment, Kara knocked and the door opened a moment later.

     

                “Hey, you got here fast,” Alex greeted her, ushering her inside, looking exhausted from a long shift. 

     

                “Lena dropped me off.”

     

                “Oh. Is she staying to eat?”

     

                “No, just dropping me off.”

     

                “Right, well, Kelly’s still at the hospital so it’s just us. I ordered Chinese.”

     

                Dinner was already on the coffee table and Kara set her backpack down and removed her coat as she settled in. Thanking her sister as a beer was handed off, Kara took a sip and then ferreted out the dumplings first, popping the container off and fishing one out.

     

                They talked about work for a bit, Alex recounting the surgery of a patient the night before and skimming over a few wedding planning details, while Kara sat on her news and ate as she listened. Once the conversation came to a natural lull, Kara finished her mouthful of fried rice and cleared her throat.

     

                “I, um, I have something to talk to you about, actually. So … see the thing is, when Mike … passed away, um, so it turned out he had all this debt.”

     

                Alex stilled, surprise crossing her face as she blinked, speechless for a moment. “You’re kidding . How much?”

     

                Shrugging nonchalantly, Kara’s mouth twisted. “A lot. I- I had to remortgage the apartment to settle some of his and some of the ones he took out in both of our names and, um … it’s been getting harder to- to make my repayments for everything, so, uh-“

     

                “You need money?” Alex lightly asked. “How much? I’ve got a bit put away for the wedding that I can-“

     

                “No,” Kara breathlessly laughed, her chest aching with love for her sister’s selflessness. “No, but … thank you. I’m just- I’m selling the place.”

     

                “Oh. Oh, is that … good?”

     

                “It’s … what’s best. Lena set me up with her financial advisor-“

     

                “Wait, you told Lena about it? How long has this been going on?”

     

                “Sort of accidentally. She was at my place and saw the bills and offered to help. Well … she offered more than help but anyway, it’s been a few weeks and the apartment is officially on the market next week.”

     

                Nodding as she speared a piece of chicken, Alex looked at Kara with concern. “Well, don’t worry about a thing; I’ve got the spare room here. I’ll speak to Kelly-“

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Kara shifted on the sofa as she looked down at her lap. “I, uh, thank you but … I might already have something lined up. Maybe. I don’t know if it’ll pan out but … yeah.”

     

                Blinking, eyebrows rising in surprise, Alex swallowed. “Really? That’s good! I mean, good planning . Where is it? Still Downtown?”

     

                “Um … yeah, just a few blocks from the bay.”

     

                “The bay? You’ve found a place near the water? How is that cheaper at all?”

     

                Rubbing the back of her neck, Kara cleared her throat. “Well, I wouldn’t be living alone if I moved in there.”

     

                “Oh. That sucks. Just move in here then. I know it’s not ideal but surely I’m better than a stranger; I promise I won’t be as pushy as last time you stayed.”

     

                “So … it’s not a stranger.”

     

                “What do you mean?”

     

                “I- so Lena has a spare room …”

     

                Alex’s expression immediately dropped. She set the carton of food down on the coffee table and raked a hand through her hair before pinching the bridge of her nose. “Tell me you’re joking.”

     

                “I’m not,” Kara curtly replied, fixing her glasses as her mouth thinned. “I’ve been thinking about it and it’s actually a really generous offer and-“

     

                “And fucking stupid. Are you out of your Goddamn mind?”

     

                “What?” Kara bitingly replied, frustration boiling over as she sharply huffed. “What is it? What is your fucking problem with her?”

     

                “I don’t have a problem with her!” Alex exclaimed, laughter etched into her face as she gave Kara a pained smile. “Lena’s great! She’s been such a good friend to you and I’m glad you’ve had that through the difficult time you’ve been having but … Kara, you’ve got to be shitting me. You can’t seriously think it’s a good idea to move in with the woman you’ve been screwing for the last few months.”

     

                Spluttering as her mouth opened and closed, cheeks flushing with annoyance, Kara crossed her arms over her chest. “I don’t see a problem with it. Lena doesn’t either.”

     

                “Oh, no, I bet you don’t see a problem with it.”

     

                “What’s that supposed to mean?”

     

                “You’re so blinded to your own feelings and it’s painful to watch. I’ve kept my mouth shut because you’ve been so much happier recently but she is going to hurt you and I’m scared for you.”

     

                Exhaling softly, Kara gave her sister a mystified look as she shook her head. “She’s not. I don’t know why you think that. I’m not some naïve teenager, you know, I do know how to look after myself.”

     

                “Oh yeah? And how long did it take you to get back on your feet again after Mike died, huh? Who had to look after you?”

     

                “Sorry that my husband fucking died.”

     

                “Yes, Kara, we’re all well aware. Our lives have all revolved around your feelings ever since . But you know what? Since he died, you actually managed to get a personality again instead of revolving your life around him, so maybe he did you a favour.”

     

                Alex looked like she wanted to take it back the moment it left her mouth, wincing sheepishly as guilt welled up in her brown eyes. Kara’s mouth opened and closed for a moment as she stared at her sister with wide eyes, the breath catching in her throat with disbelief. The prickle of truth to her words only made it sting more.

     

                “You’re such an asshole,” Kara snapped, eyes bright as she shot to her feet and snatched her backpack from the floor. 

     

                “I’m not an asshole,” Alex spluttered. “I’m telling you the truth. How am I the bad guy here? You just don’t want to hear it but I’m right and you know it. And you know I’m right when I say you’re making a mistake, and I’m not being an asshole just because I don’t want to see you go back to spending every day in bed because you have nothing else to live for. Stop making your life revolve around other people.”

     

                “It’s none of your fucking business what I do! Literally none.”

     

                Holding her hands up in a defeated gesture, Alex shook her head. “Fine. It’s your life, but don’t come crying to me when you get your heart broken by her.”

     

                “Don’t worry, I won’t,” Kara ground out, struggling to get her arm through the sleeve of her coat.

     

                Her eyes were burning fiercely as she barged out of her sister’s apartment, her throat constricting as she made her way to the elevator and jammed her thumb into the button. Getting her coat the rest of the way on, she managed to slow her shallow breaths as she calmed herself, the doors dinging a moment later and spilling her out into the lobby.

     

                Fixing the strap of her backpack, Kara blinked rapidly and fumbled for her phone, pulling it out and hovering over Lena’s number before she called her. Heart beating loudly in her chest as she walked through the city, late night traffic breezing past with a cold wind, she waited for Lena to answer, knowing she would still be driving. The call connected a moment later and had the faint fuzzy quality of the car’s Bluetooth.

     

                “Hey.”

     

                “Hey,” Kara managed to get out, her anger making her stubborn as she swallowed her pride. “About that spare room …”

     

                “Is everything okay?”

     

                “Yeah, I just- I don’t think it’s going to work out staying with Alex after all.”

    Chapter 14

                Kara missed drinks on Friday and ignored the messages from her friends, peevish and stubborn as she spent the night home alone, drinking her beers and watching reality TV. It was mind-numbing and an easy distraction and she ate handfuls of cereal from the box for dinner as she brooded over the annoyance at her sister. She knew she could have called Lena but Kara didn’t like feeling as if she used her as a balm to her frustration, purely for venting her feelings instead of an equal friendship.

     

                Instead, she dwelled alone and watched episode after episode of Dance Moms until she fell asleep at midnight, sprawled out on the sofa with a knitted blanket draped over her. Waking to the lightening of dawn, her back stiff and her eyes gritty, Kara made her way to her bed and slept a few more hours in comfort until the incessant buzzing of her phone roused her just after noon.

     

                “You didn’t come to drinks last night,” Lena greeted her.

     

                “You went?” Kara thickly replied, blinking sleep away.

     

                “I always go.”

     

                “Oh. I guess.”

     

                “I missed you there. I had no one to duet with.”

     

                Scoffing, Kara sat up and rubbed her face, creased with the lines of her rumpled sheets. “Because you’re known to get up for karaoke.”

     

                “Maybe last night would’ve been my night,” Lena replied, a smile in her voice. “I guess we’ll never know.”

     

                Smiling, Kara rolled onto her back. “I didn’t feel like going.”

     

                “Anything to do with our conversation on Thursday and Alex’s shitty mood last night?”

     

                Lips twitching ruefully, Kara ran her fingers over the sheets as she paused. Letting out a soft sigh, she rubbed her eyes and grimaced. “Maybe, but I’ll need at least three drinks before getting into it all.”

     

                “Well … it’s past twelve already. Have you eaten?”

     

                “No, I was sleeping,” Kara sheepishly replied.

     

                “Okay, hang tight.”

     

                “Wha- hello?” 

     

                The line went dead and Kara pulled the phone from her ear, frowning at the screen. Mouth thinning with bewilderment, she dropped her phone to the mattress and lay there for another five minutes before moving. Shaking out the quilt, she made the bed and went to shower, putting on clean clothes and brushing her teeth as she stared at her wan reflection. 

     

                Barely having the time to hastily run the vacuum over the floor and dump a stack of dishes in the dishwasher, remnants of yesterday’s breakfast and dinner from the night before that, Kara’s phone was vibrating with a phone call announcing Lena’s arrival. Heading downstairs to let her inside, Kara anxiously chatted away as she fiddled with her fingers, feeling nervous after asking Lena if she could move in.

     

                Lena had brought them banh mi and had a bag with a few bottles of wine inside, clinking as she set it down in the kitchen. Even though it was barely one o’clock, she poured them both glasses and they ate curled up on the sofa beside each other. The TV was on and they talked as they ate but Kara was true to her word and didn’t mention what had happened between her and Alex until she’d finished her third glass and Lena had refilled it again. 

     

                The number wasn’t lost on Lena either as she cleared her throat, emptying the dregs of wine into her own glass and setting the bottle down on the table.

     

                “So, why the change of heart?”

     

                Kara’s mouth twisted with annoyance as she shrugged dismissively. Lena watched her intently though and Kara’s shoulders deflated as she sighed heavily. Trying not to seem too petulant, she toyed with her glass and clenched her jaw before sitting back, running a hand through her hair.

     

                “I had an argument with Alex.”

     

                “Oh. I’m sorry, that’s- is everything okay?”

     

                “It’s fine. She’s just- well … sisters, you know?”

     

                Lena let out a quick laugh, “no, actually. And I imagine it’s a lot different from brothers. What was it about?”

     

                With another sigh, Kara’s mouth turned down at the corners and she cast her eyes down to the table. Cocking her head to the side, a slow, knowing smile spread across Lena’s face.

     

                “Ah. Me.”

     

                “Partially. You did come up but that wasn’t all of it. It’s fine; it’s stupid. We’re too old for petty arguments.”

     

                “I’ll let my brother know. He’s nine years older than me and still loves a good argument.”

     

                Letting out a quiet scoff of laughter, Kara met her eyes and gave her a tired smile. “She doesn’t think it’s a good idea for me to stay with you.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose, Lena shrugged, “I didn’t think she would. That doesn’t matter though; it’s private. If I’m okay with you moving in, and you’re okay with being there, why should anyone else’s opinion matter? Sorry, that might sound a bit callous-”

     

                “No, not at all. You’re right. There were … a few other comments too. About Mike, my feelings, how … bad it was when he died. I know she’s just worried about me but- I don’t know, I’m sick of having to explain myself to people. They’re not going to understand but they still expect an explanation and it’s just- everyone has an opinion about how I should be managing things. And the thing is … I’m doing great! Aside from the apartment and … you know, the debt and the dead husband. Aside from all of that, I’ve never felt more myself.” 

     

                Lena gave her a small smile, “that’s good.”

     

                “I was young when we got together so a huge chunk of my adult life so far has revolved around him and now I’m learning to be independent and figuring out how I’ve changed and … I guess the people who’ve known me a long time don’t like those changes. They just like that I’m not moping around.”

     

                “I mean, that is a good thing too. Maybe they’re just worried that the changes are … I don’t know, impulsive? I know they’re not but they don’t have the other half of the story, do they? Not that they have a right to know but I guess having it dropped on you in one go that you’re selling your apartment, have a ton of debt and are moving in with your grieving lover … I- yeah, that might be a cause for concern. I’d probably question it myself.”

     

                “And how do you know that’s that problem with you?”

     

                Snorting, Lena arched an eyebrow. “Do I come off as an idiot who can’t connect two dots? Come on, Kara, she didn’t like it from the minute we became close friends, let alone when we started sleeping together. It was expected, right? You knew you wouldn’t be able to tell her without her trying to talk you out of it but you made your choice and that’s why you told her. If you’d been second-guessing yourself, you would’ve kept quiet about it.”

     

                Kara turned over a thought for a long while, sipping her wine with a glazed look in her eyes as the TV filled the silence. Eventually, she heaved a sigh and met Lena’s eyes with a sheepish look of wariness in her blue eyes.

     

                “And what if … I hadn’t made my mind up but I just- I told her knowing how she’d react so she’d make up my mind for me.”

     

                “What, you told her so you could get mad and move in with me because you had nowhere else to go?” Lena laughed, her face creasing with bewildered amusement. “Bullshit, you wanted to say yes, you just didn’t know how to. You’re not stupid either; I can see that you’re upset, and you didn’t antagonise her into it or you wouldn’t be upset.”

     

                “Alex can be brutally honest,” Kara muttered, averting her gaze as she shrugged indifferently.

     

                “You’re allowed to willingly move in with me, you know. I know I said I could be your last resort but … I could be your first choice too. You never needed an excuse, even if you have a thousand places to stay. I offered with the intention of you saying yes, not just out of politeness.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose as she smiled tightly, eyes mystified, Kara cocked her head to the side. “Why would you do that though?”

     

                “I already told you why.”

     

                “I know but it doesn’t make sense. From everything I know about you … you like your space, you like your own company. I didn’t want to take that away from you.”

     

                “I’m married,” Lena pointed out, blinking down at the rings on her left hand as her brow creased. “Or … you know, but it’s strange for me to be alone now. It never used to be before her but I’d gotten used to it so having you move in isn’t that nonsensical, is it?”

     

                Kara let out a sharp laugh, gesturing around the place, “you’ve seen my messy apartment.”

     

                Hiding her smile behind her hand as she swallowed her sip of wine. “You should see mine before my cleaner comes.”

     

                “You have a cleaner?”

     

                “I- of course. I run my own business, I don’t have time to clean.”

     

                “Okay, that’s a lie, you spend so much time with me.”

     

                “Which is why I don’t have time to clean. It’s convenient, you’ll see.”

     

                Snorting, Kara raised her eyebrows. “Okay, now you sound like a rich girl.”

     

                “And I didn’t before?” Lena countered, giving her a thin smile.

     

                “No, you just sounded … moderately wealthy.”

     

                Laughing as she shook her head, Lena drained her drink and then climbed to her feet. “Okay, well you keep thinking that so you don’t think I’m prissy and I’ll get us another bottle.”

     

                Kara smiled slightly to herself as she finished off the rest of her drink while Lena uncorked the new bottle. She was still trying to reevaluate her impression of Lena, trying to place her in life, how she was outside of their friendship. Did she frequent dive bars or was it just on account of Kara? Did she regularly eat takeout at cheap greasy places with large portions or was her usual dining experience more high-class? Did she do her own grocery shopping or did someone browse the aisles at Trader Joe’s for organic produce and deliver it to her apartment for her?

     

                “Now, what’s the plan?” Lena asked as she refilled both of their glasses and reclaimed her seat.

     

                “What plan?”

     

                “The moving plan.”

     

                “Oh, um … well, it’s on the market in a few days so I guess I’ll have to wait and see how long it takes for an offer to come through. Then the settlement and all of that. It’ll probably take a couple of months at least.”

     

                “Alright, well, let me know when you start packing. I can give you a hand.”

     

                “Thank you.”

     

     

                The apartment ended up selling after three weeks on the market and two home openings, and it took another month to settle. Kara found no reason to delay it, two offers coming through, one above the asking price and accepted without argument. She’d barely spoken to Alex in that time, despite Thanksgiving rolling around with an awkward dinner with their friends as Alex tried to subtly make amends and Kara was cordial at best. 

     

                Instead, she relayed the news of the sale to Kelly, knowing she’d pass it on for her, even though her sister-in-law hated mediating. Kara did feel a little bit guilty for ignoring her sister, especially with the holidays on the horizon and the wedding only four months away now after so many delays - which Kara knew was mostly out of respect for her - and she didn’t want to add to Alex’s stress but was still angry with her from their last conversation. Every time a text or call came through, she just ignored it. 

     

                Two weeks before the settlement was booked and a week before Christmas, Kara finally accepted a call from her though, sitting amidst the piles of cardboard boxes containing all of her things. It was a pitifully small amount in the grand scheme of things, and most of it was bound for storage with her furniture. Lena had spent all weekend helping her pack and Kara was exhausted, worn down, and perhaps that was why she answered.

     

                “Hello?”

     

                It still took her a moment to respond to the sound of Alex’s wary voice. “Hi.”

     

                “Hi, how’re you?”

     

                “Fine.”

     

                “Kelly told me you sold it.”

     

                “Mm, I move out next week.”

     

                Alex was quiet for a second. “Do you need help packing?” 

     

                Pressing her mouth into a flat line, Kara’s resolve wavered for a moment. “No, Lena’s been helping me.”

     

                “Right. So … you’re still moving in with her?”

     

                “Yeah.”

     

                “Okay.” Kara remained silent after Alex’s response, waiting until her sister forged onwards as the silence stretched into uncomfortable territory. “I’m sorry.”

     

                “Right.”

     

                “I … I shouldn’t have said what I did. I’m just worried for you-”

     

                “You don’t need to be. You weren’t entirely wrong; I am doing a lot better since he died. It might seem impulsive to you but that’s- that’s because I didn’t tell you from the beginning. I have thought it through and I had the same conversation with Lena that you had with me. We do communicate, you know. Despite what you think.”

     

                Softly sighing, Alex hesitated. “Alright. As long as you’re sure.”

     

                “It won’t be for long anyway. Just until I can get my own place.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                They lapsed into silence and Kara chewed on her bottom lip, rubbing her tired eyes as she sat amidst the mess of her place. It was starting to feel less like home already and she didn’t admit it to Alex but she’d already spent three nights at Lena’s in the last week. It hadn’t been intentional , as per se, and they’d mostly avoided sleeping with each other while the house settled but she’d woken up on the couch twice and in Lena’s bed once instead of coming home to her slowly emptying apartment.

     

                “So … you haven’t replaced me as Maid of Honour yet?” Kara weakly joked.

     

                Her sister let out a huff of laughter and Kara could envision her eye roll and hesitant smile. “Not yet. And … just in case you hadn’t already asked, Lena’s welcome to come.”

     

                “Oh, um … no, I hadn’t asked.”

     

                “Well, you should.”

     

                “No, it’s alright.”

     

                “Kara … she’s your friend. Hell, she’s got half of the group wrapped around her finger with the amount she saves them in alcohol every Friday night. Invite her to the damn wedding.”

     

                It was a peace offering and she ended up relenting, accepting it with as little fuss as possible as things somewhat eased between them. It was still slightly awkward, Kara trying to steer the conversation away from Lena and her impending living situation while Alex roped her into dinner on Tuesday with Kelly and anxiously checked if she was still coming to Christmas dinner at her apartment.

     

                Kara went to dinner, as promised, and after the first beer, it felt like it always did with her sister, complaining about work and flipping through channels, gossiping about new news - Nia and Querl were taking another break and Winn was bringing his new girlfriend to the next round of drinks - while tactfully avoiding any sore topics. Still, when Alex asked if she’d set a move-out date, Kara gave her the one she’d settled on with Lena and her sister didn’t have much to say beyond offering her help again.

     

                As hesitant as Kara was about the whole situation, it didn’t stop her from inviting her friends around on the last night in her apartment, all of them sitting on the floor with boxes of pizza and copious amounts of alcohol as they complained about how they were too old for sitting on the floor now. It was bittersweet but Kara knew she needed some sort of closure and having everyone over eased the heartache a little.

     

                Moving out in that lull between Christmas and New Year made the holidays feel like it was lacking its usual cheer, with no tree up in her apartment and no time to sit around eating leftovers on the sofa. The most she managed was to show up for the dinner parties her friends had arranged, bringing wine and Lena with her as she wore her usual Christmas sweater and tried not to think about all the things she needed to get done. For her part, Lena never got into the Christmas spirit, her apartment bare by choice and an almost bewildered look on her face when Kara invited her to Alex’s for dinner, as if Lena didn’t understand the fuss.

     

                She moved out on a Friday, Lena coming to pick her up with her things in the evening as the moving truck packed the last of her boxes away to go into storage. All too soon, the apartment was empty and Kara was left staring around at the nicks and signs of wear from years of living there. 

     

                It all hit her in a rush as her time spent there was cut down to a handful of minutes, her eyes filling with tears. She’d cried off and on for the last week and a few times that morning already and she didn’t even try to hide it from Lena as the two of them stood in the middle of the open living room, on the cusp of leaving.

     

                “Sorry,” Lena whispered, rubbing Kara’s back.

     

                Nodding, Kara’s mouth thinned as she sniffed, her eyes bloodshot. Wiping her cheeks on the cuff of her sleeve, she let out a strained laugh. “After everything, you’d think losing an apartment would be insignificant.”

     

                “Big changes are never insignificant. Come here.”

     

                Kara let her wrap her in a hug, grateful for the comfort as they stood in her empty apartment, the smell of cleaning detergent perfuming the air as the familiar sound of traffic passed by. They stood there for a long minute, holding each other as Kara blinked back tears, her heart breaking a little as she let go of the last shred of her marriage. Any memories moving forward would be without Mike, without even the ghost of his presence.

     

                Eventually, she pulled back, knowing she had to rip the bandaid off or risk never being ready to go. It being her decision, as with the sale of the apartment, made it easier to bear somehow.

     

                “Let’s go,” Kara murmured, her voice scratchy as she wiped her cheeks and glanced around the place one last time.

     

                Lena left first, giving Kara a moment before she stepped out and shut the door behind her. Walking downstairs, Kara swallowed thickly and made her way out onto the street for the last time, breathing in the smell from the bakery and listening to the sounds of the traffic and the construction workers the next block over, knowing she’d miss it. She could come back, of course, and walk that street again, but it would never be the same.

     

                Climbing into the passenger seat of Lena’s car, Kara buckled herself in and sagged against the seats. She didn’t speak as Lena drove her through the city, back to her - their - apartment. The thought made Kara uneasy but she stamped it down, staring out the window at the cloudy sky as she brooded, left to her own thoughts as Lena let her process the change.

     

                Parking in the underground lot beside a covered car caked in dust, Lena tapped the tag against the scanner beside the elevator doors and pushed the button for the penthouse, the two of them riding it silently up until it spat them out into the hallway. The apartment was dark as she unlocked the door, letting them inside to the dog approaching the door, tail wagging and dark, liquid eyes eager for attention.

     

                Lena tenderly cooed as she shed her coat and hung it up before sinking down to a crouch, scratching beneath Aristotle’s chin as his tail thumped against the wall. Hesitating, Kara removed her own coat, this time feeling different to all the times before, more permanent in a rather unsettling way. It wasn’t lost on her that if she fucked it up, she’d be homeless. Although, logically, she knew that Alex would never turn her away, no matter how they’d left things between them. Out of pride, Kara might have refused to go to her though.

     

                Removing her heeled boots, Lena carried them with her and slipped through her apartment with comfortable ease, while Kara lingered in the living room with uncertainty. It felt strange to feel out of place there, spending many nights on the sofa or days in the kitchen, and an increasing amount of time in Lena’s bedroom of late, and she wasn’t sure how she was supposed to act being there now.

     

                A minute later, Lena poked her head out of the kitchen, her face furrowing. “Are you coming?”

     

                Nodding, Kara hurried to follow, toying with the cuffs of her sweater as she rounded the kitchen island and passed through to the hallway on the other side of the sprawling apartment. Lena’s room was on the right of the hallway, spacious with its ensuite, her office right beside it. On the other side, there were two doors Kara had never opened and the one leading to the bathroom. 

     

                “I wasn’t sure which room you wanted,” Lena hesitantly started, gesturing to the two doors. “Thought I’d leave it up to you to pick. Either is fine; it makes no difference.”

     

                Pausing, Kara hesitated before she moved to the closest door, directly across from Lena’s room. Jerking it open, curious now, she poked her head inside. A perpendicular queen bed made up with a thick quilt and a mountain of pillows dominated the space, the sheets seemingly the same as Lena’s own, two bedside tables and a built-in closet spanning the far wall. There was a long bench at the foot of the bed with folded towels and a chest of drawers was situated off to the left, facing the bed, a TV above it and a decorative candle and knick-knacks on top. Along the same wall as the door was a vanity with a low stool and a mirror.

     

                Kara snorted. “Of course your guest room is nicer than my actual bedroom was.”

     

                Lena let out a quiet laugh and casually gestured inside, “change whatever you want. It’s your room now.”

     

                “Thank you. Seriously, I mean it.”

     

                “Don’t mention it.”

     

                Nodding as she ducked her head, Kara felt tongue-tied as she grazed her sock over the floor and scrambled for something to say, something that could convey just how grateful she was. Lena continued before she could scramble for something though, fishing in her pocket and pulling something out.

     

                “Um, your keys,” Lena murmured, holding up the physical key and the electronic tag.

     

                “Thanks.”

     

                She took the keys and curled her fingers around them, shifting uneasily as the gravity of her situation struck her. While not technically homeless in the literal sense, Kara had no place of her own anymore, and while it seemed a gift to not have to pay rent while living with Lena, it also left her feeling somewhat untethered.

     

                The money she’d made from selling the apartment had wiped out a good chunk of her debt and while Kara’s stress levels had decreased dramatically, there was another kind of panic eating away at her now. Only a few minutes into living with Lena, she was already anxious about cohabitating with someone else, something Kara hadn’t done in a year and a half. And she’d gotten used to living with Mike, after she’d been used to living with Alex, and she wasn’t sure if she’d get used to living with Lena. 

     

                What time did she wake up in the morning for work? What time did she eat dinner? Did she leave all the lights on and only run the dishwasher at night? What brands of food did she pick up at the store and did she have any allergies? It all felt shockingly important and unknowable all of a sudden and Kara didn’t know what to say. She felt too old to be feeling like she was at the beginning of a new relationship, knowing it for what it was but not being able to shake the feeling of knowing someone but not entirely.

     

                “I ordered Chinese for dinner already,” Lena said after a moment, breaking her spiralling train of thought.

     

                “Oh, okay. Thanks.”

     

                Smiling as she let out a quiet laugh, Lena touched her arm. “Make yourself at home.”

     

                Nodding as she gave her a faint smile, Kara turned and made her way into the bedroom, leaving the door open as she put the keys down on the dresser. Sinking into the foot of the mattress, she fished her phone out and sent Alex a message before deciding on a shower. She’d been shifting boxes and sweating as she thoroughly cleaned her place and the knees of her jeans were dusty.

     

                Feeling a little apprehensive as she made her way into the bathroom, Kara shut the door and hesitated as she considered locking it but felt stupid for thinking it. The shower head was a wide rainfall one with a panel of numerous settings that she tapped around on before stepping into the stream of steaming water. It was stocked for guests and Kara froze at the smell of the soap and shampoo, so wholly Lena that it felt wrong to envelope herself in it.

     

                Emerging pink-cheeked and a little more relaxed, the hot water knitting together some of her composure, Kara dried off her wet hair and folded the towel over the rack. A laundry basket was set beside the sink vanity and she dumped her clothes inside it before stepping out.

     

                Lena found her a few minutes later, rummaging around in her toiletries for deodorant and a hairbrush. Knocking on the doorframe, she looked a little wary herself. “Dinner’s here.”

     

                “Oh, okay. Thanks. I’ll be out now.”

     

                Leaving her hair and hastily spraying deodorant, Kara walked out to the kitchen where their usual spread was set on the table. Opening the cutlery drawer, Lena fetched forks and set them down before clearing her throat.

     

                “Drink?”

     

                “Whatever you’re having please.”

     

                Nodding, Lena fetched two tumblers and half-filled both glasses with whisky. Joining Kara, she gave her a grim smile and opened the container in front of her.

     

                “Thought you could use something strong.”

     

                “Thanks.”

     

                “How’re you holding up?”

     

                Shrugging, Kara’s cheek dimpled as she smiled unevenly. “I’m alright. I think it’ll take a while for the reality to sink in but … I guess I’m just glad I’m not alone.”

     

                “Want to watch a movie after?”

     

                “Sure.”

     

                They finished eating and Lena refilled their glasses before they sank down onto the sofa and spent a good twenty minutes trying to settle on something, even though Kara insisted she’d watch whatever Lena wanted. In the end, they put on a bad horror that Lena couldn’t help but scoff at as they watched the characters make terrible choices and snorted at the overexaggerated gouts of blood from slit throats and multiple stab wounds. It was mindless entertainment and they finished half of the whisky bottle Lena had brought through with her as they watched. 

     

                By the time the credits rolled and Lena switched the TV off, it was getting late and Kara realised how exhausted she was. It was exacerbated by the alcohol but she felt warm and leaden, worn out in a way that wasn’t entirely unpleasant as the events of the day caught up with her. Resting her head against the back of the sofa, she let it loll to the side as she gave Lena a faint smile.

     

                “I think I might go to bed if that’s okay.”

     

                Letting out a quiet laugh, Lena reached out to touch the back of Kara’s hand in a fleeting reassurance. “Of course it is.”

                

                “I’ll see you in the morning,” Kara murmured as she climbed to her feet, reaching for her empty glass and then for Lena’s.

     

                Sitting forward, Lena stopped her, despite the empty bottle, and their eyes met with a lingering look before Kara straightened. Picking up the bottle, she gave Lena a searching look as her friend averted her gaze.

     

                Hovering for a moment, wondering whether she should stay, Kara cleared her throat. “Goodnight.”

     

                “Sleep well,” Lena replied, her voice a weary sigh as she climbed to her feet as well.

     

                Kara drifted towards the kitchen and paused, glancing back to watch as Lena grabbed another bottle of liquor from the console pushed up against one wall. She poured herself another glass and took a sip, half in shadow as the lamplight failed to fully fight off the dark and Kara felt uncertainty twinge in her stomach before she turned and went to bed, reminding herself that she wasn’t there to get involved in Lena’s business, and it was the holiday season anyway. Maybe she was just indulging in her free time while the office was closed, New Year’s Eve the next day allowing for a day of heavy drinking and carelessness. Kara wasn’t so convinced though.

    Chapter 15

                The first two weeks were a cautious, uncertain thing as Kara adjusted to living with Lena, and assumed Lena did the same. Lena was always up by the time that Kara rolled out of bed, sometimes coming in through the front door in running gear, her cheeks flushed and earbuds in, other times she was already dressed for work in her pressed pleated pants and starched shirts, making coffee and reading the newspaper in the kitchen. Sometimes, she was gone by six.

     

                In contrast, Kara woke even later than usual, closer to work than she used to live which gave her the opportunity to sleep in, and she’d stumble out of bed in her old pyjamas, rubbing her eyes and looking frazzled. Most mornings, they’d eaten breakfast together and there had been a companionable silence between them, the routine of getting ready for the day, Kara’s scrubs hastily pulled on, her running shoes laced in the kitchen, Lena filling a cup with coffee and grabbing her car keys.

     

                Every morning, Lena had offered to drive Kara to work but Kara had insisted on catching the bus, not wanting to be an inconvenience and seeing the wisdom in not becoming suffocatingly co-dependent. She didn’t want to get to a point where they were living on top of each other, joined at the hip until they found it unbearable to be around each other. As much as she liked Lena, perhaps more than she was willing to admit, Kara was eager to find somewhere new, within her budget, as soon as possible before she started to feel like an imposition.

     

                There was a part of her that was reluctant though, the new insight into glimpses of Lena’s life that she hadn’t been around for making her concerned. Kara might have seemed a mess in the mornings in comparison to Lena’s composed routine but in the evenings, it seemed to be the opposite. Kara was home before Lena every night except on Thursday, when they met at Group and she got a lift home with her, and she knew Lena was busy with her company but it was the drinking that concerned Kara the most.

     

                Of course, they drank together a few times a week, usually just a glass or two some nights and then more on Fridays with their friends, and that was normally enough for Kara, except for the rare low night she indulged herself to numb the grief. It quickly became apparent to her that it wasn’t the case for Lena though. Every single night she’d had at least a few drinks, with dinner and then more after, with Kara normally heading off to bed once it got too late. It had slipped her notice before, the occasional night at Lena’s leading her to believe that it was purely a social thing like her smoking, but after leaving her staying up to drink some more alone every night so far, Kara was beginning to wonder if Lena had spent every night for the last year drinking alone.

     

                Another week passed by and Kara observed Lena’s drinking in silence, keeping her opinions to herself; how could she judge Lena for how she handled her grief? Kara had been there, at the bottom, struggling to keep going, in bad shape as she slept all day and missed work, skipped meals and showers and drank too much. If she’d had to get out of bed every morning to keep her business running, maybe she would’ve drank more too. 

     

                There was that nagging thought that it had been more than a year and a half for her now though, that Kara had slowly gotten herself together, even as some things fell apart at the same time. She had managed to get her head above water and forge onwards until she didn’t feel like she was drowning. With Lena, it seemed to be the opposite. While Kara was trying her best to overcome it, making strides to move on, it seemed like Lena was spiralling downwards . Time should have helped, should have lessened the pain a little, and allowed her to claw her way out of the all-consuming grief but instead, she seemed to be stuck.

     

                Kara didn’t know how to broach the topic with her either, sitting quietly beside her on the sofa on a Sunday in early February, a can of beer in hand as she sipped it slowly, watching Lena pour herself more wine as she recounted a call with a client earlier that day. Lena had gone out that morning without explanation, dressed warmly and looking sombre, faint stress lines at the corners of her eyes and mouth as she grabbed her keys and haltingly informed Kara she’d be back later. Asking no questions, Kara bided her time by taking Aristotle for a walk and cleaning the apartment.

     

                Lena had arrived back at five o’clock, carrying a bag of Indian food she’d picked up on the way home and looking pale and tense. In the midst of folding laundry in her room, Kara emerged and gave Lena a soft smile, resisting the urge to ask her where she’d been and accepting the delivery of dinner with thanks as she started to set the table while Lena got changed into something more comfortable.

     

                Eating in relative silence, Kara had asked a few probing questions about Lena’s day but her friend didn’t take the bait as she vaguely replied and then suggested a movie. Kara had washed up, waving away Lena’s help and then wishing she hadn’t as she watched her take a bottle of wine into the living room with her, waiting for Kara to finish up.

     

                As Lena finished her story about her phone call, looking disgruntled as she pursed her lips, a furrow between her eyebrows, Kara cocked her head to the side. She liked watching Lena talk, the way she gestured with her hands, how expressive her eyebrows were, her face animated as a litany of expressions crossed it. 

     

                “So when are you going to show me your projects?”

     

                “Ah, it’s not that exciting,” Lena dismissively replied.

     

                Shrugging, Kara gave her a small smile. “It is to me. I’m curious.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose, Lena hesitated before climbing to her feet and gesturing for Kara to follow. “Come on, it’s all in my office.”

     

                Taking her beer with her, Kara eagerly followed. She hadn’t been inside Lena’s office yet, a sacred place that she didn’t want to intrude on, even though Lena had never insisted on her privacy. Hovering on the threshold for a moment, Kara stepped inside the room and breathed in the smell of wood, paper and leather as she took in the sleek furniture and rather minimalist interior.

     

                There was a wide desk monopolising the far end, the large window situated behind it with the blinds half-drawn against the glare of the sun, a leather swivel chair behind it and a computer on the desk. A large filing cabinet that looked fashionably vintage was set off to one side and just inside the door was a drafting table with an adjustable lamp situated over it. There wasn’t much in the way of decor, just a few framed photos on the walls and Lena’s degrees beside them, a diary on the desk, a framed photo Kara couldn’t see but envisioned as Andrea and a thriving monstera on top of the filing cabinets.

     

                Lena moved through the office with ease, jerking open a drawer of the filing cabinet and rummaging through the neatly arranged files with familiarity. Pulling out a portfolio, she turned and set it on the drafting table, switching on the lamp to illuminate the leatherbound book as she flipped to the first page.

     

                “This was my first project under my own company,” Lena said as Kara drew closer.

     

                It was a blocky office building of stone, glass and dark wood with an abundance of acacia trees and ferns strategically placed. It had the same mid-century modern feel of Lena’s apartment without the cosiness of the deep colours and touches of an artfully curated home. Turning the pages through the blueprints, drafted drawings, colour swatches and photos of polished wood and concrete and glass conference rooms and bulbous lighting fixtures, Kara was intrigued by it all.

     

                She flipped through more projects, taking in the same concepts fitted and tailored for different clients. There were predominantly office buildings or headquarters for big brands, a few government buildings and parks and a few privately commissioned homes Lena informed her were owned by various millionaires. All of them felt like they belonged in an issue of Architectural Digest, and when Kara mentioned that, Lena laughed and told her there were a few issues on the shelves in the living room where her pieces were featured. 

     

                “So, most of those new buildings covered in plants are yours?” Kara asked.

     

                Lena laughed, shrugging, “a fair few of them. We’re involved in a green energy scheme at the moment. You know, reclaimed wood, recycled materials, utilising as much space for plants to help energy conservation. It’s becoming a trend though; I think half of the new builds in National City are going to be covered in plants in the next few years. Can’t complain about that.”

     

                “You built the children’s hospital?” Kara asked as she turned the page, glancing up at Lena.

     

                She hummed with faint amusement, “well, my company drafted the plans and created the design. A team of twenty of us.”

     

                “Christ, you- I don’t even want to know how much a project like that costs.”

     

                “Whatever you’re thinking, it’s more,” Lena laughed. “Commercial buildings cost a fortune . And hospitals … well, we have to consider a lot more for the feasibility of medical staff doing their jobs efficiently. It’s easier to just build an office but I hate the bland grey of commercial buildings.”

     

                “Which one was your favourite to design?”

     

                Hesitating, chewing on her bottom lip, Lena was thoughtful for a moment, her fingers stilling on the page of the portfolio. Then she quickly flicked through it and landed on a page for a towering building, tapping her finger on the photo.

     

                “Obsidian North.”

     

                “Oh, right, I remember you said you designed that one. I’ve been past it; it looks fancy.”

     

                “Yes. It’s a big company. The headquarters was moved here from Buenos Aires years ago and the new CEO wanted a brand new building to reflect the rebranding of the business after she took over.” 

     

                “Why’s it your favourite?”

     

                Lena paused, deliberating before she shrugged, letting out a sigh. “I guess it was just the most enjoyable project for me. It was when I was happiest, I … I just- it was more of a collaboration and … I enjoyed the work. It’s the only project where I just wanted to keep working, where I got to handle all of the little details myself. One thing about being in charge … it becomes less about the work that got you into the industry and more about meetings and emails and smoothing over problems and covering up the fuckups before the clients get wind of it. That project … it reminded me why I wanted to be an architect. I drafted the plans for it myself, right here.”

     

                “Maybe you should do it again.”

     

                With a slightly breathless laugh, Lena wrinkled her nose and shook her head. “No. I think … that building was my magnum opus. Maybe not to everyone else but to me … it’ll always be the most important.”

     

                Kara flipped through a few more pages, taking in the photos of the finished lobby, grey slate and walnut wood and glass giving it a luxurious look of antiquated modernity that was contradictory but suited the tech company, from what she knew about it. Admittedly, it wasn’t a lot; Kara had never gotten into gaming but had heard enough from Winn and Querl’s gossip to know the CEO had gotten sick a while ago and stepped down. She flipped through the rest of the section on that project and continued through the next one, a renovation of National City University’s business campus.

     

                “Why’d you want to become a vet?” Lena asked, distracting her.

     

                Looking up, Kara blinked and then let out a quick laugh. Straightening, she ran a hand through her hair and blew the air out of her lungs. “I just liked animals.”

     

                “That simple, huh?”

     

                “Mhm. I had a cat - I say that but it was a stray - not long after my parents passed. His name was Streaky-”

     

                “Streaky?”

     

                “Yeah … I can’t ever judge my patients. Anyway, I loved that cat. I remember he broke his leg at one point and my mom ended up forking over the cash to get it treated because I was so devastated. I nursed that cat so much that I probably almost smothered him to death. It would’ve been cheaper and easier to be a vet nurse, in hindsight, but … I was smart and ambitious.”

     

                “Ambitious?” Lena echoed with surprise.

     

                Eyelids shuttering as she smiled, Kara sipped her beer. “Maybe not so much anymore.”

     

                “I would have thought you’d have your own pets, with how much you love animals.”

     

                “Oh. We used to. Mike got a dog right out of college so he became our dog. Krypton. He was a golden retriever but, you know, nine years later, he just wasn’t doing that great. Never put down your own dog; that was a lesson I learnt the hard way. It turned me off getting another puppy but … I kind of wish I had. After Mike passed, it might’ve been nice to have company.”

     

                “Ah, so am I just a replacement for the dog you never got?” Lena asked, giving her a quick grin.

     

                “Well, the Basenji just wasn’t any good for conversation and the Husky … God, he just talked too much,” Kara wryly replied, “you’re a good middle ground.”

     

                “That’s comforting to know, I’ve always been a bit of an overachiever so it’s nice to be mediocre at something for a change.”

     

                Shrugging, Kara snorted, “I was thinking more along the lines of Goldilocks - you know, just right. If you’d like to know your bad habits though, I can write you a list.”

     

                A scoffing laugh of surprise escaped Lena and she arched an eyebrow. “That many things, huh? Maybe letting you move in was a bad idea; all of my bad habits will end up turning you off me.”

     

                “You drink too much,” Kara blurted out without even meaning to. Her face immediately flushed and she cleared her throat, looking down at the portfolio as she chewed on her next words. “I mean … sorry, I just- I’ve noticed and … if you need to talk-”

     

                “Talk ,” Lena quietly huffed with amusement, although there was a tightening at the corners of her eyes, a flashing warning to her eyes as she looked at Kara. Standing close, Lena touched her fingers to Kara’s cheek, tender as she softened her voice but left no room for misunderstanding. “You’re my best friend but that is none of your business.”

     

                “I know,” Kara whispered, passively agreeing as she fought back a wince at how she’d ruined the mood. “I just wanted to let you know that … if you need anything, I’m here.”

     

                “I’m well aware,” Lena murmured, her voice thick with frustration as her other hand briefly brushed against Kara’s thigh before she abruptly turned and stalked out of the office, a door shutting firmly a moment later. 

     

                Pressed up against the side of the drafting table, mouth opening and closing as confusion knotted in her chest and her body felt hot as her heart pounded, Kara wasn’t quite sure what had happened. Running a hand over her face, she straightened and drained the rest of her beer before crumpling the can in her hand and closing the portfolio.

     

                Stepping out of the office, she closed the door behind her and then hesitated, her eyes straying to Lena’s closed bedroom door. For a brief moment, Kara considered knocking, checking to make sure Lena was okay or apologising for overstepping, but once she reached their parallel doors, she went into her room instead, softly shutting it behind her.

     

                Setting her crushed beer can on the dresser, Kara raked a hand through her hair and then sank onto the end of the bed. Hunched forward, forearms braced on her thighs, she brooded over Lena. They had barely touched each other, even innocently, since she’d moved in three weeks ago - before then even, in anticipation of moving in - and that unbearable tension that had hung between them in the anticipation of sleeping together the first time had returned again, and Kara didn’t know what to do about it.
