                The easiest answer was to move out but she hadn’t had any luck apartment hunting yet and Lena was always quick to assure her there was no rush. But with so much pent-up frustration between them and their unspoken agreement to try and mitigate any risks by not instigating anything, it suddenly felt urgent.

     

                The next morning, Lena was sheepish as she murmured an apology and made a cup of coffee for Kara, hovering around nervously, beyond the time she usually left for work. Glancing at her, Kara took in the tensed shoulders, pale hands cupping her coffee mug as she leaned against the counters, making no move to leave.

     

                “Were you going to work today?” Kara eventually asked as her toast popped up and she started buttering the slices.

     

                “Yes, in a minute. I … I thought you could have these.”

     

                Kara glanced over at her and then did a double-take at the car keys held out to her. Brow furrowing, Kara reached out and took them, four Audi rings at the bottom of the remote.

     

                “Um …”

     

                “The car in the garage - the covered one gathering dust - it, um, it was Andrea’s car. I never had the heart to sell it but … it’s going to waste so I thought you might want to use it. Save you riding the bus everywhere.”

     

                “Lena,” Kara slowly replied, caution lacing her name.

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Lena ducked her head down and started rummaging through her handbag but there was a tautness to her face and the set of her shoulders, even as she affected nonchalance. 

     

                “It’s fine, it’s just more convenient, isn’t it? I’ll call a mechanic out to service it, just to make sure it’s all working fine. The engine might not start after so long without it being used, so you might want to take the bus today unless you want a ride.”

     

                “I- that’s a very generous offer but I can’t-”

     

                “Take it. Please.”

     

                Her voice was brittle, on the verge of breaking, and Kara knew that it was an apology at the expense of her wife’s memory, to let someone else get behind the wheel of her car, someone else to add miles to it in her place. Based on that alone, she wanted to reject the offer again but Lena’s tone made her pause.

     

                Relenting, Kara swallowed thickly. “Thank you.”

     

                Jerking her head in a quick nod, Lena didn’t look at her. “I have to go.”

     

                Draining the rest of her mug, she set it down heavy-handedly and turned quickly, dragging her handbag off the counter with such haste that she only grabbed one handle, scattering the contents on the floor. Lipsticks, cigarettes, sheaths of paper from her diary, pens, perfume and tampons and credit cards spilt across the floor and Lena’s shoulders slumped as she tipped her head back, inhaling sharply through her nose as she let her handbag drop from her hand.

     

                Already sinking to a crouch, Kara started gathering up the scattered belongings, cradling a small bottle of hand sanitiser, a lipgloss, lipstick, lip balm, hand lotion and lighter in her palms as she shovelled it all back into Lena’s bag. Scrambling for more, her arm brushed Lena’s leg as she tried to fit a few cigarettes back into the open packet and picked up yet more lipsticks, wondering how many one person could own.

     

                “Leave it.”

     

                “It’s okay,” Kara started to reassure her.

     

                “Leave it.”

     

                Blinking, Kara’s lips parted and she slowly rose to her feet, still holding the gathered items. She swallowed and then inhaled to reply but was silenced as Lena quickly moved towards her, grabbing Kara’s face in her hand and kissing her roughly.

     

                Lips parting in surprise, Kara let her handful of items clatter to the floor as she pulled Lena close, kissing her back. The abruptness of it softened after a few moments, reality jolting Kara back to herself as she broke it off, their foreheads touching as her chest rose and fell quickly.

     

                “I thought we said we weren’t going to do this anymore,” Kara whispered, their lips a scant inch apart as Lena’s warm breath fanned across her mouth.

     

                Gently bumping her nose against Kara’s cheek, Lena let out a quietly frayed laugh that made Kara’s eyelids flutter. “When did we say that?”

     

                “We agreed it was a bad idea.”

     

                “I distinctly remember not agreeing to that.”

     

                Kara’s hands slid up the back of Lena’s sweater, hands splayed across her ribs and spine as she glided her palms upwards. She held her close, forearms pressed against her back, her stomach clenched as her heart stuttered in her chest.

     

                “But if you don’t want to-“

     

                Letting out a huff of laughter at the words Lena mumbled against her jaw, Kara hummed with amusement, knowing she was being toyed with. “Funny. I could-“

     

                She trailed off, swallowing thickly. Kissing the corner of her jaw, Lena made an inquisitive sound at the back of her throat. “You could what?”

     

                “I could do this all day,” Kara softly admitted.

     

                Lena drew back a fraction and then kissed her with surprising tenderness. “Don’t go to work today. Stay home with me.”

     

                Kara knew that she shouldn’t, knew that she should have gone to work, and she wouldn’t admit it to herself but she would have done anything for Lena. Biting her bottom lip, she still hesitated a moment before nodding.

     

                “Okay.”

     

                “Really?”

     

                “Sure, just give me a second.”

     

                Crossing over to the counter, Kara picked up her phone and eyed her abandoned toast. Calling James, she held her phone to her ear as it rang, and then Lena was behind her, arms encircling Kara’s waist, the solid warmth of her making Kara’s pulse spike.

     

                “Hey, you’re calling early.”

     

                “Hey,” Kara haltingly replied, her voice catching, a little hoarse as Lena’s hands ran over the front of her scrubs. “Um, I was just- I was just calling to see if I- if I could take a day.”

     

                James was silent for a moment before he softly sighed, weary in a way that said he’d expected it. “Yeah, sure, if you need it.”

     

                Lena’s hand was beneath the waistband now and her other one ghosted over Kara’s throat, making it constrict as she tried to swallow. Trailing her fingertip along Kara’s jaw, Lena laughed into the back of her neck, raising goosebumps.

     

                “It’s just- I guess I just need a mental health day,” Kara said, her voice trembling slightly, uneven as she winced with guilt. 

     

                “Oh, okay. Yeah, no problem. Let me know if you need anything, okay? Maybe give Kelly a call as well, you know, if you’re struggling-“

     

                “I- yeah, sure, I will if I need to. And … sorry.”

     

                “Don’t worry about it. I’ll see you tomorrow?”

     

                “Definitely,” Kara promised before hanging up and setting her phone down firmly.

     

                “Oh, you’re such a liar,” Lena laughed.

     

                Turning, Lena’s hands skimming her waist as she retained her hold on her, Kara gave her a withering look. She looked sheepish but raised her chin in a stubborn manner.

     

                “It’s not a lie; it is for my mental health.”

     

                Snorting, Lena’s green eyes shone with mirth as her cheeks dimpled at her suppressed laughter. “You make me laugh,” she fondly murmured.

     

                Then she kissed her again and Kara felt the tension in her chest come undone, as if she’d been waiting for this for a month. It had seemed like the right thing to do, to avoid making things messy, but the anticipation of it felt worse than the act as she slowly messed up Lena's polished look, the heels kicked off in the kitchen, the sweater off and shirt untucked, pencil skirt unzipped. 

     

                There was a sense of satisfaction in that, and in the fervent way Lena kissed her and tore her scrubs off as if she was angry at the imposition they posed. Half-dressed, they paused in the hallway, caught between both of their bedroom doors until Lena fumbled for hers and stepped inside, unbuttoning her shirt and carelessly tossing it aside.

     

                For all their initial impatience, they didn’t rush and Kara basked in the feeling of Lena’s skin, of her mouth and hands, more than a month without her feeling far too long. Perhaps she was biassed, wrapped up in the moment, but her concerns suddenly felt stupid and she decided that any worries she’d had about how it would affect their relationship were unfounded. It didn’t matter that she’d moved into Lena’s apartment, it didn't change anything, except the knowledge that there was nothing stopping her from repeating the act over and over again. That in itself was a slippery slope into dangerous waters.

     

                They lay together afterwards, legs tangled and Lena’s head on Kara’s chest, their breaths slowly evening out as their pulses slowed. Sweat dried on their skin and Kara felt warm and loose-limbed, more at rest than she’d been in weeks as she basked in the feeling of being intimate with someone, filling up that hole of loneliness - for now.

     

                Eventually pushing herself up, Lena sat on the edge of the mattress and stretched her arms out, the bones and muscles of her back and shoulders shifting as Kara watched. “Well, I’m glad that’s out of the way.”

     

                “What, was it such a hassle?” Kara spluttered as she laughed, sitting up and running a hand through her hair.

     

                “Don’t pretend it hasn’t been getting to you as well. The tension’s been unbearable. God, I’ve felt like I could just … explode. I’ve been a raging bitch for the last month.”

     

                “That’s a bit harsh. You’ve just been … a little blunt.”

     

                Grinning over her shoulder, Lena’s eyes creased at the corners. “Oh, no, I’m not talking about to you. I think I’ve made everyone’s life hell at the office with my impatience lately.”

     

                Shifting across the mattress, Kara brushed dark hair off Lena’s shoulder and pressed a soft kiss to her skin. “You could’ve just asked.”

     

                “We were avoiding it.”

     

                “Why were you avoiding it? I thought you didn’t agree it was a bad idea.”

     

                “I don’t but … it felt like it might make things more meaningful.”

     

                “What do you mean?”

     

                Falling silent, Lena turned her head, staring at the gauzy curtains covering the windows. Kara could feel the tension that crept back into Lena’s muscles as she took her time to respond, and she stayed still, waiting patiently.

     

                “We’re living together, we’re sleeping together, we spend all of our time together. What does that sound like to you?”

     

                “It sounds like I got very lucky,” Kara joked.

     

                Eyes cutting to her face as she turned slightly, Lena’s mouth thinned. Sighing as her shoulders sagged, Kara touched the backs of her fingers to Lena’s cheek.

     

                “It would sound like we were dating, to anyone else. To me? It really does sound like I got very lucky to end up in a situation where I have no responsibilities or complications to worry about.”

     

                “I guess,” Lena agreed distractedly.

     

                Reaching out to touch her shoulder, Kara cocked her head to the side. “Hey, don’t- don’t let things build like that, okay? I’d rather you just be honest if it’s bothering you.”

     

                 “I’m not going to try and convince you when you said you don’t want this to keep happening. I can manage just fine.”

     

                “That’s not what I said,” Kara murmured as her face creased. “I’m just … worried about what could happen if it does keep happening. I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t but that doesn’t mean I don’t want y- this .”

     

                Lena fully turned then, giving her a searching look. Cheek dimpling as she smiled ruefully, Kara leaned back, the sheets pooled around her waist. “I don’t need to be convinced.”

     

                “Well, come here then,” Lena unevenly replied, cocking an eyebrow in a haughty manner when Kara raised her own eyebrows dubiously. “You did say you could do this all day, and you did call in sick to work. I’m just looking out for your mental health.”

     

                Snorting, Kara grabbed a pillow and gently whacked Lena with it and found herself on her back, wrists pinned beside her head a moment later. They were laughing and the lightness of the moment made her chest ache for something she’d forgotten she’d missed. It suddenly felt like she was ten years younger, in love for the first time.

     

                The thought struck Kara like a blow, heavy in her chest as panic made her stomach jolt. Squashing any thoughts along those lines, refusing to acknowledge any feelings for Lena that went beyond platonic, Kara closed her eyes and let her kiss her.

    Chapter 16

                The feelings didn’t die though, they flourished, with every touch, every kiss, every day that passed. It had been steadily growing for weeks, for months, since before they’d slept together the first time. It had been one of Kara’s voiced concerns but she’d never wanted to attribute anything substantially real to it, her first mistake in the slow descent into disaster.

     

                As it was, it became a regular occurrence for them to sleep together now, even more frequent than it had been before Kara had moved in, which had been what she was afraid of. Somehow, it never felt wrong and she never regretted it, although she still wondered if Lena did. It was that thought alone which compelled Kara to sneak out of Lena’s bedroom every night afterwards as if she was trying to leave without being caught, although her escape only led her a mere two steps across the hallway to her own room.

     

                But it was easier to sneak out, making it feel like less than it was to keep that boundary in place. If she woke up in Lena’s bed four times a week, Kara imagined the line would start blurring more than it already had. It helped that Lena had usually been drinking, and if she didn’t fall asleep, she usually got up to pour herself another one, giving Kara the opportunity to gather her clothes and head back across the hall, knowing she’d do the exact same thing again in a night or two.

     

                For all her worries about muddying the water, making it unnecessarily complicated for a few hours of comfort each week to keep the loneliness at bay, Kara couldn’t bring herself to stop. As weeks went by, it was like her life had settled into a comfortable routine that she liked, a life that she was genuinely happy with. It felt wrong to admit it and there were moments that made her pause, thinking hateful things towards herself as she felt Mike slip further away from her, her grief no longer a debilitating thing a few months shy of two years on. Kara often wondered if he would be happy for her if he could see her now.

     

                And it wasn’t romantic, it was something else entirely, caught in some friends-with-benefits grey area that felt too childish to be named such a thing. At thirty-five, her life had shaped up to be anything but what she’d imagined for herself but Kara was content in a different way than she’d been with Mike. Before, it had been the sort of content when one settled for a mundane life but with Lena, with the open nature of their relationship, unburdened consequences and responsibilities, she felt content in a way that felt like freedom. 

     

                She enjoyed coming home to cook dinner for them, Lena always exhausted and grateful when she stepped into the kitchen, liked that they watched TV together, and that Lena let her borrow her clothes sometimes, handing over a sweater, a coat, a dress when they were getting ready to go out. She liked that if they were going out, especially on a Friday night, she’d go into Lena’s bathroom and put on her 90s playlist and they’d bicker about their opinions on boy bands and pop stars like they were in college, helping apply eyeliner and curling hair. Kara liked the way Lena asked her opinion on things, told her about a new Podcast she’d found or summarised an interesting article. There was no shortage of little moments of living together that made Kara feel fulfilled in a way that living with a man who’d slowly neglected her over the years had left her wanting.

     

                It was no surprise, to her least of all, when those feelings slowly but surely softened into a simple kind of love. Not passionate or grand but a tender way of asking how Lena’s day was and genuinely wanting to know, of knowing her favourite colour and flower, the foods she hated and her favourite movies. Kara had thought she’d never have to memorise those facts again, that she’d found the one and would’ve wasted her whole life with Mike, but it didn’t hurt quite so much as she’d thought to repeat the process.

     

                And the entire time, Kara knew she was falling, a slow train wreck happening right before her eyes, with plenty of time for her to stop it. Each time, she cautioned herself that it was enough, that it was the last time now, that it wasn’t fair to Lena to feel something stronger and take advantage of her detachment for her own benefit. But she always went back, squashing the nagging thoughts of hidden feelings, and she was too blinded by her own worry at Lena catching on to even realise that her friend was fighting the same losing battle and was slowly becoming a wreck because of it.

     

                Nearing the end of March, Lena came home late one day to find Kara crouched on the kitchen floor as she played tug-of-war with a new dog toy she’d brought home for Aristotle. At the sound of her arrival, Kara looked up and the Cavalier bounded over to her for attention.

     

                “You’re going to spoil him if you keep bringing things home from work,” Lena murmured.

     

                Smiling as she climbed to her feet, Kara paused, taking in the odd look on Lena’s face. Her expression was pinched, taut with an unreadable emotion, her eyes distant and an air of weariness about her.

     

                “Well, I don’t have any kids to spoil and I don’t think they’d be nearly as excited about discounted treats and stuffed animals, so … he deserves it.”

     

                Lena hummed distractedly, rubbing her cheek as she blinked slowly, barely present in the moment as Kara looked at her. When she didn’t speak, Kara gave her a searching look, taking in the still pristinely applied lipstick, the smoky eyeshadow and the polished look of a carefully chosen outfit.

     

                “You look nice,” Kara said with mild surprise. 

     

                Lena always looked nice, was always dressed up for work, but there was something about the fitted dress that gave the impression that more effort had been put into her decision. That, along with the heavier makeup, and Kara wondered if she’d left for work like that or if she’d been home and left again before Kara had gotten home. The thought struck her suddenly and she smiled wryly.

     

                “Hot date?”

     

                Expression blank, Lena stiffened slightly, a flicker of annoyance sparking in her green eyes. “Why would you say that?”

     

                “Oh, no, it- I was joking,” Kara haltingly replied, her brow furrowing as her cheeks warmed slightly.

     

                Mouth turning down at the corners as her shoulders dropped, Lena squeezed her eyes shut. Kara could see a muscle twitching in her jaw as she swallowed.

     

                “No, right, of- of course.”

     

                They both fell silent, standing in the kitchen in the dim light of the hood range, the kettle for Kara’s tea boiling and then quietening to a simmer as neither of them spoke. Softly clearing her throat, Kara hugged her arms to herself and raised her eyebrows.

     

                “Peppermint tea?”

     

                “No, thank you,” Lena rasped, her voice strangled and tight.

     

                Instead, she fetched herself a bottle of scotch and then disappeared down the hallway, the soft click of her bedroom door ending the conversation. Running a hand over her face, Kara closed her eyes and stood there for a minute before she poured hot water over her teabag and let it steep.

     

                Carrying her mug back to her room, where Aristotle was sleeping on her bed, she wondered for a moment whether she should check on Lena but decided against it. A closed door meant privacy and no invitation had been forthcoming. Instead, she shut herself in her own room and watched TV in bed as she nursed her tea.

     

                Still, the TV wasn’t loud enough to quite mask the sound of muffled crying that made itself known half an hour later, and Kara stilled. Muting the TV, checking she wasn’t hearing things, she set her mug down on the bedside table and climbed to her feet. Aristotle looked at her with dark, liquid eyes and Kara hesitated, torn between checking on Lena and leaving her be. Sometimes, crying alone was a relief and she didn’t want to intrude, didn’t want her to feel embarrassed.

     

                Easing her door open on silent hinges, Kara listened and waited, the darkness of the apartment making the world beyond it seem to vanish. They could’ve been the only two people left in the world, the loneliness threatening to swallow them up, and her heart ached for Lena and she bit her bottom lip and wrung her hands. She started to quietly pace outside her door, wrestling with the part of herself that wanted to fold Lena in her arms, whisper it would be alright, and the part that wanted to give her the space to grieve for her loss the way she wanted to.

     

                Then there was the sound of something breaking, the tinkling of glass and a ragged sound of pain. Abruptly turning to the door, Kara knocked, the sound loud as it cut through the relative quiet of the night.

     

                “Lena? I’m coming in,” she softly announced, not waiting for an answer before she turned the handle.

     

                “No. No, don’t,” Lena groaned, a shuddering breath catching in her chest.

     

                The door was already halfway open though and Kara was stepping inside, the room lit by a lamp and illuminating Lena’s silhouetted form standing near the vintage art nouveau vanity, shoulders tense and one hand clutching a glass of scotch. Fragments of glass glittered on the surface of the wood, a pool of liquid catching the light as it dropped off the edge and soaked into the carpet.

     

                “Hey,” Kara gently murmured, padding across to her, her fingers ghosting against Lena’s lower back as she took in the mess. 

     

                It looked like she’d dropped the bottle on the edge of the vanity while refilling her glass, smashing it and showering herself in liquor. The smell was overpowering, the sharp honeyed scotch burning Kara’s nose as she plucked the glass from Lena’s hand and set it down.

     

                “Careful of the glass,” Kara cautioned her, mindful of her own steps as she eyes the thick carpet.

     

                Lena made a low, wounded sound at the back of her throat, offering up her left hand as she blinked, tears running down her cheeks, running through the same tracks that had already cut through her makeup. Kara’s eyes dipped to her hand, the palm red where blood welled, dripping over the sides and dotting the carpet. A panicked exclamation escaped Kara and she looked around before rushing into the bathroom and fetching a hand towel.

     

                She emerged and crossed back over to Lena, who’d moved to sit on the edge of her bed, her breaths hitching with quiet sobs that made her shoulders shake. Kneeling before her, Kara cradled her hand and wrapped it in the towel as she gently shushed her.

     

                “It’s alright. It’s okay.”

     

                That only made Lena cry harder though, her sobs loud and hitching as her shoulders hunched forward, her head ducked and tears falling freely. They dotted the thighs of the silk pyjamas she’d changed into, soaked with scotch and stained with blood now, and Kara soothingly rubbed her knee as she watched her with concern. 

     

                “What’s wrong?” she asked after a few minutes, thinking perhaps she should’ve asked the minute Lena had come home with that funny look on her face.

     

                Choking on another sob, clapping a hand to her mouth as she squeezed her eyes shut, Lena drew in a shuddering breath and then let out another broken sob. She couldn’t help herself, her pain so raw and gut-wrenching that Kara just stared with wide eyes. She hadn’t felt her grief so intensely in months, and it was frightening to see how strongly Lena’s still affected her. There was even a layer of guilt that tried and failed to take hold of her as if Kara had somehow betrayed Mike for not lingering so deeply in her grief.

                

                “It’s her birthday,” Lena managed to choke out, gasping as she wiped at her wet cheeks, makeup ruined and eyes bloodshot and raw. 

     

                “Oh. Oh, no,” Kara softly groaned, deflating as her shoulders slumped and pity welled up in her chest. “I’m sorry.”

     

                “Thirty-six,” Lena sobbed. “Thirty-six and- and we should be out for dinner celebrating. We should be drinking cocktails on vacation.  Instead, I get to visit her and be left with … all these memories instead of her. We deserved so much more time.”

     

                “It’s alright. Come here,” Kara gently coaxed her, her own eyes stinging with tears as she reached up to embrace her.

     

                Lena went willingly, leaning forward, her face buried into Kara’s shoulder in the childlike manner of hiding from the pain of the world. Her sharp, broken gasps of pain and loud sobs were muffled by the shoulder of Kara’s T-shirt and she held Lena tightly, rubbing her back and kissing her hair, her blue eyes bright with a film of tears she tried to blink back.

     

                She sobbed until she’d exhausted herself, which took the better part of twenty minutes, the amount of scotch she’d had to drink leaving Lena more susceptible to her vulnerable feelings. It didn’t so much numb the pain but blurred the lines between containing it and letting it all out. All Kara could let her do was cry into her shoulder as she held her tight and pitied her. Her joke about a hot date seemed in poor taste now and she wanted to cringe, knowing how awful Lena’s evening had really been.

     

                Once Lena had calmed down some, Kara inhaled and let out a weary sigh of regret. “We should get you cleaned up. Check on that cut.”

     

                Pulling back, her cheeks splotchy and red, her nose running and her eyes puffy, Lena looked down at the bloodstained hand towel. “I- I put it down too hard. It shattered. Cut my- my hand.”

     

                “Can I take a look?”

     

                At Lena’s nod, Kara unwrapped the towel and uncurled Lena’s fingers. Fresh blood was still welling in the wound, which was short but deeper than anticipated, on the fleshy part of her palm, below her thumb. There were a few more gouges on her upper palm as well, just below her ring and little finger. Blood stained the bands of her rings and Kara’s mouth thinned.

     

                “These are a bit deep,” she hesitantly informed her. “Looks like you might need stitches.”

     

                Shaking her head, Lena sniffed and cleared her throat as more tears cut down her cheeks. “I don’t want to go to the hospital.”

     

                “I- well, I can do them for you. I mean … I’m a vet, I do sutures all the time on animals. I’m obviously not legally allowed to treat humans but the knowledge is pretty damn close; I’ve had to help out in a public accident once or twice.”

     

                “Oh. Okay.”

     

                “Okay. Let me get my first aid kit.” Giving her knee a quick pat, Kara fetched her bag and brought it back into the bedroom, switching on the big light.

     

                Spreading the contents out on the floor, Kara went to wash her hands and then put on a pair of gloves before tearing open a wipe. Warning Lena it would sting, she dabbed it over the bleeding cuts to clean them out, Lena quietly sobbing as she hissed with pain, fresh tears falling again. It made Kara wince with guilt but she continued.

     

                She applied lidocaine topically and waited for Lena’s palm to lose feeling before she started the slow process of carefully suturing the wounds. The one at the base of her palm was about an inch and the smaller ones were a quarter of that size but deeper, which meant that it didn’t take Kara too long to close them up. 

     

                Lena was pale and refused to look away, some sort of morbid curiosity seeming to calm her as she watched Kara work, not turned off by the blood or the sight of a needle pushing through her skin. Once she was finished, Kara wiped Lena’s palm with another antiseptic wipe and then loosely taped some gauze over her hand.

     

                “There you go. Much better.”

     

                Sniffing, Lena nodded, her chin dimpling as her lip quivered. “Thank you.”

     

                “Don’t mention it,” Kara whispered, giving her a faint smile.

     

                “I mean it. I’m glad I have you. I’m glad you’re here.”

     

                Nodding, Kara started to pack everything up, her throat tight as she felt the keen cut of Lena’s loneliness in her chest. Gathering everything up, Kara climbed to her feet and cupped the side of Lena’s face, pressing a kiss to the top of her head.

     

                “You’ll always have me.”

     

                Throwing the used items and the bloody hand towel into the trash, Kara quickly washed her hands again to remove the powdery feeling of the gloves and walked back into the bedroom. Lena hadn’t moved, sitting hollow-eyed and limp at the end of her bed as her chin wobbled and she fought to keep her composure.

     

                “Come on, let’s run you a bath,” Kara murmured, her gentle tone coaxing Lena to her feet.

     

                It felt like deja vu to the last time she’d done the same for Lena, except they were inexplicably closer now, her feelings for Lena magnified tenfold as their living situation had intensified everything. While hot water filled the tub and the magnesium bath salts perfumed the air, bubbles foaming on the surface, Kara slowly unbuttoned Lena’s silk pyjama too for her.

     

                They were close, the smell of scotch and Lena’s perfume overpowering as Kara felt her breath on her mouth. She glanced up to find Lena watching her, a glazed look in her eyes, a small furrow between her brows. And then Lena kissed her, softly, hesitantly.

     

                Breaking it off, their noses bumping as she closed her eyes, Kara shook her head. “No.”

     

                “You don’t- you don’t want me?”

     

                “You’ve just had a little bit too much to drink tonight,” Kara gently let her down.

     

                “You could drink with me,” Lena suggested.

     

                Giving her a small smile, Kara touched her cheek. “How about tomorrow?”

     

                “Tomorrow? I don’t want you tomorrow, I want you now.”

     

                The slurred bluntness of her words caught Kara by surprise and she let out a quick laugh. “That’s a shame but I have surgery in the morning, so I can’t get drunk. I’d love to. You know that I would.”

     

                Leaning into her, humming as Kara removed her stained shirt, Lena dug her fingers into Kara’s waist. “I just want to feel close to someone.”

     

                “I’m right here. Let me help wash your hair for you instead.”

     

                “Would you?”

     

                “Mhm.”

     

                Helping her undress the rest of the way and making sure she kept her injured hand dry, hanging over the side of the tub, Kara knelt beside her on the tiled floor and scooped handfuls of hot water over her back and shoulders.

     

                She grabbed a flannel from the stack of neatly rolled fresh towels and dipped it in the water, murmuring as she tilted Lena’s head up. Face softening with a smile as their eyes met, Kara started to wipe away her makeup, rinsing the flannel and then wringing it out and continuing the process.

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena was silent, her breaths slow and even now, and some of the tension seemed to bleed out of her as she sat with her knees drawn to her chest, shoulders slumped with exhaustion. As Kara wiped from her temples down the side of her face, she winced slightly, face spasming with pain, and Kara paused, pulling the flannel away and tilting Lena’s head to catch the light better.

     

                “What happened here?” Kara asked, her thumb grazing over a fresh lavender bruise blossoming high on Lena’s cheekbone.

     

                She hadn’t noticed it before because of her makeup but she was sure it hadn’t been there the day before. Kara thought she would’ve noticed, had memorised Lena’s face enough to know if a new bruise appeared.

     

                Raising her hand to touch it, Lena’s face furrowed and she swallowed thickly. “An accident. Stupid mistake.”

     

                “You should be more careful,” Kara murmured, gently wiping away more makeup.

     

                Humming in agreement, Lena let her finish and Kara soaped up her arms and back, the wood sage and sea salt body wash soothing as the bathroom steamed. Tendrils of dark hair grew damp and clung to Lena’s cheeks and temple, a flush entering her pale cheeks, making her look almost feverish. Once she was done, Kara instructed Lena to sink down into the water to wet her hair and then slowly washed it for her, kneeling as tall as she could as she gently massaged her scalp.

     

                “She used to wash my hair for me all the time in the bath. Massage my shoulders if they were sore from hunching over my desk all day,” Lena murmured, her voice wobbling as she closed her eyes.

     

                “That must’ve been nice.”

     

                “Mm. We used to do the crossword in the newspaper together every Saturday morning; the weekends were when we got to spend most of our time together. She always loved the park - the one we walk Aristotle in - and it was close to her office so we’d- we’d go for walks all the time. Sometimes, I’d meet her there for lunch during the week to take a break from work; she’d always been a city girl, loved the rush of it all, so she always used to joke that going to the park was her way of going into nature for some peace. She, uh, she never used to cook that often but she made the best empanadas when she felt like it. Me … well, I never really cared that much about getting married. We knew each other from school - she was a junior when I was a freshman - and we were friends but we never stayed in touch that much after she graduated. I moved here first and I got a message from her a couple of years later. I was twenty-four, just starting up the firm here, and she just- she was persistent. What she wanted, she got, and I was so weak for her. I fell so hard, so fast. She didn’t even really propose, she just said we should get married, so we did. God, that’s almost eight years now.”

     

                Kara let her talk and talk, her words slurring together slightly as she let the conditioner sit, head leaned back against the rim of the tub. Her throat would bob occasionally as she struggled to swallow and Kara’s heart went out to Lena as she listened to her speak of her wife with so much love and adoration, so much palpable pain over all of the memories. Sitting cross-legged on the bathroom floor, Kara wished for nothing but a gentler future for Lena, hoping there would come a day when it wouldn’t hurt quite so much and she’d think back on her marriage with fondness instead of suffocating grief.

     

                Eventually, Lena climbed out of the tub and Kara fetched clean silk pyjamas for her and blow-dried her hair as Lena sat on the stool of the vanity. Making two cups of tea, she had Lena tucked up in bed and cleaned up the rest of the mess as Lena apologised repeatedly from beneath the covers, utter exhaustion in her hoarse words as Kara picked up shards of glass and assured her it was fine.

     

                She only intended to stay with her for a short while, until Lena drifted off to sleep with the help of a cup of tea, but long after Kara had finished her own, she remained. Lena had ended up coaxing her beneath the blankets before that and Kara held her close, letting her friend burrow against her side and cling to her as if she was the last lifeboat on a sinking ship, sleep offering a reprieve from her pain. 

     

                Falling asleep with Lena in her arms, Kara woke early the next morning to her still fast asleep on her chest. She knew she should get up, should break Lena’s hold on her and put some space between them, her stomach clenched with unease as she looked down and felt something in her chest give slightly. Lena’s uninjured hand clenched a fistful of Kara’s shirt in a white-knuckled grasp and the taut lines of grief were smoothed out, making Lena look peaceful. She was loath to wake her.

     

                A while later, Lena roused herself, later than she usually woke for work, and Kara stayed still as she watched her slowly push herself up, blinking owlishly as her face furrowed with confusion. Then their eyes met and Lena blinked with sudden clarity, drawing away from her. She ran both hands through her hair and over her face and then pulled them away, staring at the gauze-wrapped stitches on her left palm.

     

                “Oh. Shit.”

     

                “Let me get you some painkillers,” Kara offered, eager to get out of Lena’s bed now that she was awake.

     

                She almost tripped over her own feet in her haste and wrinkled her nose at the hard press of missed glass hidden in the carpet, not sharp enough to cut the soles of her feet but firm enough to make itself known. Aristotle’s collar jingled as he jumped off Kara’s bed, where he’d seemingly spent the night, and wagged his tail as he followed her to the kitchen. Fussing over him as she simultaneously poured a glass of water and popped two pills, Kara scattered a few dog treats on the floor and left him to hoover them up with delight.

     

                Returning to Lena’s bedroom, Kara crossed the room with easy strides and handed her the glass. Turning to face her, Lena’s shoulders sagged as she exhaled. “Thank you,” she gravelly replied, taking the pills as well and drinking them down.

     

                She finished off the rest of the water and set it down on the bedside table before her eyes strayed to the door and the dog that bounded inside. Aristotle jumped on the bed and Lena smiled faintly as she ruffled the fur beneath his chin.

     

                “There’s still bits of glass in the carpet so maybe be a bit careful with him walking on that side of the room until it’s vacuumed up.”

     

                “I’ll do it soon.”

     

                “Not going to work today?” Kara asked, cocking her head to the side.

     

                Shrugging as her mouth thinned, Lena kept her eyes down. “No, I don’t think so.”

     

                Nodding, Kara inhaled deeply, drawing herself up as she raised her eyebrows. “Well, how about breakfast then?”

     

                “Do you even have time?”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Kara grinned, “pancakes?”

     

                Hesitating, Lena relented with a huff of laughter. “Sure.”

     

                She left Lena alone and fetched her phone from her room before heading into the kitchen. Familiar with the placement of the whisk and the measuring jug, the shelf the eggs were on and where Lena kept her flour, Kara moved around with ease as she whisked up a batter and called James.

     

                “Hey, James, it’s me,” Kara said, keeping her voice low as she cupped the phone close to her ear. 

     

                “Morning,” he warily replied.

     

                “Listen, I know- I know it’s late notice but … I can’t come in today.”

     

                “Jesus, Kara. Again? I thought you were past all of this.”

     

                “I- I am, I just- something came up. It’s … an emergency.”

     

                “It’s always an emergency, isn’t it? Always some reason why you can’t be bothered to show up.”

     

                Blinking as her mouth opened and closed speechlessly, Kara flushed with indignation. “I know I haven’t been … a good employee-“

     

                “That’s an understatement. I’m your friend and I’ve been so lenient with you. I’ve been generous with all the time you’ve had off but … come on. And he was my friend too so I know how you feel-“

     

                “No, you don’t. Don't say that you know how I feel,” Kara hotly replied.

     

                “Alright. Okay. But you can’t keep not showing up to work. It leaves us down a person and we have too many patients to-“

     

                Sighing heavily, Kara pinched the bridge of her nose, eyes squeezed shut. “I know. I’m sorry, I- Lena’s having a bad day-“

     

                “Lena? You’re missing work for her?”

     

                “I- she needs support-“

     

                “You’re not her girlfriend, Kara. She’s your friend, and you’re both going through the same thing, I get that, but that doesn’t make her your problem.”

     

                “Seriously? Is that your view on friendships? God , that’s a shitty thing to say,” Kara snapped. “You and Alex, you’re both so …”

     

                “I’m speaking to you as your boss, not as a friend,” James gently replied. “And as your boss … you’re rostered on and if you miss another shift … I’m going to have to find a replacement. You can’t keep jilting me and expect me to be fine about it. I run a business, not a charity.”

     

                Teeth clenched as anger made her face feel hot, Kara’s stomach knotted as she rubbed her forehead, considering her options. She could’ve been meek and apologetic, put on her scrubs and went to work, but Kara was mad and she was proud and she wouldn’t admit to being wrong when she wasn’t. How was it wrong for her to look out for her friend? Why did everyone else think it was so wrong for her to have a shred of empathy for someone going through the same thing as her? 

     

                They all expected grief to have an expiration date and Kara suspected it bothered them to see her and Lena still caught up in it. The only one who had any patience and understanding was Kelly, who’d lost her own fiancée. It was different to lose a parent, which most of her friends had, so she felt almost alone in the sea of grief, even as she found herself doing so much better. She didn’t even bother defending herself though, didn’t bother rationalising how well she’d adjusted to life without Mike. If James wanted to criticise her, Kara didn’t care enough to explain herself.

     

                “Do what you have to do,” Kara brusquely replied. “I can’t come in today. I have to go.”

     

                “Kara-“

     

                She hung up and tossed her phone onto the counter with a clatter. Shaking her head as her anger simmered, she ladled batter into the frying pan and tried not to worry too much about the status of her job. Guilt nettled at her for another absence but she cared about Lena and if James was going to be mad at her, it would be worth it. She’d go in tomorrow and smooth things over and it would all be okay. Kara made a mental note to make sure she didn’t have any more days off for the next month, pre-scheduled or not.

     

                Making a neat stack of golden pancakes, Kara chopped the container of strawberries and a ripe banana and found the maple syrup. She heard the vacuum running while she cooked and then Lena emerged a few minutes later, filling up Aristotle’s bowls after setting the coffee machine on, and she cast Kara a wary look as the next pancake was scooped out of the pan.

     

                “Don’t you have work?” Lena listlessly asked, her eyes tired, dark circles beneath them and her cheeks pallid.

     

                “Uh, no, no, I just called James. It’s fine.”

     

                Kara gave her a fleeting smile, nudging the plate towards Lena. Toying with the edge of the plate, Lena’s expression turned brooding as her brow furrowed together. “You called out again?”

     

                “Don’t worry about it. I’m tired, anyway. I would’ve been no good in surgery.”

     

                “You didn’t sleep well?”

     

                Turning off the gas, Kara shrugged and started assembling her own stack with the fresh fruit and syrup. “I had a lot on my mind.”

     

                “Care to share?”

     

                Shaking her head as she fought back a secret smile, Kara wrinkled her nose. “I’ll spare you the boredom. How’d you sleep?”

     

                Opening her mouth, Lena shut it again and frowned. Mouth thinning, she picked up her plate and carried it to the table before coming back for cutlery and her coffee. Kara patiently awaited a response as she took her own coffee and thanked her and joined her at the table, sitting across from her.

     

                “I … I don’t know, it sounds … stupid; I always sleep better when you’re next to me. I wake up later, feel more … rested.”

     

                “That’s not stupid at all.”

     

                “Isn’t it? That a thirty-three-year-old woman can’t sleep alone?”

     

                “No, it’s not. You’re not used to it-”

     

                “It’s two years this year. For both of us. I should be used to it. You’re used to it.”

     

                Humming as she cut into her stack, Kara narrowed her eyes as she chewed her mouthful. “I mean … we had our sides of the bed so … I never really missed feeling him beside me all that much. It was just quiet without his snoring.”

     

                Lena laughed, taking a bite of her own pancakes. “We used to be like sardines, pressed right up against each other.”

     

                “I gathered,” Kara said with a quiet laugh. “At least I was nice and warm.”

     

                “Sorry,” Lena sheepishly apologised. “I didn’t mean to fall asleep.”

     

                “It’s okay, you were tired. You were upset.”

     

                “And drunk.”

     

                “That too.”

     

                Flexing the fingers of her left hand as the stitches pulled, Lena’s cheeks dimpled with regret. “Sorry for this as well. I should’ve just gone to a hospital-”

     

                “Don’t sweat it. I spend so many hours a week suturing, it’s like second nature. Just try not to get them wet or tear them and it should heal up nicely. I’ll take them out for you in the next week or two.”

     

                “Yes, Doctor Danvers.”

     

                Giving her a withering look, Kara fought back a smile. “Nice of you to show my title the respect it deserves.”

     

                Leaning back, Lena took a sip of her coffee. “So … what’s the plan for today?”

     

                “Whatever you’d like to do.”

     

                “I’d like to go back to bed for a few hours and then not have to think about anything else for the rest of the day.”

     

                “We can do that. How about a marathon of Love Island to numb our brains?”

     

                “Perfect,” Lena agreed.

     

                They did just that for the rest of the day, Lena holed up in her bedroom for the rest of the morning with her blackout curtains drawn across while Kara showered and then methodically cleaned her way through each room, bleaching the bathroom at the end of the hallway, mopping the floors, doing the laundry and folding the clean clothes into piles for her and Lena. It was comforting work, productive and peaceful and when she was finished she made two grilled cheese sandwiches and cups of tea and knocked on Lena’s door.

     

                Already awake, scrolling through her phone, Lena beckoned Kara inside with the explanation that she didn’t want to move from her bed. Crossing over to set a plate on Lena’s lap and her own down beside her, Kara went to fetch the tea and nudged the door shut with her foot before setting the cups down and crawling beneath the covers beside her. 

     

                They stayed in Lena’s bed for the rest of the afternoon, watching episodes of Love Island as the sun tracked its way across the city. For dinner, Lena ordered them pizza and they took up residence on the sofa with red wine as they continued their marathon. 

     

                After they finished eating and the first bottle was empty, Lena opened another one and Kara hesitated before indulging in a third glass. They made their way back into Lena’s bedroom and made themselves comfortable in bed as they continued their marathon, sharing a pint of ice cream back and forth as they kept up a running commentary on the messiness of the on-screen relationships while their own were no better.

     

                Kara fell asleep first that night, the wine making her drowsy and the pile of pillows and warm quilt too comfortable for her to fight off the heavy feeling in her eyes. She wasn’t even consciously aware that she was falling asleep but one moment she was making a prediction for the next episode as Lena vehemently disagreed with her characterisation and the next she was lights out. 

     

                In the dim light of the TV, Lena studied Kara’s peaceful face beside her as she sat up against the pillows with another glass of wine in her hand. It felt odd to be in the bed she shared with Andrea with another woman sleeping in it, a woman Lena was terrified to admit she was starting to love, but she couldn’t bear the thought of moving her. Instead, Lena drank alone until she’d finished the wine and stopped paying attention to the TV, her mind solely focused on the warmth of Kara beside her.

     

                She fell asleep shortly afterwards and woke to find her arm thrown across Kara’s waist as she spooned her, both of them shifting into the position during the night. Kara woke a short while later to an empty bed and a quiet apartment. Lena was already gone by the time she ventured out to the kitchen, signs of coffee and cigarettes for breakfast lingering behind.

     

                Getting ready for work, Kara grabbed her backpack and the car keys for the Audi from her room and rode the elevator down to the underground parking lot after saying goodbye to Aristotle. The Audi had looked brand new beneath the cover, and after a quick service, it had been a dream to drive, Kara getting a thrill out of driving such an expensive car. She’d taken to parking it down the block from work though, so she wouldn’t have to answer any questions about it. It was already getting unbearable to explain the thing between her and Lena to everyone with their judgemental looks and pointed silence.

     

                Driving through the city as she listened to the radio and idled in traffic, Kara parked at her usual spot and fed quarters into the machine before walking the rest of the way to work. The bell above the door chimed as she made her way inside, twenty minutes early with a sheepish look on her face as she meekly hunched her shoulders and crept through to the kitchen.

     

                James was making his morning coffee and straightened at the sight of her, grim and on the offensive, which Kara quickly found out. Hovering in the doorway, the muffled yapping of the dogs and mewling of the cats housed in the cages while they were treated filling the stretching silence, Kara swallowed the lump in her throat.

     

                “I’m sorry,” she started.

     

                “Your things are in that box,” James said, nodding to it sitting on the table.

     

                Glancing at it, Kara blinked as surprise washed over her, quickly followed by disbelief. Eyes cutting back to James, realisation making her face go slack-jawed, Kara made a small sound at the back of her throat.

     

                “You’re seriously firing me?”

     

                “I told you,” James firmly replied, not unkindly but weary, tried too many times by her antics. “If I can’t rely on you, I can’t keep you on.”

     

                “I- look, I know you’re mad … if you can just give me one last chance-“

     

                “Yesterday was your last chance.”

     

                “But I-“ she breathlessly replied, confusion crossing her face. “I really need this job, James. Things have been really tough with- with the apartment and the debt, I- there’s still a lot I have to pay off and I can’t afford to not pay it.”

     

                “I’m sure Lena can help you out.”

     

                Flushing as she stiffened, Kara adjusted her glasses, feeling embarrassed and stunned by the consequences of her own actions. She’d thought she could get by on the fact that James was her friend, had mentored her through her practical at college, and was about to become family in a few short weeks when their sisters tied the knot. Kara knew she’d taken full advantage of all of that and her entitlement was catching up to her now, a little too late. She had nothing else to say to defend herself.

     

                “I’m sorry, Kara,” James gently continued, guilt creeping into his face as he set his tea down. “Look, I’ll still give you a good reference but … you’re going to need to show up wherever you end up. They’re not going to give you any free passes.”

     

                Nodding, her throat was too tight for her to reply and her eyes were stinging fiercely. Her job had been one of the constants in her life, a position she’d held for years at that exact clinic with her little office and the same patients. Even when Mike had passed and she hadn’t been able to get out of bed most days, she knew she’d always have her job to go back to when she was ready. Now it was gone, just like that.

     

                “Here’s your last paycheck,” James said as he crossed over to the table and pulled it out of the box of Kara’s things.

     

                “Thank you,” she hoarsely replied, her voice uneven, making her wince.

     

                “Do you need me to give you a ride home with it all?”

     

                Letting out a choked laugh, she blinked rapidly, a humourless smile crookedly crossing her lips. “No, uh, no, I have a car. Lena’s wife’s old one. She’s kind so … well, at least I have that.”

     

                “Come on,” James sighed, a plea to his words as he gave her a pitying look. “It’s been a long time coming. You barely show up, for a long time you weren’t yourself. You don’t want to be here; I’m just making the hard call for you.”

     

                “It was her wife’s birthday yesterday,” Kara hotly replied, getting worked up now as she dragged her box from the table. “Just for the record, you asshole. How about you ask your sister how hard that is and think about how grateful you are that you’ll never know what that’s like.”

     

                “I know-“

     

                “Don’t. Just stop. I’m fired, I get it. Let’s leave it at that; I don’t need the lecture.”

     

                Cheeks red, Kara turned on her heel and ducked her head, hastily heading out the door. She bumped into William in the hallway and felt her mood grow even darker with the regret of sleeping with him all those months ago, pushing past him as she ignored his questions and spilling out into the city.

     

                Her anger diminished slightly on the walk back to the car and she ended up sitting behind the wheel for twenty minutes as she sobbed into her hands, grateful for the tinted windows. Every time she thought something was going right, something else backfired, as if the universe was trying to stop her from progressing too far from the pit of grief she’d been thrust into almost two years ago. 

     

                Eventually, she calmed down enough to start the engine, buckling herself in and wiping her cheeks before she pulled out into traffic. Driving back home, she carried her box upstairs and then clipped Aristotle’s leash to his collar and took him for a long walk, until he was too tired to continue and Kara had to carry him a mile home. 

     

                Wallowing in self-pity for the remainder of the morning, she ended up updating her resume on her phone and browsing a few job options, submitting her resume for two that seemed promising and then giving up, slumped with exhaustion. Her crying jag had left her tired and she couldn’t muster the motivation for anything but curling up on the sofa and watching Dance Moms for eight hours, until Lena showed up just before nine o’clock, looking equally as tired and in need of a drink.

     

                “Hey,” Lena murmured as Kara scrambled up, head poking over the back of the sofa as she watched her friend pick up her heels and set her keys in the small dish on a console unit.

     

                “Hey, good day?”

     

                Shrugging, Lena raked a hand through her windswept hair. “It was okay. Yours?”

     

                Choking on a laugh, Kara gave her a trembling smile. “Absolutely awful. Do you want to drink?”

     

                Surprise flashed across Lena’s face and she dropped her shoes and walked over to the liquor cabinet, two tumblers clinking as she slid them closet and splashed top shelf tequila into both. Turning around, she handed one to Kara and clinked their glasses together before sinking down onto the coffee table with a searching look on her face.

     

                “What happened?”

     

                Knocking back her glass, Kara winced and set her glass down heavily. “I got fired.”

     

                “You what?”

     

                Humming in agreement, Kara hesitated and reached out for Lena’s glass, knocking that one back too and then leaning forward to kiss her. She silenced any further explanations before Lena could start blaming herself, which Kara knew she would if she said it was because of one too many missed days, and instead, she fed into their worst impulses. 

     

                She knew that she wouldn’t have to convince Lena to drink with her, to sleep with her, and it was almost a relief to know that even with everything else going to shit, dangerously slipping back into that hole she’d tried her best to climb out of, Lena was already there to keep her company. Lena had never gotten out of that hole to start with.

    Chapter 17

                The next day, Kara woke late morning with the sluggish heaviness of a hangover, already undoing months of hard work as she slept away half of the day and eventually rose to make herself coffee and something greasy to take the edge off. She shouldn’t have had so much to drink but it had been freeing in a way, knowing she didn’t have to be up for work, knowing Lena would never tell her she’d had enough. 

     

                Ferreting out painkillers for her pounding headache, she felt feverishly clammy as she sat on the kitchen counters and ate her bacon sandwich, handing slivers of the meat down to the dog. Lena was long gone and Kara felt a strange pang of loneliness to be left at home without the distraction of work. It was different when it was her choice to skip and it didn’t feel so great to have taken advantage of her friend’s generosity now, knowing that she couldn’t really be mad at James for how she’d messed her around and pushed his patience to the limit. Things just felt frustrating as Kara seemed intent on holding herself back, even as she made progress in other areas.

     

                Going back to bed, Kara slept until after noon and was woken to the sound of her phone vibrating beside her on the quilt. Glancing at Alex’s name, she let out a groan and ignored the call, willing to bet her meagre savings scraped together since she’d moved in with Lena on Alex having just found out about her recent unemployment. She didn’t have to wait long for a text to come through confirming her suspicions.

     

    [Alex]: you got fired??

     

    [Alex]: answer your phone

     

    [Alex]: James is a dick

     

                The last text made Kara snort with laughter and she sighed before calling her sister back. It took a few rings before Alex answered and Kara could hear the muffled sounds of the hospital in the background.

     

                “Hey. What the fuck?”

     

                “Ah, well, it probably should’ve happened a lot sooner,” Kara wearily confessed.

     

                “Yeah, probably. Still, that’s rough. From your own mentor no less. You okay?”

     

                “I’ll be alright. You know me; I’ve already hit rock bottom so … nowhere else to go, right?”

     

                “You’re not at rock bottom. You got yourself out of that and you’ll find something new.”

     

                “Maybe.”

     

                “Definitely. Look, do you want me to come over after work? I’m off at six; I can bring Chinese food.”

     

                Kara closed her eyes and swallowed past the tightness in her throat. “I- thanks but I’m okay.”

     

                “What, are you not allowed people over? House rules?”

     

                “Funny,” Kara curtly replied. “Actually, I have Group tonight. It’s Thursday.”

     

                “Oh, right. But you’re okay?”

     

                “I mean … it sucks but … not much I can do, right? I … I just- I don’t know.”

     

                “What?”

     

                “I don’t know,” Kara repeated, a lump in her throat as her eyes stung. She blinked quickly, her face scowling and colouring with frustration. “Things were supposed to be getting better but they’re not. At least before I just had a dead husband and dead parents. Now I’ve got all of that and no apartment or job.”

     

                “Those last two are temporary. You’re smart, you’re strong, and … well, I mean, I know that I had a lot to say but … living with Lena puts you in a good position to not have to stress too much about it all right now.”

     

                Sighing, Kara sank back against the pillows as a v formed between her eyebrows. “She’s not my girlfriend. She’s not here for me to rely on because I can’t get my shit together.”

     

                “And yet she offered up her spare room with no expiration date. She cares about you.”

     

                “I know,” Kara softly agreed, “that doesn’t mean I should take advantage of that. I know- I know I’ve maybe taken everyone else for granted a bit too much and … I’m trying not to repeat that.”

     

                “It’s alright,” her sister quietly reassured her. “We’re all here for you, even James. You just let us know what you need.”

     

                “Yeah, thanks. You should go.”

     

                “Mm, I’ll see you on Saturday, though?”

     

                Choking on a laugh, Kara’s face rippled with sheepish guilt. “Of course! It’s your bachelorette party; you know I wouldn’t miss it for the world.”

     

                “Just checking.”

     

                “I’d be a shitty Maid of Honour if I didn’t show up. And I’ve worked hard on my plans; it’ll be great.”

     

                “I can’t wait.”

     

                “I’ll talk to you tomorrow. Run through everything so you’re not worried.”

     

                “Okay. I love you. Try not to be too down on yourself.”

     

                “I love you too.”

     

                Hanging up, she felt slightly better and a little relieved after getting off the phone with her sister, but underneath it all was that palpable worry that Kara couldn’t shake. She hadn’t felt so off-balance since the early days of being a widow and she knew she wouldn’t be given nearly half of the grace having a dead husband got her, especially not when her accumulated work absences were a by-product of that and it hadn’t meant much to James. 

     

                Laying in bed until it was time to get ready for Group, Kara showered and pulled on jeans and a thin sweater before grabbing her phone and a jacket and leaving. She caught the bus to Group this week, intent on coming home with Lena after so many weeks of driving herself home in the Audi. Kara had to admit that she missed their drives home together, laughing at the unhelpful advice they’d been given and finding a kindred thing in the ability to laugh amidst their grief. They still kept going, even though it was less of an excuse to see each other more often now and just a bad habit they couldn’t shake. 

     

                The bus spat her out down the block and she walked through the mild spring weather, staring up at the cloudy lavender sky and hoping the weather stayed nice, or was at least nice on the day of the wedding. Alex and Kelly had waited long enough for their day, and while it was so close now, it almost didn’t feel real. Kara had always been so excited for her sister, both times she’d gotten engaged, and could remember that ecstatic relief when Alex had moved on with Kelly and put a ring on her finger, but now she felt so detached from her life. Of course, she was excited, but Kara was muddling through her own feelings and sometimes it felt like she wasn’t experiencing them in her own body and it made it difficult to be present in the lives of her family and friends. She’d spent a good chunk of time missing out on so much - the wedding planning, Nia and Querl’s on-and-off-again bouts or Winn’s new girlfriend - and she felt guilty about it, she really did, but she also felt too tired to care sometimes.

     

                Wearily climbing the steps to the Y, she followed the familiar path to the room, which she was intimately familiar with at this point, and made two cups of tea and collected the donuts. Lena arrived fifteen minutes later, just before they were about to start, looking harried as she took her seat and let out a heavy sigh.

     

                “Hey.”

     

                “Hey,” Kara murmured. “I got here early; got us the good donuts.”

     

                “Great,” Lena replied with a thin smile, taking a distracted bite as her eyes roamed around the room. Blinking, she turned to Kara. “Good day?”

     

                Wrinkling her nose, Kara hummed dubiously. “If a hangover and laying in bed can be constituted as good. You?”

     

                “Oh, um, busy.”

     

                They started after that, cutting off any further conversation as the quiet buzz of chatter fell to silence and Thomas introduced himself and called on a new face to introduce themselves. Sitting silently as she waited for her turn, Kara sipped her tea and ate her donut, listening to the repetitive sentiments and troubles, none of it unfamiliar to her now. She’d heard it all a thousand times from two dozen people since she’d started coming. 

     

                Eventually, it was Kara’s turn and she couldn’t bring herself to admit she’d been fired from her job to a room full of relative strangers. Instead, she gave a halting explanation of her feelings over the last week, frustration boiling over, that sense of helpless confusion, so lost in her own life. Of course, it all came back to Mike, to that feeling of being untethered from her past and now so far from the person she’d been then that Kara sometimes found it hard to recognise herself. Or perhaps she’d always been that person, a little rash, a little selfish, proud and stubborn, and didn’t want to recognise that.

     

                “As more time passes … I don’t know, I feel so disconnected from the person I was with him, with who I was when I lost him. Um … I don’t know if that’s a good thing or a bad thing. I sometimes feel like I’ve become unlikable.”

     

                Kara anxiously chewed on her bottom lip as she haltingly confessed her feelings, rubbing her fingertips over her mouth as she stared at the worn carpet in the middle of the circle of chairs. 

     

                “Anyway, it’s not all bad. I, um, I don’t feel so sad all the time anymore. Maybe that’s why my friends think I should be gentle again, instead of frustrated like I am.”

     

                “Why are you frustrated?” Thomas asked, his elbow on his thigh and his chin in his hand.

     

                Shrugging, Kara searched for the words to describe the sensation of feeling confused and lost in her life. “I guess … I guess my life isn’t shaping up to be what I thought it was. I should be settled, I should be following the plan we’d come up with, the goals we made together. Instead, it’s so different from how I imagined and … I’ve been doing a lot better with a lot of things - especially things with him - but other things … it’s not working out well.”

     

                “And why is that frustrating for you?”

     

                “Because … because I feel like … I have to start from scratch. With everything. I was ahead and now … I’m not. I’m behind . We had plans for kids someday and now I’m aware I’m running out of time and we had plans for a house in the suburbs and I can’t do that by myself. If I still want all of that - and maybe I don’t - that means I need to start from scratch and it’s just- it’s difficult to do that. And if I don’t want that … that feels worse because I don’t have any other plans.”

     

                “Have you thought about a plan?”

     

                “Nothing comes to mind,” Kara said, her lips twitching with irritated amusement.

     

                “I’d like you to think about it for the next week and share it with us all at the next session.” He waited until Kara nodded and provided no further response before raising his eyebrows. “Lena?”

     

                Lena was silent for a long minute, a troubled look on her face as she gathered her thoughts, running her hands idly over the thighs of her pants. She wouldn’t look up, Lena rarely ever spoke directly to Thomas in this room, wrapped up in her own feelings of overwhelming sadness and frustration and embarrassment to even be there.

     

                “I … find it hard when it’s special occasions. It really hits me that I’ve lost her when it’s … a birthday, a holiday, an anniversary. It was her birthday recently, and it was Valentine’s Day too, of course. We were busy with our careers but we always made an effort to show up for the important things, and the little ones too when we could, and I just … I miss her more on those days. Lately, I’ve been trying to find comfort elsewhere but …”

     

                Her eyes flickered sideways to Kara for the briefest moment before she cleared her throat and straightened up, leaning back in her chair. “It’s not the same. It’ll never be the same again, and that doesn’t … it doesn’t mean it’s bad , I just- I miss what I had. I’m forced to remember every day, and it’s only getting worse. That’s the hardest part for me; I can’t move on, I can’t let go, I can’t forget. Most people think about loss in a past tense but for me … it’s present.”

     

                Thomas asked a few more cautious questions, always sensitive of Lena’s brittle patience for the charade of counselling, and after she’d spoken as much as she wanted to, he moved on to the next person. Sitting beside her, Kara felt like the tension between them was almost palpable, the air charged whenever they spoke about each other in vague terms while knowing they were side by side. It didn’t dissipate as they finished up and helped stack the chairs before leaving, Kara letting Lena know she’d caught the bus as they walked towards the Lexus.

     

                “Want to go for a drink?” Kara asked as she settled into the passenger seat.

     

                Slowly buckling herself in, Lena took a moment to respond, an odd tension on her face. “No, I think I just want to go home.”

     

                “Oh. Okay.”

     

                Nodding, Lena started the engine and they drove home in silence, the radio filling it with the chatter of the hourly news update and a series of commercials. In the parking lot, Lena slid in beside the Audi and Kara gathered up her backpack and opened her door. Riding the elevator upstairs, she was almost jittery, keyed up about something, about everything .

     

                After depositing her bag in her room and changing, she reemerged and waited until Lena came out in her pyjamas, both of them too comfortable around each other now to stay dressed in the day’s clothes as they whittled away the night on the sofa. Ordering Big Belly Burger for them, Lena was quiet and thoughtful as they waited for their food to arrive, and it was only after they’d finished eating their burgers and fries that she seemed to blink herself out of her thoughts.

     

                Once she’d finished, Kara asked if she could pour herself a drink and Lena gestured towards the liquor cabinet as she watched her closely. Perusing the bottles that always seemed to be full, no matter how many empty ones Lena dumped in the recycling each week, Kara grabbed a bottle at random.

     

                As Kara poured from a bottle of vodka, Lena walked up behind her and cradled her waist in her hands, her chin digging into Kara’s shoulder. Swallowing thickly, setting the bottle down, Kara screwed the lid back on as Lena softly sighed.

     

                “You’re not unlikable,” she murmured.

     

                “No?” Kara hoarsely asked, “sometimes it feels that way. Even my own friends are sick of me.”

     

                “They’re not sick of you. And more importantly, I’m not sick of you.”

     

                “Good to know,” Kara murmured, raising her glass of straight vodka to her lips.

     

                She drank a sip and screwed her face up, mouth turning down at the corners as it burnt its way down her throat. Quietly laughing, Lena took the glass from her and drained it all in seconds with barely a grimace. 

     

                “Don’t do this to yourself,” Lena softly chastised her, but there was a plea in her voice as well, a pained look in her clouded eyes.

     

                “Do what?”

     

                “I won’t let you lower yourself down to my level.”

     

                Turning beneath her grasp, Kara cocked her head to the side. “What’s that supposed to mean?”

     

                “I won’t let you start drinking heavily just because I do. I won’t let you sit at home all day when you have a degree and love what you do, all because your friend was an asshole because you skipped work for me. I won’t let you ruin your life because of me.”

     

                Reaching up, Kara cupped Lena’s cheek in her hand and let out a huff of laughter, a crooked smile on her lips as she gave her a long, searching look. Dropping her hand, Kara cast her eyes downwards to the buttons of Lena’s shirt and swallowed thickly.

     

                “What was it you said? You’re not my girlfriend? That’s true for me as well, you know.”

     

                Leaning in close, Lena’s stare was brittle. “Tough.”

     

                “Tough?” Kara said with a surprised laugh. “Hypocrite.”

     

                “No, I’m not a hypocrite, I’m just far more stubborn than you and I always get what I want.”

     

                “And what do you want?”

     

                “What do I want?” Lena murmured, her brow creasing as she considered the question. “I want to help you. I want … good things for you. For you to get a good job - one that pays better - and for you to be happy. I want you to not ruin your life by drinking every day to cope. I want you to move on with your life and not feel so sad all the time. I want you to be my housemate for a long, long time because I’m very selfish. I want you to be healthy and confident, to not be consumed by your regrets. I want you to be able to look back on your life and be comforted by your memories instead of devastated by them. I just … I want you to thrive. Don’t follow me down into misery. Please.”

     

                Kara opened and closed her mouth, completely blindsided by the tenderly murmured rant that fell from Lena’s lips. She wanted to kiss her, not as a precursor to sex but to just kiss Lena gently and let her feelings rise to the surface for a brief moment. As it was, Kara started crying instead.

     

                She didn’t mean to, only Lena’s words, her gentleness, her kindness, were suddenly too much. Her eyes were stinging and then they were filling with tears and before Kara could stop them they were rolling down her cheeks and she was letting out a ragged gasp. Covering her mouth with a hand, she hung her head, embarrassment washing over her as she hunched her shoulders.

     

                “It’s okay,” Lena murmured, quickly pulling her into her embrace.

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara thickly managed to get out. “It’s just so hard sometimes.”

     

                “I know, I know.”

     

                Lena’s voice was uneven too but she held Kara close, her embrace tight and comforting, and Kara’s shoulders went slack beneath her touch. The vodka was acrid on her tongue and she felt exhausted, so much sadness in her chest that she led to worry at the root. Kara had never been good with dealing with helplessness, always feeling the need to be strong and positive, to push aside her troubles so that she could be there for everyone else. It was times like this that she felt at her worst though, unable to keep up that farce of happiness.

     

                After a moment, she pulled back and wiped her cheeks, blowing the air out of her lungs and sniffing. “Sorry.”

     

                “Don’t apologise. Was it- was it something I said?”

     

                “All of it,” Kara weakly laughed, a rueful smile on her face as she brushed past Lena and sank onto the sofa.

     

                Giving her a searching look, Lena hung back for a second before taking a seat beside her, less than a foot between them. It should’ve felt uncomfortable to sit so close, the rest of the sofa empty, but Kara only felt familiar comfort in Lena’s presence.
