It troubled her more than she cared to admit, unnecessary stress that was added to her situation with the knowledge that she could never voice. It would result in an awkward situation they wouldn’t be able to overcome, and Kara didn’t have anywhere else to live to even risk considering it.

     

                “I’m sorry if I-”

     

                Patting her knee, Kara smiled wanly, “You didn’t. I just … I don’t think I deserve your kindness.”

     

                “Of course you do.”

     

                They sat there for ten minutes until Kara’s breaths evened out and she felt a prickling heat creeping into her cheeks for how quickly she’d broken down over nothing. Abruptly lurching to her feet, she wiped her face on her sleeve.

     

                “I might go to bed.”

                

                “Alright.”

     

                Lena let her go and Kara was angry at herself as she dragged off her jeans and shift and swapped them for sweatpants and an old college t-shirt, yanking back the heavy covers and curling up beneath the quilt. 

     

                Laying in the dark, she listened to the quiet sounds of Lena moving about in the kitchen, and after a few minutes, there was a knock on her door. At Kara’s mumbled invitation, Lena managed to turn the door handle with her elbow and nudge it open with her foot, silhouetted in the doorway with two cups of tea in hand.

     

                Padding inside, she set the cups down and waited until Aristotle trotted inside before closing the door. Then she climbed onto the bed with the dog and sighed, resting her head on the pillow beside Kara’s and giving her a searching look in the dark.

     

                “I’m fine,” Kara insisted through clenched teeth as her eyes smarted.

     

                “I know you’re going to be fine but that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t have some company. Unless you’d like me to go, which means you just have to tell me to fuck off and I’ll leave you alone for the rest of the night. But I should tell you, I’ve ordered shawarma for dinner and it’ll be here in twenty minutes. In case you’re hungry.”

     

                Sighing, Kara rolled over to face her. “You know the way to a woman’s heart.”

     

                “Mm, so I’m told,” Lena wryly replied.

     

                Rolling the other way, Kara switched on the lamp and then rolled back onto her back, feeling Lena’s eyes on her as she stared up at the ceiling, chewing on her bottom lip. Reaching out, Lena pressed a finger to Kara’s lip to stop her and Kara’s lips parted as she heaved another sigh.

     

                “Tell me what you’re thinking?”

     

                Shaking her head, Kara swallowed thickly. “Nothing. I’m just caught up in it all.”

     

                “Alright, well put it aside for the rest of tonight. We’ll sort it out tomorrow.”

     

                “This is my mess.”

     

                “And you’re my friend. Don’t be stubborn or I’ll be ten times worse.”

     

                Then Kara was laughing, her shoulders shaking with the effort as some of the knotted worry in her chest loosened. A smile crossed her face and her eyes crinkled at the corners, even as she closed them.

     

                “You’re a menace.”

     

                “I can be so much worse,” Lena gravely promised.

     

                “I’d still like you, even if you were.”

                

                “I’d still like you too, I just don’t want you to be worse. Be better, for both of our sakes. If these are the cards we’ve been dealt, one of us should hold a winning hand and I’ll try and make sure it’s you.”

     

                “Why not you?”

     

                Lena hummed thoughtfully, closing her eyes as she pillowed her head beneath her arm. “I’m stuck with my lot for the foreseeable future. You don’t have to be.”

     

                “All those things you said out there … I want it all for you too, you know. You don’t have to be stuck either.”

     

                “I know, but I am. I’ve committed myself to it and I’m okay with that. I made my peace with it long before we even met.”

     

                Inhaling deeply, her heart pounding as she tried to pluck up the courage to ask a dangerous question, Kara’s voice was low and trembling. “Do you think we-”

     

                The sound of the front door’s intercom buzzing loudly through the apartment interrupted her and Lena rose from her pillow, facing the door. Kara stayed in bed and listened to the silence of the apartment as Lena buzzed the delivery person up and returned five minutes later with a bursting bag of food. She knelt on the edge of the bed and removed the boxes and waxed paper-wrapped pitas in a variety of lamb and falafel before going to fetch them a seltzer each. Without invitation, Lena was back in Kara’s bed, turning on the TV as she asked what she wanted to watch. The message was clear; she wasn’t leaving Kara alone.

     

                They ate in bed as they watched the latest episode of Succession, which Kara had only seen the first half of season one of but picked it because she knew Lena enjoyed it, and Kara drank her tea and her seltzer and ate until she was so full that she felt tired. By the time the episode was finished, she was ready for bed and Lena tidied away the leftovers and the trash and ushered Aristotle out of the room. With a quiet goodnight, she left Kara to her thoughts until sleep claimed her and Kara didn’t know how to ask her to stay.

     

                She was woken up at seven o’clock the next morning, groggy and confused as she looked around for her alarm until she realised it was a knock on the door. Fumbling for her glasses, she pushed them on and mumbled in response until the door cracked open and Lena gave her an expectant look.

     

                “Come on, up. We have work to do.”

     

                “What’re you talking about?” Kara yawned, sitting up now, stretching her arms out as her face furrowed with confusion.

     

                “Breakfast is cooking. Coffee’s on the table. Quick.”

     

                Lena offered no other explanation and Kara sighed, throwing back the blankets and climbing to her feet. By the time she’d shuffled out to the kitchen after making her bed, Lena was scooping poached eggs out of a simmering pot and carefully nestling them on top of avocado toast.

     

                “What’s going on?” Kara asked.

     

                “I’m helping,” Lena proclaimed with a quick smile.

     

                “By waking me up at the crack of dawn?”

     

                “Seven o’clock is not the crack of dawn; you’re lucky I didn’t wake you up at six for a jog.”

     

                “If you ever do that, I’ll just assume that you hate me,” Kara grumbled.

     

                A plate was thrust into her hands a moment later and Kara stood there as she frowned at Lena’s casual appearance - no makeup, her hair messily clipped up and the loungewear she liked to wear around the place on the weekend. 

     

                “Shouldn’t you be ready for work already?”

     

                “I’m not going in today.”

     

                “You can’t just-”

     

                “No one’s going to fire me for not showing up to my own business. I’ll work from my office later, I just wanted to help sort things out for you first.”

     

                “Lena-”

     

                “Sit. Eat your eggs. Drink your coffee. And listen.”

     

                A scoff of laughter escaped Kara as she fell silent, surprised by the bossiness but not entirely. Lena wasn’t shy about speaking her mind when she felt like it and Kara knew that it would be easier to cooperate - for now - than to argue. Her curiosity got the better of her as well and she was interested in what Lena’s plan was. Giving her the benefit of the doubt on account of her assistance with Kara sorting out her debt and selling her apartment, Kara obediently sat down and picked up her cutlery.

     

                “First things first, a job,” Lena started as she took her own seat, immediately cutting into her softly poached eggs.

     

                “Well connected within the veterinarian community, are you?”

     

                “I did have a vet before you poached me. One that caters to upper-class lap dogs, of course.”

     

                “Of course.”

     

                “I can make some calls if you’re okay with that.”

     

                “You don’t have-”

     

                “I know, but I’d like to. I don’t have anyone to take care of anymore so it’s a fulfilling thing for me. I promise you I’m driven by purely selfish motivations here,” Lena grinned.

     

                Pursing her lips, Kara considered the offer for a moment and knew this was a time to swallow her pride. “That would be great, thank you.”

     

                “Secondly-”

     

                “How long is this list? Or are you tired of me monopolising your spare room and screening a bunch of potential roommates for me?”

     

                “I’m too jealous to share you with another roommate,” Lena blithely replied before forging onwards. “Your sister is getting married in a little over two weeks. That means you can’t stress her out. Not even unintentionally.”

     

                “Well, she knows I got fired. No secrets between my friends.”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Lena shrugged. “That’s fine, it is what it is, but from now on no stress. You’re Maid of Honor and you need to make sure you can handle her stress for her. It’s shit timing and I would put the fear of God in James if I could get my hands on him for choosing now to potentially fuck up his sister’s wedding, but anyway … no drinking.”

     

                “No drinking?” Kara laughed. “Now you’re really being hypocritical.”

     

                “You’re not getting yourself in a state when you have a lot to help organise. I , on the other hand, have no responsibilities, so I can drink as much as I want. No heavy drinking. No sloppiness allowed. Have you written a speech yet?”

     

                “I’ve started.”

     

                “Give me what you have and I’ll fill in the rest.”

     

                “Lena-”

     

                “Kara, shut up . You are going to let me help you even if you curse me the whole time, even if you hate me. You don’t even have to be grateful , okay? I just- I have very few people in my life and I will not let you fuck up your own life by giving up. You said you used to have ambition so find it . ”

     

                Swallowing thickly, ducking her head as she cut a small bite from her plate, Kara chewed thoughtfully as her eyebrows drew together in a brooding look. 

     

                They spent the next two hours with Lena rattling off a list of things Kara needed to follow up on, fetching her laptop and trying to track down the vendors Alex or Kelly had mentioned in the past and making a dozen phone calls to various people as she confirmed details and tried to put in as much effort as she could to help her sister. By the time Lena was satisfied with their progress, Kara felt like her brain was melting but there was a sense of purpose, of accomplishment and pride in fulfilling her role, if nothing else was going right for her.

     

                “What else?”

     

                “That’s pretty much it. Just … find a new job and look after yourself, okay? Leave the self-destruction up to me.”

     

                “You know, it’s really not something to joke about.”

     

                “I know, but if I don’t joke about it, it just makes me feel like shit.”

     

                Lena gave her a weak smile and shrugged. Face softening with aching tenderness, Kara set down her cutlery. “You could do it too, you know. Stop drinking, look after yourself. I could help you and you could help me.”

     

                “You already help me just by being here.”

     

                “Do I?” Kara sceptically asked. “Because … sometimes it feels like you’re getting worse and I don’t know how to reach you, don’t know how to help you. I know- I know it hurts, it’s painful and lonely and- and it’s a horrible situation but … it feels like it’s hitting you harder now than it did at the start and I just- I don’t understand why.”

     

                Lips twitching, a muscle jumped in Lena’s jaw and she kept her eyes on her plate. “No, you don’t.”

     

                “But you can talk to me.”

     

                “I know I can.”

     

                “Well … you should.”

     

                Laughter cut through the mask of pain on Lena’s face as she looked up and gave her a warm look of resignation, sighing. “Thank you, but I’m doing okay. It’s a carefully managed trainwreck, I promise. I have a lot of experience with it as well; if you knew my mom, the way I grew up, you’d understand why I am the way I am.”

     

                Nodding as she had to accept that there was a large portion of Lena’s life and history she knew nothing about, Kara finished her breakfast in silence and then sipped her coffee as she quietly considered their talk. She knew that Lena was mostly trying to mitigate any potential risks before Kara could fall off the wagon, and Kara knew she should be grateful that her friend stubbornly refused to let her fall apart, but for the most part, Kara was just tired and frustrated, wishing she was given the leniency of the early days of her grief to fall apart in peace and quiet.

     

                “I’ve also invited Alex and Kelly over for dinner,” Lena said after a few minutes.

     

                “Why?”

     

                “They’re your family and you live here. You’re not a guest , you know. This is your home so … you should have your sister over for dinner. Go over all the wedding stuff, you know? Maybe she’ll lay off a bit if you’re the one putting your foot forward.”

     

                “Mm, maybe.”

     

                “It’ll be good; I’ll cook. Is steak and salad alright? Any allergies I should be aware of?”

     

                “Nothing with blueberries. Kelly’s deathly allergic.”

                

                “Noted.”

     

                Kara cleared their plates away and Lena paced by the windows as she lit a cigarette and dialled the vet clinic she used to take Aristotle to. Tuning out the quiet conversation, Kara hand-washed the dishes and then wiped down the counters, keeping on top of the mess, unlike her half-hearted attempts at her own apartment. Her mind kept straying back to Lena calling the penthouse Kara’s home too, that she wasn’t a guest, and while Kara felt welcome, it still struck her as something that ultimately wasn’t hers. She wasn’t going to live there for the next ten years and make a life with someone there, it wasn’t like her old apartment. But there was the potential and she couldn’t deny it, even as she turned her mind away from that dangerous line of thinking.

     

                Stubbing out a cigarette as Kara carried two fresh cups of coffee over to the table, Lena said goodbye and hung up, smiling brightly as she set her phone down. “Sorted. Interview next Wednesday at one o’clock.”

     

                “What?”

     

                “At the clinic. He wants to meet with you.”

     

                “What’s his name?”

     

                “Jack Spheer. I’ve known him since I moved to the city. Nice guy. English. Handsome.”

     

                “Is this an interview or a blind date?” Kara snorted.

     

                “Well, I assumed that was your type, given William-”

     

                Scoffing, Kara rolled her eyes, giving Lena an exasperated look. “Okay. You clearly don’t know my type well.”

     

                “I’m just kidding. He’s a bit sweet on me though; I redesigned and renovated his clinic as a thank you when Aristotle had to have surgery after eating six chicken wings.”

     

                “Oh … that’s generous.”

     

                “Wednesday. One o’clock.”

     

                “Right. Thank you.”

     

                Nodding, Lena watched her for a long minute and then folded her arms over her chest, cocking her head to the side. “You alright?”

     

                Swallowing thickly, Kara nodded. “Yeah, I just- I liked my job. Not just the job but working with my friends. James used to be my mentor and offered me a job out of college, so that’s the extent of my career. And then his sister moved here and started working at the same hospital as my sister and they’re about to get married. And I have to find a new job for the first time in like a decade because my husband died and … I just have no energy anymore. I don’t have that ambition. I don’t want to go for a new interview, I just- I want my job. I want the ease of it, I don’t want to try.”

     

                Rounding the table, Lena cupped Kara’s upper arms and gave her a grim look of sympathy. “I know but if you don’t try, you’re never going to break out of this feeling of hopelessness.”

     

                “And maybe I don’t want to,” Kara hotly replied. “Why are you the only one who’s allowed to be a mess?”

     

                “Because our circumstances are different-”

     

                “Oh, bullshit. You’re just rich enough to not feel the consequences. You can take the day off and not even bat an eye at the thought of missing out on a chunk of your paycheck. This isn’t my life, Lena. I don’t have a penthouse, or drive a nice car, or a really good career with millions in the bank.” 

     

                Reaching up to cup her cheek, Lena smiled slightly. “But you could. That’s why I want to help you.”

     

                “I’m not some stray charity project.”

     

                Dropping her hand, Lena frowned, a look of irritation flickering in her eyes. “I never said you were.”

     

                Flustered as shame quickly crawled over her, Kara opened and closed her mouth, ducking her head as she adjusted her glasses on the bridge of her nose. “I know, I’m sorry, I just- I don’t want to be dependent on you. I’m not- I’m not your burden to bear.”

     

                “You’re not a burden at all,” Lena rasped, a wavering smile on her lips as her eyes shone brightly, bitter and upset. “I’m just- I’m trying to do for you what I hope someone would do for me in the same situation.”

     

                Kara choked on a laugh, a mystified look on her face. “No one would do the same. People aren’t generally that selfless.”

     

                “I’ve told you, it’s entirely selfishly motivated.”

     

                “How is it selfish?”

     

                Lena was silent for a moment, shifting restlessly as she averted her gaze, struggling with herself as she scrambled for a response. Gesturing vaguely, she smiled faintly, two shallow dimples appearing on her cheeks. 

     

                “I’d be all alone if I didn’t have you.”

     

                Amusement softened Kara’s frustration and a smile was still spreading when Lena grabbed her face in her hands and kissed her, firm but lingering and tender. As soon as Kara started kissing her back, Lena’s grip went slack and her mouth pulled back a fraction, their shared breath warm between their lips. Leaning in a fraction, as if she was going to kiss her again, Lena jerked back and ran a hand over her face as she turned.

     

                “Sorry, I, uh, I wasn’t trying to start anything.”

     

                “Oh. Okay.”

     

                “Um … I think I need to- to go for … a walk. Did you- did you want to come or …?”

     

                Stammering for a moment, caught off guard, Kara made a strained sound of agreement at the back of her throat. She hadn’t showered yet but she pulled on her long camel coat and running shoes and tugged a baseball cap down snugly on her greasy hair before she met Lena at the front door.

     

                Looking marginally more put together, Lena unlocked the door and let Aristotle lead the way. Riding the elevator down to the lobby, they stepped out onto the sidewalk and walked through the family part of the city to the park they always came to. Kara had started looking at it in a different light since Lena had mentioned it was one of her wife’s favourite places to go, and it made her feel a prickle of guilt to feel like a poor replacement for company.

     

                They walked around for almost an hour, letting Aristotle off once they reached the fenced-in dog park, throwing a stick for him and letting him socialise with the other dogs before they left. Instead of going home, they went grocery shopping for dinner, tying the dog up outside the store and stepping into the frigid air-conditioned organic store. Kara held the basket while Lena deliberated over the cuts of steak and selected the perfect tomatoes, asking Kara’s opinion on dessert before she paid and they left.

     

                Back at the apartment building, Lena let them into the foyer and they both reached for the door at the same time. Fingers brushing, Lena hesitated a moment, glancing quickly at Kara and inhaling as if she was about to speak. Quickly pulling her hand free, she let Kara open it. Kara ushered her friend inside with the dog and then followed her with the groceries.

     

                Waiting for the elevator, Kara glanced around the foyer, the security guard listening to a sports channel on a radio behind her desk, and then met Lena’s eyes. Lena was looking at her with an odd look on her face and Kara blinked, a smile softening the corners of her mouth.

     

                “What’s wrong?”

     

                “Nothing,” Lena quickly replied, although there was a touch of pink to her cheeks that made Kara frown.

     

                “Are you alright? You’re not getting sick are you?” she asked, reaching out to touch the back of her fingers to Lena’s forehead.

     

                Jerking away as she clicked her tongue with annoyance, Lena flushed a deeper pink and the elevator doors opened a moment later. They stepped inside and Kara was quiet and thoughtful as they rode up to the penthouse, sure that something had just gone awry, although she couldn’t figure out what.

     

                Inside, Kara put the groceries away and Lena shut herself in her office to do some work for the remainder of the morning and into the afternoon. To distract herself, Kara tried reading one of the self-help books Kelly had gifted her shortly after Mike had died, which she’d never gotten around to, but she found herself too busy thinking about Lena. It would’ve been easy to knock on the office door and break that awkwardly thick tension that had seemingly blossomed out of nowhere but Kara gave her space instead.

     

                After giving up on her book, Kara showered and dressed in anticipation of dinner, trying to look like she wasn’t a frustrated mess, even if she felt like it inside. She tidied up as well, vacuuming and wiping down the counters, straightening pillows and hiding Lena’s clutter in the drawers before she lit a few of the candles around the apartment and opened the windows.

     

                Lena emerged just before five o’clock and started prepping a salad while Kara nervously hovered about until Lena opened a bottle of wine to deglaze the pan for a white wine sauce and poured a small glass for Kara. Sliding it across the counter, she didn’t quite meet her eyes but Kara had the vague notion that Lena felt guilty about something and was relenting by offering alcohol, despite the earlier strict rules she’d enacted.

     

                Sipping the wine slowly, Kara leaned against the counters until there was a buzz on the intercom and she went to fetch her family. It was nerve-wracking in a strange way, to let them into Lena’s penthouse, and Kara felt flustered and a little embarrassed, knowing it wasn’t her place and knowing it wasn’t the life her family lived. When Alex knocked on the door, Kara opened it and anxiously invited the two women into the apartment.

     

                They hung their jackets and took off their shoes and Kara introduced them to Aristotle as he excitedly greeted the guests. As far as Kara was aware since moving in, Lena never had guests, and she didn’t think Lena had guests other than Kara before she’d moved in either.

     

                “Um, she’s just in the kitchen getting dinner started,” Kara explained as she led them further inside.

     

                Alex let out a low whistle as she looked around the spacious living room and the view of the bay through the wall of windows at the back. The place looked like a staged scene for a magazine with its carefully curated furniture and artwork, the tall ceilings and the herringbone floor.

     

                “Okay, yeah, I’d move in here before my place too,” Kelly mused aloud.

     

                Giving her a wry smile, Kara jerked her head to the open archway leading to the kitchen. Lena was just heading out as she approached and Kara startled slightly, pulling up short before they collided and letting out a nervous laugh as they both simultaneously reached out to instinctively stop each other, fingers brushing before dropping to their sides.

     

                “They’re here,” Kara needlessly announced.

     

                “Hi, come on in. How are you? Can I get you drinks?”

     

                They all made themselves comfortable in the kitchen, Lena pouring wine as their guests took their seats at the laid table before she returned to the stove where she got started on heating the pan for the steak. After the niceties were out of the way, the conversation flowed to work and Kara wrinkled her nose as she took another sip of wine, trying not to gulp it down as fresh embarrassment hit her. But then she straightened, a reserved smile on her lips as her eyes slid to Lena.

     

                “I actually have an interview lined up next week.”

     

                “Good for you,” Kelly said, clinking her glass against Kara’s. “I hope you get it and teach my brother a lesson about prioritising profit over friendships.”

     

                “Ah, well, I can’t hold it against him. James has been good to me, better than I deserved so … no hard feelings.”

     

                “He doesn’t get it,” Kelly continued, her face clouding with past memories, a shadow of guilt in her eyes. “We lost our dad but I’ve told him … it’s not the same.”

     

                Shrugging again, Kara really didn’t want to dwell on the conversation. Clearing her throat, she shifted and took another sip of wine.

     

                “So, excited for tomorrow?”

     

                “Yes,” Alex eagerly replied. “Tell me what you’ve planned.”

     

                “Nope.”

     

                “Come on, I’m thirty-seven, getting married for the first time ; it’s not going to be some youthful bender, full of surprises.”

     

                Smiling slightly, Kara cocked her head to the side. “It might be.”

     

                “Lena, what’s she planned?”

     

                “I‘ve made a vow of secrecy, sorry,” Lena said over her shoulder. “It’ll be great though.”

     

                “You’re still coming?” Alex slowly asked. “And as Kara’s date to the wedding?”

     

                Flustered, Kara quickly leapt in to correct her. “Not date, she’s my guest-“

     

                “Yes, didn’t she RSVP for me?” Lena answered at the same time, her tone casual and indifferent at the insinuation.

     

                “She did,” Kelly quickly assured her, “we’ve just been doing final guest list checks.”

     

                “I’m all over it, don’t even worry about it,” Kara quickly told her. “I’m Maid of Honor so … don’t stress. Everything is going to be perfect.”

     

                Doubt flickered in her sister’s eyes and Alex couldn’t stop the scepticism from creeping into her voice. “Really? I mean, I know you’ve got a lot going on. We’ve been sorting stuff out-“

     

                “I mean, if anything, I have even more time to help out but don’t worry about a thing, okay? I’ve followed up on the cake, the catering, the flowers and the venue already. Hair and makeup will get there at seven to set up. The photographer will definitely be there at seven-thirty.”

     

                “Y-you did?” Alex slowly asked.

     

                “Yep. I’ve also checked with J’onn to make sure he’s ordained, Winn’s all good to perform with me and my speech is going through a final edit. Everything’s all under control.”

                

                There was a look exchanged between the couple and Kara felt her heart rate spike slightly at her casual recital of all the work she’d done. 

     

                “What?” she asked.

     

                “Nothing,” Alex quickly replied. “We just- we thought we’d … you know, do it ourselves while you figured things out. I didn’t want you to stress over it-“

     

                “You don’t need to stress over it,” Kara interrupted with a quick smile. “Just enjoy it. It’s going to be your day and it- it just goes by so quickly so enjoy it. You had my back when I got married, so trust that I have yours.”

     

                “Of course I trust you.”

     

                “Good.”

     

                “How does everyone like their steaks?” Lena asked as the conversation reached a natural lull.

     

                The four of them were seated at the table with their plates in front of them, a playlist quietly coming through the speakers and a chilled bottle of wine, which Lena poured from as she refilled their glasses as soon as they got low. Conversation flowed easily, about everything from Lena’s latest project, to Kelly’s patients, to whether they’d bought enough beer for the wedding and who had tried the new Korean barbecue place a few blocks over.

     

                For dessert, they’d bought tiramisu at the store and Kara dished up portions and set them down until they all had a bowl. Lena had made little espressos for them all as well and the four of them lingered over dessert as the evening dragged on. 

     

                It was almost nine o’clock when Alex and Kelly made their leave, thanking Lena, with Alex seeming a little warmer to her, perhaps a little more at ease to see how well Kara was doing. Of course, most of that was thanks to Lena, and partially in regard to Kara’s effort to mask the cracks as best as she could. She insisted on seeing them down to the foyer to catch their Uber and she snagged her key from the bowl on the console before following them down in the elevator.

     

                She hugged Kelly goodbye with the promise of seeing her tomorrow for the small bachelorette party she’d planned and then hugged her sister. Alex pulled back and cupped her face in her hands, giving Kara a searching look as she shifted restlessly, not quite meeting her sister’s eyes.

     

                “I’ll see you tomorrow.”

     

                Nodding, Alex still stared at her, uncomfortably appraising, until Kara met her eyes as she exhaled softly. 

     

                “You seem … different.”

     

                “What do you mean?”

     

                “With her. In her apartment. I … you were never like that with Mike. It never felt like … a partnership. Equal.”

     

                “Oh, yeah, I mean … we split the chores and all that but she has a cleaner, so-“

     

                Alex let out a quiet huff of laughter, shaking her head. “I don’t mean it like that, I just- there’s … I don’t know. It’s like watching two people who- two people who are …”

     

                She trailed off without finishing her thought, and Kara wasn’t sure whose benefit that was for. Inhaling deeply, Alex exhaled sharply and gave her a wavering smile as she took her hands, squeezing tightly.

     

                “I know we’ve done this already but … I’m going to ask you one more time and then I’ll leave it alone for good,” Alex quietly said, a pained look of concern creasing her face. “Are you sure you know what you’re doing?”

     

                Blinking, a laugh died in Kara’s mouth before she could fully get it out. “I- yes, I told you, we’re friends.”

     

                “But you love her.”

     

                It wasn’t a question and Kara was flustered for a moment, a grimace crossing her face at the embarrassment of unrequited love. She still answered anyway. “Yes. But you don’t need to worry about it.”

     

                “I do,” Alex murmured, pity welling in her brown eyes as her shoulders dropped. “I’m worried because … I think she might love you back - but she won’t.”

    Chapter 18

                Alex’s words stayed with Kara, unshakable and haunting as they dogged her every waking minute. She could scarcely focus the next evening, at an upscale bar Lena had helped pick, owned by one of her old boarding school friends. Kara had taken it easy, taking Lena’s words to heart and sipping at her wine as she watched her sister and her friends and colleagues get drunk out of their mind on the capped tab that Kara had set, and which oddly never seemed to be maxed out. Lena stayed by her side the whole time, drinking her scotch as they quietly conversed, existing in their own bubble as they leaned in close to be heard over the music. It made Kara’s heart leap into her throat and she was overly attentive to every gentle brush and glance from Lena, wondering if her sister’s words held any validity.

     

                Of course, she put on a good show for Alex’s benefit as well, trying to force that exuberance that had deserted her for two years now as she got up to dance, wishing she was at least drunk enough to ease her troubles. Still, the happiness for Alex and Kelly was enough for it to be genuine, and she managed to convince Lena to get up and dance with them too, which only made Kara laugh, a lightness in her chest as she allowed herself to enjoy the moment.

     

                It wasn’t anything too rowdy, just dinner before they’d gone to the bar, and then a lot of drinking before they went to a drag show Kara had booked tickets for and then more drinking at Al’s as they took it in turns on the karaoke machine and set Alex and Kelly a scavenger hunt challenge of things to cross off within the bar; getting the number of another customer, taking a selfie with someone with a face tattoo, getting someone to buy them a drink. Alex was far more competitive and won the challenge, which won her a gaudy pink tiara with Bride wrought in glitter and rhinestones across the front.

     

                Still relatively sober by the end of the night, Kara ensured everyone was bundled into cabs in groups of four before she slipped into the passenger seat of the one shared with Lena, Alex and Kelly and had the driver stop off at the latter’s apartment first. Getting out, she helped them into the lobby, smiling slightly at the drunken state of them both, and hugged them goodbye, watching them climb into the elevator before she headed back outside. In the back of the cab this time, she sat beside Lena, who immediately leaned into her, heaving a slurred sigh of contentment.

     

                “It was a fun night.”

     

                “You think so?” Kara softly murmured, her arm going around Lena, her fingers idly stroking her arm.

     

                “Mm. You did a good job planning it.”

     

                Kara smiled and looked out the window as she watched the city blur past, already well past midnight and a bone-leaden weariness filled her as she blinked through the heaviness in her eyelids. The cab pulled up outside and Kara paid him in cash and helped Lena out of the car, keeping a tight grip on her hand as they walked up the front steps to the old building and she let them into the foyer.

     

                The security guard nodded to her and Kara smiled slightly, leading Lena over to the elevator and stepping in as it dinged immediately. With her arm around Lena’s waist, as Lena heavily leaned on her, Kara kept her upright until they made it to the top floor and she unlocked the door to the penthouse. The apartment was dark and Kara kicked off her heels as soon as she was across the threshold before sinking to a crouch as she made Lena lean against the wall and helped her out of her heels as well, carefully cupping her calves as she eased them off her feet.

     

                When she straightened up, Lena was looking at her through heavy-lidded eyes, her lips parted and her pulse fluttering at her throat. Giving her a quick smile, Kara helped her out of her coat and hung it up. “You alright?”

     

                “Mhm. I’m a little bit drunk.”

     

                “Just a little,” Kara agreed with a huff of laughter. “Let’s get you to bed.”

     

                “Are you coming?”

                

                “Yeah, I’m going to go to bed as well.”

     

                “In my bed?”

     

                “Well … I don’t think that’s a good idea tonight.”

     

                “Oh, no, don’t worry, I’m not trying to sleep with you. I’m very drunk; I wouldn’t be any good.”

     

                More laughter escaped Kara as she gripped Lena’s hand and started guiding her down the hallway. She left the lights off, using memory and moonlight to guide her through the shadowed apartment, and Lena kept talking.

     

                “But you can sleep in my bed. Next to me.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “Do you want to? Sleep in my bed, I mean.”

     

                “I- well, I have my own bed.”

     

                “I can sleep in your bed then. I could- I could wake up next to you every day, you know. You’re always so … warm. It’s nice.”

     

                Pausing at the doorway to the kitchen, Kara looked at her, a brooding expression on her face as she tried to parse Lena’s words, searching for a deeper meaning. After a second, she swallowed thickly and then continued to tow her down the hallway, opening the door to Lena’s room and propelling her to the end of her bed. Slumping heavily, Lena’s eyelids shuttered and she smiled slightly, reaching out for Kara’s hands, her thumbs running across the knuckles.

     

                “Let’s go to bed,” Kara whispered.

     

                She helped Lena out of her dress and into a pair of pyjamas before fetching a face wipe to remove her makeup, gently wiping lipstick and eyeliner until the smudges were gone. Lena reached up to touch her face and let out a small laugh.

     

                “You’re very beautiful, you know.”

     

                “How drunk are you?”

     

                “Only a little,” Lena murmured, leaning in conspiratorially and pitching forward as she overbalanced.

     

                Catching her shoulders, Kara straightened her up and smiled warmly, giving her chin a quick, affectionate squeeze. “Come on, into bed.”

     

                “Are you staying?”

     

                Hesitating, biting her lip, Kara swallowed and nodded. “Sure.”

     

                Nodding, Lena turned and dragged back the covers and Kara wiped her own makeup off in the ensuite and borrowed one of the short silk nightdresses Lena wore before joining her. She slipped beneath the covers and pummelled a pillow into shape before relaxing against the pile and removing her glasses. 

     

                As she let the silence of the dark envelope her, the quiet hum of not nearly enough alcohol in her veins, Kara exhaled slowly, too keyed up from her overthinking. And she was too old to be overthinking a relationship, trying to pick apart the meaning of every touch and look when they’d been sleeping together for so many months now. 

     

                And then the bed jostled and Lena quickly scooted closer, her arm wrapped tightly around Kara’s waist as she pressed her face into her shoulder blades, humming with pleasure. The sound of it made Kara’s stomach clench and she closed her eyes, feeling her heart pulse in her throat. 

     

                “So warm,” Lena hummed, a smile in her voice.

     

                “If you’re cold, I can- I can turn the thermostat up.”

     

                “No, I’m not cold. Your warmth just- it just makes me feel less alone. You’re like … a little sun. You make my heart feel warm.”

     

                “Go to sleep,” Kara rasped, her voice oddly strangled.

     

                Lena hummed, the sound a faint sigh of contentment, and she was asleep in minutes, leaving Kara wide awake as her body thrummed with the close proximity of them, of being held by someone else. It was different to waking up in the morning, unconsciously gravitating towards each other in sleep. This was intentional, a deliberate, if drunken, decision. 

     

                They slept in late and Kara was up first, avoiding a hangover with the limited amount of wine she’d drunk. She took Aristotle for a walk and then had a bath when she came back, trying to let the hot water scour her thoughts of Lena from her mind, before emerging to dress in comfortable sweatpants and a t-shirt. Still warm and pink from the bath, Kara let her hair air dry in ragged curls as she ate a bowl of cereal and watched the coffee machine pour into a cup.

     

                Lena didn’t appear until lunchtime, scowling as she rubbed her eyes and shuffled into the kitchen, looking pale and irate. She yawned and then mumbled a greeting and Kara offered to fix her some cereal and coffee as she pushed back her seat, where she’d been editing her speech for the wedding. Giving her a wan smile of gratitude, Lena sank onto a chair and curled up, her knees to her chest and her forehead on her knees.

     

                Fetching her Tylenol and water as well, Kara set everything down in front of her as the coffee poured and then reclaimed her seat. “Did you have a good night?”

     

                “Perhaps too good,” Lena grumbled. “You should be thanking me for talking sense into you or this could be you.”

     

                “Well, I never said I was a better friend than you are,” Kara grinned.

     

                Snorting, Lena shook her head. “At least I don’t have to put your drunk ass to bed every weekend.”

     

                “Ah, well, you’re not as stubborn when you’re drunk. It’s harder to put you to bed when you haven’t been drinking,” Kara whispered, giving her a quick wink before shooting to her feet as the coffee machine finished.

     

                Lena thanked her as the cup was set down in front of her, and took a scalding sip before clearing her throat. “Sorry for making you sleep in my bed. You didn’t have to.”

     

                “Yeah, um, don’t mention it.”

     

                And that was the end of it. No discussion about any misconstrued implications, no explanations for anything said, no questions about whether there had been a misunderstanding. They just went about their day as usual and Lena had to go somewhere in the evening, leaving Kara home alone to edit the speech Lena had expanded on for her. 

     

                The following week, Kara made herself busy at home with chores and working out, trying to keep her body drained so she fell asleep quickly, the thought of laying awake at night to dwell on things too exhausting. On Wednesday, she went for her scheduled interview and Jack was nice and charming, as Lena had said, and offered her a position on the spot with Lena’s recommendation doing wonders for his opinion on her. He offered her a significantly higher amount than James had been paying her and Kara was confused by the drastic turn her life was taking, going from one extreme to the other with dizzying speed.

     

                Lena was pleased and nonchalant as if she’d never doubted Kara for a second, and Alex was ecstatic and James a little sheepish when she told her friends the following Friday at drinks. She was due to start work just after the wedding, giving her some time to process it all first before she was thrown into her new environment. It gave Kara ample time to help with last-minute wedding planning as well, spending her days double-checking seating charts and counting the number of wedding favours they had, getting coffee with Alex or Kelly, and sometimes both, to go over confirmations and schedules.

     

                The wedding rapidly came around and a few weeks later, Kara woke early with her alarm on Saturday and threw a coat over her pyjamas and laced on her shoes before heading out of her bedroom. Lena was already up, flipping through a business magazine she’d picked up the day before and she nudged a cup of coffee forwards as Kara emerged.

     

                “Morning.”

     

                “Ready for today?” Lena asked, glancing up.

     

                “Mhm. It’s going to be a long one, though. I think I was awake half of the night thinking about my speech. You always hope someone is only going to get married once so that means I only have one shot to get it right.”

     

                “You’ll do great. Make sure you have some tea before you head down the aisle though. It’s no good having vocals like that if you’re not going to showcase them properly.”

     

                Kara laughed, wrinkling her nose as she nodded. “Yes, boss.”

     

                “Let me know if you forget anything and I’ll come and drop it off. I’ll just be home all morning.”

     

                “You’re the best.”

     

                “Ah, well, I’m just soft on you.”

     

                They both laughed and Kara’s heart twinged slightly as her expression softened. She started reaching out before she could stop herself and had to settle for resting her hand on Lena’s shoulder and gently squeezing before she did something infinitely worse. She pulled away a second later and drained her coffee, crossing over to the island to dump it in the sink.

     

                “I have to go,” Kara murmured, gathering up all of her things and double-checking she had everything. “I’ll see you there?”

     

                “Yes, go. Have fun.”

     

                Nodding, she smiled and then turned, carrying her things with her and snagging the car keys from the bowl on the hallway console. Riding the elevator down to the parking lot, Kara stowed everything in the Audi and climbed behind the wheel and drove to Alex and Kelly’s. Eliza had gotten in a few days ago and was staying there with them and Kelly had stayed with James and her mom at his place last night so the apartment was relatively quiet as Alex let her inside, looking a little wild with panic.

     

                “How’re you feeling?” Kara asked as she pulled back with a wide smile on her face, squeezing her sister’s arms.

     

                “Nervous,” Alex confessed. “Mostly because I can’t believe it’s finally happening.”

     

                “Mm, it’s been a long time coming. Hi mom.”

     

                She brushed past and hugged Eliza and the three of them milled about until hair and makeup showed up. Alex insisted on a drink while they got ready so Kara sipped her mimosa as her hair was curled and then elaborately braided and pinned up, the three of them conversing from different points within the apartment.

     

                “How’s Lena getting there?” Alex asked, her eyes closed as the makeup artist applied eyeshadow.

     

                “I think she said she hired a driver.”

     

                Snorting, Alex smiled. “Of course she did.”

     

                “I’m curious to meet her,” Eliza said from the sofa as she held her own mimosa and flipped through a medical journal. “It seems like she’s helped a lot.”

     

                “Mm, she’s great.”

     

                “It’s good to see you moving on. You seem happy.”

     

                “Mom, I- we’re not dating?”

     

                Eliza turned to look at her, raising her eyebrows as mild surprise crossed her face. “Oh. Aren’t you?”

     

                “No. She’s a good friend.”

     

                “But you sold your apartment and moved in with her.”

     

                Kara’s eyes strayed to Alex, whose lips were pressed into a flat line. Sighing, Kara rolled her eyes, feeling a hot flush creep into her cheeks. Eliza was warm and maternal but had always been far too busy with work to be around that often, especially after her daughters had moved to National City, so Kara wasn’t that surprised her mother had seemingly made her own assumptions about her relationship with Lena. Trust Eliza to think she was moving on and not feel the need to make a fuss about it.

     

                “Well … you certainly seem fond of her.”

     

                Lips twitching with annoyance, Kara closed her eyes. “Can we focus on Alex’s relationship? She’s the one getting married for the first time. And last; I’ve only got one good speech in me, I’m afraid.”

     

                “You know you don’t have to give one if it’s too difficult-“

     

                “Of course it’s not,” Kara cut her off. “I’m happy for you. You know that. I’m not- I’m not bitter about it.”

     

                “I know you’re not but … it must be hard.”

     

                “Well, yeah, it generally is when your husband dies.”

     

                Sighing, Eliza shook her head. “I wish your father was here today. He’d be so happy.”

     

                Kara smiled sadly as she looked at her mom and then her sister, a feeling of grief and heavy minds as memories swept through the room. She hadn’t known Jeremiah long before he’d passed away but she knew all too well how it felt to miss your parents on important occasions. Lately, it felt like all Kara did was miss her loved ones who were gone on special occasions. 

     

                Even then, Mike should’ve been going to the wedding, wearing his favourite blue work suit, dancing with Kara and doing shots with the boys, dancing badly and the sharp sound of his whistling as the audience clapped for the newlyweds. He always seemed to fill a room, monopolising the space, the attention, his voice louder, his laughter deafening. How could someone so full of life be absent from every day going forward? How could he miss Alex’s wedding, her birthday, and their anniversary?

     

                “I brought you something,” Kara said as soon as everyone’s hair and makeup were finished, standing and crossing over to her bag. 

     

                Her mother had had a lacy handkerchief with her initials embroidered in blue on it at her own wedding to Kara’s father, and it was one of the few things she’d inherited and kept after all these years. Kara had it with her on her own wedding day and she ran a thumb over the softly washed fabric before holding it out to Alex.

     

                “Old, borrowed and blue. And your suit is new.”

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                Giving her a small smile, Kara nodded. “Let’s get you married.”

     

                Kara had arranged to drive the three of them to the venue herself, with Lena’s permission for the use of the Audi, freely given, and it was past eleven when they all bundled into the car with their garment bags and heels. Driving them out of the city, Kara kept up a stream of chatter to try and keep Alex’s mind distracted, knowing that it was nerve-wracking to stand in front of a bunch of people, no matter how badly you wanted to marry someone.

     

                They arrived just after twelve and she made sure the coast was clear before ushering Alex into one of the guest houses. Another one was occupied by Kelly, who’d beaten them there, and Kara ducked her head in to visit once Alex was settled.

     

                Eventually, she had to finish getting ready herself, changing into the pale blue dress picked out for her and making a cup of tea to make sure her throat wasn’t dry. She’d swapped out her glasses for contacts too and added the little pearl earrings that had also been her mother’s, which she’d worn at her own wedding. Fingers worrying at them, Kara was quiet and reminiscent as she thought of Mike and wished for a happier life for her sister.

     

                At three o’clock, Kara kissed her sister’s cheek and squeezed her hand, wishing her luck before she gathered her bouquet and followed after Eliza. At the end of the aisle, she took her spot on Alex’s side, where Winn was waiting at a mic stand, another one beside him for Kara. 

     

                She thought she must have been out of her mind to agree to sing in front of everyone but her eyes picked Lena out in the crowd, dressed in the backless gold dress she’d showcased for Kara weeks ago. Kara knew exactly how low the back went, where the zipper was situated, and just how high the slit went up her thigh. She also knew that Lena looked breathtakingly beautiful, sitting in the front row on Alex’s side of the crowd, a standout with her fine-boned face and dark wavy hair. 

     

                The music started up a moment later and Kara tore her eyes away from her friend as Winn took the lead and Alex appeared. Smiling brightly as she joined in on the duet, Kara watched her sister approach and then Kelly a minute after Alex had reached the floral arbour at the front.

     

                The ceremony was short and sweet, the two brides radiant with happiness as they finally tied the knot, and Kara couldn’t have been happier for them. She cried, naturally, standing by her sister’s side as J’onn officiated and they kissed, and then she followed them back down the aisle, arm in arm with James as everyone clapped and cheered. 

     

                There was a long period of congratulations as all of the guests followed after them, and then family photos before the couple went off for their own photos. During the cocktail hour, Kara sought out Lena and they fetched glasses of wine at the bar and Kara pointed out Eliza to her as they drank. She ended up introducing her mother to Lena a few minutes after that when Eliza spotted them.

     

                “Mom, this is Lena.”

     

                “Lena! It’s so lovely to finally meet you.”

     

                Looking surprised by the sentiment, Lena held her hand out and gave Eliza a polite smile. “And you, Doctor Danvers.”

     

                “Please, call me Eliza. And thank you for all that you’ve done for Kara. You know, you never stop worrying about your children, no matter how old they get.”

     

                “Mom.”

     

                Lena smiled, amused as her eyes cut across to Kara, who seemed fifteen instead of thirty-five, embarrassed by her oblivious mother. Taking a sip of wine, Kara cleared her throat.

     

                “I’ve told you, you don’t need to worry. I’m doing great. I start my new job next week.”

     

                “And you’re going to be wonderful.”

     

                “I agree,” Lena lightly interjected. 

     

                “And what do you do for work, Lena?”

     

                “Oh, I run my own architecture firm.”

     

                “Really? Do you enjoy it?”

     

                “I do, yes. Very much.”

     

                “And how are you doing, sweetie?”

     

                Taken aback by the question, Lena blinked and a smile quickly spread across her face as her eyebrows furrowed ever so slightly. Letting out a quiet huff of laughter, she nodded and Kara wanted to wince.

     

                “I’m good,” Lena politely replied, and Kara knew it was a lie, and Lena knew that she knew but Eliza didn’t and she wasn’t about to spill her guts to her.

     

                Softly sighing with shared empathy, Eliza reached out to squeeze her arm. “It’s hard. My husband’s been gone for twenty years now and, God, if I don’t miss him every day. But it gets easier too, the more time passes by. It’s a blessing and a curse.”

     

                “Do you think they’ll be done with the photos soon?” Kara interrupted, sparing Lena a response and Eliza the opportunity to continue.

     

                It would’ve been sad for the three widows to be conversing about their dead spouses at a wedding. The only way it could’ve been worse was if Kara invited Kelly’s mom over to join and make it into a quartet. Craning her neck to try and spot Alex and Kelly, Kara swallowed the lump in her throat.

     

                “We should get another drink,” Lena quickly suggested.

     

                She escorted Eliza off, giving Kara a pointed look of reassurance. Trying not to be too paranoid about what was being said, Kara fiddled with her glass and then joined Nia and Querl at the tall barrel they were standing around with their own drinks.

     

                It was a nice day, the sky cloudless and the weather still a little cool for that time of year, meaning it was just right for an outdoor wedding. The newlyweds returned a short while after to a round of applause and Lena returned to Kara’s side, informing her that Eliza had gotten into a conversation with Kelly’s mom. She rested a reassuring hand against Kara’s lower back and Kara felt some of her worry recede as Lena seemed unfazed by whatever else Eliza might have brought up. Kara didn’t want her to be thinking about her dead wife all day; there was nothing worse than being constantly reminded of it.

     

                They were seated for dinner a short while later, sitting at a table with Alex and Kelly, James and Lucy and their mothers. Kara ordered the lamb for her main dish and after another two glasses of wine, she unwound a little, her laughter coming more easily, the tension receding and a slight rosiness about her as she chatted animatedly with everyone.

     

                The cake was cut after dinner had been cleared away, and Kara ate the rest of Lena’s slice as well as she nudged her plate closer. Giving her a quick smile, Lena leaned in and told her she was going to the smoker’s area and would be back shortly, and Kara was left wondering what she was so stressed about. It was obvious though; being at a wedding while grieving was no easy thing, even though Kara was trying her best.

     

                When Lena was back and everyone returned from the bar and bathrooms, it was time for speeches and Kara rose to her feet as the mic was handed to her first. Clearing her throat, she faced the sea of faces surrounding the tables.

     

                “Hi everyone, for those who don’t know me, I’m Alex’s sister, Kara. I’d just like to congratulate the happy couple; I couldn’t think of two people who deserve this moment more and I’m so happy to be here tonight, celebrating this special moment with them. Um … if there’s one thing I’ve learnt, it’s that people come into your life in strange ways. Sometimes first impressions can be wrong, maybe it takes a while to realise what’s in front of you, and sometimes … you just know. For Alex and Kelly, it was clear from the moment they met they just knew. I think we all knew; we had a running bet on how long it would take for them to get together, and James, you still owe me fifty bucks. Never have two people seemed to fit together more perfectly than these two. It’s taken a while for them to get here, tonight, to finally be married, but I know every single second of that wait has been worth it. Kelly, I want to thank you for making my sister so happy. I know often a wedding can feel like you’re losing a piece of your family to someone else but … for me, I’m not losing a sister, I’m gaining one. And I couldn’t be happier that it’s you. It’s a privilege in life to find someone to love, who brings out the best parts of you, who … makes your heart feel warm. Over the years, I’ve seen my sister become the best version of herself with Kelly, and I know that they’re going to be happy together for a long, long time. So … congratulations. I love you both and I’m so happy for you.”

     

                Alex squeezed her hand and Kara ducked down to kiss her cheek before handing the mic off to James and taking her seat. Her cheeks felt a little warm and she swore she could feel Lena’s eyes glancing over to her every second or so, James’ speech an indecipherable drone as she struggled to focus on what he was saying.

     

                When he finished, there was more applause and then a toast before it led straight into the first dance. After the first dance, the DJ started up and the dance floor slowly filled, getting rowdier and sloppier as the night progressed. 

     

                Kara nursed another drink and found herself on and off the dance floor in sporadic bursts, laughing as she dragged Lena with her, dancing with her friends as they shouted the lyrics to their favourite songs. Towards the end of the night, most people already wasted and the party winding down, there were a few slower songs and as Kara finished off her last drink, a hand touched her elbow and slid down to her hand, lacing their fingers together.

     

                Her eyes met Lena’s and her friend arched an eyebrow, cocking her head to the side. She’d had far more to drink than Kara had, a drunken glaze in her eyes as she smiled wryly, and Lena jerked her head towards the dance floor.

     

                “Can I have this one?”

     

                “You don’t even like dancing.”

     

                “I’m better at slow dancing. Easier to pretend I don’t have two left feet.”

     

                Exhaling softly, Kara smiled faintly. “Go on then.”

     

                She let Lena tow her towards the swaying couples and then she cradled her waist and held her hand as they fell into the rhythm of the song. As they gravitated closer to each other, Kara’s hand slid around Lena’s back, and she was conscious of her dress again, making Kara feel warm as she thought about sliding her hand up over Lena’s spine, breathing in the smell of her perfume as she imagined kissing her neck there. Swaying, Kara closed her eyes as she banished the thoughts. They didn’t speak as they slow-danced, not until the song was almost over and Lena softly sighed in her ear.

     

                “You stole my line,” Lena murmured.

     

                Kara swallowed thickly, looking away, focusing on the other couples dancing or getting drinks at the bar. “I know you meant it differently but … it was a nice sentiment.”

     

                They were silent for a moment as the music crooned, filling the empty space their conversation left, and Lena looked away as well, a rigid set to her shoulders and jaw. “Did I?”

     

                Eyes quickly flitting up and sideways to Lena, Kara’s heart lurched in her chest. Her mouth opened and closed and she didn’t know what to say to that, Lena’s feelings so unknowable that Kara wasn’t sure if she was making a weak joke or muddying things between them with her vague riddles that left Kara wondering whether there was the potential for something more or not.

     

                She stopped their slow swaying and Lena met her eyes, the two of them staring at each other for a moment. Then Kara dropped her hands from Lena’s waist and hand and turned around, slipping through the crowd as a cold sweat made her skin damp. 

     

                Anger rushed through, belated, but at the root of it was fear and worry. Finding a quiet corner away from the stifling heat of people pressed in together, Kara breathed slowly and tried to make sense of her muddled thoughts. She was far too sober for the frustration welling in her chest and she ended up at the bar, ordering a shot of tequila and a glass of wine. Drinking them both at the bar, she then found a seat at an empty table and was joined by Eliza a while later.

     

                Her mother appeared behind her chair, ducking down to wrap her arms around Kara, who turned her head to see who it was. Squeezing Eliza’s hand, she smiled slightly. “What’s wrong?”

     

                “Me? Nothing.”

     

                Sighing, Eliza took a seat beside her and gave Kara a tenderly pointed look. “You’re my daughter; don’t think just because you’re all the way out here I can’t tell when something’s the matter, Kara Danvers.”

     

                Lips twitching with amusement, Kara’s eyelids shuttered and she shook her head, shrugging. “There’s just a lot going on at the moment. It’s … confusing.”

     

                “I know,” Eliza whispered. “But the hard part is over.”

     

                “Can I- can I ask you something?”

     

                “Sure, sweetie.”

     

                “Why did you never- afterwards, why didn’t you … move on?”

     

                Blinking, Eliza sat back in her chair, her expression clouding with deep thought as she considered the question. “I think … I was just too busy with life. Raising the two of you, and my job … that was already a lot to handle. And don’t forget, I was older than you are now. I didn’t have time for dating.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Kara let out a small huff of annoyance, rubbing her eyes. “I feel like I’m too old for it too.”

     

                “Kara,” Eliza snorted, “you’re thirty-five. Some people are falling in love for the first time at your age. Your sister’s only just older than you and she’s getting married for the first time. You have … all the time in the world to move on - if that’s what you want.”

     

                “I think I do. That’s not the hard part.”

     

                Eliza’s gaze softened with understanding. “Ah. The hard part is trying to figure out if someone else is ready to move on. The drama of young love.”

     

                “Yes but … I’m too mature for that drama. I wish it was as simple as just asking.”

     

                “It could be.”

     

                “No, it couldn’t. If I’m wrong, or if I’m jumping the gun a bit … I would ruin everything.”

     

                Inhaling deeply as she drew herself up to her full seated height, Eliza patted Kara’s knee and gave her a quick nod. “Then you just have to consider whether it’s worth it or not.”

     

                “It would be. Of course it would. But … Mike. How do I pretend that never happened? How is she supposed to pretend her wife never happened?”

     

                Clicking her tongue, Eliza laughed. “Sweetie, that’s not going to happen. Both of you will spend the rest of your lives imagining a different future from the one you’re going to have. Whether or not it’s with each other, it’s not going to be with them. It’s the harsh and bitter truth, I’m afraid.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose at the sting of honesty, Kara nodded. “Yeah, I guess.”

     

                Her attention was snagged by Lena approaching then, a wary look on her face as she interrupted. “Sorry, um, Alex and Kelly are about to head off.”

     

                Nodding, Kara quickly climbed to her feet with her mother and they joined the crowd of guests congregating at the exit, where a vintage car was waiting to whisk the couple away. Hugging them both, Kara stepped back and let Eliza say goodbye as well before the couple climbed into the car. The driver set off down the driveway as everyone cheered and the party started to dwindle down after that, guests trickling off.

     

                “My driver is here,” Lena told Kara a short while after. “He’ll wait until you’re ready to go.”

     

                “Oh. Okay. Let’s go now,” Kara murmured, suddenly aware of her exhaustion.

     

                They went to say goodbye to their remaining friends and Eliza and then Kara slid into the back of the town car beside Lena. The drive home was quiet and Kara stared out the window, an unbearable tension filling the back of the car. She couldn’t even bear to look at Lena out of her own fear of doing something irreparably stupid.

     

                She took the keys from Lena when she struggled to fit them in the lock and let them into the apartment. Lena led the way down the hallway and Kara kicked her heels off, feet aching and shoulders slumped from a long day. It was already past midnight and it felt like she’d been awake for even longer, the emotional toll of it all catching up to her in anticipation of bed now.

     

                “What’s wrong?” Lena whispered, breaking her out of her brooding thoughts as they reached the end of the hallway, the apartment opening up to the spacious living room.

     

                Kara was glad it was dark, that she couldn’t see Lena’s face and Lena couldn’t see hers. Swallowing thickly, she carried on walking.

     

                “Nothing.”

     

                “Kara-“

     

                “It’s been a long day.”

     

                “If it’s something I said-“

     

                Choking on a quiet laugh, Kara ran a hand over her face. “No, you haven’t said anything.”

     

                “Okay,” Lena mumbled, following Kara into the kitchen. “Well … can you help unzip me?”

     

                Her voice was coy, a little playful and a low tenderness to it as she tried to lure Kara into a better mood. Mouth thinning, so much confusion making her tense and a little uptight, Kara moved in behind her and found the zipper, quickly jerking it down. The dress moved like liquid, the thin straps slipping off Lena’s shoulders as the hem started pooling around her feet.

     

                “Goodnight,” Kara murmured, stepping away and carrying on towards her bedroom.

     

                She left Lena standing in the kitchen with a look of indignant surprise on her face, which quickly turned to wounded hurt.

    Chapter 19

                After the wedding, Kara found it difficult to be within Lena’s close vicinity, prone to knocking over glasses, spilling her coffee, walking into the corners of the tables or counters or catching her shoulder on the doorframes anytime she was within three feet of her. That wasn’t to say that she ignored Lena; things seemed much the same as they cooked for each other and ate breakfast and dinner together, went to Group and drinks on Fridays together. They had their world-weary and sarcastic conversations and enough laughter to stave off the inevitable boiling point of everything that was wrong.

     

                It had become something of a relief whenever they parted, Kara eager to start work at her new job for the distance it offered her from her tangled feelings. The job was great, Jack a charming and funny boss who was gentle with the animals and was like James in some ways, and the pay was even better. It wasn’t that she wanted to be away from Lena, only that it was becoming increasingly difficult to stamp down her feelings and at times it felt like Lena knew and was goading her for her own enjoyment. Maybe not in such a malicious way, but her little odd comments always left Kara feeling a little heartbroken and annoyed, and she wasn’t even sure that Lena knew it. If she did, it might have been the fact that Kara didn’t let her so much as touch her that gave it away.

     

                They managed to make it a few weeks before it all came to a head, late April in the throes of a warm spring that had led to many days outdoors, walking the dog and going for brunch and coffee on the weekends before they went about their individual days. Kara felt torn in two, her contradictory desire to be so close to Lena, to sleep beside her and touch her and let herself give in to her feelings, even if it wasn’t reciprocated, at war with the cold fear of rejection and abandonment that made her put some distance between them. It hurt her just as much as it hurt Lena to be left in the lurch, her cold comfort taken from her.

     

                But Lena wasn’t known for her patience, and after giving Kara a grace period to sort out whatever her problem was, she’d had enough. Kara had come home from work to a hot shower and started prepping for dinner, the apartment peaceful as she let her mind wander, mindful of the knife. She had chicken in a creamy garlic sauce simmering on the stove as it thickened while the pot boiled, waiting for pasta, by the time the front door unlocked. Her heart skipped a beat in her chest, stomach swooping with nervous elation.

     

                That was the worst part, that no matter what she did, her body reacted so strongly to Lena. It wasn’t as simple as saying she didn’t have feelings for her when her body reacted as if she was a teenager with her first crush. It was painfully frustrating but Kara perked up at her arrival, eager to see her, even though she knew it would result in another slightly awkward encounter where she had to fight to keep her hands to herself while trying to act as if nothing was wrong.

     

                “Hi,” she greeted Lena with a smile as she stepped into the kitchen. “Good day?”

     

                “It was okay,” Lena grumbled, running a hand through her hair, her expression clouded and a tired slump to her shoulders. “You?”

     

                “We had a Cavoodle deliver the cutest litter today. Tiny little things. I would’ve brought them all home if I could.”

     

                Lena gave her a small smile, glancing down at Aristotle, who was sitting practically on top of her feet. “Maybe Aristotle needs a little Plato.”

     

                Kara just hummed vaguely in response as she dumped an estimated amount of pasta into the bubbling pot and then stirred the pan. Lena moved towards the island counter, setting her handbag down and staring at Kara’s back as she watched her cook, waiting for a response.

     

                “We could, you know. Get a puppy. If you wanted to.”

     

                Quietly scoffing, Kara turned her head slightly, not far enough to be looking at Lena though. “What would we do with a puppy?”

     

                “Raise it.”

     

                “And then share custody when I move out? I’m already going to miss this guy, it’ll break my heart to add another one to the list.”

     

                “You don’t have to move out, I told you.”

     

                Lena moved up behind her as she spoke and cradled Kara’s waist, something she’d done dozens of times before. Startling slightly, going rigid, Kara twisted out of her grip and moved to a cupboard, taking out two pasta bowls as she tried to pretend it had been a deliberate action. Clearing her throat, a tremor in her hands, Kara moved back to the stove as Lena retreated, a wounded look on her face.

     

                “What is wrong?” Lena blurted out, her voice thick with frustration and annoyance.

     

                “What?” Kara mumbled, glancing over her shoulder.

     

                Lena was leaning against the island counter, head tipped back as she pinched the bridge of her nose, eyes screwed shut. The lines of her body were full of tension and Kara turned to face her.

     

                “What’s wrong?”

     

                “N-“

     

                “Do not say nothing, I swear to God, Kara. You haven’t let me touch you in weeks. You jump as if I’m going to attack you the second I’m within a foot of you. What did I do? Because I- I feel like I’m losing my mind and … I can’t figure out what I did so if you- if you just tell me , I’ll fix it.”

     

                She lowered her head and met Kara’s eyes, her own pleading and heartbreaking. Looking at the floor, Kara slowly shook her head, her mouth thinning as she shrugged dismissively.

     

                “You don’t need to fix anything. It’s fine, I just- I’m finding it … hard at the moment. It’s not you.”

     

                “Well, it sure fucking feels like it’s me,” Lena hotly replied. “You can’t even look at me right now.”

     

                Raising her head, Kara felt a lump in her throat as her shoulders sagged with defeat. There was a pained look on her face, a deep ache suffusing her, so unbearable that she wanted to look away again. It was becoming increasingly harder to be around Lena so much, to come home to the apartment they both lived in and eat dinner together, walk the dog together, watch TV together and tidy up together. There was a whole life there and so many muddled feelings that Kara felt conflicted but now, more than ever, sure that her feelings for Lena were deeper than she’d ever anticipated. She could no longer dismissively push them aside.

     

                “What happened to just … talking about things? We’ve always been honest, we- we were very clear about how things would work between us, that we’re adults and we would handle it-“

     

                “I know,” Kara hoarsely exclaimed, her cheeks reddening, her eyes bright with a sudden stinging of tears as she choked on the words. “Don’t you think I know that? But I can’t. I can’t talk about it because … I can’t fuck up my life any further. I just- I can’t.”

     

                “And shutting me out is fine? It’s not going to fuck things up for you is it? Living with me while you avoid me.”

     

                Scoffing, Kara rubbed her forehead, closing her eyes. “I’m not avoiding you. I just-“

     

                “What? What is it? If you need help with something, just tell me and I’ll help you. You know I will. That’s all I want, to help you, to make sure you’re okay. Not … whatever this is, I mean … fuck, Kara, I thought I was your best friend.”

     

                Eyes snapping open, Kara gave Lena a look of unabashed yearning, her voice wavering as she replied. “You are but … it’s getting complicated. When you told me to move in, I said it was a bad idea, I told you we’d be complicating things and … I don’t want to do that. I-“

     

                Letting out a quiet huff, Kara paused and then let out a small sob. Her eyes blurred with tears and she covered her mouth as she looked down, shoulders taut, dinner starting to stick to the pan as she ignored it on the stove. Shaking her head, she drew in a ragged inhale, shuddering in her chest as she refused to look up.

     

                “I’m really sorry.”

     

                “I- what, you- you have feelings for me?” Lena hollowly asked.

     

                Flushing as she covered her face with her hands, embarrassment slamming into her, more mortifying than she could admit, Kara turned around. 

     

                “That’s what it’s about? That’s what you can’t look me in the eye and tell me?”

     

                “No,” Kara rasped, angrily reaching for the knobs of the stove and turning off the gas. “I can’t look you in the eye and ask you if you feel the same way.”

     

                Lena huffed, not quite a laugh but laced with bitter humour as her eyes quickly filled with tears and spilt over, running down her cheeks. Choking on a sob, she wiped her tears away with the heels of her palms and scowled, her face ashen and angry as Kara turned around, shock rippling across her face at the reaction.

     

                “Of course I love you,” she confessed, her voice broken and scratchy as she gestured helplessly. “Is that what you want to hear? Of course I fucking do and I shouldn’t .
