                Glancing down at it, Andrea slowly reached out and took it, running her fingers over the cheap material and raising it to her chest as she held it close. She didn’t move to put it on and Kara hovered two feet away, wary and brimming with nervous tension.

     

                “Do you want some help?”

     

                Holding it out, Andrea’s face furrowed and Kara took the sweatshirt back, quickly crumpling the hem to the neck and extending it.

     

                “Duck your head for me,” she gently murmured. As Andrea closed her eyes and hunched over, Kara slipped it over her head and pulled it down, smiling as their eyes met. “You know, you have beautiful blue eyes.”

     

                “Do I?”

     

                “Mhm. Very pretty. Just slip your arm through. Good. And the other one.”

     

                “I … my dog-“

     

                “Aristotle?”

     

                “You know him?”

     

                “I do. I know where to find him,” Kara murmured, taking her hand and easing it through the other sleeve. 

     

                Her fingers were so cold that Kara clutched them tightly, concern welling up as she reached for Andrea’s other hand, mindful of the cast. Holding her fingers in her own grasp, which was by no means warm but hadn’t been subjected to the cold night for an unknown amount of hours, Kara tried to think. Eyebrows drawing together, a scar between them dimpling from the act, Andrea’s lips parted as she inhaled. Kara opened her eyes and blinked, staring at her and Andrea tried to draw back.

     

                “Who are you?”

                

                “I’m Kara.”

     

                “And who am I?”

     

                The question made Kara’s throat close up, her eyes stinging with tears at the shock of watching this stranger unravel before her eyes. They didn’t know each other at all but it was like being plunged into cold water, the shock of witnessing the cyclical conversation, the loose threads of her thoughts spin off into nothing. 

     

                “You’re Andrea,” she lightly replied. 

     

                “Oh. Oh, yes, of course. That’s a nice name.”

     

                Giving her a watery smile, Kara nodded, squeezing her hands. “It is.”

     

                “I’d like to go home now. I don’t like it here. I don’t- I want to go home, I don’t know where I am. I- what is this place?”

     

                She was starting to get worked up now, her agitation palpable as her eyes darted around and her shoulders grew taut beneath Kara’s worn sweater. Baby blue eyes filling with tears, Andrea let out a small sob, her face crumpling as tears spilt down her cheeks. Slowly stepping forward, she closed the gap between them and broke down, putting her head on Kara’s shoulders as she shook with the effort.

     

                “I want to go home. Please take me home.”

     

                “It’s alright,” Kara murmured, her voice coming out gravelly and just a little broken as she quickly wrapped her in her embrace. “It’s okay, it’s scary, I know, but you’re going to be okay.”

     

                Her own vision blurred with tears and she clenched her teeth, tipping her head back as she gently rubbed the back of her lover’s wife. Something inside of her was inexplicably tangled up in this situation, and even though she was no one to Andrea, she felt responsible for her the way that family was. 

     

                “Shall we walk back through the park for a bit? My car is nearby. I can drive you back home for something to eat. It’s such a lovely day; it’s so sunny. You’ll feel alright in a minute; it’ll be alright.”

     

                “I want to go home.”

     

                “Okay, I’ll take you home,” Kara whispered, rubbing her back and gently rocking her until Andrea quietened, comforted by her presence. Easing her back, Kara gave her a kind smile and brushed her hair out of her face, wiping away her tears as her heart ached for her. “Okay, let’s go back to my car.”

     

                “You’ll take me home?”

     

                “Yes, I’ll take you home. Just … hold my hand, okay?”

     

                She reached for Andrea’s good hand, scared to let go of her, as if she might vanish into thin air if Kara didn’t have a tangible hold on her. Andrea held her hand, lacing their fingers together, and she started to swing them as Kara led her back towards the path.

     

                “Remind me once we’re back at the office that I need to call my father,” Andrea said as they walked. Kara looked at her, apprehension on her face, until the other woman looked at her, raising her eyebrows haughtily. “Did you get that?”

     

                “I- yes. Yes, Mrs Rojas.”

     

                “Mrs? I’m not married,” Andrea snorted.

     

                “No, of course not, I- sorry, Miss Rojas.”

     

                “Sorry?”

     

                “I- yes, I’m sorry.”

     

                “You’re sorry?”

     

                “Yes?” Kara slowly replied, her pitch rising to make it sound like a question.

     

                “Did you do something wrong?”

     

                “No?”

     

                “What?”

     

                “I … um, it’s such a lovely day, isn’t it?” Kara asked, grasping at straws.

     

                Looking around, Andrea closed her eyes as if basking in the warmth of the sun, humming with pleasure. “Mm, I think I might like it here. It’s a bit lonely though.”

     

                “Oh, well, you have me.”

     

                “Sorry, I- I’ve forgotten your name. Who are you?”

     

                “Kara.”

     

                “Oh. I’m Andrea. It’s nice to meet you.”

     

                “It’s nice to meet you too. You know, if- if you’re looking for friends, there’s someone I know who I think you’d really like.”

     

                “Really? And what’s her name?”

     

                “Lena.”

     

                “Lena? I had a friend called that once. God, it’s- it’s been years. I heard she moved … somewhere. I can’t- I can’t remember. Where did she go? Her name … God, what was her name?”

     

                “Lena Luthor?”

     

                Face softening with reminiscent fondness, Andrea nodded. “That’s right. Do you know her?”

     

                “I do. She’s my … friend.”

     

                “Your friend? Am I your friend?”

     

                “You are,” Kara agreed with a wavering smile, a stone settling heavily in her stomach. 

     

                “Well, quickly,” Andrea brusquely commanded.

     

                “What?”

     

                “Aren’t you calling your friend?”

     

                Letting out a breathless laugh, Kara nodded, smiling weakly. “Right. Of course. So silly of me to forget. I’ll call her now.”

     

                She fished her phone out and dialled Lena’s number with a shaky hand, quietly pleading for her to pick up as she tried to retrace her steps back to the car. Lena didn’t answer, of course, and Kara bit back a curse as she hit her voicemail.

     

                “Hey, it’s me again. I’ve found her. Please call me back.”

     

                Hanging up, she slipped her phone into her pocket and turned to Andrea, smiling apologetically. “She didn’t answer.”

     

                “Who?”

     

                “Lena.”

     

                “Who’s Lena?”

     

                “I- it’s getting late. Let me drive you home.”

     

                “I- no, I don’t- I don’t think I want to go home with you.”

     

                “That’s okay, I’ll take you to your home.”

     

                “My home?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “I … I don’t remember where that is. It’s- it’s-“

     

                “Near the harbour.”

     

                Shaking her head as she objected to that notion, Andrea came to a stop. “No, I live- I live- dónde está? Dios, mi cabeza.”

     

                Pressing a hand to her forehead, Andrea squeezed her eyes shut and hunched forward. She slipped into a torrent of Spanish that was too quick for Kara’s rudimentary memories of her high school class to comprehend. She kept a tight hold on her hand and squatted before her though.

     

                “Hey, hey, Andrea? It’s okay. It’s okay, I can help you.”

     

                “I- I don’t know you. I don’t know … where I am. I- I need to go- I need to go home. Which way is home? I can’t remember.”

     

                As she started to panic, confusion filling her eyes as she stared at Kara, her breaths short and sharp and her bottom lip sobbing, Kara straightened up. Scrambling for a way to soothe her, to coax her back to the car, the stress of the evening catching up with her as she felt out of her depth, Kara ran a hand through her hair. She could’ve called the cops like the alert said and let them deal with Andrea, but Kara couldn’t leave her. If she was handed off, she might be frightened, confused by what was going on with no one to placate her, and so she was fixated on the idea of getting her to the car while she tried to contact Lena, who would know what to do.

     

                “I can take you home. I’m a- a friend; I remember the way. Aristotle is waiting there. Your dog.”

     

                Shoulders going slack as her words had a calming effect on her, Andrea let out a wispy sigh, exhaustion written in the lines of her face. “Aristotle. My dog is called that.”

     

                “Is he?” Kara asked, coaxing her into motion. “What’s he like?”

     

                “He’s a- a … I can’t remember the breed. A … cavalier?”

     

                “Oh, really? Like a King Charles?”

     

                “Yes! That’s it,” she agreed, perking up, her eyes still holding a sliver of tears along her waterline. “Do you have a dog?”

     

                “I did. Years ago.”

     

                “Oh. Oh no.”

     

                Kara glanced over at her and watched her eyes fill, panic settling in. Mouth opening and closing, she let out a quiet squawk of surprise. “No, no, it’s okay. The dog- he’s fine. I, um, I split up with my husband so … he has the dog. But I’m a vet! I’m a vet so I get to see dogs every day.”

     

                “A vet?”

     

                “Yes. I really like animals.”

     

                “Oh. I have a dog.”

     

                “Do you? I’d love to meet him.”

     

                “He’s at home. I’ll show you.”

     

                She set off with more urgency, dragging Kara by the hand, and Kara wasn’t sure how to react to the contrary moods as she let herself get towed along. It was another forty minutes before she located the car, moving in fits and starts as Andrea’s mind went around and around the same topics, the bouts of Spanish, the stubborn, tearful objection to going any further to the silent, placid agreeableness.

     

                Finding Alex’s car, Kara almost went weak in the knees with the keen cut of relief. “This one is mine,” she explained to Andrea.

     

                Nodding, Andrea held onto her hand as Kara led her to the passenger side door. Opening it, she helped her inside and buckled her in and shut the door. Quickly rounding the car, Kara climbed behind the wheel and locked them in so Andrea couldn’t open the door, a precaution she wasn’t sure was necessary but she wouldn’t take any risks.

     

                Bucking herself in, she started the engine and sat there for a moment, not sure what to do now. Her alarm at the situation had built over the evening and it was past two o’clock in the morning now, bone-deep tiredness and frayed nerves getting the better of Kara as she let out a choked breath.

     

                “Can we get coffee?”

     

                She glanced over at Andrea’s hopeful expression and wanted to let out a hysterical laugh at the innocent question. But it was something to do while she tried to figure out what happened next.

     

                “Coffee? Sure, let’s get coffee.”

     

                Driving them to the nearest Starbucks with a drive-through window, Kara ordered a caramel latte for herself and an oat milk latte with vanilla for Andrea. Sitting at the window as they waited for their drinks, Kara tried calling Lena again and again to no avail before sending a series of texts. 

     

    [Kara]: I found her

     

    [Kara]: answer your phone. I don’t know where to take her

     

    [Kara]: I have Andrea in the car. call me back

     

    [Kara]: please call me back asap

     

                After no response, she caved and called Alex, returning one of the multitude of missed calls that had ended at midnight.

     

                “Hello?”

     

                “Hi, it’s me,” Kara rasped, her voice cracking as her emotions suddenly got the better of her. 

     

                “Where the hell are you? Have you been driving around this whole time?”

     

                “Yeah. Kind of. I- I found her.”

     

                “You found her? Lena’s wife?”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara quietly sobbed, breaking down now. “I need you to- to call Lena for me. She’s not picking up and … I don't know what to do.”

     

                “She doesn’t know yet?”

     

                “No. I don’t know if- if it’s because she’s busy searching or because it’s- it’s me, but I don’t know what I’m supposed to do now. I don’t know where to take her back to and I can’t- I can’t just hand her to the cops.”

     

                “Wait, she’s still with you?”

     

                “Yeah. We’re just getting coffee at Starbucks.”

     

                “Starbucks? Jesus Christ, Kara, take her to a fucking hospital. Is she okay? She’s been out there for hours by herself.”

     

                Glancing sideways at Andrea, who was fiddling with the stereo, Kara drew in a shuddering breath, wiping her cheeks. “She looks fine. She was at the park and she was so cold. But I gave her my sweatshirt and she- she looks fine but-“

     

                “Get to the hospital. Now.”

     

                “I don’t know which one Lena uses - it’s one of the private ones.”

     

                “It doesn’t matter. Go to mine. I’ll meet you there; I’m fifteen minutes out-“

     

                “Wha- how?”

     

                “We’ve been looking,” her sister roughly sighed. “Kelly’s calling Lena now; I’ll meet you at the hospital.”

     

                The line went dead and Kara let out a choked sound of relief to have some guidance. The barista appeared at the window a moment later and handed Kara their coffees and she nestled hers in the drinks holder and handed Andrea hers.

     

                Trying not to show her worry, Kara decided to play her music through the car, remembering an old comment about how Andrea loved 90s and early 2000s music. Kara had plenty of that on her phone and at the first note of I Want It That Way, Andrea’s face lit up and she started to sing along.

     

                It unknotted something inside Kara and she relaxed behind the wheel as she drove towards National City General Hospital, singing along. After a few minutes, she almost started to forget, the music seeming to capture both of them in the nostalgia of it, and when Britney came on next, they were both bonded over it like old friends.

     

                “Oh man, I haven’t heard this one in ages,” Kara laughed.“Okay, this Britney was her prime. Don’t you think so?”

     

                “What? No way. Blackout was her best album.”

     

                Kara spluttered, aghast as she shook her head, taking a sip of coffee. “I think you mean In The Zone.”

     

                “Okay, that’s a great album too but she was early to the EDM craze and I don’t think people gave it enough credit.”

     

                “Maybe but In The Zone has Toxic on it. You can’t argue with that.”

     

                Deliberating, Andrea shrugged and laughed. “Okay, you’ve got me there.” She leaned forward suddenly and pointed. “It’s left here.”

     

                Jerked back to her reality, Kara straightened, shifting in her seat, and cleared her throat. “I actually know a shortcut. Mind if we use it?”

     

                “Sure, no problem. I’ve still got a while before my meeting.”

     

                Kara watched from the corner of her eye as Andrea checked a non-existent watch on her wrist. Clearing her throat, Kara gestured towards the stereo. “And what about NSYNC and Backstreet Boys? Who’s the better group?”

     

                “Oh, Backstreet Boys, without a doubt but I’ve always loved NSYNC.”

     

                “But NSYNC has Justin Timberlake.”

     

                “I never liked him,” Andrea replied, wrinkling her nose.

     

                “What?” Kara said with forced levity, trying to keep the mood light and Andrea present in the conversation as the music managed to get through to her a bit. “What about him and Britney?”

     

                “Yeah, I just always thought he was a dick, you know? Never understood the appeal.”

     

                “Ah, unfortunately, I would’ve fallen for that trap. Bad habit, I guess.”

     

                “You should turn left here,” Andrea said again, tapping the window.

     

                “Oh, I was just taking a shortcut.”

     

                “It’s quicker.”

     

                “Is it? I didn’t realise.”

     

                Nodding, Andrea took a sip of coffee and then skipped to the next song, falling suddenly silent. Kara continued on her way to the hospital, the traffic practically nonexistent and the hospital not too far from where she’d been. Everything seemed pretty local once you were properly Downtown, and she knew the park wasn’t a far drive. 

     

                Still, she hadn’t managed to reach the hospital before her phone started to ring. Glancing down at it in the centre console, Kara’s heart lurched in her chest as the name on the screen and she tried to answer with shaky hands, dividing her attention between the road and her phone.

     

                “Hello? Hello? Kara, are you- Kelly said you-“

     

                The sound of Lena’s distraught voice after six weeks suffused Kara with such intense longing that she thought she might fall apart then and there. Managing to rein her emotions in, not wanting to make Andrea restless and uneasy, Kara’s voice trembled slightly as she cut Lena off.

     

                “I’ve got her. She’s fine, I- I couldn’t reach you so I’m almost at the hospital so- so someone can take a look at her. The General one.”

     

                “I know, Kelly said-“

     

                “I’m a few minutes out.”

     

                “I’m here.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                There was a prolonged moment, fraught with the tension of all the unsaid things between them. Kara’s throat closed up around the lump there and she clutched the wheel tightly to stop her hands from shaking.

     

                “Kara, I'm-“

     

                “See you in a bit.”

     

                She hung up before Lena could finish her sentence. Fear and panic threatened to overwhelm Kara and the car was silent for a beat before the music started back up, blinking back the burning pressure in her eyes. She could feel Andrea’s eyes on her as she drove.

     

                “You’re upset.”

     

                “Yes,” Kara softly admitted.

     

                Reaching over, Andrea pulled her right hand free from the wheel and held it in her lap. “It’s okay.”

     

                Letting out a frayed laugh, Kara nodded and squeezed her hand. The bright lights of the hospital approached shortly afterwards, windows of the wards and private rooms cutting through the darkness, and she pulled into the parking lot and found a spot as close as possible.

     

                “Where are we?”

     

                Easing the cup of coffee from Andrea’s hand, Kara set it in the cup holder and unbuckled both of their seatbelts.

     

                “We’re at the hospital.”

     

                “Oh. For the charity event?”

     

                “Yes,” Kara whispered, smiling thinly. “Yes, they were hoping to speak to you, maybe get a quick photo for tomorrow’s paper.”

     

                Sighing, Andrea reached for the door. “Alright. We’ll have to make it quick. I- I’m meeting someone. I’m not- I’m not supposed to be here. How-”

     

                “I’ll get the door,” Kara said as she grabbed her phone and the car keys and quickly climbed out, shutting her own door.

     

                She rounded the car and helped Andrea out, giving her a warm smile, pain cutting through her anew. Guilt crept up on her at the deception and she gently shut the door and took her hand, squeezing reassuringly.

     

                “This way,” she murmured, her voice wobbling.

     

                Leading Andrea towards the bright lights of the Emergency Department lobby, Kara’s throat felt tight and she watched as a dark figure came running towards them. Lena looked haggard, her eyes bloodshot, ringed with dark circles and yesterday’s smudged makeup as she bore down on them with a ragged sound of relief that cut cleanly through Kara.

     

                “Oh God,” she breathlessly wept, barrelling into her wife, wrapping her in a tight hug, her eyes squeezed shut and teeth bared as she sobbed. 

     

                Kara let go of Andrea’s hand as Lena engulfed her, her hitching sobs slurring into breathless babbling. Her hands fluttered nervously over her wife, reassuring herself that she was fine, and Andrea closed her eyes, expression clouding as she shook her head and then jerked back as Lena tried to cup her face.

     

                “I- no, no,” she murmured before her voice grew louder. “No, I- I don’t know you. Stop. Stop.”

     

                Shoving Lena away, Andrea shied towards Kara with a sullen, apprehensive look on her face. A tentative smile broke out on Lena’s face as she held her hands up defensively and took a cautious step in as Kara was left watching the reunion with the nauseating feeling of unease at the blatant display of love from Lena and the resulting antsy blankness from Andrea.

     

                “Hey, it’s me,” Lena murmured, her expression faltering. “It’s alright, you’re safe now. You should come inside. Come with me. Come on.”

     

                Reaching out to snag her hand, Lena suddenly closed the gap between them and Andrea tried to jerk her hand back. Panic flashed across her face and she shook her head. “No, I don’t want to.”

     

                “I- Andrea-“

     

                “I want to go home.”

     

                “Let me-“

     

                Yanking her hand free, anger flashed across Andrea’s face and she hit Lena across the cheek, quick and firm, the heavy impact of her cast sending Lena staggering slightly. Kara blinked, stunned by the fleeting moment of aggression, and reacted quickly, stepping between them as she grabbed Andrea’s bicep.

     

                Wrapping her arms around Andrea she pinned her arms to her sides, effectively immobilising her for the time being. Struggling in her embrace, Andrea snarled a few words in Spanish that Kara knew enough curses to recognise, and a broken sound of helplessness came out as barely more than a whimper when she couldn’t break Kara’s hold. Softly shushing her, Kara swayed them both as she rubbed her back as she hummed and then haltingly started to sing.

     

    “Baby, please try to forgive me

    Stay here don't put out the glow

    Hold me now don't bother

    If every minute it makes me weaker

    You can save me from the man that I've become, oh yeah

     

    Looking back on the things I've done

    I was trying to be someone

    I played my part, kept you in the dark

    Now let me show you the shape of my heart”

     

                She wasn’t sure it would help at all but Andrea had liked the music in the car, loved Backstreet Boys, Britney and NSYNC, and like a child soothed by a lullaby, she calmed down at the gentle murmur of Kara’s voice. Resting her head on Kara’s shoulder as they swayed, she closed her eyes and started to mumble the lyrics and Kara’s eyes landed on Lena as she’d managed to sway them in an arc.

     

                White as a ghost, save for her quickly reddening cheek, Lena watched with wounded yearning painfully visible in her teary green eyes. She was making a brave effort to keep her composure, and Kara could see she wanted to be the one holding her wife, calming her down instead of being seen as a threat. 

     

                A car door slammed nearby a moment later and footsteps rushed across the asphalt, Alex and Kelly arriving with harried looks of exhaustion. No one moved or spoke, keeping a safe distance away and Kara kept singing until she finished the song. Once her singing tapered off, she swayed them for a moment longer before pulling back slightly.

     

                “Andrea, do you want to come inside with me?”

     

                “Inside?”

     

                “Yes, it’s warmer there. We can finish our coffee.”

     

                “Where are we?”

     

                “At the hospital.”

     

                “Oh. Can I go home?”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara whispered, giving her a gentle squeeze. “Yes, you can go home. But come with me first, okay?”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                Slowly letting her go, Kara gave her a quick smile and drew in a shuddering breath as she stepped back. Then Andrea reached out for her hand and Kara made a small sound of surprise before giving her a sweet smile and squeezing her fingers.

     

                “Let’s go,” she murmured, jerking her head toward the entrance.

     

                Guiding her towards the hospital, the other three women slowly shepherded her inside, trying not to make her skittish at their presence. Kara started to hum a different song, an NSYNC one this time, trying to occupy Andrea’s mind to keep her from fighting against entering the hospital.

     

                Once they were over the threshold, Alex made towards the nurse’s station where the patients were admitted and spoke quietly to one of them before opening a door and gesturing them through. Kara couldn’t shake Andrea’s grip, not until they had her stretched out on a bed, admitted for a checkup. 

     

                “I’ll do this one,” Alex told an Intern that hurried over.

     

                Once her hand was freed, Kara hesitated a moment before she turned and left, slipping through the curtain and making her way outside. Kelly had stayed in the lobby and Kara was caught up in her own thoughts, rubbing her forehead as she tried to wrap her head around it, and walked straight past her. 

     

                Her sister-in-law quickly followed and as Kara walked through the automatic doors and into the night air, Kelly’s hand fell on her shoulder. “Hey.”

     

                Turning, Kara ducked her head and practically fell on Kelly, the first broken sob escaping her as she buried her face in her sister-in-law’s shoulder. Chest heaving with violent sobs, Kara gripped fistfuls of Kelly’s cardigan as she let all the pent-up anxiety come rushing out of her. It was like a flood of emotions, unstoppable and overwhelming, and Kelly hugged her tightly, patting her back as she murmured sympathetic platitudes.

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara cried when she finally found the strength to draw back. Wiping her cheeks on the backs of her hands, her arms pimpling from the cold wind as she shivered in her t-shirt, she quietly sobbed. “I’m sorry, I- oh, God. That was … awful. Oh my God, it’s like- it’s like-”

     

                “I know,” Kelly softly sighed, shoulders slumping from a long night. “It’s a shock, I know, but it’s alright. She’ll be okay.”

     

                “I didn’t know,” Kara choked out, covering her mouth with a hand as she shook her head, a lost look of disbelief in her eyes. “How can- how can she just … be like that? She doesn’t even know her, Kelly.”

     

                “Yeah. It’s a difficult one to watch.”

     

                Cheeks blotchy and eyes bloodshot, Kara managed to get her hitching breaths under control and she paced back and forth outside the doors to the lobby of the Emergency Department as she waited. With Alex seeing them straight through and doing the checkup herself, it significantly reduced the wait time but it was still forty minutes before her sister stepped through the automatic doors with news.

     

                “She’s fine,” Alex informed them, running a hand through her hair and blinking owlishly against the heaviness in her eyes. “I’ve done a checkup, they’re just doing an x-ray on her arm to make sure she didn’t injure it any further.”

     

                Nodding, Kara wiped her damp eyes and swallowed thickly. “Thank you.”

     

                “You alright?” Alex gently murmured, resting a hand on Kara’s shoulder and coaxing her into a hug. 

     

                “Yeah, it’s just … horrible.”

     

                Smoothing her hair, Alex rocked her for a moment and then pulled back. Her face was soft with sadness and pity and she squeezed her sister’s arm. “I know. We should go home. It’s been a long night.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara slowly shook her head. “No, I- I’m going to wait.”

     

                “Kara, there’s nothing you can do now.”

     

                “I know. I just- I want to make sure Lena’s okay. She got hit pretty hard.”

     

                “Yeah, I saw. I got a nurse to fetch her some ice. Probably be a nasty bruise there tomorrow.”

     

                “Thank you,” Kara gravelly replied.

     

                Pausing, Alex softly sighed and then accepted that Kara wouldn’t be budging anytime soon. Unzipping her leather jacket, she held it out to her and gave her a grim smile. “Here. It’s too cold to stand around outside; go into the lobby. They’ll let you wait.”

     

                Nodding, her throat closed up, Kara shrugged her sister’s jacket on, the smell of worn leather and Alex’s perfume a comfort as her wrists stuck out of the cuffs of the too-small jacket. Hugging Alex again, and then Kelly, Kara felt depleted and empty as she ran a hand through her hair and let out a heavy sigh.

     

                “Thank you for looking,” she rasped.

     

                “Of course,” her sister murmured, giving her a wan smile.

     

                Pale and face drawn with worry, Kara was left alone to wait and made her way into the lobby to take a seat. The harsh fluorescents made her eyelids heavy, the urge to sleep almost overwhelming as the adrenaline of the evening fled and Kara was left limp as she breathed in the antiseptic smell of the hospital, listening to the muffled intercom and eyeing the patients waiting to be seen. A blonde woman arrived in mint green scrubs and was let through and ambulances pulled up outside, paramedics unloading gurneys as patients were rushed in and admitted for serious injuries.

     

                Considering getting one of those awful coffees from the vending machine, Kara was quietly restless as the night dragged on. It was past four o’clock by the time the door opened and Andrea was wheeled out by the woman she’d seen enter in mint green scrubs. Lena walked beside her, holding Andrea’s good hand while a nurse spoke to her. 

     

                Climbing to her feet, stiff and aching from not moving for so long, Kara drew Lena’s attention, watching her eyes flicker over to her as she nodded to what the nurse said and then do a double-take as she realised it was Kara. Warily approaching, Kara shadowed the group outside and watched as a van with Leviathan’s Respite Centre splashed across the side idled outside. 

     

                Hanging back, Kara was fidgety as she watched a man climb out of the van and help the woman get Andrea into the back of the van. They buckled her in and Lena murmured something to her wife before kissing the knuckles of her left hand and stepping back as the door slid shut. The two people in mint scrubs conversed quietly with Lena, nodding as they all stood close together, and then Lena’s shoulders slumped and the man gave her shoulder a quick pat.

     

                They climbed into the front of the van, the man driving, and the van lurched into motion a moment later, leaving Lena behind. She didn’t pause, didn’t even look at Kara, although she must have known she was there, setting off towards where she’d parked her car. Hurrying after her, Kara’s heart felt like it was in her throat, her voice wavering as she called after her.

     

                “Lena.”

     

                Without pausing, Lena waved a hand dismissively, keeping her back to Kara. Her voice was thick with pain when she replied though, trembling and vulnerable, and Kara had seen her cry enough times to know how her face would look.

     

                “I need to go.”

     

                “Lena, wait-”

     

                Kara lunged forward, her long legs closing the distance so she could snag Lena’s arm, trying to stop her. Stiffening at the contact, Lena grabbed Kara’s wrist in turn, the two of them face-to-face in a standoff as Lena clenched her teeth, a resentful look on her face as she didn’t quite look at Kara.

     

                “I’m grateful to you for finding her but I don’t have time for this. This isn’t any of your business.”

     

                “But-”

     

                “Go home, Kara. Just … leave me alone.”

     

                Pulling Kara’s hand off her, Lena let go and then turned around, leaving Kara standing in the middle of the car park with a lost, wounded look on her face. She was still standing there when the headlights of the Lexus flashed in the darkness as Lena unlocked it, the sound of the engine starting and gravel crunching beneath the wheels cutting through the quiet of the night.

     

                It was cold and late and Kara couldn’t remember ever feeling so exhausted in her life, feeling like the night would never end, even though dawn was barely an hour away. Defeated, after a few minutes she finally managed to make herself move, socked feet pricked by the gravelly chips of the asphalt, and she slowly trudged back to Alex’s car and climbed inside.

     

                Sitting there for another five minutes, staring at the two Starbucks cups nestled in the holders, Kara felt so empty that she could almost believe she was grieving for the loss of a woman she’d never known. It hit her hard, the harsh slap of Lena’s reality, and Kara finally understood why she hadn’t gotten better, why it had only gotten worse for her, and finally understood how Lena could grieve as deeply as she had without suffering the loss of life. 

     

                It was a horrifying realisation and Kara’s bottom lip trembled the entire drive back to her sister’s, the deafening silence of the car as she refused to put on her music to fill the gap, the passenger seat empty and her heartache fresh. Parking outside, she climbed out of the car and brought the coffee cups with her, making her way inside and taking the stairs as she plodded up two flights and quietly let herself into the apartment. The lights were off and Alex and Kelly had gone to bed.

     

                Kara stood just inside the door for a few minutes as she held the coffee cups in hand, long since cold, and the start of the sunrise was starting to lighten the darkness of the apartment, black turning to a deep blue. Faltering, Kara just looked confused by the whole thing, unsure how she was supposed to just go about her life now, with no Lena, none of her business. 

     

                Making her way into the spare room, hovering in the doorway as she removed her filthy socks before treading on the new carpet, Kara moved stiffly, feeling out of sorts as she moved to the bed and set the Starbucks cups down on the nightstand. Sitting on the edge of the bed, she sagged on the mattress, elbows on her thighs and shoulders sloping as she put her head in her hands and softly started to cry again, this time without holding back.

    Chapter 24

                Sunday felt extraordinarily long as Lena made her way back to Leviathan’s and stayed until Andrea was settled in, warm from a shower and dressed in clean pyjamas. She’d been wearing a crewneck that Lena immediately recognised as Kara’s and she took it with her when she finally left, past eight o’clock in the morning and exhausted from a sleepless night.

     

                Lena’s face was already swelling, the bluish beginnings of nasty bruising making itself known, and the left side of her face felt stiff and numb. Gemma, the head carer, had been on duty when Andrea had managed to slip out with a couple leaving after their own visit, too young and seemingly fine to have aroused suspicion as she was buzzed through the double sets of doors by a new receptionist and released into National City. Russell was scheduled for a night shift but had come in early as soon as the alert was sent out, police contacted and a Silver Alert chiming on phones within the nearby vicinity after a few hours had passed by and no one had found her.

     

                Driving in circles, Lena had been out of her mind with worry, crying intermittently, making phone calls to Obsidian North, calling Bernardo and Sam, and stopping at every place Andrea had loved to visit. She’d walked through the park for an hour to no avail, sticking to the spots they’d taken their lunch breaks together or walked Aristotle. She’d had to stop and refuel when her tank neared empty and continued her aimless driving as she lost hope of Andrea showing up at any of their usual haunts.

     

                The missed calls from Kara had only served to bother Lena, lacking the energy to speak to her right then, even though six weeks had been far too long without her. She’d stopped rejecting the calls after the third earlier that evening, letting her phone ring out and vibrate with texts. It wasn’t until Kelly’s name kept lighting up her screen that she had an inkling that maybe something was wrong. Lena wasn’t sure she could cope with anything else but she had to know, only to find out Kara had somehow found Andrea.

     

                Lena had made a sharp u-turn and was anticipating two speeding fines in the mail by the time she made it to the hospital, backtracking the moment Kelly mentioned where Kara was heading. She’d then called her friend, her lover, whatever she was, barely keeping it together as she felt relief flood through her at Andrea’s safety, cringing at the thought of Kara alone with her, that glimpse of Lena’s reality without her to mediate. She’d been desperate and out of her mind and hadn’t even seen the strike coming, blinding pain catching her off guard as she tasted blood and blinked past it to try and coax her wife inside.

     

                It had all been a drag after that, a blur of Alex’s reassurances as she checked Andrea over, her fleeting glances towards Lena as if biting back a dozen questions about the situation. Gemma had arrived a short while after Andrea had been admitted, joining Lena behind the curtain as they waited until she was cleared, until the x-ray results came through with no further damage to her fractured arm. Once a doctor had signed off on Andrea’s discharge, Lena made her way back outside and had shaken Kara off and went straight to the centre. 

     

                After she’d gotten home, she’d fallen straight into bed with Kara’s crewneck, curling herself around it as the familiar smell of her mingled faintly with Andrea’s perfume wrapped around her, a soothing, yet agonising thing to clutch onto. Lena cried herself to sleep and slept until late in the afternoon, waking to a dull pain on the left side of her face as she blinked back the gritty feeling in her eyes. Her appearance had been shocking when she’d gone to shower, her skin mottled with dark bruising and evidence of not enough sleep.

     

                Changing into clean clothes, she’d fussed over Aristotle for a moment, making sure he had food and water before she pulled on a coat and grabbed her keys. She went shopping for a little while after that, a large pair of sunglasses trying to hide the bruising as she picked up things for Andrea and then drove to Leviathan’s, feeling like she’d only just left.

     

                Lena avoided work on Monday, given the state of her face, and waited until the evening to visit Andrea, needing some time to just be. She walked Aristotle and kept her face covered behind her sunglasses as she bought a coffee and sat in the park for a while before heading home to brood over her circumstances. Skipping dinner, she climbed behind the wheel of her car and made the short drive to Leviathan’s. Signing it at the front desk, Lena rode the elevator up to Andrea’s floor and found Russell watching soccer on his phone as he sat behind the computer amidst a sea of paperwork. Straightening up at Lena’s arrival, he grinned and raised his eyebrows slightly.

     

                “Afternoon.”

     

                “Hey, how’s she doing?”

     

                “In a really good mood. The new one has a special touch with her. You chose well.”

     

                Looking confused, Lena swept past the desk with a snort, calling back over her shoulder. “New carer? Why am I getting congratulated for that?”

     

                Russell looked momentarily perplexed before he opened his mouth to respond but Lena was already nearing Andrea’s open door and then came to an abrupt stop. Her eyes immediately found Andrea’s face but quickly cut to Kara, who was sitting cross-legged on the bed across from Andrea, who was doing her makeup. Visibly paling, Lena’s lips parted with surprise, her stomach lurching, and Kara’s eyes cracked open a fraction as Andrea jostled the bed, climbing off it.

     

                She walked over to Lena with a cluelessly delighted look on her face, smiling warmly as she hugged her. Lena’s expression faltered before softening as she gently hugged her back, her heart twinging in her chest as a sense of relief swept through her. On the good days, Andrea was sweet, loving Lena even though she couldn’t remember why, and Lena cherished those days. 

     

                “Hey, you,” she murmured, rubbing Andrea’s back.

     

                Pulling back, Andrea kissed her cheek, right over the mottled black and blue bruise marring the left side of Lena’s face. As she stepped back, Andrea’s face furrowed and she reached up as if to touch the bruise, her mouth turning down at the corners.

     

                “You’re hurt.”

     

                “Oh, no, it’s okay,” Lena quickly assured her. 

     

                “You’re hurt.”

     

                “It’s fine. Look,” she poked her cheek as softly as she could, masking a wince at the bright pain that suffused her. “Doesn’t even hurt.”

     

                The ice pack she’d been given at the hospital had helped with the swelling but it was a brutally nasty mottle of dark bruises. Lena knew she wouldn’t even attempt to go to work for the rest of the week with the sight of her, her cheekbone tender and swollen and a few blood vessels in her eye bursting, giving her a ghastly bloodshot look in the corner of her left eye. It wasn’t so bad though, just a little harder than the usual mishaps thanks to the addition of the cast. Lena was just glad she hadn’t broken her eye socket or cheek.

     

                Andrea curiously touched her fingers to Lena’s cheek, barely a brush but still present enough for the left side of Lena’s face to twitch, a quietly shuddering breath escaping her as she tried not to show her pain. Lena gave her a thin smile, learning the mistake of smiling fully the day before when she’d visited. They’d gone through a similar thing then, Andrea’s eyes filling with tears as she’d fussed over Lena, not recognising her at all but still knowing her on some level, knowing her enough for that innate empathy and worry to surface. 

     

                “What are you doing?” Lena murmured, her eyes moving over to Kara, who looked sheepish at being there uninvited.

     

                Andrea turned, her face lighting up before she turned back to Lena and took her hand. “Makeup. We’re going out tonight. I’ll do yours.”

     

                Lena choked on a quiet laugh as she let her wife lead her to the bed, pointing for her to sit as she started to rummage through her makeup. An awkward tension filled the room as Lena sat a few feet away from Kara, her wife standing in between them as neither of them spoke or really acknowledged each other. 

     

                “Did you finish your essay?” Andrea asked, holding a handful of lipsticks as she inspected the colours and then jerked her head up to give Kara an expectant look.

     

                Blinking in surprise, one eyelid clumsily powdered with eyeshadow and her cheeks exuberantly rouged, Kara opened and closed her mouth, caught off guard. “Me? Oh, um, yes, last night.”

     

                Eyes flitting sideways, Lena was stiff and surprised as she listened to Kara play along. The breath caught in her throat as her chest ached and she closed her eyes as she tried to reconcile these two parts of her life being in the same place, two people she loved and two people who would never know each other properly. 

     

                “¿Qué color?”

     

                Lena opened her eyes to three lipsticks presented to her. Reaching out, she tapped the red one. “El rojo, por favor.”

     

                “El rojo. El rojo es bonito.”

     

                “Sí. ¿Debo hacer la tuya roja?”

     

                “No, quiero rosa.”

     

                “¿Rosa?” Lena quietly laughed. “Pense que odiabas la rosa.”

     

                “I don’t hate pink.”

     

                “No? Is it your favourite colour?”

     

                “No, it’s- it’s … verde.”

     

                “Still?”

     

                “Yes, still green. I like green. It’s like … my wife’s eyes.”

     

                Lena closed her eyes, her stomach lurching as her lips parted and Andrea started to drag the red lipstick across her mouth. She drew in a shaky breath, used to this familiar bittersweet feeling of Andrea occasionally remembering she was married but never recognising her wife in front of her, and rarely remembering her wife’s name either.

     

                “You’re married?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “That’s nice. Do you remember her name?”

     

                She felt the touch of the lipstick vanish and opened her eyes to meet Andrea’s own clouded stare. Mouth turning down at the corners, she shook her head and then squeezed her eyes shut, a flush creeping into her cheeks.

     

                “No, I- I can’t- I don’t know. I don’t know. Don’t-”

     

                “That’s okay,” Lena murmured, reaching out to touch her hand.

     

                Pulling it back, Andrea frowned for a few more moments before her expression smoothed out. Letting out a quick laugh, she looked at the lipstick in her hands and rolled her eyes.

     

                “I almost forgot to do your eyes.”

     

                “You need to finish Kara’s as well,” Lena gently reminded her.

     

                “Kara? Who’s that?”

     

                “That’s Kara.”

     

                Lena gestured towards Kara, who had been sitting there silently the whole time. Blinking in surprise, Andrea smiled politely and extended a hand. “Oh, sorry. I’m Andrea.”

     

                Taking her good hand, Kara gently shook it. “It’s nice to meet you. I’m Kara.”

     

                “That’s a nice name.”

     

                “Thank you. So is yours.”

     

                “Do you want your makeup done? We’re going out for drinks,” Andrea said as she gestured between herself and Lena.

     

                Nose crinkling endearingly as she smiled, eyes creasing, Kara nodded. “I would love that.”

     

                Clearing her throat, Lena raised her eyebrows suggestively. “Should we put music on while we get ready?”

     

                “My CDs are over there,” Andrea dismissively waved at the corner of the room, devoid of any CDs.

     

                Lena fished out her phone and put on the Spotify playlist that had been Andrea’s favourite to play in the car, back when they’d been able to go places together. A song by the Spice Girls came on first and Andrea immediately started murmuring the words as she picked up an eyeshadow palette and started doing Kara’s other eye in a completely different shade.

     

                She went back and forth between the two women, applying foundation a few shades too dark for Lena to her face, Lena’s face a mask of pain as she subjected herself to the repetitive tapping of the sponge on her cheek to blend it in, while Kara had yet more blush added to her cheeks and then lipstick as well. Andrea’s motor skills weren’t as refined as they used to be, just one of a long line of side effects of her illness that was slowly declining but they both sat there patiently, silent with each other but keeping up a running conversation with Andrea to keep her mind focused on the task as the playlist progressed through a variety of 90s and early 2000s music.

     

                An hour passed by quickly and Lena watched her wife occasionally wander aimlessly around the room as she forgot what she’d been doing, until she or Kara managed to reel her back in. She still didn’t speak to Kara, or if it was in response to something she’d said, Lena would reply to no one, just stating her opinion or question to the room as she studiously avoided Kara’s eye. Eventually, they were disturbed by a knock on the doorframe and they all glanced towards it.

     

                “Sorry to break up the party, ladies,” Russell apologetically sighed, glancing down at his watch. “But it’s six-fifteen and dinner started fifteen minutes ago, so I need to take her down.”

     

                “Alright, let me just put her things away.”

     

                Lena paused the music and slowly climbed to her feet as Kara likewise got off the bed. Gathering up the scattered makeup products, Lena shoved it all into Andrea’s makeup bag and let her help before she neatened up the room. Hovering nervously at the sudden activity, the sudden silence without the music, Andrea shadowed her around the room as Lena put things away and opened up the bag she’d brought with her.

     

                “That’s not mine,” Andrea blurted out as Lena opened her closet to hang up a few new sweaters, soft pieces of cashmere, alpaca and Highland sheep wool neatly hanging alongside soft cotton sweatpants and twill shirts.

     

                “I bought it for you.”

     

                “Oh. Thank you.”

     

                “You’re welcome,” Lena murmured, touching her cheek as she smiled slightly. “Come see what else you have.”

     

                Andrea pulled out slippers and new socks, the bottles of expensive shampoo and conditioner and body wash Lena insisted on buying herself, instead of letting them use the products the centre bought in bulk. Twice a week, if she was lucky, she would wash Andrea’s hair for her if she was cooperative, blow dry it and apply serums that made it sleek and soft. These days, Andrea spent more time sleeping during the day, in between Lena’s morning and evening visits, as opposed to at night, so Lena had taken to rubbing lotions into her hands and applying moisturisers, retinol and sleep masks before she left, looking after her wife the way she’d looked after herself when she’d remembered to. 

     

                On almost every visit, Lena brought something for her. Whether it was new clothes, refills of hygiene products, a new blanket for cold nights or new bed sheets, diffusers for the room or the little macaroons Andrea liked from a patisserie a few blocks north of their apartment. Her wife didn’t notice half of the time or didn’t remember why she should have liked the products but Lena remembered, and Lena noticed, and Lena loved her enough to continue doing the little things to make Andrea’s life a little bit more comfortable at the respite centre, even when the other residents were slowly abandoned by their families as they shed the burden of their care. 

     

                “Right, all done,” she murmured a few minutes later. “Are you hungry?”

     

                “Hungry? I … I’m hungry.”

     

                “Should we go down to dinner?”

     

                “Dinner. Yes, what’s for dinner?”

     

                “We’ll get you a menu once you’re in the restaurant, shall we?”

     

                “Oh, we’re eating out tonight? I should get dressed.”

     

                Lena caught her hand as Andrea started looking around, a stern look on her face. “You already look beautiful. We’re going to miss our reservation.”

     

                “Oh. Okay.”

     

                Squeezing her hand, Lena nodded and started leading her towards the door, where Russell was waiting and Kara beyond, already in the hallway. Going slowly, she led Andrea towards the elevator and Russell used his card to activate it, taking them down to the ground floor. The four of them stepped out and Andrea slightly swung her and Lena’s joined hands as she looked around with open curiosity on her face as Lena guided her towards the dining room and paused as the short hallway forked.

     

                “Hey, time to say goodbye,” Lena murmured, an ache in her chest as the time to go home alone arrived again.

     

                Andrea hugged her, closing her eyes and resting her cheek on Lena’s shoulder for a moment. Her own eyes squeezed tightly shut, a grave look on her face as she held her close, basking in the familiarity of that embrace, of the perfume and shampoo that was so wholly her wife, Lena held on for as long as possible. 

     

                Pulling back, Andrea hesitated and then kissed her quickly, and Lena let out a small laugh. “Thank you.”

     

                The smile on Andrea’s face faltered slightly as she raised a hand to touch Lena’s face. “You’re hurt.”

     

                “I’m okay. I have to go; I’ll see you in the morning.”

     

                “Good morning.”

     

                Face crumpling with agonised weariness, Lena took her hand and squeezed it before kissing her knuckles. “Good morning.”

     

                Her eyes landed on Kara then and she swallowed thickly. “Do you want to say goodbye to Kara as well?”

     

                “Kara?”

     

                “Yes, she’s a friend. She’s over there.”

     

                “Oh, yes. Hello,” Andrea brightly greeted Kara, pulling her hand from Lena’s grasp and holding it out to shake Kara’s.

     

                She wrapped her in a hug then and kissed her quickly and Kara blinked, her eyes widening a fraction, startled and helpless before Andrea let her go just as quickly. “Um … hello.”

     

                Cringing, Lena quickly wrapped an arm around Andrea’s shoulders and firmly guided her away, her mouth a grim line. Leading her towards the dining room’s open archway where other residents were already eating their dinner while carers drifted about and waitstaff delivered meals and drinks, Lena paused. Gesturing towards it, her throat closed up.

     

                “You have a table booked.”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “Go and eat and I’ll see you tomorrow.”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “I love you.”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                Russell took over from there and Lena drew in a shuddering breath, closing her eyes and standing there for a long minute. Forcing herself to move, she turned and her eyes flickered over to Kara and then towards the door before she quickly set off, her frustration catching up with her as she quickly made her way towards the lobby, passing through the first set of doors to the open reception area and then buzzed through the two sets of doors leading out to the mild evening.

     

                She could hear Kara’s running shoes squeaking behind her as she followed and Lena felt the building urge to cry, her frustration making her eyes sting as she had so many things to say, her resentment building over the last six weeks. Of course, it was entirely brought on by her omission of the truth but it hurt that Kara hadn’t looked past that to understand Lena’s situation. It was so difficult - to talk about, to cope with, to live it every day - and she hadn’t wanted to drag Kara into that while she was trying to manage her own grief, hadn’t wanted to drag her into her marriage problems when they weren’t together, when it wasn’t Kara’s responsibility to bear. But it hadn’t been entirely selflessly motivated either; Lena had liked the reprieve from her ordinary life enough to warrant keeping the lie going.

     

                “Lena-”

     

                “I can’t do this. Really, I- thank you for the other night, for looking for her, I’m so grateful, but please leave me alone.”

     

                “Hey.”

     

                Kara’s voice was achingly soft and Lena all but fell apart the second her fingers grazed her shoulders. Shaking with the heaving sobs that overcame her, she paused in the middle of the parking lot and hunched over, burying her face in her hands as she cried loudly, her pain so raw that she couldn’t hold it in any longer. Slowly sinking to a crouch, Lena cried freely, the ragged sound scratching her throat as tears wet her cheeks and her nose ran and her face hurt and her heart hurt and everything hurt. 

     

                And then Kara was crouching in front of her, trying to coax Lena’s hands away from her face as Lena resisted, until it made Lena angry and she cursed Kara out in between the broken sounds of her grief. Curling in on herself, she hid away from the world like a little kid, her face full of makeup smudging into a mess on her mess of a face. In the end, Kara resorted to just wrapping Lena in her arms, sinking onto her knees and cupping the back of her head as she rubbed her back with her other hand.

     

                Slowly but surely, the sorely missed comfort of her presence coaxed Lena out of her isolated ball of pain and she scrabbled for fistfuls of Kara’s scrubs, clutching her so tightly she wrinkled the fabric as she buried her face in her chest. Kara cried too, quietly and unobtrusively as she let Lena get it all out, all the festering anger and hurt and gut-wrenching sadness, holding her close as they both slowly sagged as fatigue settled in now that they were outside of the centre.

     

                For thirty minutes, Lena cried nonstop, breathless and hitching towards the end as she exhausted herself, and twice carers arriving for their night shifts approached and were held at bay by Kara’s held-up hand, mouthing reassurances. For her own part, Kara just held Lena, murmuring quiet platitudes into her hair and rubbing her back as she waited for her to finish. There was nothing else for it and all Lena needed to do then was get it out. 

     

                Eventually, the sobs subsided to shallow, uneven breaths as she pressed her face into Kara’s shoulder, as close as she could get, and Lena felt utterly depleted. Her face was bone white, save for the nasty bruising and slightly swollen left side of her face, her cheeks blotchy and eyes bloodshot, and she looked every inch of the mess she felt inside, usually kept so tightly under wraps. Now it was all out in the open and there was no need for the pretence. 

     

                Sniffing, she swallowed the thick lump in her throat and stiffly drew back, her body aching from the slumped position she’d taken up on the asphalt. Pushing herself to her feet, she felt a strong hand cup her elbow as Kara rose with her, guiding her up. Lena couldn’t look at her, just stared down at their feet - her polished leather boots and Kara’s scuffed running shoes - biting the inside of her lip as she tried to find her voice, the awkwardness of the moment prolonged and unbearably thick.

     

                “Why’d you come?” she finally rasped. 

     

                “I just wanted to make sure she was okay.”

     

                Letting out a frayed laugh, hot tears trickled down Lena’s cheeks and she ran her coat sleeve over her face. “No, Kara, she’s not okay .”

     

                “I know,” Kara defeatedly replied, her voice pained. “But she’s your wife and I … I love you.”

     

                Eyelids shuttering, Lena let out a wisp of a sigh, her shoulders slumping. She’d wanted to hear that six weeks ago, wanted to know that it wouldn’t have changed a thing that her wife was alive and sick, that things wouldn’t have changed between them. That had been wishful thinking, the way it was wishful thinking to hope for a cure one day, for her wife to suddenly regain the clarity of her mind and remember her, come home to their apartment and resume their life, the way they’d thought it would be. Lena knew she very rarely got what she wished for. God knew she’d tried enough, making quiet prayers, trying to bargain with some unseen force, that if she kept her promises it would all be over. But Lena knew that grief didn’t strike bargains, that there was no way of avoiding the agony of a torturously slow goodbye, no hope of even getting through it faster. 

     

                It had held her in its claws for six years now, barely a whisper at first, when Andrea was home and the avenues of her mind hadn’t been shut off to her, and then in an iron fist when she’d wound up at Leviathan’s and Lena had been left with empty wishes and hollow promises. More tears slid down her cheeks as she kept her eyes closed, and it wasn’t until Kara’s cool fingers cupped her chin and urged her head up that she finally faced her.

     

                Kara’s eyes were fixated on the left side of Lena’s face, her mouth thin with displeasure, her thumb a gentle brush over the lower part of Lena’s cheek, making sure she didn’t hurt her. Mouth twitching at the corners, Kara’s eyes finally met Lena’s, unwavering but bright with pain and guilt.

     

                “And I wanted to make sure you were okay, and I know you’re not either but … I wanted to know and I was too scared to go to you first so …”

     

                “Scared,” Lena quietly scoffed.

     

                “Yes.”

     

                Lips twitching ruefully, Lena sniffed and ducked her head, fiddling with the straps of her handbag. Her voice was quiet and resigned when she spoke.

     

                “I should go. Can I drop you-”

     

                “Can we go somewhere-”

     

                They spoke at the same time and Lena choked on a laugh as Kara let out a strained one, rubbing the back of her neck. Sighing heavily, Lena jerked her head towards the Lexus.

     

                “Come on.”

     

                She climbed behind the wheel and buckled herself in before fishing tissues out of her bag and folding down the visor to open the little mirror. Clicking her tongue as she hoarsely laughed at her appearance, red lipstick smudged around her mouth, patches of foundation that looked almost orangey against her pallor, and raccoon-looking eyeshadow, Lena tried her best to wipe it off. She had a packet of antibacterial wipes in the door of her car for dust and resorted to them and handed it over to Kara.

     

                “I was going to say but …” Kara weakly murmured as she took a wipe and tried to remove her own makeup as best as she could.

     

                After a few minutes, Lena started the car and inhaled deeply before exhaling forcefully. Hesitating as she gripped the wheel, she closed her eyes and then sighed, shaking her head.

     

                “Are you hungry?”

     

                “I- um … I thought-“

     

                “Are you hungry?”

     

                “It’s seven o’clock,” Kara quietly laughed. “You know me; I’m starving.”

     

                Cheeks shallowly dimpling with a smile that made her wince with pain, softly hissing as the left side of her face flared up, Lena reversed out of her spot. They didn’t speak as she drove them through the city until she found the first neon sign for Big Belly Burger.

     

                Pulling into the queue of cars, she grabbed her purse and slid out her credit card and inched forward with the flow of traffic until she reached the speaker box. It crackled with the voice on the other end and she leaned out of the window.

     

                “Can I please get two large cheeseburger meals? One with a strawberry milkshake and the other one with a Coke. And an extra pickled on the side, please. Thank you.”

     

                Shrinking back into the car, Lena held her credit card between her index and middle fingers as she gripped the wheel and moved forward. Kara was watching her from the corner of her eye and she did a double-take when she spotted it, raising her eyebrows.

     

                “What?”

     

                “Nothing, I just- you remembered the pickle.”

     

                Snorting, Lena’s mouth twisted wryly. “I would remember your order even if you ignored me for the next six years .”

     

                “I wasn’t- I wasn’t ignoring you, I just-“

     

                “No?” Lena haughtily replied, a brittle edge to the word.

     

                She pulled up at the window and handed over her card before slipping it back into her purse. They were silent as they waited for their order, and Lena thanked the man that handed over their drinks and a paper bag with their order. Handing the bag over to Kara once the drinks were settled in the cup holders, Lena closed the window and drove off. After a few minutes, Kara opened her mouth and tried again, meek and apologetic.

     

                “I wasn’t ignoring you.”

     

                “What else would you call it?”

     

                “I thought it would be better to … I don’t know, have space to think?”

     

                Lena’s lip curled slightly as she made a right turn at the next intersection. There was a shakiness in her chest as she swallowed dryly. “Well, I’m glad you could do that for yourself,” she sarcastically replied. “I hope you enjoyed your peaceful little break to figure things out while I-“

     

                “You didn’t call either.”

                

                “Because I knew you wouldn’t want me to,” Lena thickly replied, her eyes burning with tears.

     

                “Of course I did! Of course I wanted you to call, to- to make me feel like you … wanted me. Like I mattered to you.”

     

                Sharply yanking the wheel to the right, Lena pulled up onto the side of the road, parallel parking at a bit of an angle as she yanked up the handbrake and put the car in park. Turning in her seat, her vision blurred as her chest rose and fell quickly with her growing anger.

     

                “I begged you not to go. You knew I wanted you; I begged you to stay. To listen. Don’t you dare make this about me not making you feel like you mattered .”

     

                Splaying her hands, Kara faced her with wide eyes, her voice uneven as she stressed her response. “You have a wife. You talked about her like she was still everything to you and now I know that she is . This whole fucking time. It’s me who’s nothing to you.”

     

                “That is not true,” Lena harshly whispered, wiping her cheeks. “You are all that I have. Yes, I love her and I’m sorry if that- I know it wasn’t fair to keep that from you and then drop it all on you at once, it just- it hasn’t been easy for me to figure it out, loving the two of you but … she doesn’t remember . Sometimes- sometimes she remembers she was married, sometimes she remembers she went to school with me, but she doesn’t know it’s me. When I sit in front of her … I could be anyone. She remembers virtually nothing of our life together. The details, the specific moments … they’ve all faded away. She doesn’t know who I am anymore; she hasn’t recognised me for months.”

     

                “And you still visit every day?”

     

                “She doesn’t know who I am, but … I know who she is.”

     

                The fight drained from Kara and her face furrowed with concern as she reached out to gently cup Lena’s cheek. Closing her eyes, Lena let out a shaky breath. “I don’t expect you to understand-“

     

                “I do,” Kara whispered. “I do now. I- it shouldn’t have taken me seeing it to know but … I don’t think I could’ve understood if I hadn’t. I just- she was missing and she’s your wife. How could I not look for her? How could I pretend as if I didn’t care? Even if that was it for you and me … she’s your wife, and you love her.”

     

                “I do,” Lena tearfully agreed. “And I love you too. It’s just been … so difficult . All this guilt .”

     

                Kara let out a hoarse laugh, running a hand over her face, “you know, I always used to think you were reacting as if you’d mistakenly had an affair.”

     

                Choking on a laugh, Lena gave Kara a sharp look before her face softened with amusement. Wiping her damp eyes, she sniffed. “Yeah. It felt that way at the start. The first time with you … I didn’t mean for it to happen but she hadn’t remembered me in weeks and I- I didn’t think she would again.”

     

                “And I was there,” Kara said with an awkward laugh that died in her mouth.

     

                “Yes,” Lena murmured. “Yes, you were there, but not … the way you mean it. You weren’t just there. I- there was something. I’d tried to deny it but then we’d been drinking and I was upset and I wanted to regret it but … I didn’t. That just made me feel like shit. She remembered me two days later and I couldn’t- I couldn’t look her in the eye.”

     

                She paused, drawing in a shuddering breath before swallowing thickly. “And then it happened again. Every time she didn’t remember me. I guess I kind of … liked how you numbed the pain,” Lena admitted, her lips a grim line of resignation. “When we met … I felt like I was drowning and … that wasn’t even the worst of it. You said back then that I hid it well, and that’s because … I still had her. Not all the time but sometimes , and it got worse and worse, but I had you. And you, my God , you made it all seem bearable. How could I not have fallen for you?” 

     

                Kara wiped her cheeks and looked down at her lap, holding the greasy bag with their food in her arms. Lena blew the air out of her cheeks and gripped the steering wheel tightly as the car idled. After a moment, she turned the engine off and gestured to the bag.

     

                “We should eat before it gets cold.”

     

                “Lena,” Kara wearily sighed.

     

                “It’s fine.”

     

                “No. No, it’s not.”

     

                “Well … I don’t want to talk about it. I just- I want to eat my cheeseburger and go home and sleep so I don’t have to be awake for all of this … shit.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara nodded after a moment and opened the crumpled bag. Fishing out a serving of fries, she passed them onto Lena, and then a burger as well. Angrily jamming a straw into her drink, Lena took a sip and cleared her throat. It felt dry and raw and she sniffed as she unwrapped the greaseproof paper of her burger.

     

                Taking a bite with little relish, Lena chewed glumly, a muscle twitching in her jaw as her anger simmered just below the surface. Really, she was just frustrated and tired, the emotional turbulence of the last few days leaving her sensitive and confused. Kara started to eat her own food and the silence felt awkward, filled with the rustling of paper and the clinking of ice in their cups.

     

                Kara took a bite of her big pickle, the crunch so loud in the close confines of the car that Lena couldn’t help but give her a baleful glance of exasperation. Flushing as she smiled weakly, Kara swallowed and set her pickle down.

     

                “Sorry,” she sheepishly murmured.

     

                It broke the tension a little and Lena set her burger down, sighing and reaching for a couple of fries. Her mouth twisted ruefully and she paused, her hand lowering as she glanced over at Kara again. 

     

                “How’ve you been?”

     

                “Oh … you know,” Kara shrugged, a furrowed look of dismay crossing her face. “It’s been a bit shit.”

     

                Lena snorted, lips twitching slightly with amusement. “Really? I wouldn’t have guessed.”

     

                “Mm,” Kara hummed before falling silent for a moment. Lena knew what was coming as soon as she drew in a shaky breath. “Lena, I’m sor-”

     

                “Stop,” Lena brusquely cut her off. “Don’t say anything else. I deserved your anger for not telling you sooner so don’t apologise for it. I think … maybe I also deserved your understanding but … I know it was a shock for you. And it’s not something that’s easy to understand.”

     

                Nodding, Kara took a bite of her burger, chewing slowly as she stared at her lap. After a couple of minutes of silence, she peeked sideways at her and hesitated, softly clearing her throat. “I understand now. Not really, but … I understand in the way you understand what it’s like for me. It’s- it’s different but … it’s all the same pain. I shouldn’t have said- it’s still a loss. ”

     

                “Yes,” Lena whispered, her voice gravelly.

     

                They lapsed into silence for a moment and then Kara looked at her again as she took a fry from her carton. “You speak Spanish?”

     

                Snorting, Lena rolled her eyes and fixed Kara with a tired look of amusement. “Of course I do. It’s her first language.”

     

                “Right.”

     

                “She speaks it more and more these days. She forgets words more in English.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “Still at Alex and Kelly’s?”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara murmured, hesitating before continuing. “But I’ve signed a lease for a new place. I move in at the end of the month.”

     

                “Oh.” Lena couldn’t squash the disappointment that gutted her, her stomach sinking and a lump catching in her throat as she accepted the news with as much grace as she could. “That’s … that’s really good. You know … you didn’t have to move out though.”

     

                Shrugging as her mouth twisted ruefully, Kara sighed heavily. “I know but … I did.”

     

                “I know. I-” Lena faltered, taking a sip of her Coke and trying again. “I wish you hadn’t. Aristotle … he misses you.”

     

                A quick hint of a smile crossed Kara’s face. “Oh, yeah? I miss him too. I hope he knows that.”

     

                “He does.”

     

                “Good.”

     

                “And I’ve stopped drinking - and smoking. Forty-seven days now.”

     

                “That’s really good,” Kara earnestly replied, her voice scratchy as she smiled.

     

                Nodding, Lena was pale and nervous, reaching out to thumb the little bottlecap inscribed with a 30 hanging from her car keys. She swallowed thickly, giving Kara a weak smile. 

     

                “I know I’m not an alcoholic but … you were right and it was a problem. I’ve been going to AA anyway, just for something to do. It’s about … as helpful as Group was for me but … I couldn’t go there so …”

     

                “Oh, well … I stopped going, actually. Haven’t been in … five weeks now? Must be.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “So if you want it … it’s yours.”

     

                Letting out a quiet scoff of laughter, Lena’s eyelids shuttered. “I never wanted it. I only went because of you.”

     

                “Not the donuts?”

     

                “I do miss them. AA has cookies; they’re always stale somehow. And the company is lacking.”

     

                Clicking her tongue, Kara sighed, “that’s disappointing.”

     

                “Mm, I was thinking about quitting. I just needed something to fill my Thursday nights,” Lena sighed, balling up her trash and leaning across to put it in the bag between Kara’s feet. 

     

                Kara was still finishing off her own food but Lena started the car, easing out into traffic and slowly driving towards Alex’s. They didn’t speak on the drive home, both of them burdened with their own thoughts and yesterday’s exhaustion, but Lena stewed in her feelings as she took the familiar turns, hating that she was taking Kara home and it wasn’t to her penthouse.

     

                Pulling up outside the lit lobby of the apartment building, Lena put the car in park. There was a restless shakiness in her chest, a sense of urgency building as Kara gathered up their trash and unbuckled her seatbelt. She opened the car door to climb out and Lena suddenly lunged across the centre console to grab her arm.

     

                “This is all the time we get,” Lena said, her voice low and trembling, her eyes wide and mournful. “So I know I lied to you but if- if you can find it in yourself to forgive me … please knock on my door. Or … pretend you forgot something at my place so you can come back for it. I- we just- we have so little time. ”

     

                Faltering, Lena let go of Kara’s arm as her stomach sank, pulling away as she was left weary and resigned to her fate now. Her eyes burned and her throat was tight and she didn’t want to beg but she didn’t want to lose her either. She might have had her wife but not in the way she wanted, and if she couldn’t have Andrea, she wanted Kara. It felt cruel to treat her as a second option, and it wasn’t how Lena intended it, but she didn’t know how to say it, how to articulate her tangled feelings.

     

                Kara was half out of the car and slowly climbed the rest of the way out. Her expression was slightly furrowed, her mouth pursed into a displeased line, and she didn’t say anything. Lena watched her straighten and pause, slipping one arm out of her denim jacket and then shifting the crumpled Big Belly Burger bag to her other hand to pull the jacket the rest of the way off. 

     

                Stooping, teeth worrying at her bottom lip with a guarded look in her blue eyes as their gaze briefly met, Kara set her jacket down on the passenger seat and shut the car door behind her, leaving a reason behind. 

    Chapter 25
