                The security guard let Kara into the lobby when he saw her through the tall windows, and she waved slightly as she smiled before the door buzzed and she opened it. The perfumed air was a gut punch of familiarity and she drifted towards the front desk and set down a coffee and thanked the man. 

     

                Moving towards the elevator, Kara stepped inside and hesitated before pressing the button for the penthouse. She felt a little jittery as she held the coffee tray and white box close to her chest, her throat already constricted with nerves as she rose quickly through the building and was spat out at the top. Drawing in a shaky breath, she walked down the hallway to Lena’s door.

     

                Kara hesitated and raised a hand, knocking on the door. Her heart was hammering in her chest and her skin felt clammy as she shifted restlessly. She didn’t know what she was going to say, didn’t know how to even begin, only that it was Thursday and she hadn’t stopped thinking about Lena since Monday, or for the last seven weeks really. 

     

                Seeing her again in the early hours of Sunday morning, seeing Andrea, had pushed her into motion, the realisation that Kara was deeply unhappy with her life, with the way things had gone. It didn’t matter how hard it was going to be, how confusing and difficult the situation was, she just kept going back to Eliza’s advice that they could have each other in their futures or not but either way they couldn’t have their partners back.

     

                Listening to the sound of scrabbling claws as Aristotle rushed to the door, slowly followed by quiet padding footsteps, the door was jerked open and Lena’s expression of mild curiosity fell into one of surprise as she held the dog at bay.

     

                “Oh,” Lena murmured, caught off guard by the sight of her. “Hi.”

     

                “Hi,” Kara hoarsely replied. “I, um … I think … I left my jacket in your car the other night.”

     

                Choking on a laugh, Lena arched an eyebrow, “did you? Well … you should come inside while I look for it.”

     

                Expression softening with a smile, the knot of worry in Kara’s chest loosened some and she stepped over the threshold. Letting go of Aristotle, Lena stepped back to give Kara room in the spacious hallway and Kara shut the door and awkwardly sank to a crouch as she balanced the coffee and the box, fussing over the Cavalier as he licked her chin. Eyes creasing at the corners as she laughed, she felt a lightness steal over her, that simple act of being missed by a dog making her feel like it would all be okay in the end. 

     

                Climbing back to her feet, Kara deposited her backpack on the floor and kicked off her running shoes before she followed Lena, who had retreated further inside and left her to find her own way. Crossing over to the sofa where Lena had curled up, Kara settled down a safe distance away after setting down the coffee and putting the box between them.

                

                “I, um, I thought … well, it’s Thursday and … it’s fifty days,” Kara slowly explained as she opened the white box to reveal a big chocolate chip cookie with sky blue frosting piped around the edges and a 50 in the middle. “It deserved a good cookie. And I can’t speak for the company but … I hope it’s not a disappointment.”

     

                Eyes brightening with a film of tears, Lena let out a quiet laugh, the sound breaking as her emotions choked her up. Blinking rapidly, she swallowed audibly, reaching for the box and tilting it to get a better look. Choking on another laugh, Lena’s face furrowed and she pressed her lips into a flat line as she dabbed at her eyes, the left side of her face still a nasty mess of bruises, the swelling gone down some but still painful to look at.

     

                “Thank you,” Lena whispered, her voice tremulous.

     

                Nodding, Kara’s lips twitched and she hesitated before replying. “It’s okay. I just- I wanted you to know that I’m proud of you. And … I think she would be too.”

     

                A small sound of anguish escaped Lena and her eyes filled. Laughing, she covered her face with her hands and shook her head, trying to regain her composure before she let out a withering sigh.

     

                “God, I don’t think I’ve ever been so emotional in my life. I never used to cry this much but now it’s all I do. I never used to cry at all. ”

     

                “Some people might say it’s healthy for you,” Kara reasoned.

     

                “Maybe. It doesn’t mean I have to like it.”

     

                Shrugging nonchalantly, Kara deliberated and reached for the cups of coffee, handing Lena hers and then gently tapping her own against it. Lena met her gaze, her own sad and doleful but the hint of a smile on the corners of her mouth as she held the cup between her palms, letting it warm them.

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                “So … fifty days, huh? How’s it been?”

     

                “Like hell,” Lena snorted. “Never have I felt more like drinking than in the last seven weeks.”

     

                “But you didn’t.”

     

                “No, I didn’t. I, uh, I drank a lot that night . Then I went to visit Andrea and she could tell I- something was wrong and … she’s perceptive, you know. She doesn’t remember things but she can pick up on people’s body language and moods, all of that, she’s not- she’s not stupid. You told me she wouldn’t like what she saw, and then she told me I needed help and … I guess when two people you love are telling you the same thing, you should listen so … I came home and I wanted to drink but I emptied all the bottles down the drain instead.”

     

                Kara blinked in surprise, remembering Alex’s comment on how much Lena had drunk when they were picking up Kara’s things, and it was a quiet relief to know she hadn’t finished off the remnants of a dozen bottles in her liquor cabinet alone. Nodding, Kara sipped her coffee and gestured towards the cookie.

     

                “Well, you’ve earned it.” 

     

                She nudged the cookie box closer to Lena. They’d subconsciously gravitated towards each other on the sofa, in between small shifts in their posture, and there were barely two feet between them now. Staring at each other for a second too long, Lena smiled faintly and wedged her coffee cup between her thighs as she reached for the cookie, breaking off a portion and taking a bite.

     

                “Definitely better than the AA ones,” Lena hummed appreciatively before they both laughed. She nudged the box back towards Kara. “Have some.”

     

                “Oh, no, the only thing I’ve gone without for the last fifty days is you, and … that’s not worth celebrating.”

     

                “That’s a matter of opinion,” Lena snorted. “Go on, have some. I can’t do it by myself.”

     

                Breaking a piece off, Kara chewed slowly and silence descended over them. After a minute, Kara cleared her throat and shifted her position on the sofa, apprehension on her face as she smiled tentatively.

     

                “So … how was your day?”

     

                Shrugging dismissively, Lena’s cheek shallowly dimpled. “Had to work from home again. This,” she sighed, gesturing airily at her face, “isn’t a good look when dealing with corporate contractors and site superintendents. And … I went to the centre this morning and before dinner.”

     

                “How is she?”

     

                “She was okay. She’s sweet most of the time, it’s just … when she gets confused or agitated … she gets a bit overwhelmed so she, well … she can lash out. She doesn’t mean to but … well, how would you react to a stranger trying to touch you, trying to make you remember things you can’t?”

     

                Kara’s mouth thinned grimly and she nodded. “She got a little … confused after I found her.”

     

                “Did she- did she hurt you?” Lena asked, her voice a low rasp, breathlessly hitching as her face rippled with pain.

     

                “No,” Kara whispered, “no, she didn’t hurt me. She was lovely but it …” Wrinkling her nose as she smiled tightly, ruefully, her blue eyes aching and resigned, she looked at Lena and shrugged. “It hurt to see it.”

     

                Letting out a shaky breath, Lena ducked her head and nodded. Her chin wobbled slightly and she took a sip of her coffee before looking at Kara again. “Where did you find her? I never got the chance to ask.”

     

                “The park.”

     

                “The park? I checked the park.”

     

                “You must have missed each other. She was … off the path. I heard her calling for Aristotle and … well, it took a while to get her to the car. You weren’t answering-”

     

                Regret flashed across Lena’s face and she smiled bitterly. “Mm, that’ll teach me, I guess.”

     

                Kara reached out and gently set a hand on her knee. “You couldn’t have known that I was looking.”

     

                “Maybe not but … when Kelly kept calling, I thought something was wrong. Maybe something had happened to you. You said you don’t like leaving things in a bad place in case and … for a second, I worried …”

     

                “No, I just- I didn’t know what to do with her after I found her,” Kara laughed, running a hand through her hair. “I didn’t want to call the cops because … I thought they might not understand, that they might not … be gentle. She wanted coffee so I took her to Starbucks while I tried calling you again.”

     

                A loud laugh of surprise escaped Lena as she raised her eyebrows. “You took her to Starbucks?”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara sheepishly replied, “oat milk latte with vanilla.”

     

                A slow smile spread across Lena’s face, her eyes tender as her shoulders slumped slightly. “That’s the one. Thank you for doing that. For finding her, keeping her safe.”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Kara’s cheek dimpled with a weak, crooked smile. “It was nothing.”

     

                “Not to me. To me … it’s everything. I can’t thank you enough-”

     

                “You don’t have to.”

     

                “I do. I- you were right; she is everything to me. Even now. I wish … I wish you knew what she was like before. So much of her is still here but it’s slowly slipping away but … I was lucky enough to have been loved by her for a little while and … I’m glad I’ll always have those memories. I just wish other people did too.”

     

                “What is it Thomas would say? Tell me about her so I can miss her too.”

     

                Lena was silent for a while, sipping her coffee while Kara nursed her own and broke off pieces of the cookie as she patiently waited. After a couple of minutes, Lena let out a soft sigh and looked over at her.

     

                “She was an only child. Grew up in Buenos Aires, spoiled rotten by her father but not really close to her mother. Her mom moved to England to marry some Duke, so she stayed in Argentina and her father ended up sending her to boarding school in America. That’s where we met; she was my best friend for a while. She was a couple of years ahead of me so we sort of lost touch when she graduated and … I regret that now, that I missed out on a few extra years with her. Her favourite colour is green, so … I’m glad she still remembers that. For our first date, we did it all backwards; she kissed me when she picked me up and one thing led to another and we ended up in my room - I used to live on the north side then - and we missed our dinner reservations so we had to wait an hour outside of Il Palazzo and she bought me flowers after the date as an apology. She was very forward, very brusque, expected everything and was charming to a fault so she did get everything, including me. Obsidian North hadn’t been doing all that well here but she headed the VR and AI projects she’d proposed and … it took off. Revolutionised the gaming industry and tech and all that, so her father stepped down and let her run it when his health started to fail. The last trip we went on together was to see her father, about six months before she went to Leviathan’s. We were supposed to go on that Metropolis trip together but … well, I think the flight would have been confusing for her. She was already forgetting who I was but she made me promise I’d go anyway. I didn’t want to, and I hated to admit it but … I think I needed that break, and I don’t think I’ll get that chance again. I can’t … jet off somewhere for a holiday because she’s getting worse and worse and I don’t- I don’t want to leave her behind. If something like the other night happened while I was off … sunning myself in Greece, I’d never forgive myself. I think if I didn’t work … I think I’d sit there from the moment visiting hours start until they end, and I know I don’t have to work but I- it’s a break from it all and I think … I just don’t know who I am anymore. I started losing her years ago and now I can never be myself with other people, never convince people to stay. I told you, I’m a naturally destructive person.”

     

                “When you said you knew the thing that would ruin us … you were talking about her,” Kara murmured, the memory of that conversation coming back to her now as she pieced the clues together.

     

                “Yes.”

     

                “You’d already decided I wouldn’t take it well.”

     

                “Yes. Since we’ve met … you’ve argued with your sister enough times for me to know that when you’re mad, you run.” 

     

                Kara choked on a laugh, shaking her head as her mouth curled wryly. “I hate to be so predictable.”

     

                “If it’s any consolation, I couldn’t predict whether you’d come back or not. They all warned you against me and I thought … maybe you’d listen to them this time. I bet- I bet Alex enjoyed that.”

     

                Blinking in surprise, Kara let out a quick bark of laughter, eyebrows rising towards her hairline as she cocked her head to the side. Narrowing her eyes slightly, she nudged her glasses up her nose and smiled with wry amusement.

     

                “Actually, she’s spent the last seven weeks trying to get me to call you. I’d like to say it was just because they’re about to adopt and they need their spare room back but … she gave me this big lecture on how I hadn’t actually gotten any better, I just- I just had you , and you made me happier, and her reasoning was that I’d be better off being the lover instead of alone because at least I would be happy.”

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena let out a defeated sigh and haltingly replied. “That’s not how it would have been.”

     

                “I know, I just- when you find out someone has a secret wife … it’s not really a moment for clarity or logical thinking, is it?”

     

                “No, I suppose not.”

     

                “I- I haven’t been a good friend-“ she trailed off and rolled her eyes at the droll look Lena gave her, rubbing her pink cheek as she hung her head. “I wish- I wish I could’ve handled it better and I- you did deserve my understanding but … you kept that from me for a long time. That’s- almost two years - that’s such a long time, I- and it’s- I would’ve helped you if I’d known. You never let me help you. You took care of me but you never-“

     

                Swallowing thickly, Lena nodded curtly. “I didn’t want your help. I didn’t want you to meet her, to know about her. I- you shouldn’t have shown up there the other day-“

     

                “I know,” Kara mumbled, wincing. “I know I shouldn’t have but … she’s all I’ve thought about for weeks. And you, of course. I overstepped, I know that, but I just wanted to see her again, to make sure- to know-“

     

                “I understand it’s confusing for you. I’m trying not to be mad about it, really, I am but … you can’t do shit like that, Kara. You can’t walk away and then visit my sick wife. You can’t do that ever again, do you understand?”

     

                “Yes. I’m sorry. I’m sorry for all of it. I just- I feel like … everything got fucked up so quickly and I never even had the chance to process it before it all went to shit. I- there are a lot of things I regret so … I just didn’t want to regret anything else,” Kara said, her voice thick and wavering. She trailed off, her eyes flitting up to the ceiling as she blinked back the burning feeling, her voice a broken whisper when she continued. “I’m sorry.”

     

                Lips twitching with grim weariness, Lena closed her eyes, shoulders sagging. “I know you are. So am I.”

     

                Kara’s eyes darted to her and she felt that deep ache in her chest that had been inescapable for weeks, futilely beaten back by her pride as she tried to process it all, tried to pluck up the courage to go to her, to not let her rash decisions and anger determine the rest of her life. There was more she wanted to say but the exhausted air about Lena let her know it was already too much and Kara didn’t want to leave her alone, depleted and defeated, when she left. The silence was unbearable though.

     

                “Tell me more,” Kara urged her after a moment. “What does she like? What does she hate? Where’s she been and what did she want to do?”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena stammered for a moment, uncertain and surprised by the simple act of understanding from Kara, of wanting to know Andrea instead of wanting to ignore that part of Lena’s life. She wasn’t sure if she’d expected that or not but Lena had tried to separate the two, so maybe Kara would have wanted the same. Kara didn’t though, sitting there patiently and apologetically, wanting to know everything, wanting to understand it more.

     

                “She likes mate ; it’s this caffeinated herbal drink. I found teabags of it for her so she can have it at the centre. She’s a morning person but you have to give her coffee and twenty minutes to wake up before you talk to her. Her favourite animal is the Fennec fox. She liked skiing but she wasn’t really good at it. She likes reading biographies, hates poetry. Doesn’t mind art but wasn’t really invested in it that much. She prefers wine and is very fussy about the types, the brands, the regions. She never liked to drive if she could get out of it. She likes desserts and hates seafood, but she’ll try almost everything. She’s hard but … I always just found her a little cocky rather than unapproachable. You already know the music she likes, but she hates anything classical. Her family is more … new money but mine is old money, so we didn’t really grow up the same. She loves very easily, hates very easily, does everything easily. Her favourite flowers are red carnations and she likes the heat so she found boarding school difficult in the winter months. She taught me Spanish at school and we liked the same movies; Titanic was both of our favourites.”

     

                She spoke for almost an hour about Andrea, recounting every minuscule detail about her wife. From the scar on her forehead to the places she wanted to travel, how she proposed, what perfume she liked to wear, her dry sense of humour, her thin patience, her preference for scrambled eggs and how she couldn’t ride a bike. Kara listened without speaking for the most part, her coffee cup empty, slowly relaxing into the sofa until she had her feet curled up beneath her and it could have been one of many nights spent at Lena’s. 

     

                “I just … I miss her. Even when she still remembered everything most of the time, I missed her being here. Sleeping beside her, eating breakfast or dinner with her, walking the dog with her.”

     

                It wasn’t lost on Kara that those were things they now did together, and yet it would never eclipse that gut-wrenching desire for Lena to do those things with her wife. Letting out a quiet laugh, Lena smiled thinly, rubbing her forehead.

     

                “I miss how often I had to help her find her keys. Eventually, I put that little dish on the hallway table that she got in the habit of using. A couple of weeks after I put her in there, I got a text from her that said she missed being able to find her keys.”

     

                They lapsed into silence and Lena stared at the wall with a glazed look of disbelief in her eyes, as if even after years of knowing, she still hadn’t processed her wife’s illness. Eventually, Lena ran a hand over her face, wincing slightly as she forgot about her bruises and Kara shifted forward, her elbows on her knees as she nudged her glasses up and swiped her thumb and forefinger over her eyelids.

     

                “I’m really sorry,” Kara quietly said, her voice cracking.

     

                “It’s okay,” Lena mumbled.

     

                “I- it’s just- I don’t know what to say.”

     

                “I know. That’s okay too.”

     

                Lena said nothing else and the silence dragged on, weighted with tense expectation. But there was no sign that Lena forgave her, that she wanted her, and Kara felt that hollow shakiness of her own mistakes catching up to her, the same way Lena had felt seven weeks ago in the event of her own. Exhaling roughly, her shoulders caving, Kara shook her head. She glanced down at her phone beside her and tapped the screen for the time. It was past eight o’clock and she didn’t want to impose on Lena for too long, except that she did want to, wanted to become an indefinite imposition so she didn’t have to leave.

     

                Clearing her throat, Kara ran her palms over the thighs of her scrubs and chewed on her words before speaking. “I think I’d better go.”

     

                “Okay,” Lena whispered, making no objections, revealing nothing of herself.

     

                Climbing to her feet, Kara picked up her phone and gave Aristotle a quick pat where he was laying, curled up beside her with his cheek pressed against her outer thigh. Kara really had missed him, even if her thinly veiled excuse a few days before had been about Lena. She gave him another pat, unsure of things, and then made her way down the hallway, sparing a glance at the small decorative dish with Lena’s and Andrea’s keys in it. A lump lodged itself in her throat.

     

                Picking up her backpack, Kara worked her feet into her running shoes and Lena snagged her denim jacket from the hook. She gave Kara a small smile, a yearning look in her eyes as she held it out.

     

                “Here.”

     

                Looking down at it, Kara hesitated, uncertain about taking her reason with her. Maybe if she left it again, insisted that the weather was too warm for her to need it, she’d be able to come back again. But maybe she didn’t need a reason. She never had.

     

                Her fingers closed around it and she returned Lena’s smile, hesitating before she stepped forward and wrapped her in a hug. It was far too short for both of their liking and Kara’s stomach was clenched with unease from the anxious thought of losing Lena for good before she relinquished her hold on her, so Lena could care for her wife without the complication of a relationship with Kara getting in the way. 

     

                “Thank you for the coffee and the cookie,” Lena murmured.

     

                “Any time.”

     

                “The company wasn’t disappointing.”

     

                Kara hoarsely laughed at the reassurance, her eyes creasing at the corners. “I’m glad.”

     

                Smiling faintly, Lena leaned against the hallway wall, her arms folded over her chest as she bit her lower lip. After a moment, she sighed softly. “Can I give you a ride?”

     

                “No,” Kara whispered, her nose wrinkling as she smiled. “But thank you.”

     

                “You’ll let me know once you’re home safe?”

                

                “Sure.”

     

                “Okay. Have a good night.”

     

                Nodding, Kara reached for the door handle and opened it. “You too.”

     

                Stepping forward, Lena caught the edge of the door, their fingers brushing slightly, and Kara stepped out into the hallway. Adjusting the strap of her backpack, Kara gave her one more glance and a fleeting smile before setting off down the hallway, hearing the door click shut a moment later.

     

                She made it halfway to the elevator before she paused. Shoulders slumping with defeat, dragging her feet as she tried to resist the building urge in her chest, Kara closed her eyes and stood still. Torn between what she hoped Lena wanted and what she thought Lena wanted, two very different things that hinged on the fact that seven weeks ago Kara had walked out, she lingered with uncertainty for a long minute, the muffled silence of the hallway pressing in on her.

     

                “Make the chilli,” she whispered to herself.

     

                Quickly backtracking, she took a deep breath to steel herself, doing what she should have done weeks ago when she’d walked out with her bags, and then knocked on the door again. It took a moment for Lena to answer it, looking bemused as she smiled unevenly, her eyes bloodshot, the two of them staring at each other.

     

                “I think I forgot something,” Kara blurted out a moment later.

     

                “Oh?”

     

                She stepped inside, forcing Lena back or risking collision, but Kara kept coming anyway, dropping her backpack and her jacket and reaching for Lena. Cupping the right side of her face and the left side of her neck, Kara kissed her roughly and, after her initial surprise, Lena kissed her back.

     

                Lena was backed up against the hallway wall and Kara’s hand ghosted down her neck, down to her waist, holding her firmly in place. The kiss softened and Kara broke it off after a few moments, their breaths short and quick, chests rising and falling. She moved slightly, bumping their noses, and she could read the wary doubt in Lena’s eyes as she pulled back minutely. 

     

                “Kara …”

     

                Closing her eyes, Kara rested her forehead against Lena’s, her voice so low that if they weren’t pressed up against each other, Lena would’ve had a hard time hearing her. “I don’t want to leave my jacket behind for an excuse to see you again. I don’t want to need a reason.”

     

                “Kara.”

     

                “You said it yourself; this is the only time we ever get. I know- I know that you love her … but I love you, and I can’t be your first choice but I can be your second.”

     

                “Just … hold on a minute.”

     

                “Have I- have I … misunderstood? I thought …”

     

                Kara shifted back and Lena reached for her hands, holding them tightly as she hung her head, looking at their intertwined fingers. Drawing in a shaky breath, she looked pale and tense and she wouldn’t meet Kara’s gaze.

     

                “I love you,” Lena firmly stated. “But I love Andrea. And I can never leave her.”

     

                A wavering smile crossed Kara’s face as she swallowed thickly. “I would think less of you if you did.”

     

                Letting out a breathless laugh, Lena’s eyes quickly lifted, bewilderment crumpling her face. “You have to be sure because … it wouldn’t be fair to you. I mean … I visit her pretty much every day. Twice most days. It’s … it’s a big part of my life; you know how late I used to get home most days, how early I left. When we were friends … it was fine, but to be in a relationship and expect you to sit at home waiting around for me to finish visiting my wife … you deserve to be a priority, and I wish it could be me but I will always have to put her first.”

     

                “I know,” Kara murmured. “It’s what took me so long to process. I wasn’t sure that I- that I could be around for something like that but … I would rather spend every morning, night and weekend with you and your wife and be loved by you than miserable without you.”

     

                “Kara. She is not your wife; she’s not your responsibility.”

     

                “I know, but she’s yours. And you’re mine. It won’t be easy, I know it’s going to get increasingly more difficult, for you and her, and I can’t bear to watch you go through it but … I’ll be damned if I let you go through it alone . I won’t. So, she might not be my wife or my responsibility but I know she will always be yours, and if- if you can love the both of us … we can figure the rest out. I’m not asking you to choose me over her. I’m not asking you to choose her over me. She is going to be in your life no matter what, I just- I’m asking you to let me be in it too.”

     

                Lena’s expression was unreadable, a wavering smile on her lips, a faint crease between her eyebrows, green eyes clouded. Kara squeezed her hands, tensed with expectation as she waited for a response. Her heart was pounding in her chest, the nauseating feeling of baring her feelings to be met with a wall clawing up her throat, making it hard for her to swallow. She knew what Lena must have felt like, confessing the truth about her wife and being met with nothing but the closed-off rejection of Kara’s avoidance. 

     

                After a long moment, Lena’s shoulders visibly went slack as the tension receded and, a faint softening to her face, almost mournful and aching. She pulled a hand free from Kara’s warm grip and tenderly stroked the back of her knuckles over Kara’s cheek, her eyelids shuttering, tired and full of yearning. Kara couldn’t even speak, couldn’t say anything else, a shakiness to her as she waited, the silence dragging on as she stared at Lena, her whole body coiled with anticipation. 

     

                “I lied to you,” Lena haltingly said.

     

                “You did,” Kara gravelly replied, a wretched smile on her lips as her eyes stung fiercely.

     

                “I hurt you.”

     

                “I hurt you too.”

     

                “I have a wife.”

     

                “You do.”

     

                “And I love her.”

     

                “Of course,” Kara murmured, stepping in closer.

     

                “And I love you.”

     

                “Good.”

     

                “But I can’t marry you. Ever.”

     

                “I’m not asking you to.”

     

                “Or have kids with you.”

     

                “I’m not asking that either.”

     

                “My wife … is going to die.”

     

                Reaching up to thumb away a tear, Kara exhaled softly as her face turned grave. “I wish that she wasn’t.”

     

                “It’s a heavy burden to live with.”

     

                “It’s easier when it’s shared.”

     

                “It’s not your-”

     

                Letting out a huff of laughter, Kara rested her forehead against Lena’s, their noses bumping as she closed her eyes. “Lena, I swear to God, if you tell me it’s not my burden to bear, I- well, I don’t know what I’ll do but I- you’re not going to make me change my mind. Not again.”

     

                “I-” Lena faltered, drawing in a shuddering breath. “I want to be with you. I always did. I just- I wanted to keep it all separate. You were never supposed to- to meet her or … for things to end up like this. I was- I was supposed to tell you properly, explain it all, I- it shouldn’t have been like this. From the beginning, we’ve made … every wrong decision possible.”

     

                “I understand why but … you can’t keep it separate. I would’ve wanted to meet her anyway. If you’d told me sooner, I would’ve wanted to know your wife. I still do.”

     

                “Why?”

     

                “Because … there was a point in time where she remembered that she loved you and made you happy, and looked after you, and made you feel less alone and … that makes me want to love her too. All that love she had for you is left to me now, so let me do it. You begged me to stay before, and now I’m begging you to let me.”

     

                “Of course I want you to,” Lena softly exclaimed, her eyes filling with tears and her hands going to Kara’s waist, moving in close until they were pressed together. “I love you and … it’s not as a last resort. I just- I’m scared that … you’re going to wake up one day and realise that this is not worth it for you.”

                

                “You will always be worth it. I’m sorry it took me so long to figure that out but …” Kara trailed off, her face puckering with concentration as she tried to remember Lena’s wording from months ago. “You are going to let me help you … even if you curse me the whole time, even if you hate me. You don’t even … have to be grateful , okay? It’s entirely selfishly motivated.”

     

                Her voice was lightly mocking at the end, as Lena laughed, burying her face in Kara’s shoulder as Kara smiled. The thick tension of the moment was cut through by her echoed words and Kara wrapped Lena in a hug, sighing heavily and kissing her hair.

     

                “I mean it.”

     

                “I know you do. I mean it too; you’re not a last resort. You’re the other half of my heart.”

     

                “Well, I’ve always been good at sharing,” Kara whispered, swaying them slightly.

     

                Lena pulled back, a pained look on her face, and Kara scrunched her nose as she smiled faintly. It wasn’t the way she thought it would be, wasn’t ideal, but it was the way it was, and if she had to be the girlfriend who visited the wife with her, who tried to lighten the suffocating weight of grief as Andrea’s illness progressed, that was what Kara would do. 

     

                It had been a difficult prospect to come to terms with over the last seven weeks but, ultimately, Kara knew that even if Lena had truly lost Andrea almost two years ago now, she never would’ve had her whole heart anyway. At least half of it would have always belonged to her wife, the same way Kara’s would never belong entirely to Lena. They had both loved other people and lost them in different ways; they just happened to love each other too.

     

                “I- will you stay?” Lena haltingly asked.

     

                Kara cradled Lena’s hands in her own and gave her a wry smile. “When you told me you knew what would destroy us, do you remember what I said? I told you you couldn’t get rid of me. It might take me a while to stop being an ass but you’re stuck with me. I wouldn’t know what to do without you.”

    Chapter 26

                Waking to soft sheets, a wide bed, the absent sound of traffic and, perhaps most notably, the warm press of a back against her chest, Kara blearily blinked as the droning of an alarm cut through the fog of sleep. Fumbling for the nightstand, Lena turned off her alarm and burrowed into the pillows, scooting back against Kara without a word.

     

                “Morning,” Kara murmured as she pushed herself up onto her elbow, lazily dragging her fingertips over Lena’s arm. “How did you sleep?”

     

                Lena was quiet and thoughtful for a moment before she rolled over, her brow furrowing slightly with a serious look. “Better than I have in weeks.”

     

                Choking on a laugh, Kara hummed in agreement. “Me too.”

     

                “I know it wasn’t often but … I’d gotten used to sleeping next to you. And I missed the sounds of you getting ready for work too. It’s been so quiet without you here.”

     

                “Well, my sister’s place was definitely not quiet but I missed it too - when you were still here. God, no wonder you were always up at the crack of dawn. I thought you were just really passionate about your work but … this makes more sense.”

     

                Letting out a quietly choked laugh, Lena ran a hand over her face. “Speaking of, I should probably get ready to go. I should probably show my face at least once this week.”

     

                “Of course,” Kara murmured, throwing the covers back and sitting up. “Coffee to go? Do you want breakfast?”

     

                “You have to get ready for work too, you know.”

     

                “I have plenty of time. I could probably walk to work from here quicker than it takes me to catch the bus from Alex’s. What will it be? Eggs? Granola? Toast?”

     

                Deliberating as she climbed out of bed, Lena stretched, a pucker between her eyebrows, and smiled faintly. “We don’t have to-”

     

                “I know,” Kara murmured, a pained look on her face as she smiled gingerly. “But … it’s breakfast. You need to eat breakfast.”

     

                Chewing on her lip, Lena warily met her eyes and let out a huff of laughter. “Toast would be great.”

     

                “Great! What do you want on it? Avocado? Bacon?”

     

                Smiling softly to herself, Lena started making the bed. “You know what I like; I’m not fussy.”

     

                “Okay. I’ll surprise you,” Kara solemnly replied, nodding to herself before she hovered for a moment and then turned, making herself useful.

     

                She padded barefoot into the kitchen and set two slices of bread down in the toaster and raided the fridge. Spreading cream cheese over the toast, she pitted and sliced an avocado and then topped their breakfasts with smoked salmon, while the coffee machine whirred away, espresso filtering into two cups. Pouring the steamed milk from the machine, Kara set the table as Lena emerged, hair slightly damp from a hasty shower.

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                Giving her a quick smile, Kara took her seat across from her, surprised by how normal it all felt. Whatever pall had been lingering over them after their stilted reunion on Monday had vanished last night, over the course of a few hours of talking and some firm honesty and a surprising kiss. There was still a nervous sense of anticipation between them though, so much left unspoken, so much to unpack, so much anger to deal with, but there was a tangible air of relief and a tenuous peace between the two of them as they settled in for breakfast, as they had so many times before.

     

                “So, are drinks on tonight?” Lena slowly asked.

     

                “Probably but … I haven’t been going. I … well, I had a falling out with James. And I guess I’m a little bit annoyed with Winn too but he was just on the sideline. Um … they were both right, in a way, I just- I haven’t … I’ve been my own worst enemy recently and I- well, I didn’t want to hear it. Anyway … yeah, I don’t know.”

     

                “Well, if you feel like going, let me know. I, uh, I just- Andrea has a scheduled appointment with her neurologist tomorrow to do a bunch of scans. You know, CT, MRI, PET.”

     

                Kara paused, setting down her knife and fork and taking a sip of coffee before rubbing a hand through her hair. “I- sorry if this is invasive-” 

     

                “Now you’re concerned about that?” Lena wryly asked, arching an eyebrow.

     

                Wincing as she flushed red, Kara closed her mouth and Lena chuckled to herself, although there was still that firm spark of annoyance in her eyes. “Go on. Ask.”

     

                “Is she on any treatments for it? I know there’s no- there’s no cure but … clinical trials? Anything like that?”

     

                “She’s on donepezil. It’s an AChE inhibitor to help slow the progress of it. It’s, um, it’s- well they tell you not to get your hopes up. It won’t stop the disease and it’s questionable if it even does anything but … at least we’re trying.”

     

                “Yes,” Kara murmured in agreement. “It’s better to try.”

     

                Nodding, Lena swallowed thickly and cut into her breakfast for another bite. “So, I, uh, I probably won’t be around for much of tomorrow.”

     

                “That’s okay. I need to pack this weekend. Maybe we can get dinner afterwards?”

     

                “Move back in,” Lena blurted out, ignoring Kara’s question.

     

                Swallowing her mouthful, Kara hesitated, slow to reply. “I … I’m not sure I can break the lease agreement. I’ve already paid the deposit and-“

     

                “I’ll pay your deposit. I’ll pay the termination fee. I’ll pay any rent you owe until they can find a new tenant, just … move back in.”

     

                “Lena-“

     

                “I’m not saying that you have to … give up your own space, sleep in my room every night with me, or even move in again if you don’t want to, I just- your room is there and the offer hasn’t changed and … I miss you being here so if you’re comfortable moving back in, I would like it.”

     

                Swallowing thickly, Kara’s heart twinged in her chest. “I don’t care about the deposit or any fees-”

     

                “Is that a yes?”

     

                “It’s a maybe . I just- I think I need to think about it before I decide. It’s not that I don’t want to live with you because I do but … I know it was me who decided to move out after everything, and that was a rash decision that I wasn’t really thinking clearly about but … it also- I put myself in a situation where I was completely dependent on you for a lot of things. I’m so grateful for everything you did, of course, I just want to make sure that … I’m doing things for the right reasons this time, and not because I have nowhere else to go. I know that … whatever happens next, it’s not going to be easy or fun to sort out. I know you’re angry at me and … you know, I’m angry at you too. I think we’re both entitled to our feelings and … I don’t want it to get in the way of it all and I think- I think sorting that out first would be a good idea before we rush into anything.”

     

                Giving her a crooked smile, Lena reached for her cup of coffee. “You’re right, I am angry but … I’m just- I’m tired. I’m too tired to be angry. I’ve been angry for six years now - almost seven - and … I don’t want to feel that way anymore. I just- you’ve been the only thing to give me any peace, any comfort in a long time so … be angry if you want, because it’s not going to be fun or easy, I- I think … you and I are not coping well and it’s … a shit show and I don’t see how it’ll ever get better but I don’t feel like I’m drowning with you. Um … so I don’t care if I’m mad, I just- I want you to stay, move in. And how about next time we fuck it up and you pack your bags, I’ll make sure I have an empty apartment for you to move into.”

     

                Teary-eyed, Kara’s mouth twisted into a wavering smile as she blinked back the urge to cry. “Very funny. And how many apartments do you own?”

     

                “A few buildings,” Lena hedged, trying to stamp down her own surfacing emotions.

     

                “Buildings? As in the whole thing? A few?”

     

                “Yes, a few.”

     

                “Right,” Kara slowly replied. 

     

                “I’m kidding though; I don’t have any other skeletons in the closet, so unless you take issue with … you know, me, we should be safe.”

     

                Giving her an aching look, Kara softly sighed. “She’s not a skeleton in the closet; she’s your wife .”

     

                “I know. I just- I’m terribly selfish - I’ve already told you that. I thought … maybe I could’ve had both of you without it having to be a problem.”

     

                “I- well, everyone's a little bit selfish and you can have both of us, and it’s not a problem, it’s just … it’s shit. Shit for you. ”

     

                “It’s shit for you too, Kara,” Lena murmured as her expression furrowed.

     

                Pausing, mouth a flat line, twitching slightly as she grimaced, Kara fiddled with her knife and fork as she looked at Lena, taking in the look of dismay, the edge of guilt. “It’s not shit for me,” Kara gently replied. “I mean, it’s not i deal but … with you, I get a second chance at something I’d given up on - maybe even before Mike died. So, it’s not shit for me because I get to be happy, even if it’s confusing, even if- even if I’m not coping well, and … I know if you had the choice between me and her, you would pick her, and that’s okay, I- it doesn’t mean I don’t believe you when you say you love me too, it’s just- it’s different, and I wish so badly that you could be happy with your wife, so … yeah, it’s shit for you . Because you’re right, I am lucky; my husband is dead so … at least I got that closure. And I can’t even wish that for you because … I don’t want you to lose her for good.”

     

                Wincing slightly, Lena rubbed her furrowed brow as she stared at her plate. “I shouldn’t have said that. That you’re lucky, I mean. It was … insensitive and I was upset but … I’m sorry.”

     

                “But you’re right,” Kara said with a strained laugh. “At the time, I thought you were being a completely insensitive asshole but … I think you were right.”

     

                “For once, I wish I was wrong.”

     

                “Either way, he’d be gone and he wouldn’t be coming back. I think … I should consider myself lucky that even with everyone I’ve lost, I’m resilient enough to bounce back. And I haven’t lost that ability to love again.”

     

                “You don’t have to be resilient, you know.”

     

                “Coming from you,” Kara laughed.

     

                Lena gave her a thin smile, “you mistook resilience for a carefully composed mask that I had to put on to face Andrea every day. She would worry about me a lot, that I wasn’t coping well, so I pretended to be. She could see right through it, of course, but it used to overwhelm her if I cried every time I left, so I quickly learnt to put on that mask and wait until I got home at night to break down. I thought I’d crack under the weight of it all … and then I met you.”

     

                “And I just thought you were the most stoic widow to ever exist.”

     

                Humming, Lena’s lips twitched with a smile. “I was always pretty stoic before but … well, it gets to you.”

     

                “Mm. Do you think you’ve changed much?”

     

                “Not too much. Maybe I’m more anxious and pessimistic now; every time I visit or get a call, I expect the worst. I wouldn’t really say I was an optimist before anyway but … I never used to be a worrier. It’s chipped away at me over the years though, so I started to drink more to deal with the stress of it, I guess the same way she used to smoke more. Other than that, I don’t know, it probably is just the fact that I cry a lot. Why? Trying to figure out if you would’ve liked me before?”

     

                Shrugging, Kara looked a little sheepish. “Maybe a little. I think I would’ve, though.”

     

                “And what were you like?”

     

                “I don’t know,” Kara murmured, “happier? More … complacent. I would’ve let anyone walk all over me but then he died and I got angry so … that sort of stopped. Now, I was an optimist, and I don’t know if that was out of some forced desire to not think about my parents, to get past the loss of them, but I think my friends miss that about me. I haven’t been easy to be around for the last couple of years.”

     

                “I disagree. Or maybe I’m just as angry as you are. Either way … raft in the middle of the ocean.”

     

                “You’re biassed.”

     

                “Of course I am. But isn’t everyone who loves someone?”

     

                The words sent a small thrill through Kara, even though it wasn’t the first time hearing them. Even last night had reiterated their feelings but it was such a relief to know they hadn’t fucked things up irreparably. A faint smile tugged at the corners of Kara’s mouth and she cut another bite from her breakfast and basked in that feeling she’d fleetingly held for a week before it had all gone to shit. 

     

                Somehow, they’d made it through to the other side of it but that was the least of their troubles. It seemed easy to accept the truth, to get past a lie, to apologise and beg to stay, in light of what Lena would have to go through in the future. And by deciding to stay, Kara was choosing to go through that too, knowing it would hurt for her as well, to a minuscule extent in comparison to the mountain of agony it would be for Lena. She didn’t want to watch Lena lose her wife as much as Lena didn’t want to lose her wife. Everything else was put into perspective when set beside that elephant in the room that they’d touched on but didn’t want to discuss or acknowledge again until the eventuality of it.

     

                Finishing off her breakfast, Kara insisted on tidying up and Lena went to get ready. It didn’t take Kara anywhere near as long, and she had spare scrubs at work she could change into later, so once she’d finished with the dishes she showered in the spare bathroom and raided Lena’s closet for pants that were long enough to hide her ankles. In the midst of her search, she came across her sweatshirt from Sunday, the one she’d helped Andrea into, the one she’d completely forgotten about in light of everything else.

     

                Lena came out of the bathroom, her makeup done and a robe pulled on and paused at the sight of Kara running the pilled cotton of the sweatshirt through her fingers. Letting out a quiet laugh, Lena approached her closet to find her own clothes for work.

     

                “I took it from her once we’d gotten her changed into something clean. Cried myself to sleep holding it on Sunday. It smelled like you; smelled a little bit like her too.”

     

                Reaching out, Kara hung it back on the rack of pressed designer, out of place but claiming a spot anyway. Turning to Lena, she smiled crookedly and reached out to cup her chin briefly.

     

                “Then I guess I’ll let you keep it. Just in case I ever need another excuse to knock on your door.”

     

                “Are you anticipating needing another excuse?”

     

                “You never know.”

     

                Lips twitching, Lena hesitated and then reached for Kara’s hand, smoothing her thumb across her knuckles and then raising it to her lips. Kissing her fingers gently enough to leave only the slightest smudge of red lipstick, Lena met her gaze with a spark there. 

     

                “You’re going to be late.”

     

                “I make my own hours,” Lena murmured.

     

                “I do not, and neither does the respite centre.”

     

                Softly sighing, Lena sobered up. “Right.”

     

                Kara was pretty much ready, her shoes and backpack waiting by the front door, so she perched on the edge of the bed and watched Lena get ready. Hangers clicked as Lena slid them across the rail before settling on a dress. Without being asked, Kara rose from her spot and crossed over to Lena, pulling the zipper up, her fingers warm against Lena’s cool back.

     

                Stepping back once she’d zipped it, Kara let out a regretful sigh. “I need to go.”

     

                “I’ll drive you.”

     

                “Alright, I’ll wait. Thank you.”

     

                Passing the time by playing tug of war on the living room floor with Aristotle, Kara dusted off her borrowed jeans and climbed to her feet as Lena made an appearance, handbag looped over her arm and her heels in hand. Lacing on her running shoes at the end of the hallway, Kara snagged her denim jacket and slung her backpack over her shoulder as Lena chose a coat from the rack and slipped on her heels.

     

                They made their way down to the basement garage together and Kara slipped into the passenger side, wedging her backpack between her feet. Starting the car, Lena backed out of her spot and turned down the radio before she drove them to Noonan’s first for takeaway coffees and then drove Kara to the clinic. Putting the car in park as she idled out front, Lena turned to Kara, who unbuckled her seatbelt and let out a soft sigh.

     

                “Say hello to her for me,” Kara murmured, giving Lena’s hand a quick squeeze. “I’ll see you tomorrow.”

     

                “Have a good day.”

     

                “And you.”

     

                Slipping out of the car, Kara gave her a smile as she pulled her backpack out and shut the door. Walking towards the front door, she could hear that Lena hadn’t moved yet and turned to wave goodbye before stepping into the lobby. 

     

                Work was a blur of activity. She had three scheduled surgeries that ate up a chunk of her day, although they were nothing serious, and Kara spent an hour after lunch updating her files and filling out the necessary paperwork. For a brief moment towards the end of her shift, Kara considered going out for drinks as the messages came through in the group chat but it had been an emotionally tumultuous week and she was exhausted from it.

     

                Although she knew she could have messaged Lena to see if she wanted to get dinner, Kara thought it would be wise not to rush things, to have a modicum of space where before they’d spent almost all of their spare time together. Now she knew that for Lena, it came at the cost of spending time with her wife, on an already limited number of hours left, no matter if they didn’t know the figure. Kara would not begrudge her the chance to spend as much time with Andrea as possible; they would have dinner tomorrow and they could talk more then, figuring out what they were doing and how things would be between them.

     

                Instead, after work she rode the bus home and focused on her meditation Podcast, a sense of peace in her chest after so much knotted worry and festering bitterness. It was better for Kara this way, allowing herself the freedom to forgive, to move on, instead of letting her stubbornness get in the way of things, reacting as she was expected to instead of how she wanted to. Her pride was always a prickly thing that had gotten her into frustrating situations - especially when it came to her sister - but Kara didn’t want to have so much pride that she drowned herself in misery. It undoubtedly would go that way without Lena.

     

                Arriving home just after six, Kara let herself into her sister’s place to find her and Kelly both home. Raising her eyebrows as she watched them finishing dinner in the kitchen, Kara smiled slightly. “Not going to drinks?”

     

                “No, we thought a quiet night in would be nicer,” Alex explained.

     

                Kelly held up a plate. “Hungry?”

     

                Shrugging, Kara removed her backpack and kicked off her running shoes, leaving them near the front door, on the rack. “Sure, I could eat. Thank you.”

     

                Alex took the plate from her wife and dished up another portion, handing it over to Kara before she walked to the table. Fetching herself a fork for the pasta, Kara nudged the drawer shut with her hip as the other two women took their seats.

     

                “Did you go to Group last night? I didn’t hear you come in,” Alex asked as she settled in.

     

                Kara’s movements slowed and she cleared her throat as she carried her plate to the table. “No, I, uh, I went to visit Lena, actually.”

     

                “Really?” Alex perked up, her eyebrows rising in surprise. “And?”

     

                Shrugging nonchalantly, Kara scooted her chair in a fraction more and held her fork. Her sister huffed, giving her a withering look.

     

                “Don’t just shrug. Did you end it or are you back on? Did you sleep with her? Tell us.”

     

                “You’re so nosy.”

     

                “Okay, and? I want to know.”

     

                “I left my jacket in her car so I went to pick it up,” Kara started to explain.

     

                Face falling as her eagerness dimmed, Alex’s mouth thinned. “Oh. So-“

     

                “Will you let her speak?” Kelly crowed, a spluttering laugh escaping her.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Alex gestured for Kara to continue and twirled pasta around her fork, grumbling under her breath. Sighing, Kara set down her fork and ran a hand through her hair.

     

                “I left my jacket in her car on Monday-“

     

                “Mon-“ Alex started to exclaim before quickly shutting her mouth.

     

                “I went to visit Andrea.”

     

                “Okay, sorry, I’m interrupting again; you visited her wife? Did you ask Lena? I mean did she offer to take you or?”

     

                Opening her mouth, Kara quickly closed it again and looked sheepishly down at her plate. “No, I just … went there.”

     

                “Kara. That’s a huge boundary to violate. What is wrong with you?”

     

                “I know! I just- I wanted to make sure she was okay and I wanted to make sure Lena was okay but I couldn’t call her-“

     

                “How is her face?” Kelly chimed in.

     

                Wincing, Kara bared her teeth in a pained manner. “Awful. It wasn’t as swollen last night and the bruises have faded a lot but it was black and blue on Monday. She’s got burst blood vessels in her eyes, which looks … awful. It makes my face hurt.”

     

                Huffing, Alex rolled her eyes. “Okay, great, her bruises are healing, that’s very good news, now continue. You just showed up there?”

     

                “I- well … the carer recognised me from the hospital so he let me in when I said I was there to visit her. Anyway, so then Lena showed up and … well she pretty much ignored me the whole time because … you know, we weren’t really speaking. Then we left and … I don’t know, she got upset and then we went for Big Belly Burger and she got mad at me and I- well, I deserved it but then she drove me home and I left my jacket in her car.”

     

                “Yes, you’ve mentioned. And then what?”

     

                “I went to get my jacket. I, uh, we talked. For a while.” A crooked smile crossed Kara’s face, her eyes creasing at the corners. “I made the chilli.”

     

                “You made the chilli?” Alex asked, elation on her face and her shoulders slumping with relief.

     

                “I made the chilli.”

     

                “What the hell are you two talking about?” Kelly asked, bemused as she reached for her glass of wine.

     

                Alex laughed, turning to her wife and resting a hand on her arm. “It’s a long story. We had a fight like a year ago. Anyway , it’s about going out of your way to do something for someone you love - like swallowing your pride and patching things up for the sake of everyone’s happiness.”

     

                “Right,” Kelly dubiously hummed. “And where does the chilli come into this?”

     

                “It’s not about the chilli!” both sisters exasperatedly exclaimed.

     

                Arching a sceptical eyebrow, Kelly just sighed and shook her head. “Sure. So … you and Lena?”

     

                Biting her lip, Kara shrugged slightly. “I stayed over last night. Nothing happened. I just- we talked a lot. Mostly about Andrea. I think … it’ll be okay now.” 

     

                “So …?”

     

                “Um … so yeah, we’re back on, and … she’s married and … it’s going to be really hard over the next however many years with- with her wife. I hope there are a lot of them left. She said … usually eight to ten years after diagnosis; it’s already been six but she’s young so … I don’t know, I’m not an expert but … maybe that means her body will be strong enough to fight it for longer.”

     

                There was an exchange of glances between the surgeon and psychiatrist that Kara missed as she reached for her drink. Taking a sip, she set her glass back down and cleared her throat.

     

                “She also asked me to move back in.”

     

                “She did?” Alex blinked.

     

                “And before you get all up in arms about it-”

     

                Snorting, Alex rolled her eyes, “why would I? Oh, no, you’re moving too quickly after you already lived together for months? Yeah, that seems a bit belated - except I already warned you about it last time so why bother?”

     

                “Well, you were right last time.”

     

                “Yeah, that wasn’t quite as satisfying as I’d hoped,” Alex grimly replied with a rueful smile.

     

                “Anyway, I haven’t decided if I will or not. I thought I should at least sleep on it; I don’t want to rush anything.”

     

                With a scoff of laughter, Alex raised a sceptical eyebrow. “Except where you rushed everything before. And in the completely wrong order. Slept together, moved in, then fell in love.”

     

                “It’s different this time.”

     

                “What, the fact that she’s married? She always was married, you just didn’t know it was to a wife that was alive . Is that the only thing stopping you?”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Kara struggled to articulate herself. “No, I- it’s just … if things go wrong again, I- well, I won’t have anything. And you’ll have a kid and I don’t want to be forty, bouncing around the sofas of all of our friends until I find my own place.”

     

                “You know that’s a risk with every relationship, right?”

     

                “A very valid risk,” Kelly curtly interrupted. “Although, it’s not uncommon for people to move quickly in new relationships after the ending of a long-term one. That’s less to do with rushing than being more aware of one's wants in a partner, which is usually contrary to the last one in a lot of areas. You know, the last one didn’t do any housework so the next one you look for a partner who does housework. That sort of thing.”

     

                “I already know what it’s like to live with her.”

                

                “Which mitigates the risk,” Kelly reasoned.

     

                “Unless there was something off-putting about living with her,” Alex mused.

     

                Laughing, Kara shook her head, her eyelids shuttering. “You said it yourself, it was equal.”

     

                A faintly pleased smile crossed Alex’s face as she leaned back in her chair. “Well … there we go. But you don’t have to move back in with her just because you liked living with her. Having your own space is good. And living in someone else’s house would feel weird, but … hey, you thought you were sleeping in a dead woman’s bed, so maybe not that weird, huh?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Kara stabbed at her plate. “I had my own room, you know that. And I would if I moved back in. It would be just like last time. You know, space. ”

     

                “Oh. Well … if you decide to move back in, I think it’s a good idea to have space,” Kelly stated.

     

                Giving her a warm smile, Kara dug back into her food and the conversation continued, her sister seeming pleased with the fact that she’d bitten the bullet and spoke to Lena, regardless of the outcome. As for herself, Kara felt a sense of relief, that the worst of it was over now, that she’d patched things up and, given enough time, things between her and Lena would be as familiar as ever, once they’d gotten past this moment of precarious indecision on Kara’s behalf. 

     

                Tired, Kara didn’t stay up long with the couple as they found something to watch on TV, and instead had a hot shower and climbed into bed. Spending an hour or so listening to a new episode of a Podcast and folding her laundry. Slipping out for a cup of tea, she retreated back to her room and replied to Nia’s texts about her whereabouts and promised to get breakfast with her in the morning to make up for it.

     

                She went to bed early and slept soundly, waking up at nine o’clock and hurriedly getting ready for breakfast before rushing out of the apartment and catching the bus to the other side of Downtown. Meeting Nia and Querl at Noonan’s, Kara slowed at the sight of James sitting beside Querl. Rankling slightly, Kara jerked her chair out and sat.

     

                “Morning,” she warily greeted them all.

     

                “Hi!” Nia brightly replied, turning in her seat to give Kara a slightly sheepish smile.

     

                “Let’s order,” Kara quickly declared.

     

                They all frequented Noonan’s so they already had their set orders and Kara was out of her chair quickly, making for the counter with Nia trailing along behind her. Sighing, the younger woman gave her a wavering smile as Kara cast her a peevish look.

     

                “Thanks for the heads up.”

     

                “He overheard me telling Querl about our plans last night. I didn’t know he was going to hijack them,” Nia apologetically replied.

     

                “It’s fine.”

     

                “He feels bad.”

     

                “Good.”

     

                Nia went first, placing hers and Querl’s orders together and then Kara stepped up to the counter as James approached. She was aware of his presence but studiously ignored him as she folded her arms over her chest and waited for the cashier to finish running a coffee and muffin and take her order.

     

                “I’m sorry,” James softly said.

     

                Lips twitching, Kara didn’t respond, glancing at him from the corner of her eye as she tried to appraise his sincerity. 

     

                “I said some things I shouldn’t have. And you’re right; maybe I do have something against Lena. I think … ages ago when I said you were the glue holding us together, the reason that we were all friends - friends with Mike too - I meant it and … you having Lena meant that we were losing the glue. It’s felt like we’ve lost two friends at times, and maybe I’ve been a bit bitter about that, about her taking his spot when you do come out for drinks or dinner. I’m sorry. I still shouldn’t have said those things. I think … for me, I just can’t wrap my head around why you wouldn’t want to come to us for support during it but I spoke to Kelly and she explained why you might not want to. So, if you need that space, that’s okay, but I hope you know I’m still your friend, even when things get messed up between us. And I’m sorry for the way things worked out with Lena.”

     

                Fighting back a smile, Kara raised her eyebrows as she rounded on James. “Are you?”

     

                “She was nice. I can’t say I knew her well, but you seemed happy so I am sorry the way it worked out, yes.”

     

                “Then you’ll be happy to know that we’ve worked things out,” Kara continued, her blue eyes bright with amusement as she watched the surprise flash across her friend's face.

     

                James faltered for a moment before swallowing whatever was on the tip of his tongue and nodding. “That’s good to hear.”

     

                “Thank you,” Kara gently replied, giving his arm a squeeze. “I’ve missed you too, by the way. It was just … difficult. You all wanted me to be who I was instead of who I’ve become.”

     

                “We still love you for who you are, even if we miss who you were. Just … come to drinks. Come over for dinner. Come to games night. We miss you. ”

     

                “It’s been almost two years,” Kara murmured. 

     

                “It has.”

     

                “I think … it’s time for me to start sorting my shit out. Properly this time. I’m sorry as well, for how things went at work. I know- I know I deserved it, that I took advantage of our friendship. I shouldn’t have done that and … I- it’s different now. I am doing better even if I’m still working things out. I just- it’s been difficult but I don’t want to lose everything in my past just because I lost Mike. I don’t want to lose everyone; I just need you all to trust me to sort out my own mess, even when I do a bad job of it.”

     

                James slung an arm around her shoulder, “well, I think that’s a great idea. Just let us know how we can help.”

     

                Breakfast was a little less tense after that and Kara hesitantly shared the news with Nia and Querl as well as they sipped their coffee and she cut into a stack of pancakes, her mind weighted with thoughts of her late husband. She rarely got pancakes when eating out anymore because they always reminded her of him, but lately, Kara was starting to realise that avoiding the painful things didn’t make it easier, it was confronting them, thinking fondly of those memories, that helped the most. 

     

                Eating her pancakes, she engaged in the conversation, laughing with a little more ease as things started to fall into place in a few areas of her life. Kara realised that there were some things she needed a fresh start with - a new job, selling the apartment, a new relationship - but there were some things, like her friends, that she didn’t need to set aside in order to get through it all.

     

                Feeling even more relieved at her revelation and subsequent patching up of friendships, Kara made her way back to Alex and Kelly’s, finding the latter home, she spent a long morning packing away her clothes and ruminating over everything. It was quiet and peaceful, listening to music as she knelt in the middle of the bedroom and folded things into piles and weighed her options. It was simple, of course, but doubts had a way of creeping up on Kara and she wanted to be sure.

     

                She stopped by the library on the way home and checked out five books that had even a chapter on Alzheimer’s or dementia before heading home and having a late lunch with Kelly. The two of them ate their sandwiches as Kara mined Kelly for as much information on the disease as she could, outlining her plan to read up on it so she could better understand it, and better equip herself to handle her budding relationship and her girlfriend’s wife. She missed the aching look in her sister-in-law’s eyes as she tried to help her as much as she could, both of them knowing it wouldn’t change anything in the long run. 

     

                Spending the rest of her afternoon drinking tea and poring over her borrowed books at the dining table, the hours slipped by until Kara received a text from Lena letting her know she was home. After tidying up and giving Lena some time to unwind after her day, Kara said goodbye to Kelly and took the stairs down to the lobby and outside, the afternoon blurring into night as she walked to the bus stop and caught the line to Lena’s apartment. 

     

                Stopping off for flowers, she walked to Lena’s building and pressed the buzzer as she arrived outside. Lena let her in and Kara waved to the security guard as she crossed over to the elevator. Riding it up, she felt nervous excitement kindle in her stomach, the quiet thrill of seeing Lena again making her a little jittery as she was dropped off at the top floor and walked down the hallway to her front door. Knocking, she waited a minute for the door to open.

     

                “Hi,” Lena murmured, a coy smile curling her lips as she opened the door wider to let Kara inside.

     

                “Hi. How’re you?” Kara asked, her own face softening with a smile.

     

                Lena’s hand slid up Kara’s sleeve, up to the side of her neck. Eyelids closing as her smile grew, Kara leaned into her touch and felt Lena lean in, the brush of her lips making warmth blossom in Kara’s chest as her stomach clenched. She pushed back against the kiss, as fleeting as it was and then covered Lena’s hand with her own as she opened her eyes to look at her.

     

                “If this is the welcome home I’ll get, you’re being very convincing in getting me to move back in,” Kara whispered. “These are for you.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena slipped her hand free, fingertips brushing Kara’s neck before she reached for the bouquet. “Is that all it takes? And before I had to sleep with you for months and then not at all to convince you. Thank you.”

     

                “And look how that worked out for you,” Kara murmured. “Now, how was your day?”

     

                “Oh, it was … long. How was yours?”

     

                “Quiet.”

     

                “Hungry?” Lena hopefully asked, her voice laced with caution.

     

                Wrinkling her nose, Kara let out a quiet huff of laughter. “Always. What do you feel like?”

     

                “I thought I’d cook.”

     

                “Sounds good. What’s on the menu?”

     

                She followed Lena through the apartment after hanging up her coat and slipping off her oxfords. Stepping through the archway of the kitchen, Kara paused at the dimly lit table, draped with a tablecloth and a few candles wavering amidst the table set for two. Lena had a bottle of wine chilling in a bucket and a bouquet of roses in a vase and she gave Kara a waveringly uncertain smile.

     

                “What’s all this?” Kara wondered aloud, cocking her head to the side.

     

                “There has been … a shocking lack of romance between us, which … understandable, I guess, seeing as things were never- I mean there was a week but … um, well, I guess this is me trying to wine and dine you - with something other than Big Belly Burger. I thought maybe we could talk. Properly this time.”

     

                A surprised laugh worked its way up Kara’s throat, “oh, well, now I’m really convinced.”

     

                Pulling out a chair, Lena gestured for her to sit. “Dinner will be a three-course affair,” she loftily murmured with a grin on her face. “For our appetiser, we have a tapas board.”

     

                Moving over to the counter, Lena picked up the platter and carried it to the table, setting it safely in the middle. Kara appraised the cheeses, cured hams and chorizo and smiled, a little restless with her delight as she bit her lip.

     

                “Looks amazing.”

     

                Flashing her a quick smile, Lena reached for the bottle resting in the bucket of ice, setting it down on the table and reaching for the corkscrew.

     

                “Wine?” Kara asked.

     

                “For you. I bought a bottle of a very convincing fake for myself.”

     

                Giving her a tender smile, Kara propped her chin up in her hand. “I’ll have the same.”

     

                “You don’t have to-”

     

                “I know, I want to.”

     

                Hesitating, Lena nodded and quickly walked to the fridge, swapping the bottle of Chardonnay for an alcohol-free variety. Popping the cork, she poured them both a glass and Kara sipped it with trepidation before finding it similar enough to ignore the difference. Taking a seat across from her, Lena gestured for Kara to start eating. Cutting a sliver of Manchego cheese, Kara somewhat easily cleared her throat.

     

                “So … how did it go at the hospital?”

     

                Shoulders sagging, Lena closed her eyes, her mouth a thin line as she exhaled through her nose. 

     

                “Kara, we don’t- we don’t have to talk about her all the time now,” Lena slowly said, a clouded look on her face. “I mean, I’m glad that you can get past the fact that I’m married and she’s a big part of my life. I appreciate the effort to be mature about it but … we don’t have to bring up the elephant in the room all the time.”

     

                “Oh. No. That’s- I’m curious. Genuinely. I’m not doing it to be polite, I just- I really would like to know how she is, if- if she had a good day, what you guys talked about. If you want to share, that is. I don’t want you to think that we- that you shouldn’t talk about her with me because of … the way things are. And you’ve had to keep everything to yourself for so long so if you want to - only if you want to - you could tell me about your visit and maybe … I don’t know, maybe it’ll just lighten the weight of it all.”

     

                Cautiously surprised by her response, Lena pressed her lips into a flat line as she plucked an olive from the platter and eyed it before popping it in her mouth. She chewed quickly and swallowed, leaning back in her chair as she toyed with her glass of non-alcoholic wine, and Kara could practically see her desire for it to be the real deal radiating from her. It was evident it hadn’t gone well.

     

                Shrugging half-heartedly, Lena gave her a humourless smile, eyes bright with pain. “What’s there to say? It’s never going to be good news. It’s … degenerative. Slowly in her case but progressing all the same. Her scans came back as expected and aside from having the cast taken off a recently broken arm, she’s as fit as expected too. So … that’s about the extent of it.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “And how was your day?” Lena dryly asked.

     

                “Um … it was okay,” Kara haltingly replied. “I got everything packed. I guess it’s lucky I didn’t have much to take with me anyway.”

     

                Nodding, Lena hesitated. “Have you thought about what I said? I’m not trying to rush you-“

     

                “I know,” Kara murmured, giving her a tender smile. “I have been thinking about it.”

     

                “Good. Just … let me know when you’re sure.”

     

                “I will.”

     

                They picked at the platter as the conversation flowed on to other topics - work, Alex and Kelly’s adoption process, Sam’s intention to visit soon, a new TV show Lena had started - and Lena rose to her feet to start prepping the main course once the little platter was almost bare. Kara tried to help but was firmly ordered to stay seated, so she sipped her nonalcoholic wine and watched Lena move around the kitchen, finishing off whatever she had simmering in a pan and plating it up.

     

                “For our main course,” Lena murmured, her fingers brushing Kara’s shoulders as she leaned over her to set her plate down. “Braised beef in a red wine jus with pureed mash.”

     

                “Did you actually cook all this or did you get a private chef in to sneakily prep it all before I got here?”

     

                Lena laughed at her scepticism. “All me. I rarely cook but when I do, I try to make an effort.”

     

                “Colour me impressed.”

     

                “You’d be impressed if I plated up your usual order for Chinese takeout,” Lena snorted, reclaiming her seat across from her.
