                After their main course, Lena served up two slices of pie, which she admitted to buying at a bakery as she scooped vanilla bean ice cream onto the side of the warm wedges and carried them to the table. The coffee machine was pouring creamy espresso into two cups to go with it and Kara was feeling pleasantly full and comfortable as she dug into her slice.

     

                “Can we talk for a minute?” she slowly asked as Lena rejoined her.

     

                Humming as she took a sip of her coffee, Lena’s eyebrows rose and fell quickly in an encouraging response. Setting her cup down, she cleared her throat. “Of course.”

     

                “Um … just quickly, I- if I moved back in … how would- how would you want that to be?”

     

                “Well … how it was before. More like that last week, if I had it my way.”

     

                “So … I’d keep the room I had before.”

     

                A flicker of surprise crossed Lena’s face and she opened her mouth, inhaling, before closing it again. “Oh. I mean … if you wanted to stay in my room, I think I’d need some time to think-”

     

                “I- no, that’s not- I mean … I like sleeping beside you but I think … it would be good to have our own space. With the way things are … I know it seems silly to- to be hesitant about it when we’ve been here before but I just- I know we don’t have to go slow but … we both need to be making the right choices for both of our sakes so I just wasn’t sure- we both have a lot going on so I think that keeping it separate … that would be the best idea. I just wasn’t sure if you thought- if you expected me to …”

     

                “Take her place?” Lena asked, a wry twist to her lips as she arched an eyebrow slightly.

     

                Wincing faintly, Kara shrugged, training her eyes on her pie as she used her spoon to cut a bite off. “After a fashion, yes.”

     

                “No. We do have a lot going on; it hasn’t even been two years for you yet. We don’t have to rush anything, I just- I like coming home to you. I want you here. I want to eat dinner with you and talk about our days and kiss you and go to bed with you. Two months without that has made me appreciate my own mind a lot more and … I know that’s what I want. But I like the idea of having our own things. I don’t think I’m ready for that step yet, to have … your side of the bed, your clothes in my closet. It might sound stupid-”

     

                “It’s not.”

     

                Their eyes met, wary and vulnerable before a tentative smile tugged at Kara’s lips. Setting her spoon down, Lena paused before climbing to her feet. “Come here.”

     

                Rising, abandoning her own slice of pie, Kara rounded the corner of the table as Lena met her halfway, reaching for her face and kissing her fervently as she turned her and pressed Kara into the table. Pulling her closer, Kara kissed her back, her stomach swooping as desire washed through her, that stamped need to be held and touched flaring strongly to life after weeks without her. Pausing, she went still at the feel of Lena’s hands going to her buttons, breaking off the kiss as she breathed quickly.

     

                “Lena, I- are you sure- it’s okay if we-”

     

                “Shut up.”

     

                Kara’s words died in her mouth and she considered pressing the matter for a moment before snapping her jaw shut and swallowing any objections. Pulling Lena close again, she kissed her fervently. As Lena started to unbutton Kara’s shirt, making quick work of it, Kara half-turned, tearing her lips away reluctantly as she scrabbled behind her. 

     

                “Hang on,” she rasped, her voice a little rough.

     

                Picking up a candle, she blew out the little flame and reached for the others as Lena kissed her neck and slid her shirt over her shoulders, pooling in the crook of her elbows. Dimming the kitchen, Kara turned back around and recaptured Lena’s lips, any potential fire hazards taken care of, leaving her with plenty of undisturbed time on her hands. Shedding her shirt, Kara tossed it onto the floor and picked Lena up with a small sound of surprised protest from her.

     

                Carrying her to her room, Kara set her down on the bed and neither of them moved from it for the better part of the next two hours, wrapped up in each other, basking in the feeling of taking their time, nothing inhibiting them, no lies or disproportionate feelings holding them back. 

     

                Kara could have stayed that way all night, sweat cooling on her skin, her chest rising and falling quickly with Lena’s cheek pressed against it, her hairline damp as she struggled to catch her breath. Caressing the length of Lena’s spine with her fingertips, Kara realised she had the option to stay that way all night. That if she made the right choice she could lay beside her every night, maybe in a different bed across the hall, and they would have more than a week - they’d have a lifetime together. She felt a flicker of guilt at the feeling that she was stealing a future that should have belonged to Andrea but, ultimately, it was out of Kara’s hands and all she could do now was decide what she wanted to do for herself and for Lena.

     

                “Lena?” she whispered to the darkness of the room, waiting for the low hum in response. “I’d like to move back in again if that’s alright.”

    Chapter 27

                A few days later, Lena was parked outside Alex’s place while Kara assembled her few bags inside the trunk and gave her sister a quick smile, hands buried in the pockets of her jeans as she raised her eyebrows quickly. Dusting her hands off, Kara walked over to her and Alex straightened, giving her a tight hug.

     

                “The couch is always free but do yourself a favour and don’t mess it up.”

     

                Choking on a quiet laugh, Kara squeezed her eyes shut. “I’ll be alright.”

     

                “I know you will,” Alex said with conviction.

     

                “Thanks again.”

     

                Pulling back, Alex gave her a look of exasperation, “you don’t have to thank me. I’m your sister; I just want you to be happy. Even if I haven’t always managed to say it properly.”

     

                Nodding, Kara gave her a quick smile, “I know you do.”

     

                Giving her shoulder a squeeze, Alex gestured towards the Lexus, where Lena was waiting patiently, toying with her wedding and engagement rings as she watched the two of them. The corners of her mouth twitched with a faint smile, her eyes sliding to Alex.

     

                “You should come over for dinner again soon.”

     

                “And maybe you should finally come for dinner here,” Alex wryly replied, folding her arms over her chest. 

     

                Nodding in agreement of the offer, Lena smiled slightly. “Maybe I should.”

     

                “Next week?” Alex asked, her eyes sliding back to her sister. “It’s fine, we’ll sort it out later. You probably want to go and unpack everything.”

     

                “Alright, well, let me know how your meeting goes tomorrow morning,” Kara sternly told her.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Alex smiled. “ Obviously. I’m not going to come home with a child one day without telling you.”

     

                Scoffing, Kara said goodbye and made her way over to the car, buckling herself into the passenger seat as Lena climbed in behind the wheel. Starting the car, she pulled out and joined the flow of traffic, fiddling with the radio and then looking over at Kara.

     

                “Are you sure you want to do this?”

     

                Giving her a quick grin, Kara sank into the seat. “It’s a bit late for second-guessing now, don’t you think? I’ve already eaten the cost of giving up my lease-”

     

                “Which I will reimburse you for-”

     

                “Which you will absolutely not do because I get to live rent-free in your astronomically expensive penthouse. Even my deposit and first month’s rent aside, yes, I’m sure. I … well, if I hadn’t been so wrapped up in my own feelings, I wouldn’t have moved out anyway. I mean, not that I expected you to let me stay there without talking about things, with how it was that last week, but you know what I mean.”

     

                Reaching across, Lena gently squeezed her knee. “I know what you mean.”

     

                Still, Kara felt a prickle of nervousness as Lena drove them home - to their home. Not in a roommate sort of way, not as a temporary solution to debt but as the beginning of something permanent. And it wasn’t a bad sort of nervousness, the edge of excitement, of keen relief, making her calm instead of jittery, knowing what to expect and feeling pleased to have recovered what had been missing for almost two months.

     

                Parking in the underground garage, Lena popped the trunk and Kara hauled two of her bags out while Lena grabbed the other one. They rode the elevator upstairs and Lena unlocked the front door, Aristotle sitting at the door with his tail fanning across the floor with excitement. Lena stooped and scooped him up before carrying on to Kara’s designated bedroom and dropping her bag onto the made bed before leaving to fetch her dog a treat.

     

                Stepping inside, Kara felt a sliver of peace cut through her as she lingered inside the doorway before crossing over to the bed. Setting down the last of her things in her room, Kara looked around at the familiar room and had the vague feeling of someone who’d gone on vacation for a while, or been away for college and come home to their childhood bedroom. That was, it felt like home already, without any of her things unpacked yet, instantly at ease in the room she’d occupied for months until it had all gone to shit.

     

                Exhaling with a bone-deep sense of relief, Kara glanced over to the door and smiled at Lena, who was leaning against the doorframe with her arms folded. She arched an eyebrow in response. “Need help unpacking?”

     

                “I’ll do it later. It’s not much.”

     

                “Good thing you didn’t have a lot to take with you or we would’ve been hogging the elevator all afternoon.”

     

                Raising her eyebrows, Kara smiled grimly, taking a few steps towards her. “Mm, I guess now I just need to sort through all of the junk you have in storage for me. What do you think; Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, free curbside pickings?”

     

                Scoffing as she pushed off the doorframe and started down the hallway to the kitchen, Lena rolled her eyes. “You can just leave it in storage. No one will touch it.”

     

                “What’s the point? It’s not like I’m going to use it, it’ll just be collecting dust.”

     

                “They’re your things .”

     

                “Yeah, my old bed and some dishes and … I don’t know, a lamp. It’s nothing important.”

     

                “Still, you don’t have to sell it all,” Lena murmured.

     

                “Be honest with me; would you want to change anything about your apartment? The home you made with your wife?”

     

                “I- no,” Lena admitted. “No, I don’t- I don’t think I’m ready for that just yet. But those things were what you used to make a home with your husband .”

     

                “The home I had with my husband is gone . It’s- it’s just a bunch of furniture now.”

     

                Kara wasn’t even being blasé about it, she was just weary of grief, of the long process of clinging to the past, wondering if she was being too dismissive but not feeling strongly attached to any of the packed away belongings to really miss much of it. There were the things she’d keep, of course. The photos, the trinkets from their trips, the mementoes of a life built with someone but she didn’t need his old computer chair or the rug from their living room, hauled around with her as a reminder of their apartment. The memories were heavy enough to carry.

     

                “And this is your home now.”

     

                “So maybe we- maybe eventually we'll pick out a new paint colour or something. Buy a new rug together. But this place is still your home that you had with Andrea and I don’t need to change anything for myself so …”

     

                Grabbing two mugs out of the cupboard, Lena set them down beneath the coffee filter and pushed a few buttons on the machine. Walking up behind her, Kara hesitantly cradled her waist from behind, a little uncertain, a little nervous. 

     

                “Okay,” Lena sighed, turning. “Just … don’t think you have to rush into decisions because you’re here. I know the storage situation was supposed to be short-term for you but it can stay and collect dust for the next sixty years if you don’t want to let go-”

     

                Her throat feeling a little tight, Kara smiled weakly, “I’ve got to let go at some point. I already have. Look … I know Andrea is the great love of your life but … Mike wasn’t mine. It’s … painful and … confusing but it’s the truth and it’s been hard to come to terms with it. And that’s okay. I loved him but I’m not going to drag the past around with me for the rest of my life because … that’s just not good for me. I know- I know it’s different for you and I don’t expect you to cut the past loose but … this is a fresh start for me. It’s- it’s good.”

     

                A quick laugh escaped Lena. “You don’t sound sure.”

     

                Eyelids shuttering, Kara’s lips twitched with exasperated amusement. “I’m sure,” she decidedly replied before hesitating. “I- it’s soon, I know that, and …”

     

                “And what?”

     

                Wariness flickered in Kara’s eyes for a brief moment and her lips parted to reply, a quiet inhale preceding silence before she closed her mouth again. Humming dubiously, Kara’s mouth thinned and she kept her eyes down as she tried again.

     

                “And it’s not … normal between us.”

     

                “It never has been.”

     

                “I know,” Kara agreed, her voice somewhat strained as she winced slightly. “I just mean … I don’t know how it’s supposed to be. With us. It’s- obviously before I thought … but you still have a wife and I don’t know what that means for us-”

     

                “I thought we’d talked about-”

     

                “No, I know that, I’m okay with how it’ll be, I just- I don’t know how to … behave.”

     

                “Behave?” Lena echoed, bemused.

     

                Looking sheepish, Kara sighed. “I’m just overthinking it. I’m in my head too much.”

     

                Reaching up, Lena cupped her cheeks in her hands, her eyes flitting around Kara’s face with earnest interest. “What are you thinking?”

     

                Closing her eyes and leaning into Lena’s touch, Kara took a moment to confess. “What it must be like for you to see her and be touched by me and if you even want that. I know it was hard for you-”

     

                “Kara,” Lena softly sighed, a pained look of amusement softening her face. “I’m not thinking of her when I’m with you. ”

     

                “I know but … it’s just- I would understand if you didn’t- if there were things that you didn’t want to do, things that might be too unbearable for you.”

     

                “Like what?”

     

                Her voice was gentle and curious, her hand cradling the side of Kara’s neck as she met her eyes. Lips twitching, Kara shrugged nonchalantly. “I don’t know … maybe you had a bad day and you don’t want to come home and cuddle up on the sofa with me because you used to do that with Andrea. Maybe you don’t want someone else to massage your shoulders in the bath after a long day in the office. Maybe you look at me and see someone you just want to have sex with instead of all the little nuances of dating. That’s okay, I just- some clarification would be good because I don’t want to mess it up again and-”

     

                “There were so many days I would have loved to come home to cuddle with you on the sofa - especially after a bad visit,” Lena confessed with a choked laugh. “There’s nothing I would have liked more than that but … we were never there. And I’d be lying if I said I didn’t wish I could do that with Andrea but that doesn’t- that doesn’t change how I feel about you. That’s the hard part for me. But being with you isn’t unbearable; you’re my raft in the middle of the ocean that is having a sick wife. I’m sorry to throw you into the middle of all that chaos, especially so unprepared for it all - I regret that, I do - but … I’m glad you’re here.”

     

                Some of the worry in Kara’s chest receded and her mouth thinned slightly with relieved acceptance, even if she was still getting used to the idea of being with someone else. It wasn’t so difficult for her, almost two years since they’d met with a relationship that had eased into its current state, but it was different to how it had been before she’d found out about Andrea. Fundamentally, nothing was different but that knowledge of Lena’s living wife had added a layer of anxiety to Kara’s image of their relationship, even though she’d willingly walked back into it.

     

                “I just don’t want you to think you have to be okay with things you’re not ready for for my sake,” Kara murmured.

     

                “You’re just about the only thing in my life I’m okay with,” Lena murmured, her eyelid shuttering as she smiled weakly. “And it took me a while to be ready for that and it wasn’t for your sake. It was for mine too. I’ve already told you I love my wife and I love you. I didn’t … want to put you through this, I know it’s not fair but I wouldn’t have told you that if I wasn’t prepared for what that would mean for us, knowing how you felt too.”

                

                The coffee machine fell silent and Lena reached over to snag two cups, handing one off to Kara with a wry look on her face. “Now, at the beginning … I definitely wasn’t okay with the fact that I was falling in love with someone else. It had been a shock to fall in love the first time, let alone with someone else while married. I came around to it though.”

     

                Raising her eyebrows as she inhaled deeply, shoulders squaring, Kara grimaced as she nursed her cup. “Yeah?”

     

                “Mm,” Lena hummed, taking a sip. “Not in my finest moment but …”

     

                “That wasn’t my finest moment either,” Kara murmured, her face crumpling.

     

                “It’s not like I gave you any warning.”

     

                “I don’t think that’s something you can really warn someone about. Not unless you drop it on them at the beginning and … I probably wouldn’t have touched you with a ten-foot pole if I’d known you were still married. Just out of principle.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose, Lena jerked her head towards the living room and Kara trailed after her, listening to Lena as she replied, laughing. “Okay, well now I really feel like a piece of shit for having less morals than you.”

     

                “It’s different for you,” Kara sighed, sinking onto the sofa, “you knew what your circumstances were like. I wouldn’t have known that even if I’d known the truth. It was up to you to choose - it always will be.”

     

                “Come here,” Lena said, setting down her cup of coffee and then sitting back, holding an arm out.

     

                “What?”

     

                “Come here.”

     

                “Why?”

     

                “Because … today is a good day, and I’m choosing to cuddle with you on the sofa and let it be a good day for a little while longer.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara let out a huff of laughter, sipped her coffee and then set it down before going to Lena. Curling her feet up with her, she sank into the side of her and let out a long breath, some of the residual tension bleeding out of her. Lena idly stroked her hair as they sat in silence for a bit and then pressed a kiss to Kara’s hair.

     

                “Better?”

     

                Kara hummed in agreement and then shifted forward for their coffees, her legs over Lena’s lap as she adjusted her position, leaning against the back of the sofa and taking a sip. They turned the TV on and sat together as they watched a movie, getting comfortable beside each other, Lena grabbing the folded throw blanket from the back of the sofa and spreading it over their legs, Aristotle jumping up and curling in between them. Kara would have given anything for every day to have been as comfortable as that.

     

                They didn’t move for most of the afternoon but as the day crept towards evening, Lena’s eyes kept straying towards the stretch of windows and when she got to her feet to take their empty coffee cups to the kitchen, she was a little restless. Rubbing her palms together, she ducked her head and let out a soft sigh before meeting Kara’s eyes over the end of the sofa.

     

                “I should go and see her before dinner,” Lena murmured.

     

                Kara raked a hand through her hair, nodding before she hesitated. “Do you want me to come or-”

     

                “No,” Lena softly cut her off. “It’s- no, I’ll go by myself. You don’t-”

     

                “I know but I know it’s hard for you so-”

     

                “No. No, thank you.”

     

                Lena’s reply was firm and Kara trailed off, her blue eyes wide and aching as she fiddled with her hands in her lap, still cross-legged on the sofa. Closing her eyes, Lena’s mouth flattened and she exhaled through her nose before looking at Kara.

     

                “I know you’re just trying to help but … this is something that’s personal for me. I don’t- I don’t want to have to try and manage Andrea’s and your feelings at the same time. I love spending time with you and I cherish my time with her too, but I don’t want things to overlap like that because it’s- that’s where things get messy.”

     

                “Oh. That’s okay,” Kara quickly insisted, climbing to her feet, pushing the blanket aside and crossing over to Lena. “You do what you have to do. But if you ever feel like you want me there - if you’re caught up with something at work or if there’s ever anything you need dropped off - just let me know. If- if we’re together then that makes you my family and she’s your family, so she’s also a part of us . It’s going to overlap regardless but … I can help. Only when you want it though. I won’t- I won’t just show up there again.”

     

                “Thank you,” Lena whispered, a hint of a smile on her lips. She leaned in and kissed her quickly. “I have to go.”

     

                “Take your time. I’ll get started on dinner.”

     

                Nodding, Lena gathered her things and shrugged into a jacket and shoes at the door before calling goodbye down the hallway and leaving. It was still relatively early in the afternoon so Kara decided to take Aristotle for a walk for an hour before starting dinner, enjoying the fresh air and the familiar routine that she’d been missing, a tennis ball taken with her to throw for him in the dog park. Returning back home, she settled on an easy dinner of chicken and salad and did all of the prepping while she waited for Lena to come home.

     

                In the meantime, Kara started unpacking her clothes, sorting out piles and hanging up her nicer items in the closet. It ate up the next hour as she watched TV in the process, Aristotle keeping her company on the bed, and she didn’t hear Lena come home, turning at the sound of a knock on the bedroom door before calling out for Lena to open it.

     

                “Your chicken is looking … charred,” Lena greeted her.

     

                The faint smell of smoke drifted in and Kara dropped her sneakers as she swore. Laughing, Lena shook her head, the corners of her eyes creasing, and Kara winced sheepishly. “Ah, well, there goes my plan to keep it simple.”

     

                “There’s salmon in the fridge,” Lena said, turning. “That’ll do as a replacement.”

     

                Abandoning the few remaining items, Kara followed her back to the kitchen. “How is she?”

     

                “Good. She was a bit restless but she settled down when I started reading to her.”

     

                “What did you read?”

     

                Leaning against the countertop, Kara watched Lena fetch the salmon and set a pan over the heat. “We’re halfway through a new biography on Marie Curie.”

     

                “Oh. Interesting?”

     

                “Yeah, well, interesting enough to hold her attention anyway. I’m not really big on biographies myself. Still, history is interesting.”

     

                She set the pieces of salmon skin down in the pan and leaned against the counter beside the stove, arms folded over her chest. “What did you get up to?”

                

                “I took Aristotle for a walk and then just unpacked.”

     

                “Do you need anything? I can go shopping for you tomorrow. I need to get some things for Andrea anyway.”

     

                Pushing off the counter, Kara slowly crossed over to Lena and reached out, hooking a finger through the belt loop of her jeans and pulling her closer. A smile twitched at the corners of Lena’s mouth as Kara leaned in to brush their noses together, laughing softly.

     

                “You’ll do.”

     

                “Anything else?”

     

                “No. Just you.”

    Chapter 28

                They fell back into the easy routine of living together, picking up from where they’d left off in that week that had felt so perfect to Kara until disaster struck. Now, it was something constant, something familiarly comforting as they tried to navigate the new territory of a relationship, the early days of uncertainty and boundaries and relearning things about each other that hadn’t existed within the confines of their friendship. 

     

                Yes, there were days when Lena was exhausted and vulnerable, coming home late from her visits with Andrea and unreachable by Kara’s attempts to coax her out of her brooding, but at least she knew why. There were still things they didn’t know about each other but it no longer felt like there were any secrets between them.

     

                That cloud of worry that had dogged Kara for months, if not longer, wondering why Lena was struggling so much and feeling as if she couldn’t help her, had lightened as well, that bridge of honesty helping to make sense of things. The knowledge of why made it easier for Lena to make her daily visits and haltingly explain how they had gone, instead of bottling it all up with the aid of vodka. 

     

                Although she’d brushed off the effectiveness of AA meetings in her situation, Lena was still intent on remaining sober as she tried to muddle through the ongoing grief of Andrea’s illness, and they’d both made a pact to seek genuine help with referrals from Kelly to different psychologist’s offices Downtown. It was another step in trying to make sense of things, of unpacking their separate feelings, their individual griefs and past relationships in a way that wasn’t centred around their relationship with each other. They both needed that space, that time to muddle through everything that had happened within the last two years and beyond, working on themselves in a way they hadn’t while attending Group. 

     

                And it really did help, both of them wryly admitting to the benefits of therapy when it wasn’t at a shitty Y centre, where they didn’t have to be bribed by each other’s company and tea and donuts to show up. They were at that place now where they wanted to work on themselves, break free of the weight of their grief where they’d only wanted to dwell before. And it was purely the fact that they had each other that enabled them to do it, knowing there was some future for themselves that didn’t revolve around their grief. That didn’t mean there weren’t hard days but they were both processing things better, handling their emotions, fixing things that had been neglected or broken in their grief. For Kara, that was largely repairing the relationships with her friends in a way that didn’t revolve around her anger towards their expectations. For Lena, it was coming to terms with the circumstances of her marriage.

     

                Despite the difficulty of it, it was something of a relief for both of them, Lena no longer shutting Kara out, even if it meant Kara spent more than one night holding her tightly in whichever bed they’d settled into, listening to Lena’s hitching breaths as she tried to explain how she’d gotten the new lavender bruises on her arms or Andrea’s erratic mood that visit, how she hadn’t recognised her wife for another day. Conversely, there were nights when Kara confessed with a wavering voice all her doubts about herself, the flaws in her relationships, finally bringing herself to talk about her lost parents as well as Mike, so much anxiety around losing people that Lena would murmur promises that she wouldn’t leave her too, that they’d always have each other.

     

                In the meantime, the second anniversary of losing Mike crept up on Kara within a couple of months of moving in with Lena again. It was a reminder that made her feel that prickling guilt at moving on so quickly but things had always been difficult in her marriage, in a very anticlimactic way, and Kara had resolved not to think about how Mike would have felt about it. It wasn’t that Kara had moved on , as such, because he was still a big part of her life, her memories, her behaviour as she managed her own losses, but she was in that same place as Lena where her heart held enough room for both of them and she knew her husband was gone for good.

     

                It was strange to think how so much had changed, how it felt like an eternity had passed without him, how different she was to the person she’d been two years ago, but then in some ways, it felt like no time at all. Kara had Lena now but that didn’t mean she wasn’t hit with sudden waves of grief that stopped her in her tracks, the guilt that crept up on her at the most inopportune times.

     

                On the day of the anniversary, she woke up early in Lena’s bed and didn’t move. She’d asked Jack for the Friday off and he’d been all too understanding and sympathetic, so she stayed in bed and listened to the sounds of Lena showering, the cupboards opening and closing and the droning of the hair dryer. Then finally the bathroom door opened. 

     

                “Oh, morning,” Lena softly greeted her, wrapped in a bathrobe as she came out with her hair and makeup done. “I hope I didn’t wake you.”

     

                “No,” Kara murmured, nudging up her glasses to rub her eyes.

     

                Moving over to the bed, Lena sank onto the edge of the mattress and reached out to smooth Kara’s hair back. “How’re you feeling?”

     

                Shrugging as her mouth twisted down at the corners, Kara couldn’t explain the odd vacancy in her chest. “I’m okay,” she mumbled.

     

                “Are you sure you don’t want me to come with you?”

     

                “Yeah. You need to go and see Andrea, and go to work.”

     

                “I don’t have to go to work.”

     

                “I know. I just- I think I’d prefer it if you did today.”

     

                Nodding in acceptance of Kara’s wishes, Lena hesitated and then reached for her hand. Kara let her pick it up and press a kiss to the back of it, managing a weak smile in response. Smoothing the smudge of lipstick off the back of Kara’s hand, Lena retreated and Kara watched her get dressed as she propped herself up on the pillows, brooding quietly.

     

                She emerged from the bedroom a short while later as Lena was on her way to bring her some coffee and Kara joined her in the kitchen for breakfast, picking at a bowl of cereal as she curled up on her seat. Lena lingered longer than usual, fussing around in the kitchen as she tidied up and insisted on doing a load of laundry - she never did her own laundry - before Kara raised her eyebrows, a small smile on her lips as her blue eyes shone with amusement. 

     

                “Go and see your wife.”

     

                “I will,” Lena insisted. “I’m cleaning.”

     

                “You’re stalling .”

     

                “Well, maybe I want to see you today.”

     

                “You’ll see me tonight.”

     

                “I can see Andrea tonight too.”

     

                “Yes, you can see her this morning and tonight.”

     

                Lena exhaled softly as she stopped wiping over the counters and fixed Kara with a searching look. Swallowing the lump in her throat, Kara gave her a wavering smile, her eyes bright with pain as she firmly insisted.

     

                “I’m fine. I mean … it’s not like it’s the first so …”

     

                “Are you sure? I can come with you if-”

     

                Uncurling, Kara let her spoon fall against the edge of her bowl and climbed to her feet, rounding the kitchen island and stopping in front of Lena. She folded her arms over her chest and cocked her head to the side, giving her a pointed look.

     

                “You have to go and see her. I don’t want you to ever feel bad about that.”

     

                “Yes, but … today’s not just any day. It’s a hard day for you and it’s- it’s a day for Andrea and … she doesn’t need me. I want to see her, of course, but if you need me-”

     

                Letting out a breathless laugh, Kara straightened, cupping Lena’s shoulders and giving her a wry look. “What I need is for you to go and see Andrea and treat it like any normal day, okay? You don’t- you don’t know … how many good days are left. Don’t miss any.”

     

                Agonised by the unfairness of even being forced to consider choosing, Lena winced gingerly, her green eyes apologetic as she cradled Kara’s waist. “I want all of her good days but you deserve someone here for your bad days too.”

     

                “I woke up to you and I’m having lunch with Alex. I’ll be okay. I’d actually … prefer to have some space today. Just for a few hours. You know, to process it all properly.”

     

                Face crumpling slightly, as if bewildered by Kara’s easy acceptance of the complexity of their circumstances, Lena pulled her a little bit closer. “I love you,” she murmured, a reminder that Kara didn’t need but was grateful for all the same.

     

                Kissing her in response, Kara let her go and gave her a stern look. “I love you too. Now off with you.”

     

                Laughing as she shook her head, Lena let Kara usher her to the door, picking up her things as she went. They said goodbye and Kara closed the front door behind her before she was left with her own devices. Not feeling motivated to do anything, she decided to crawl back into bed until eleven, when she dragged herself back out and showered for lunch.

     

                Alex picked her up and drove them to Noonan’s, where they ordered their usual and Kara tried to quickly get past the pitying sympathies that came with having a dead husband. Altogether, lunch was a good distraction and Alex quickly fell into the ritual of their usual gossiping and steered away from anything sensitive, anything that might have detracted from the weight of Kara’s grief.

     

                Eventually, she had to leave to get ready for a night shift and Kara declined a ride home, explaining that she needed to go to the cemetery and would prefer to walk. Alex didn’t push her, just hugged her tightly with instructions to call her if she needed anything. Parting ways, Kara put in her earphones and returned Eliza’s missed call as she walked, going through the motions of wearily reassuring her mom that she was fine.

     

                Before she reached the cemetery, Kara stopped off at a convenience store and picked up a bouquet of flowers that was looking dismally limp and then hesitated before making her way to the fridges lining the back wall. She hadn’t had anything to drink since reconciling with Lena, in an effort of solidarity for her girlfriend’s staunch determination for sobriety, but she picked up a six-pack of Coors from the fridge and paid at the front counter.

     

                Walking the rest of the way to the cemetery, Kara’s footsteps became heavier, a reluctance in her bones to enter the sprawling expanse of so much loss and grief. She’d been there before though and she did it again, walking along the path and down rows of headstones as she retraced the rarely walked route to Mike’s grave.

     

                “Hey,” she murmured to the headstone, staring broodingly at it for a moment, the complex feeling of grieving incorrectly leaving Kara confused.

     

                Hesitating, her six-pack of Coors hanging from her hand as she stood, shoulders slumped before sinking to the damp grass in the shade of the overarching oak tree. She crossed her legs beneath her and faced the headstone, teeth worrying at her bottom lip as she sat with that empty feeling in her chest.

     

                After a prolonged moment, Kara cracked open the first can of beer and took a sip, the can sweating in her palm from being refrigerated, and she swallowed the mouthful, her lips twisting grimly. 

     

                “So … two years,” she sighed. “They’ve gone by quickly. I’ve been busy. All that debt got the better of me in the end - thanks for that; I’m not mad anymore - so I had to move. Got a new job too - James fired me. And I’m seeing someone new. You might think it’s too soon, I don’t know. They don’t really give you a manual on moving on as a widow. She’s nice though, so lovely, so beautiful. You’d probably hate her; you always did feel threatened by anyone who outshone you.”

     

                Taking another sip of beer, Kara wrinkled her nose. “Sorry, that wasn’t very nice. All this space and time has let me see things with more clarity though. I was complicit too, I know that, but God, we made each other miserable, didn’t we? Or was I just the miserable one? I wish you were still here though. I do miss you.”

     

                Finishing off her first beer, she opened another one and continued to talk, taking sips whenever her throat got dry. Last year, on the first anniversary, she hadn’t been able to make herself stay for long, everything still so fresh and raw and her guilt at not being able to cry or react normally left her eager to get away from the cemetery. This time, it felt appropriate to stay, to talk to her late husband as if he could hear her, filling him in on the things he’d missed out on. Kara quite liked the opportunity to speak uninterrupted, something she would never have been able to do if he was sitting across from her. 

     

                An hour and then two passed by and she shifted her position, sitting with her back against the headstone, knees drawn up to her chest at first before she stretched her legs out in front of her. She only had one more beer left, the day quite hot as she sat in the shade, which was steadily moving, the crumpled cans amassing beside her as she finished them off one by one. Fortunately, the beer wasn’t strong enough to affect her greatly after five but Kara still felt the pleasant hum of it in her veins and was surprised to not feel very weepy. It was almost freeing, the torrent of words that spilt from her as she told Mike about Lena and Andrea, about Alex, Kelly and Esme, about her new job and Lena’s penthouse, about how Nia and Querl were thinking of having a courthouse wedding at the end of the year.

     

                Halfway through her last beer, she cut off mid-story at the sound of approaching footsteps and the ensuing pause. Cracking open her eyes, Kara blinked against the brightness, straightening up as she shaded her eyes, squinting. A woman around her age with dark hair held a bouquet with uncertainty in her eyes as she stood rooted to the spot. Kara was struck with the sudden realisation that she was there to visit Mike.

     

                Confused, her face furrowed as she cocked her head to the side. “Hi, um, you’re- you’re visiting Mike?”

     

                “Sorry, I- uh, I can come back,” the woman said.

     

                She was English, her accent not so refined as the news anchors she sometimes caught on TV, and that confused Kara even more. The woman wasn’t familiar to her as one of Mike’s coworkers, as an ex from college, or even recognisable from his funeral. Hand slowly dropping from her face, Kara swallowed.

     

                “No, it’s- it’s okay. I was just about to leave,” Kara insisted. “Um … were you his …”

     

                “Girlfriend. Imra.”

     

                Her suspicions were confirmed with such little drama that all Kara could do was smile thinly, surprised, but then again, not really. For so long, she’d found her marriage unsatisfying, like a dead-end road that she’d felt guilty for seeing the end of when Mike hadn’t voiced any discontent at all. But he’d felt it too, and it was like a sharp knife cutting cleanly through the ties of their marriage they’d clung to, to hear this stranger speak of her late husband’s similar feelings of dissatisfaction, two years too late. Of course, she had never considered this.

     

                “Oh,” Kara managed to get out, her tongue feeling clumsy in her mouth.

     

                “You’re Kara?”

     

                “He- he told you about me?”

     

                Surprised by the notion, Kara knocked back the rest of her beer and crumpled the can. Imra’s expression crumpled with bewildered amusement for a moment. “Of course. He said you’d moved back upstate when you separated.”

     

                A quick laugh escaped Kara and she shifted, gathering up her cans and stuffing them in her backpack before climbing to her feet. She gave Imra a wry smile, slinging the strap of the backpack over her shoulder.

     

                “We weren’t separated.”

     

                “You … weren’t?”

     

                “Sorry,” Kara murmured. “I was still his wife.”

     

                “Oh. Oh, I … I’m so-”

     

                Her smile was more genuine now, a little grim with pity, but Kara couldn’t find it in herself to blame this woman caught in the middle of something so complicated. She cut her off mid-apology. “It’s okay. Um … I’ll leave you to it then.”

     

                Surprised by her own tolerance, or perhaps simultaneously feeling freed or too stunned by the revelation to react appropriately, Kara turned to the headstone and gave the top of it a quick pat. A small laugh escaped her and she sighed wearily.

     

                “You bastard. I’ll see you next year.”

     

                Leaving nothing but the bouquet she’d brought with her behind, Kara walked past Imra, who floundered speechlessly, as if torn between attempting to apologise again and approaching the grave of her cheating boyfriend. Kara was spared any further discomfort as Imra remained rooted to the spot, and she let out a relieved breath as she walked through the cemetery with the encounter playing over in her mind, feeling as if she should have been devastated by the revelation but remarkably quiet and serene as she left.

     

                Emptying her beer cans into the trash once she’d left the cemetery, Kara aimlessly walked a few blocks before she had a conscious thought about where she was going and tracked down the nearest bus stop to take her back home. Between the heat of the day and the beers she’d knocked back, she felt a little clammy, a little faint, and there was a nauseous undercurrent to her shallow breaths as she lingered at the stop, traffic and bikes and pedestrians swarming past her as she reeled from the latest shock to her life. 

     

                The bus came and she climbed on and sank onto a seat with a glazed look in her eyes as she rode the route twice, putting her earphones in at some point as the droning voice of a Podcaster failed to distract her. All Kara could think about was the years of their marriage, trying to pinpoint the moment the affair might have started, if there had been signs she’d missed. Kara thought of herself as quite perceptive and not nearly as naïve as her doe-eyed look of innocence led people to think, and she was fairly certain Mike had been careful. There had never been bank statements with hotel stays, no deductions for luxury retailers, and maybe a few too many dinners but he’d always said they were tax-deductible business expenses. There were the large amounts of credit card debt, but that could have been honestly racked up the way he’d claimed. Kara mused over her careful dissection of their marriage as the late afternoon bled into the evening.

     

                By the time she roused herself to realise she was still on the bus, it was starting to get late and she hurriedly glanced at the time on her phone. Blinking, she looked around and found herself almost passing by her stop for the third time and gathered up her things, climbed to her feet and stood as the next few stops passed by. Lena would be home soon and Kara didn’t want to miss her stop again. 

     

                The late afternoon sun left the heat waning as sunlight reflected off a thousand windows and Kara was lost in her own thoughts as she side-stepped dog walkers and strollers and made for the apartment building. Letting herself in, she beat Lena home by the sounds of the empty apartment, Aristotle padding to the door to meet her, and took a long shower before changing into something comfortable.

     

                Her wet hair soaked into the back of her sweater as she made a cup of tea and curled up on the sofa with her laptop, scouring Google and her rarely-used social media for a woman named Imra. No results came up with mutual friends, which was accompanied by a keen feeling of relief to know her friends hadn’t been covering for Mike and the ugly feeling of resentment that he’d covered his tracks well, but there was a match with a Facebook profile picture of the woman she’d come face to face with. 

     

                Clicking on the profile, Kara browsed the facts. Imra Ardeen, 34, from Manchester. Worked as a consultant at UNICEF. Single. Clicking through the photos of her, Kara felt a little bitter. Imra was beautiful, well-travelled and had a seemingly vast array of hobbies, as seen on her Instagram - including other women’s husbands it seemed, albeit, ignorantly - and Kara’s stomach sank as she scrolled back through to two years ago and found a solitary photo of Mike on a hike with her. 

     

                She would have known him anywhere, even from the back with his head ducked down, a baseball cap on his head. Kara knew those worn hiking boots, the running shorts and the broad width of his shoulders and the backpack that was the same brand as the one he’d bought her. Clicking out of the tab, she felt a numbness spread through her, wondering how long it had gone on. It couldn’t have been long; Imra hadn’t been at the funeral, that much Kara was sure of. Maybe she hadn’t even known he was dead until weeks afterwards.

     

                The sound of the key in the front door roused her and Kara’s head turned in a jerky manner, a blank look in her eyes as she stared at the mouth of the hallway. Listening to the sound of heels clattering to the floor and the jangle of keys falling into the dish on the console, she waited for Lena to appear.

     

                “Hey,” Kara murmured, closing her laptop as she gave Lena a thin smile, her eyes landing on the bouquet of flowers.

     

                “Hey,” Lena replied, holding the flowers out and ducking her head to kiss the top of Kara’s. “How was it?”

     

                “Thanks,” Kara mumbled, glancing down at the arrangement of tulips, looking up and giving her another smile. She set her laptop aside and unfolded her legs, rising to her feet to put the flowers in water. “It was … okay. How was your day? How is she?”

     

                Understanding she might not have wanted to discuss her feelings on the matter of the anniversary, especially with the reminder of a new relationship staring her right in the face, Lena let the conversation swiftly move on. Blowing the air out of her cheeks, Lena followed Kara through to the kitchen as Kara opened and closed a few cupboards until Lena helped her out and procured a vase.

     

                Giving her a more genuine smile this time, Kara thanked her and ran the tap to fill it, the tulips carefully placed on the countertop as Lena set down her handbag and shed her coat. There was a grim set to her mouth and she looked tired, a little stressed perhaps, and Kara waited for her response.

     

                “She was okay today. Better this evening - she was a little erratic this morning but she hadn’t slept all night so that- well, it wasn’t surprising.”

     

                “And work?”

     

                “Ah, work is always the same. Clients, contractors, office spats. What’s new, right? Come here.”

     

                Setting the tulips in the vase, Kara turned away from it and walked towards Lena, her eyes creasing at the corners as she tiredly smiled, not really wanting to look her in the eye, afraid that the stinging that stole upon her would tip over into something else if she had to watch Lena look at her with so much concern. Still, she went willingly into Lena’s embrace, her chin propping on her shoulder as she let out a heavy sigh. Holding her tightly and rubbing her back, Lena comforted her the only way she could before pulling back. 

     

                Kissing her quickly, Kara watched the flicker of suspicion in Lena’s eyes grow. “Beer?”

     

                Touching her fingers to her lips, Kara shrugged, wrinkling her nose as she looked down. “A few. I … well, I didn’t think I could bring myself to stay there long sober.”

     

                “I could’ve gone-”

     

                “I know,” Kara whispered, reaching out to grab her hand, squeezing gratefully. “I just- I wanted to go alone. It’s easier to … I don’t know, feel the whole range of it alone. Same way you feel about it, I guess.”

     

                “Okay,” Lena murmured, cupping her chin and then kissing her again. Stepping back, she inhaled deeply and looked around. “So … what do you want for dinner? Is it a Chinese takeout kind of day or Big Belly Burger? I can also cook so don’t discount that if you feel like something homecooked.”

     

                Raking a hand through her hair, Kara shrugged. “I don’t mind. You pick.”

     

                Lena’s smile wavered slightly as her attempt to try not to dwell on Kara’s loss - for her sake - didn’t seem to work very well. But she thought it might have been more than that, that there was nothing about her loss that Kara had withheld before, letting Lena see so much of the conflicted grief that it was a little disconcerting to see her so closed off now, especially when they were closer now.

     

                “Is- is everything okay?”

     

                Swallowing past the tightness in her throat, Kara ducked her head in a quick nod and hummed lightly. “Mhm. I’m … a little tired.”

     

                “Okay,” Lena murmured, reaching out to tuck a strand of hair behind her ear. “I’ll sort something out. Did you- did you want something else to drink? I can run to the store.”

     

                “No, thank you. I’m fine.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                Lena’s repeated response sounded anything but reassured but Kara found it difficult to talk, her throat tight as her eyes avoidantly flitted around the room. Rubbing the back of her neck, she was silent as Lena moved around, settling in from a long day and watching her girlfriend closely. It was obvious something beyond the heaviness of the anniversary was bothering her, a drastic difference in her demeanour from that morning but Lena didn’t push it.

     

                Lena ended up ordering Chinese, knowing it was Kara’s favourite and deciding for her when she uncharacteristically didn’t leap at the opportunity. Kara sat at the kitchen table as Lena got changed into something more comfortable, lips pursed as she brooded, idly spinning her phone on the tabletop. 

     

                When Lena reemerged, she smiled fleetingly and rubbed at her tired eyes, the tension in her shoulders making her muscles ache. Stifling a yawn, Kara watched as Lena fetched two sparkling waters for them and walked over to Kara’s chair, cupping her chin and tilting her head up so their eyes met. They stared at each other for a long moment before Lena clicked her tongue, a furrow between her eyebrows, worry etched into the lines of her bare face.

     

                Whatever she read in Kara’s features, she didn’t push it and Kara was glad as she opened the bottle of water and took a sip. Their food arrived shortly afterwards and they dished up their own portions and sat across from each other. Quiet and thoughtful, Kara didn’t have much to say through dinner, pushing her food around her plate as Lena watched her closely, sensing something off despite Kara’s reassurances. The whole time, Kara was turning over the idea of telling Lena, unsure of how she felt about the whole thing.

     

                Lena finished eating first, watching with concern as Kara barely picked at her food, her green eyes intense as she leaned back, sipping her water. Once Kara set her fork down, sighing heavily, Lena rose to her feet and removed the plate with a grim set to her mouth.

     

                Sitting still, Kara stared at the bottle cap in front of her as Lena scraped the plates and opened the dishwasher. Drawing in a shaky breath, Kara couldn’t look at her as the burning desire to tell Lena stole over her.

     

                “Um … so I found something out today,” Kara conversationally started, her words slow to form as she stood.

     

                Lena was rinsing off a plate before loading it in the dishwasher, straightening up as she replied, trying to remain casual as she picked up on the significance of the moment, expecting to hear what was bothering Kara. “Oh, really? What was it?”

     

                “Mike … was having an affair.”

     

                There was a clatter as Lena dropped the next plate into the sink, cracking as it struck the metal basin and took out two wine glasses with a tinkling of broken glass. Kara watched, gripping the back of her chair as she scuffed her socked foot across the floor, taking in the sharpness of Lena’s gaze as their eyes met, her shoulders taut as she held her empty hands over the sink, the water still running.

     

                A multitude of emotions flashed across Lena’s face in quick succession, primarily shock, before it softened into aching pity as her shoulders drooped. A lump got caught in Kara’s throat and she felt a hollow shakiness in her stomach, the expectation of some further explanation hanging in the silence that stretched between them.

     

                When she didn’t say anything, Lena slowly shut the water off and braced her hands against the edge of the sink, hanging her head as she exhaled forcefully. “I’m sorry.”

     

                “It’s okay.”

     

                Lips parting in surprise, Lena’s head rose to meet her eyes, rooted to the spot. Kara’s face was pinched with confusion and shockingly pale as she stood there, fiddling with her fingers. Other than that, she seemed so calm that all Lena could do was stare at her, waiting for some emotional response. 

     

                And then it came, a moment later, as if it had taken Kara’s body a minute to catch up with the admission. Her shoulders started to shake and she let out a small whimper, ducking her head as she covered her mouth with a hand. Her vision blurred and she sniffed, trying to stifle the building sob in her chest, it coming out as laughter in some bizarre reaction that made Lena even more concerned.

     

                And then Lena was there, her arms wrapping around her with such fierce tightness that Kara felt as if she was being held together but the truth was that she wasn’t even falling apart. The breath got stuck in her chest and she made a strangled sound, pitiful and raw and tangled with contrasting laughter, Lena’s murmured words lost on deaf ears as Kara buried her face in the side of her neck, the smell of her perfume suffusing her with an aching comfort. She’d never known anything like that; if anything, it was the reason that she started to cry freely, that ache in her filled with the notion of her, not him .

     

                Her tears soaked the shoulder of Lena’s thin sweater and Kara held onto her with a child-like neediness, trying to ground herself in the present to make the belated, confusing pain of the past sting a little less. Once she’d started to calm down, Lena coaxed her over to the sofa, fetching tissues and a blanket, putting the kettle on for tea and then pulling Kara towards her as she held her close and rubbed soothing circles on her back.

     

                “How-” Lena tried to ask, her voice coming out strained, wincing at the mere idea of a betrayal like that, of how maybe she’d made Kara feel caught on the opposite end of that feeling herself.

     

                “She was at the cemetery. She, uh, she knew about me. He told her we’d separated,” Kara hoarsely explained, her cheeks blotchy as she fiddled with the tissues in her hands. “She seemed nice. I kind of feel sorry for her.”

     

                “Sorry for her?”

     

                “Yeah. He lied to her as well. And, you know, maybe they were happy together when she lost him. We weren’t.”

     

                “He was your husband. You had years together, so much of your life, and this is how he hurts you? Feel sorry for yourself, not some other woman.”

     

                Looking up at her, Kara smiled tightly. “I don’t.”

     

                Taken aback, Lena’s mouth opened and closed as she struggled to comprehend Kara’s evident lack of anger. But Kara’s anger would have been an empty thing, directed at no one. That didn’t mean she wasn’t hurt , that there wouldn’t be a lot to unpack when she felt like she had the capacity for it, but anger evaded her and Kara thought it a pointless pursuit. 

     

                “This whole time I’ve been feeling guilty for the way I felt about it all, that … maybe I was moving on too quickly, that it was a shitty thing for me to do to sleep with you when … he’d barely been dead a year, but … my marriage was over . I know I told you that I- I couldn’t have seen us staying together but … now there’s proof and I just- I did love him and I know he loved me but he did this so … should I have felt guilty about it this whole time?” 

     

                She trailed off, wiping her cheeks on the cuff of her sweatshirt and then letting out a choked laugh, her eyes cutting sideways to Lena. Smiling, her bloodshot eyes creasing at the corners, Kara swallowed thickly as she reached out to brush the backs of her fingers over Lena’s cheek before her hand fell limply onto the back of the sofa.

     

                “And I guess I should be glad I didn’t feel too guilty about it all because I have you and … now I just feel like … the rest of it is going to be so easy now. Maybe he checked out of our marriage before I even did and I should be grateful for that because I no longer have to wonder if it was salvageable. And if I’m being honest, she told me and … all I felt was relief . It felt freeing.”

     

                “Kara-”

     

                “No,” Kara quickly cut her off, taking in the hesitant wariness on Lena’s face and giving her a pained smile. “Don’t say anything. I don’t want your pity, I don’t want you to make me feel better about it, I just- I’m- I’ll be fine. I already went through losing him so it’s not like I have to do it again, it’s just … I think I’m going to need to reevaluate some things.”

     

                She let out a quick laugh, her brow crumpling, and Lena reached out to smooth her hair out of her face. Head tilting to the side as she leaned against the sofa cushions, she smiled crookedly. 

     

                “I know you’ll be fine, and I’m not going to try and make you feel better about it. I just wanted to tell you that I love you and … you’re a very strong person. You’ve been through so much and I wish you didn’t have to do that but … you’re not alone. No matter what happens now.”

     

                “I know. I know I’m not and … I just- it’s bizarre but I just … feel so relieved. I don’t know what’s wrong with me but I’m not crying because I’m upset. I mean, she was there and I just wanted to laugh because it was like … this weight just suddenly vanished. So much of my life has changed over the last two years and it really does feel like it’s all behind me now. I get to move on, I get to be happy. I have a future ahead of me and- and I don’t have to dwell on the past and … it feels good to know that, to feel secure in that. I think … a part of me might have always felt a little guilty about that, as if it was never quite finished, but now … honestly, that’s the best gift he could have given me.”

     

                Pressing a hand to Kara’s cheek, Lena gave her a tender smile. “You have the rest of your life ahead of you,” she murmured. “An entire future. You get to decide what happens now, who you want to be, what you want to do.”

     

                “You know … you get to decide that too,” Kara slowly replied, leaning into her touch.

     

                Lips twitching with a ghost of a smile, Lena hummed in agreement, the sound faintly strained. A moment later, she drew in a shuddering breath, her green eyes clouding with confusion. “Can I be honest with you? I think … lately I’ve been getting used to the idea that I have the rest of my life too. Without her. That one day this will all be the past, and … it will be horrible but … I think … I don’t think I- that I … love her the same anymore. I haven’t for a while. I love her, of course I do but I- she’s so … different now, even though there’s still so much of her there, it just- I have a wife but I don’t have a marriage. The relationship I have is with you. I think … I’ve accepted that. Finally. And I know that one day I won’t have a wife anymore but … I’ll be okay. She’s half of my heart but she’s not my whole life and I just- I love you, I really do, so … I’ve already decided what I want my future to look like. I’ve been stuck in the past for so long but I-  I can see it clearly now and … I know she would want that for me. And I don’t feel guilty anymore, I just feel … hopeful that there’s a lot of good to come with you and it doesn’t have to mean writing over all the good I had with her. I just- I want you to know that I’m here and I’m not going anywhere. I pick you.”

     

                Leaning in, Kara kissed her slowly, savouring the knowledge that she was loved, she wasn’t alone, and she mattered to someone even if it hadn’t been the man she’d married. But that was all in the past, and she was there with Lena, and that felt more important than the reminder of her ended marriage, regardless of the reason it was over. She felt the last bit of blame she’d cast upon herself for moving on so quickly vanish, no longer beholden to the memories of the man she’d felt obligated to honour. It was liberating and Kara kissed Lena again.

    Chapter 29

                A week passed by, a painfully slow thing that left Kara feeling weighed down heavily with her thoughts, although she insisted to Lena that she was fine, and felt fine. It was still a big shift in her reality though, and even though it fundamentally changed nothing about her future, it changed everything about how she viewed the past. She’d revealed her findings to Alex over dinner during the week to a string of expletives and curses that surprised even Lena but Kara didn’t feel strongly about it in any way.

     

                She hadn’t been lying that it was freeing to no longer feel any sense of obligation or duty to honour her marriage and feel guilty about moving on quickly. In hindsight, it really was the best gift Mike had ever given her and something Kara may not have been able to give to herself. Still, Lena worried over her silence, over her solemn disposition as she tried to reconcile things in her mind. 

     

                Rising early for a Saturday, as was usual, Lena’s movements woke Kara, who blearily blinked at her, face creased with sleep as she smiled sweetly and fumbled for her glasses. Stifling a yawn and then rolling over to kiss her, Kara burrowed into the warmth of her girlfriend with the desire to stay wrapped up in bed for the rest of the day.

     

                “What’re you thinking about?” Lena intruded on her quiet thoughts.

     

                “How I wish we could stay in bed for the whole day,” Kara mumbled into her shoulder.

     

                “Come with me today,” Lena murmured, running her fingers down Kara’s arm, her eyebrows raised expectedly.

     

                “It’s okay.”

     

                “No, really. Come with me. It’s a nice day; we’ll take a picnic and sit in the gardens. She’ll love it.”

     

                “I’m fine. You don’t need to worry about me.”

     

                “But I do worry about you. There’s only so much one person can take and … this is a lot to process after everything with my secret wife and- and the lying and I-”

     

                Exhaling softly, trailing into a breathless laugh, Kara pushed herself up onto her elbows and gave Lena a bemused smile. “Lena … I know it’s probably not normal but I’m doing better now than I have been in years. For so long it’s felt like I was stuck in a rut but I have so many things in my life that are better now. My job, my home, my partner. The only thing I feel about my past is a relief that I’m not stuck in it any longer, and I wish Mike was alive to have his own happy future but he’s made that abundantly clear that even if I’d wanted to stay with him, our marriage was over. I … have so much to be grateful for - thanks to you.”

     

                Mouth twitching ruefully, Lena looked at her with brooding green eyes. “It’s not thanks to me . You pulled yourself out of a shit situation, over and over again. You’re resilient. You don’t need to be but it’s … admirable.”

     

                “No, I did it partly thanks to you. I am resilient but … I met you . You have changed so much for me and I’m not going to feel sorry for myself for being better off. So don’t worry. Please. Enjoy your picnic.”

     

                “Okay. I won’t worry. But come on the picnic. You said if I ever wanted anything to ask; I want you to come today.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara blew out her breath and then snorted. “Why today?”

     

                Sitting up, Lena shrugged and raked her hair back before giving Kara a crooked smile. “I just really want to spend today with you but I don’t want to rush my time with her. I feel like you need it - don’t interrupt - and you deserve my attention as well … so for today, I’d like you to come. Only if you want to. I can’t- I can’t guarantee it’ll be a nice picnic, I don’t know what mood she’ll be in or if she’ll even feel up to it but …”

     

                Kara was silent for a moment, her gaze searching, making sure Lena wasn’t asking out of guilt or some desire to make Kara feel better about her situation. She never wanted Lena to feel bad for having had a loving marriage and a wife who was alive, if not one who remembered her.

     

                “Okay,” she murmured after a moment.

     

                “Okay,” Lena agreed with a smile.

     

                She climbed out of bed after giving Kara a quick kiss and went to make them both some coffee. Laying back against the pillows, Kara stared up at the ceiling with a thoughtful look on her face and lowered her eyes when Lena came back. Sitting side by side, they sipped their coffee and watched the news until they’d finished and then showered and dressed for the day. 

     

                They walked Aristotle first, heading to a nearby store and picking out little pastries and cheeses and cured meats, fresh fruit and premade sandwiches. Carrying everything home, Lena went off in search of a picnic basket and blanket and Kara helped wash and prep the necessities before they packed everything away. Kara felt apprehension twist her stomach at the thought of a day spent with Andrea; it would be different this time and she didn’t quite know how to go about it. She would keep her hands to herself, she would let Lena lead the way and hope for a nice day for her girlfriend’s sake.

     

                Once they were ready to go, they bundled up in Lena’s car with their things and she drove them to Leviathan’s, parking out front and letting Kara carry the basket inside. They were buzzed through the double set of doors and Lena used her visitor’s pass to set the elevator into motion, taking them upstairs to Andrea’s room. Russell was on duty again and he greeted them warmly, seemingly unsurprised to see Kara there, which she took as a sign that Lena must have informed him of things between them in the last couple of weeks. 

     

                Lingering at the nurse’s station with the picnic basket and blanket, Kara spoke to Russell as she let Lena see to Andrea and try to coax her out for a picnic. Russell had already let them know she was in a good mood, rather relaxed, smiling, and lucid even if she didn’t remember anything. Patiently waiting five minutes, Kara smiled as she watched the two women appear, Andrea holding Lena’s hand with a bewildered look on her face, sky blue eyes slightly owlish as she blinked at Kara, the scar between her eyebrows deepening the perplexed furrow.

     

                “This is Kara,” Lena introduced her. “She’s coming to the picnic as well.”

     

                “Oh. Hello.”

     

                Kara gave her a warm smile, if a little reserved, trying not to spook her. “It’s nice to meet you.”

     

                Andrea’s face smoothed out into a polite smile and she nodded, shuffling a little closer to Lena, who gave her hand a reassuring squeeze. The four of them made their way downstairs, Kara shaking the blanket out in the shade of the tree dominating the courtyard garden, and she unpacked the food as the other two women made themselves comfortable. 

     

                Russell stayed long enough to ensure Andrea was okay before he vanished to his other duties, leaving her under the supervision of the other nurses in the garden. Residents were enjoying the warm weather, lounging on benches in patches of sunlight, some with visitors and others keeping their own company, and Lena softly pointed out the different foods to her wife as Kara pulled out the plastic plates and glasses.

     

                It was a peaceful late morning, the day warm but cut through by the relief of the overhanging shade of the tree, Andrea questioning both of them about their work, extending offers for a tour of her office at some point, talking about people from her childhood that Lena was familiar with as Kara listened politely. They talked about the news and the weather, the best places to eat in town and all manner of things as if they were three people at some corporate event, making small talk over their food.

     

                A couple of hours passed by and Lena showed Andrea videos of Aristotle, photos of the places she’d been, or corporate events, their heads ducked in close as Kara was content to sit quietly, watching the two of them together, privy to this special kind of heartbreak. There was a palpable ease between the three of them as lunchtime gave way to early afternoon, the sun following its arc overhead, and when Russell reappeared to do a lap and check in with the residents, Kara unobtrusively climbed to her feet and went to join him in the shady corner near the door to talk, giving the wives some time alone.

     

                The garden had emptied somewhat since they’d settled in, the heat driving everyone indoors to the various recreation rooms or for their lunch in the restaurant. There was a slight shift in the energy between them as Lena watched Kara go, her eyes tracking her movements across the garden. Her wife was giving her a scrutinising look as she read the open tenderness on Lena’s face, perceptive of her feelings even though she didn’t even know her.

     

                “You love her.”

     

                Lena blinked in surprise, turning to look at Andrea. Her face softened with a small smile. “I do.”

     

                “Is she your wife?”

     

                A quiet laugh escaped Lena and she covered Andrea’s hand with her own on the blanket. “No, you’re my wife.”

     

                Mild surprise flashed across her wife’s face and Andrea cocked her head to the side. “I’m your wife?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                Brow creasing with confusion, Andrea drew back slightly, taking a moment to reply as she considered it. “No, my wife is Lena.”

     

                The corners of her mouth twitched with a ghost of a smile at being remembered, albeit as a memory and not presently, and Lena’s eyelids shuttered. Drawing in a shuddering breath, she slowly exhaled.

     

                “It’s me, Andrea. I’m Lena,” she explained.

     

                “You’re Lena?”

     

                “Yes, I’m your wife.”

     

                Throat closing up, Lena glanced over at Kara, who was still quietly conversing with Russell. Their eyes met and she smiled slightly before closing her eyes. It left an odd feeling in her chest to be with the two women she loved, one of them clueless to their circumstances and the other with perhaps more understanding than Lena deserved. 

     

                “Lena.”

     

                Her name was tender coming out of Andrea’s mouth, barely louder than a murmur but laced with familiarity, love and almost a wistful sigh. Eyelids fluttering, Lena turned to look at her and froze. There was a spark in those sky blue eyes, however faint, that spoke of familiarity, had been there less often until it had vanished altogether months ago now. But now it was there and Lena’s lips parted slightly as she dared to hope, her reply tentative.

     

                “Andrea.”

     

                “Lena,” Andrea said with more conviction this time, her shoulders slumping as she smiled, that recognition filling her eyes now.

     

                “Is it you?” Lena whispered, her voice faltering, barely audible.

     

                “Who else would I be, my love?” Andrea replied, her face crumpling with bewildered amusement, laughing.

     

                The sob that escaped Lena was breathless and broken, her eyes quickly overflowing with hot tears that ran down her cheeks, her shoulders heaving as if she couldn’t catch her breath as her hands went to Andrea’s face. Cupping her cheeks in her hands, Lena choked on a pitiful sob, aching and desperate.

     

                “Oh. Oh, God. I’ve missed you.”

     

                “I’m right here.”

     

                Letting out a strangled sound of anguish, Lena’s hands fluttered around her wife’s face, shaking terribly from the shock. It had happened a few times, weeks between being remembered and always catching her off-guard, in those calm moments where Lena wasn’t trying to encourage Andrea to recognise her, when they were just enjoying each other’s company, allowing her mind to bridge that gap between her memories and herself. But it had been so long that Lena had thought that was it, that the last time they would know each other had gone without her even realising. Until now.

     

                Andrea hushed her, looking confused, wariness in her eyes as she wiped Lena’s tears away. Leaning in, she kissed her softly, surprised when Lena crushed their lips together in response, clutching fistfuls of Andrea’s cardigan as if trying to hold onto her, to make her stay. Breaking apart, Lena let out a hitching sob.

     

                “It’s okay,” Andrea murmured, kissing her cheeks and brushing her hair out of her face. “What’s wrong?”

     

                “It’s been so … hard .”

     

                “I’m- I’m here. I … something’s wrong. Isn’t it? My head, I- it’s so … I’m confused, Lena.”

     

                Sniffing as she tried to calm herself, swallowing her sobs as tears wet her cheeks, so much pent-up agony pouring out of her in a wave, Lena cupped Andrea’s hand to her cheek, leaning into her touch. 

     

                “It’s okay, it’s okay. You’re- you’re going to be fine. You … you have Alzheimer’s. Do you remember?”

     

                “That word … I don’t know what that word is,” Andrea murmured, her brow crumpling, deepening the scar.

     

                Breath hitching, Lena’s chin wobbled as she wiped her cheeks on the cuffs of her shirt. “It means … you forget things. Like me.”

     

                A confused laugh escaped Andrea. “I would never forget you.”

     

                Swallowing thickly, Lena gave her a thin smile. “That’s good.”

     

                “I’m … I’m sick. Yes, I remember now. How long have I forgotten?”

     

                “Not long,” Lena whispered, her voice uneven as she lied to spare her wife the pain of knowing she was getting worse.

     

                Her eyes stung fiercely and her throat felt so tight that she could barely breathe, each breath a shallow, painful ache. She looked at Andrea as if she could hardly believe she was real, and from the sidelines, Kara watched with aching understanding on her face, realising what was happening and affording Lena the space to exist in this rare moment of bliss with her wife before it was snatched away from her once more.

     

                And Lena didn’t want to waste a second, swallowing thickly and cupping Andrea’s face, devastation and adoration on her own as she gave her a pleading look. What she would have given to exist in that moment forever.

     

                “I love you,” she whispered, her voice rough with fervour and torn with anguish. “I love you, I love you.”

     

                Reaching up, Andrea pressed her fingertips to Lena’s temples, a featherlight touch, and let out a quick laugh, so easy, so sweet and light. It split Lena in half, that yearning ache of missing her wife making her eyes fill with fresh tears.
